[Definition def:admissible of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let $f\colon B_1(0)\to [0,\infty)$, let
		\[
		X=\{\bm{x}_1,\dots,\bm{x}_s\}\subset B_1(0),
		\]
		and let $\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1$ satisfy
		\[
			0\leq\varepsilon<\rho,
			\qquad
			0\le \tau_0<\tau_1.
		\]
		We say that $f$ is a threshold-admissible optimization landscape for $X$,
		with parameters
		$(\varepsilon,\rho,\tau_0,\tau_1)$, if:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item for every $j=1,\dots,s$, the function $f$ has a 
			local minimum
			$\widetilde{\bm{x}}_j\in
			\overline{B_\varepsilon(\bm{x}_j)}$;
			\item the relevant minima are uniformly shallow and all points
			outside the certified neighborhoods are uniformly higher:
			\begin{eqnarray}
			\max_{1\le j\le s} f(\widetilde{\bm{x}}_j)&\le& \tau_0,\\
			f(\bm{z})&\ge &\tau_1, 
			\quad
			\forall
			\bm{z}\in B_1(0)\setminus
			\bigcup_{j=1}^s B_\rho(\bm{x}_j).
			\end{eqnarray}
		\end{enumerate}
title: Threshold-admissible landscape

body:
Let X_n, X be random variables or vectors with X_n -> X in distribution as n -> infinity, and let Y_n -> c in probability for a constant c. Then X_n + Y_n -> X + c in distribution, X_n Y_n -> c X in distribution, and, provided c is not 0, X_n / Y_n -> X / c in distribution. More generally, if g(x,y) is continuous at every point (x,c), then g(X_n,Y_n) -> g(X,c) in distribution. Slutsky's theorem lets one combine a distributional limit with a probability limit as though the latter were a genuine constant. Due to Eugen Slutsky.
For the scalar arithmetic conclusions, X_n, X, and Y_n are real-valued random variables and c is a deterministic real constant.
X_n converges in distribution to X.
Y_n converges in probability to c.
For division, c is nonzero.
For a vector or general mapping formulation, explicitly choose separable metric state spaces S, T, and U; take X_n and X to be measurable S-valued random elements, Y_n to be measurable T-valued random elements, and c in T deterministic.
For the general mapping conclusion, g:S x T -> U is measurable and continuous at every point (x,c) with x in S; a weaker almost-sure continuity formulation would require a separately revised statement.
Any named vector addition, multiplication, or division operation must be explicitly defined and continuous on the selected state spaces; scalar multiplication cX is distinct from an unspecified vector product.

[Defn of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] We say that an area process $\mathbb{A}$ on $Z\in C^\gamma \times C^\gamma$ is \emph{time translation--invariant} if for all $(s,t) \in \triangle$ and $\tau \geq 0$ such that $t + \tau \leq 1$ and $Z_{s + \tau,u + \tau} = Z_{s,u}$ for all $u \in [s,t]$, one has
\[
\mathbb{A}_{s + \tau, t + \tau}(Z) = \mathbb{A}_{s, t}(Z)\;.
\]

Let $\phi$ be a bounded continuous function on $\partial D$. [Proposition prop:pseudo-bloch of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $N=2M$ and let $\{\Sigma_a\}_{a=1}^{d}$, with $d=\tfrac{N(N+1)}2-1$, be a
trace-orthonormal basis of the traceless complex-symmetric matrices, so that
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_a=0$, and
$\Sigma_a^{T}=\Sigma_a$. Orthonormality here is meant for the bilinear trace form
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)$, with no complex conjugation, and such a basis exists
because that form is nondegenerate on the complex-symmetric matrices, for instance
the symmetrised units $(E_{ij}+E_{ji})/\sqrt2$ for $i<j$ together with an
orthonormal set of $N-1$ real traceless diagonal matrices work. The
$\Sigma_a$ are complex symmetric, not Hermitian, so they are the bilinear analogue
of the Gell-Mann matrices rather than the matrices themselves. Write

\[
\rho_z=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}\rho_z}{N}\,\mathrm{I}+\sum_{a=1}^{d}r_a(z)\,\Sigma_a,\qquad
r_a(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_z\Sigma_a).
\]

Then the coordinate vector obeys the linear flow

\[
\dot r_a(z)=\sum_{b}\Omega_{ab}\,r_b(z),\qquad
\Omega_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Sigma_a[K,\Sigma_b]\bigr),\qquad \Omega^{T}=-\Omega.
\]

Hence the flow lies in $\OO(d,\mathbb{C})$ and preserves the bilinear quantity
$\sum_a r_a^{2}$.

[Theorem thm:geounicont of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$.
	\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=\arabic*.]
		\item Almost surely, for all $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, there exists at least one geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
		\item Almost surely, all geodesics in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ are H\"older-$(2/3-\epsilon)$ continuous for all $\epsilon > 0$.
		\item For any fixed $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, almost surely there is a unique geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix training data D of size n>=1, a prior probability pi, model likelihood p(D|theta), and a test-observation distribution nu on pairs s=(y,x). For lambda in a positive open interval containing1, assume Z(lambda)=integral p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta) is finite and positive, and define q_lambda(dtheta)=p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta)/Z(lambda). This is likelihood-only tempering; the prior is not raised to lambda. Temperature T=1/lambda is cold when lambda>1. For a posterior rho let m_rho(y|x)=E_rho p(y|x,theta), B(rho)=E_nu[-log m_rho(y|x)], J(rho)=E_rho[-log p(D|theta)], and Ghat(rho,D)=J(rho)/n. Assume the losses used are finite and lambda->B(q_lambda) is differentiable at1. Definition1 calls the local CPE present exactly when Bprime(1)<0. This definition concerns infinitesimal cooling at1; Bprime(1)=0 alone does not imply a minimum or rule out improvement at another temperature. The authors call q_1 underfitting if some posterior rho has simultaneously B(rho)<B(q_1) and Ghat(rho,D)<Ghat(q_1,D).

[Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Fix a set $\Sigma = \llbracket 1, N \rrbracket$ with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ or $N = \infty$ and $T_0, T_1\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $T_0 \leq T_1$. A $\Sigma$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L} : \Sigma \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ is said to satisfy the {\em interlacing Gibbs property} if it is interlacing, meaning that 
$$ L_i(j-1) \geq L_{i+1}(j) \mbox{ for all $i \in \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $j \in \llbracket T_0 + 1, T_1 \rrbracket$},$$
and for any finite $K = \llbracket k_1, k_2 \rrbracket \subseteq \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $a,b \in \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$ with $a < b$ the following holds.  Suppose that $f, g$ are two increasing paths drawn in $\{ (r,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : a \leq r \leq b\}$ and $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \mathfrak{W}_k$ with $k=k_2-k_1+1$ altogether satisfy that $\mathbb{P}(A) > 0$ where $A$ denotes the event $$A =\{ \vec{x} = ({L}_{k_1}(a), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(a)), \vec{y} = ({L}_{k_1}(b), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(b)), L_{k_1-1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = f, L_{k_2+1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = g \},$$
where if $k_1 = 1$ we adopt the convention $f = \infty = L_0$. Then, we have for any $\{ B_i \in \Omega(a, b, x_i , y_i) \}_{i = 1}^k$ that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\left( L_{i + k_1-1}\llbracket a,b \rrbracket = B_{i} \mbox{ for $i \in \llbracket 1, k \rrbracket$} \, \vert  A \, \right) = \mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{Inter}, \operatorname{Geom}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, f, g} \left( \cap_{i = 1}^k\{ Q_i = B_i \} \right).
\end{equation}
title: Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899

Fix 0<alpha<log(2)/2 and rho in [0,1/2) with 2alpha<I(1-2rho), where I(t)=((1+t)log(1+t)+(1-t)log(1-t))/2 and I(1)=log(2). For integers N with rho N integral, let M=floor(exp(alpha N))+1 and let xi^1,...,xi^M be iid uniform patterns in {-1,+1}^N (all bits mutually independent). Conditional on the stored patterns, draw one input sigma^nu independently and uniformly on the Hamming sphere of radius rho N about xi^nu, for every nu. Set T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu [exp(xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)-exp(-xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)]). Equivalently T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu xi_i^mu exp(sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)), since the omitted common factor is 2sinh(1)>0. Then P(exists nu exists i: T_i(sigma^nu)!=xi_i^nu) tends to zero as N tends to infinity. The sign at zero may be arbitrary. In particular rho=0 gives simultaneous fixed-point stability of every stored pattern whenever alpha<log(2)/2. This is one random corrupted input per pattern and coordinate evaluation on that initial input, not uniform correction of all Hamming-ball inputs and not a claim about an adaptively changing asynchronous trajectory. Source: Demircigil--Heusel--Lowe--Upgang--Vermet, Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.4, arXiv:1702.01929v2, PDF p4; model equation (1), PDF p2. Integer rounding of the paper's M=exp(alpha N)+1 is immaterial.

 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]

 \end{enumerate}
 Then there is a subsequence $(K_{n_k},f_{n_k})$ that converges in the $d_\infty$ metric. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrable supremum of routes to a bounded region structural attempt Result: Let L(x)=len R(0,x). Suppose on a containing square E|L(x)-L(y)|^p<=C*|x-y|^p for a p>2, with a jointly measurable version and finite mean at one anchor. On the dyadic grid of mesh2^-k there are order2^(2k) parent-child or neighbor pairs. The expected maximum increment is at most Cprime*2^(-k*(1-2/p)). This is summable, so telescoping along grid ancestors constructs a continuous modification with finite expected supremum. Check: Use max_j |Z_j|<=(sum_j |Z_j|^p)^(1/p) and Jensen, then sum the resulting geometric series. The increment bound implies stochastic continuity, identifying the modification at each deterministic point; Fubini identifies it at each independent uniform sample point, and countability handles the entire sampled sequence. Obstruction: The source only gives first moments of individual route lengths, not p-moment increments of L. Its compatibility condition does not make Euclidean route length an automatic metric with a triangle inequality, so a metric-chaining shortcut is unjustified.

body: [Proposition prop:big_loops_are_fat_simple_cle of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] Let $(\kappa_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be a sequence in $(8/3,4)$ with $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$. For all $\varepsilon>0$ such that a.s.\ no loop of $\Gamma^4$ has diameter exactly $\varepsilon$ (all but countably many $\varepsilon$, since $\varepsilon \mapsto \BE[\#\{\SCL \in \Gamma^4 \colon \diam(\SCL) \ge \varepsilon\}]$ is finite and non-increasing, hence has countably many discontinuities), the number of loops of $\Gamma^{\kappa_{n}}$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$ converges in law as $n \to \infty$ to the number of loops of $\Gamma^4$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$. Moreover, for all $\varepsilon, \varepsilon'>0$, there exists $\delta>0$ (depending on $\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon'$, and on the sequence $(\kappa_n)_{n \ge 1}$) such that for all $n\ge 1$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon'$, all the loops of $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$ encircle a Euclidean ball of radius $\delta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 4 (Order properties) of arXiv:2607.29560, 'Tractable Relaxations of Multivariate Stochastic Dominance via Optimal Transport and CVaR'] For fixed $\gamma\in[0,1]$, CSD is a preorder, is preserved under
common-weight mixtures. In addition CSD is nested in $\gamma$, i.e., $P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}Q$ implies $
P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma'}^{\rm CSD}Q$  whenever $0\le\gamma\le\gamma'\le1$ and if $\gamma<1$, then
$ 
P\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}Q
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q\preceq_{s,\lambda,\gamma}^{\rm CSD}P
$ 
hold if and only if $W_s(P,Q)=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:entropy-decomp of arXiv:2606.09221, 'Log-Sobolev under random monotone censoring'] For every $0\le s \le n$ and $f:\, H_s\to \mathbb{R}$, we have
$$     
\operatorname{Ent}_{\pi_s}(f^2) =\operatorname{Ent}_{p}(\bar{f}^2)+\sum_{k= s}^{n-1}p_{k}\operatorname{Ent}_{\nu_k}(f^2),
$$
where $\bar{f}:\, \{s,\ldots,n\}\to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $\bar{f}(k)= (\mathbb{E}_{\nu_k}f^2)^{\frac12}=\Vert f(X_k)\Vert_{L^2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Entropy decomposition

[Lemma lem:haar-passive-zero of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $V_-$ and $V_+$ be orthogonal $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-modules.  On their
star dilations write $\mathscr T_\pm,\mathscr E_\pm,\mathsf Q_\pm$ and
$\mathscr G_\pm=\mathsf Q_\pm\mathscr T_\pm$ for the maps in (eq:3.2.2 of the paper).
Let $\mathsf M:(V_-)_\star\to(V_+)_\star$ be a typed passive singleton,
so that
\[
 (\mathsf Mh)(i,\theta)=M_i h(i,\theta),\qquad
 \rho_+(R_i(\theta))^*M_i\rho_-(R_i(\theta))=M_i,
 \qquad \sum_iM_i=0.
\tag{3.2.10s$_1$}
\]
Put $\mathsf S^+_{+,-}=\mathsf Q_+\mathsf M\mathscr E_-^*$.
If $\Pi_-$ is the projection onto $V_-^{\mathrm{SO}(n)}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr G_+^*\mathsf S^+_{+,-}\Pi_-=0.}
\tag{3.2.10s$_2$}
\]
Writing
$\mathsf S^-_{-,+}=\mathscr E_-\mathsf M^*\mathsf Q_+$, applying the
same statement to $\mathsf M^*$ gives the oppositely oriented identity
$\Pi_-\mathsf S^-_{-,+}\mathscr G_+=0$.
Consequently every maximal residual temporal component made only of
passive singleton supernodes is identically zero, term by term in its
weak order and finite residual gaps.  This includes either end component
under the common auxiliary Haar projection of
(lem:haar-residual of the paper).

body: [Definition of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] For a bond $b \in \gamma$, call a pocket $D_b = D_b(\gamma)$ the connected component of all finite regions in $\mathbb Z^2 \setminus \gamma$ containing a region that has $b$ as part of its boundary. If there is no such finite region adjacent to $b$, then $D_b = \emptyset$.

body: Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space and let p, q in [1, infinity] be conjugate exponents, meaning 1/p + 1/q = 1 (with 1/infinity read as 0). If f is in L^p(mu) and g is in L^q(mu), then fg is in L^1(mu) and integral of |fg| dmu <= ||f||_p ||g||_q, where ||f||_p = (integral |f|^p dmu)^(1/p) for p < infinity and the essential supremum of |f| for p = infinity. The discrete form is sum |x_i y_i| <= (sum |x_i|^p)^(1/p) (sum |y_i|^q)^(1/q). For 1 < p < infinity, equality holds iff |f|^p and |g|^q are proportional a.e.
title: Holder's inequality

[Lemma 27 (Matsuda, Lemma 3.4 and Remark 3.5) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186']

Let $t>0$ be fixed.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]
=\frac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log t\big)+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{b-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1)\]
and
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_{\leq}}(B^0)\big]
=\tfrac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log(b-a)-1\big)+o(1).\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$, then as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-a}^{d-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r
-\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-b}^{d-b}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1).\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.06953, 'Asymptotic Results for Uniform Group Drawing in the Coupon Collector's Problem'] Let $t\ge 2$ be an integer. \newline\newline
    (a) If $s = n -\lambda\cdot n^{\frac{t-1}{t}}$, where $\lambda >0$, then $$\lim_{n \to \infty} \E[Y] = te^{-\lambda^t}+(t+1)(1-e^{-\lambda^t}).$$ Moreover, $Y \xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{\mathcal{D}} Z$, where $Z$ is a random variable with the distribution $$\PP[Z=i] = 
    \begin{cases}
            e^{-\lambda^t}, &i=t, \\
            1-e^{-\lambda^t}, &i=t+1.
        \end{cases}$$
    (b) If $s = n-o(n^{t/(t+1)})$ and $s = n-\omega(n^{(t-1)/t})$ then 
    $$ \lim_{n \to \infty} \E[Y] = t+1.$$
    Moreover, $Y \xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{\mathcal{P}} t+1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.06953

For Macdonald polynomials P_lambda(x; q, t) and the weights b^el_lambda(q, t) = prod over the boxes s of lambda with even leg length l(s) of b_lambda(s; q, t) = (1 - q^{a(s)} t^{l(s)+1}) / (1 - q^{a(s)+1} t^{l(s)}), where a(s) and l(s) are the arm and leg lengths of s, the summation over all partitions lambda evaluates to the explicit product: sum_lambda b^el_lambda(q, t) * P_lambda(x; q, t) = prod_{i >= 1} (t*x_i; q)_infinity / (x_i; q)_infinity * prod_{i < j} (t*x_i*x_j; q)_infinity / (x_i*x_j; q)_infinity, with (a; q)_infinity = prod_{r >= 0} (1 - a*q^r). This is Macdonald's identity (Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., p. 349, Example 4(ii)), quoted as Lemma 3.2, (3.3), of arXiv:2505.17825; its skew form, Lemma 3.3, (3.12) there, is sum_lambda b^el_lambda P_{lambda/eta}(x; q, t) = Theta_el(x) * sum_mu b^el_mu Q_{eta/mu}(x; q, t), with Theta_el(x) the product above.
Absolute convergence of the series (|x_i| < 1)
Parameters |q|, |t| < 1

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2604.05138, 'Convergence rate of $H$-property for step-graphons'] The following two items hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $W$ does not satisfy Condition $B'$, then there exist positive constants $c$ and $\lambda$ such that
    $$
    P_n(W) \leq c \, e^{-\lambda n}. 
    $$
    \item If $W$ satisfies Conditions $A$ and $B$, then there exist positive constants $c$ and $\lambda$ such that
    $$
    1 - P_n(W) \leq c \, e^{-\lambda n}.
    $$
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 18 of arXiv:2604.05138

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Under assumption \eqref{psicondition}, for any $1 \le p\le \infty$, we have the limit laws
\[ \sqrt{N} W_{I,p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \| Y \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{and} \quad \sqrt{N} W_{\mathbb{T},p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| Y -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])}, \]
and the laws of the iterated logarithm
\[ \begin{split} \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{I,p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \| f \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.}, \\ \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{\mathbb{T},p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| f -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.} \end{split} \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 3 of arXiv:2512.03884

body: [Proposition AC homeo extension on Cantor of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(A\) and \(B\) be closed, non-empty and nowhere dense subsets of \(2^\mathbb{N}\). Suppose there is a homeomorphism \(h: A \to B\) such that for every Borel \(E \subset A\) we have \(\lambda^0(E) = 0 \iff \lambda^0(h(E)) = 0 \). Then there is a homeomorphism \(\hat{h} \in \AC(2^\mathbb{N})\) extending \(h\).

Own-work draft, claim w733-T363-023 v1; proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. On x1=(1,1/4),x2=(-1,1/4), labels+1, train both layers of f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x), with no biases, by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially require exactly one positive-output both-active neuron C, at least one positive-output x1-only neuron A, no x2-only neuron, and all remaining neurons strictly dead with arbitrary output. There is no initial restriction on C tilt, output-to-hidden norm ratio, initialization scale, or prediction imbalance. A global absolutely continuous flow exists; every such flow creates a positive x2-only B seed at finite time and then attains global normalized margin sqrt17/16, with normalization by total parameter squared norm. Reflection exchanges the two points. This is an entire activation-pattern family, extending the prior tilted balanced subcone. A C-to-A exit is impossible because the incoming C normal velocity at that boundary is positive. Under hypothetical absence of B, y and v diverge, homogeneity gives v>=3y/4 eventually, and a late E=f1-f2 barrier becomes invariant. The weighted variable s=v+(w.x1)/a then obeys s<=s(base)exp(aI1-bI2), a=sqrt17/4,b=15/(8sqrt17)-1/3>0, I_i=integral[-ell_prime(fi)]dt; the clock contradiction forces B creation. For iid Gaussian hidden/output coordinates N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0, p=atan(1/4)/pi, the exact probability of this family and its disjoint reflection is J_m=m*p[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. It adds70 proposed global signed permutation orbits at widths2..6:2,6,12,20,30. With the prior two-initial-seed family this gives196 proposed global orbits and2643 unclassified. These are sufficient-family masses and unaudited labels, not total basin probabilities or a solution of the general max-margin question. Do not add the full prior subcone mass P_m to H_m+J_m: its single-C contribution is already contained in J_m. Only k>=2 subcone terms are disjoint extras. Multiple C neurons and negative-output live neurons remain outside this theorem.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:86c95ee5c518a4ff7c79edfa250fa9c9df7efed33ab77cee6fa0382902b47bb1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/86/86c95ee5c518a4ff7c79edfa250fa9c9df7efed33ab77cee6fa0382902b47bb1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:56e2e2bd2381e05c2195d21c80a6b1c17bb0c5790cd5c7d1e142530e422186f2","bundle_entry_key":"exactly-one-shared-positive-neuron-global-margin","bundle_id":"population.relu-exactly-one-shared-positive-neuron-global-margin","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:relu-two-point-one-shared-positive-neuron-one-point-seed-global-margin","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A permanent one-point sector and exactly one positive shared neuron reach global margin
Claim w733-T363-023 v1; kind moved; target2; proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

## Statement
Consider x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels+1, f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x), no biases, both layers trained by continuous gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially there is exactly one positive-output both-active neuron C, at least one positive-output x1-only neuron A, and all remaining neurons are strictly dead with arbitrary output. There is no x2-only neuron initially. There are NO restrictions on the tilt, output-to-hidden norm ratio, scale, or initial prediction imbalance. A global absolutely continuous flow exists; every such flow creates a positive x2-only seed at finite time and then attains the global normalized margin sqrt17/16. Reflection exchanges the two inputs. This is a whole activation-pattern family.

The margin is min(f(x1),f(x2))/N, N=sum_j(v_j^2+||w_j||^2). This theorem does not classify initializations with two or more C neurons or with a negative-output live neuron. No independent review or literature novelty is claimed.

## 1. Setup and the only possible strict exit
Use claims015/017 section1 for positive-live continuation: A stays strictly A, dead neurons stay dead, C output v increases and stays positive. Global absolutely continuous continuation exists; Ndot<=2a(a1+a2)N, where a=||x_i||=sqrt17/4 and ai=-ell_prime(fi)>0. Since fi>=0, ai<=1 and no finite-time blowup occurs. C boundary contacts have measure zero under the prescribed zero-derivative convention: the surviving input gives a strictly negative normal derivative at the missing-input boundary, whereas an absolutely continuous function has derivative zero almost everywhere on a level set. Thus C-mask equations hold almost everywhere before a strict exit. Uniqueness at grazing contacts is not assumed.

Write C hidden weights as w=(u,y), its output as v>0, and H_A=sum_A v_j(w_j.x1)>0. A prospective exit into A would reach z2=w.x2=0,z1>0. At that boundary f2=0 and f1>0, hence a1<a2. The incoming C-mask normal velocity would be
 z2dot=v[(-15/16)a1+(17/16)a2]>0.
This excludes a first such hit from the strict C side: continuity makes z2dot positive in a preceding neighborhood, incompatible with positive z2 approaching zero. Near that boundary the other preactivation is positive, so there is no other mask change in that neighborhood. The same argument applies after any earlier grazing contacts at the other boundary. Therefore C cannot exit into A. Since y increases, C cannot hit both preactivations zero. Its only possible strict exit is into B (x2-only), after which B persists by claim015.

It remains to prove that a strict B exit occurs in finite time. Assume for contradiction that no strict B exit ever occurs. Then C remains in the closed C cone y>=4|u| for all time, with its equations holding almost everywhere. In the rest of the proof all clocks may be reset at a finite base time; constant prefactors depend on that base time.

## 2. Eventual output-to-height control without an initial hypothesis
Put Ii=integral ai dt and T=I1+I2. Bounded T would bound N and both predictions by the norm inequality, keeping a1+a2 bounded below on the infinite physical-time trajectory; contradiction. Thus T->infinity.

Almost everywhere ydot=v(a1+a2)/4 and v>=v(0)>0, so y>=y(0)+v(0)T/4->infinity. Homogeneity preserves delta=v^2-u^2-y^2. Hence v^2>=y^2+delta, and at all sufficiently late times
 v>=3y/4.
No sign assumption on delta or initial v/y was used. Fix L after this inequality holds permanently.

## 3. A permanent positive prediction imbalance eventually appears
Let E=f1-f2=H_A+2vu. At E=0, u<0, a1=a2=b0>0, and the C equations give udot=0, vdot=b0*y/2. Thus
 Edot=b0[||grad H_A||^2+u*y].
At E=0, uv=-H_A/2; since y/v<=4/3 and uv<0, u*y>=(4/3)u*v=-2H_A/3. The one-point gradient bound is ||grad H_A||^2>=2aH_A. Therefore, for times after L,
 Edot>=b0(2a-2/3)H_A>0.
An E=0 contact cannot occur on a C boundary: on the A-side boundary f2=0<f1, while on the B-side boundary E=0 would give a1=a2 and incoming z1dot=v(a^2-15/16)b0=v*b0/8>0, excluding an incoming hit from C. The preceding inequality is therefore a genuine local inward derivative at every possible late E=0 contact. Once E>0 after L, it remains positive under the no-B assumption.

Such a positive E must occur after L. Otherwise E<=0 for all sufficiently late times, so a1>=a2 and, after resetting clocks there, I1>=T/2. The exact A hyperbolic formula gives H_A>=H_A(base) exp(2aI1). Claim016's C-cone estimate, which needs no output balance assumption, gives
 N_C<=N_C(base) exp(kappa T), kappa=4/sqrt17<a,
 and f2<=N_C/sqrt17.
Consequently E>=H_A-f2>=H_A(base)exp(aT)-N_C(base)exp(kappa T)/sqrt17->infinity, contradicting E<=0. Hence choose L1>=L with E>0 forever afterward.

## 4. The shared neuron eventually leans toward the missing point
For t>=L1, a1<a2 and udot=v(a1-a2)<0 almost everywhere. If u is already nonpositive, it stays so. Otherwise suppose u remains positive forever. Then E=H_A+2vu>=H_A(L1)=h0>0. For exponential loss a1/a2<=exp(-h0)<1. For logistic loss, f2>=0 and E>=h0 imply
 a1/a2=(1+exp(f2))/(1+exp(f2+E))<=2/(1+exp(h0))<1.
Thus a1<=r*a2 for a constant r<1. Since T->infinity and eventually a1<=a2, I2->infinity. Integrating udot<=-(1-r)v(0)a2 forces u->-infinity, a contradiction. Hence at some finite L2>=L1 we have u<=0 permanently, while E>0 and v>=3y/4.

## 5. A dissipative clock variable forces the missing B seed
Reset clocks at L2. Let q1=(w.x1)/a>=0 and s=v+q1. In C with u<=0 and y<=4v/3,
 v<=s<=v+y/sqrt17<=v(1+4/(3sqrt17))<2v,
 z2=-u+y/4<=y/2<=2v/3.
The exact C equations give
 sdot=a*a1*s+a2[z2-(15/(4sqrt17))*v]
      <=(a*a1-b*a2)*s,
 b=15/(8sqrt17)-1/3>0.
The sign of b follows from45>8sqrt17, or2025>1088. Thus
 s<=s(L2)exp(aI1-bI2).
Also ||w||^2<=17y^2/16<=17v^2/9, so N_C=v^2+||w||^2<=26v^2/9<=26s^2/9. Therefore
 N_C<=C exp(2aI1-2bI2),
 H_A>=H_A(L2)exp(2aI1),
 N_C/H_A<=C' exp(-2bI2)->0.
If I1 were bounded, N_C->0 would contradict v>=v(0)>0. Thus I1->infinity, H_A->infinity, and E>=H_A-N_C/sqrt17->infinity. For exponential or logistic loss, a1/a2->0. Integrating the eventual inequality a1<=epsilon*a2, for each epsilon>0, gives I1/I2->0. Hence aI1-bI2->-infinity, forcing s->0 and contradicting s>=v(0)>0. The no-B assumption is impossible.

After a finite strict B entry, the network has positive A and B neurons and only dead neurons otherwise. Claim009 supplies global normalized margin sqrt17/16 for this no-C family. No mixed-C asymptotic theorem is needed for this final implication.

## 6. Exact Gaussian probability and new whole-pattern labels
For iid hidden/output N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, sigma>0, let p=atan(1/4)/pi and q=1/4-p/2. C+ has probability p/2, A+ and B+ each have probability q, and a dead neuron with arbitrary output has probability p. A family with exactly one C+, at least one A+, and all other neurons dead has probability m(p/2)[(q+p)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. The reflected family is disjoint, so their combined exact mass is
 J_m=m*p[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)].
This holds at any positive scale, including1e-6. It is a sufficient-family probability, not a total basin probability.

Resolving dead output signs produces m(m-1)/2 permutation orbits per orientation, or m(m-1) combined:2,6,12,20,30 at widths2..6, totaling70. These are disjoint from claim017's two-initial-seed family, whose whole-orbit count was126. The resulting proposed global labels total196; the prior2994-orbit inventory then contains196 global,20 source-bad,135 nonfitting, and2643 unclassified. These labels all inherit their proofs' unaudited status.

The whole-family mass H_m+J_m is disjoint. Do NOT add the full P_m of claim020 to that sum: its k=1 contribution is now contained in J_m. Only the k>=2 terms of that subcone formula are disjoint additional contributions. This prevents double counting while preserving the older sufficient bounds.

## Review limits
The hardest new points are the eventual imbalance barrier in section3 and excluding a C-to-A exit at a boundary. Sections2?5 contain the new seed-creation argument; existing claims009/015/016 and017 section1 are used at their stated scope and remain independently unaudited dependencies. No floating-point result or formal certificate is needed or asserted for this analytic proof. Prior subcone simulations concern only a subset of this larger family. Full unconstrained Gaussian basin classification remains open, especially multiple C and negative-output live neurons.

[Theorem slowvaryingtails of arXiv:2412.06246, 'The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries'] Let $\zeta$ be a random variable that satisfies, for some $\alpha\in(0,2)$ and some slow-varying function $L(t)$, the tail estimate 
    \begin{equation}\mathbb{P}(|\zeta|\geq t)=L(t)t^{-\alpha},\quad\forall t\geq 1\end{equation} and that $\zeta$ has a symmetric distribution. Let $X=(x_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq N,1\leq j\leq n}$ be a rectangular random matrix (where $N=\lfloor \delta n\rfloor$ for some $\delta>1$) with i.i.d. entries of distribution $\zeta$. Then we can find a slow varying function $L'(t)$ such that we have
    $$
\mathbb{P}(\sigma_{min}(X)\geq n^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}L'(n)^{-1})\geq 1-n^{-D}.
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem slowvaryingtails of arXiv:2412.06246

At d=250 on two random a no interior bulk local maximum was found (slab face f-Ef ~1.05, an ascent direction), the component maxima near a_i reach 1.13-1.26, so the bulk/component crossover is between 150 and 250; a_i are saddles below d~108. [Lemma lemlocal of arXiv:2606.29036, 'The limit law of the largest interpoint distance in a $d$-dimensional ellipsoid'] There exist constants $C>0$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the following
holds. Let $x=x(e,\delta,w)$, $y=x(e',\delta',w')$, and suppose that
$2-\|x-y\|\le\varepsilon$ for some $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$. Then
\[
\delta+\delta'\le C\varepsilon,
\]
and
\[
\|w\|^2+\|w'\|^2\le C\varepsilon.
\]
Moreover, $\langle e,e'\rangle+1\le C\varepsilon$.

Equivalently, if $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ is defined by
$\langle e,-e'\rangle=\cos\theta$,
then $\theta^2\le C\varepsilon$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Localization

body:
[Theorem th:poly of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] Assume that $n\geq2$, and consider the following:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item Two symmetric functions, which are polynomials with respect to $z$ and $\bar{z}$:
    \begin{equation}
      S(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n z_j
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      R(z)=\sum_{1\leq j<k\leq n}|z_j-z_k|^2=n\sum_{j=1}^n\left|z_j-\frac{S(z)}n\right|^2.
    \end{equation}
  \item The normalized complex Hermite polynomial\footnote{The Rodrigues
      formula is
      $\mathrm H_{a,b}(s,\overline
      s)=\frac{(-1)^{a+b}}{\sqrt{a!b!}}\mathrm{e}^{|s|^2}\bar\partial_s^{a}\partial_s^{b}\mathrm{e}^{-|s|^2}$.}$\mathrm
    H_{a,b}$ of bidegree $(a,b)$ for $\gamma_1$.
  \item The classical generalized Laguerre polynomial\footnote{Defined by the
      Laguerre equation (equation eq:laguerre of the paper) and normalized by
      $L^{\alpha}_m(0)=\binom{m+\alpha}{m}$. These polynomials are orthogonal
      with respect to the probability distribution
      $\mathrm{Gamma}(\kappa,1)=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\kappa)}x^{\kappa-1}\mathrm{e}^{-x}\mathbf{1}_{x\geq0}\mathrm{d}x$.
      However, they are not orthonormal.} $L_m^{(\kappa-1)}$ of degree $m$,
    with $\kappa=\frac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}$.
  \end{itemize}
  Then for every $a,b,m\in\mathbb N$, the symmetric polynomial
  \begin{equation}
    P_{a,b,m}(z)
    =\mathrm H_{a,b}\bigl(S(z),\overline{S(z)}\bigr)
    L_m^{(\kappa-1)}\bigl(R(z)\bigr)
  \end{equation}
  is an eigenfunction of $A_n$ in the sense that
  \begin{equation}
    -A_nP_{a,b,m}  =\lambda_{a,b,m}P_{a,b,m}
    \quad\text{where}\quad
    \lambda_{a,b,m}=2\frac{\alpha_n}{n}(a+b+2m).
  \end{equation}
  Moreover, the family $\{P_{a,b,m}:a,b,m\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is a basis of the
  polynomial algebra $\mathbb C[S,\overline S,R]$. In particular, this algebra
  is invariant under $A_n$ in the sense that
  $A_n\bigl(\mathbb C[S,\overline S,R]\bigr)\subset\mathbb C[S,\overline
  S,R]$. Furthermore, the elements of the family are mutually orthogonal in
  $L^2(\mu_n)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Polynomial eigenfunctions

[Theorem hittingprobforregularmeasure of arXiv:2506.10448, 'Hitting probabilities and the Ekstr\"om--Persson conjecture'] Let $X:=[0,1]^d$ and denote by $\Leb$ the restriction of the $d$-di\-men\-sion\-al Lebesgue 
measure to $X$. Let $\underline{r}$ be a sequence of radii such that 
$s_2(\underline{r})\leq d$. Then, for  analytic sets $C\subseteq X$, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[i)] if 
          $\dimp C<d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then $C\cap E_{\underline r}(\omega)=\emptyset$
          almost surely,
 \item[ii)] if 
           $\dimh C>d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then 
           $C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)\neq\emptyset$ almost surely,        
\item[iii)] if  $C$ is compact and
           $\dimMBl C>d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then 
           $C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)\neq\emptyset$ almost surely,
\item[iv)]  if 
             $\underline r=\underline r{(\alpha)}$  for some  
            $\alpha>0$ and $\dimp C>d-\frac 1\alpha$, then 
            $C\cap E_{ \alpha}(\omega)\neq \emptyset$ almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem hittingprobforregularmeasure of arXiv:2506.10448

[Proposition prop:pi-moments of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] In the framework of this section, assume that the service time
distribution has finite moments of all orders:
$\mathbb{E} \sigma_1^n = \int_0^\infty y^ng(y)dy < \infty$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$.
Then the Markov chain $\boldsymbol{Y}:=\{Y_n\}$ of the stage length process 
has a unique stationary probability measure $\pi$ with
density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^+$, $f$, 

which satisfies the integral equation 
\begin{equation} 
f(y)=\int_0^\infty f(x) q(x,y)dx \hspace{0.2in} \mbox{ for all $y \in \mathbb{R}^+$.}
\end{equation}
The stationary measure $\pi$ has finite moments of all orders: 
$\int_0^\infty y^n \pi(dy) <\infty$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:pi-moments of arXiv:2603.20078

PROOF (UNAUDITED). For 0<q<=1, -1<=c<1, n>=64, take n independent standard Gaussian pairs of correlation c, apply tanh(sqrt(q)*x), and let Dhat be one minus the uncentered empirical Gram correlation. Writing delta=1-E[tanh(sqrt(q)X)tanh(sqrt(q)Y)]/E[tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2], there is an explicit universal rational K (given in the proof) such that |E Dhat-delta|<=K*delta/n, E(Dhat/delta-1)^2<=K/n, and Var Dhat<=K*delta^2/n. At c=1 both gaps are exactly zero. Bounds hold conditionally on any past with equal CURRENT variances and fresh independent paired Gaussian rows. Equal initial variances alone do not justify iteration: with |c0|<1 their next empirical variances differ almost surely.
Equal current Gaussian marginal variances q in (0,1]; n>=64; independent rows; empirical means not subtracted.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c7de1d1270fea600cf249739b297f9b29e8cca36a1ecb90de84a7fe77545d9f6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c7/c7de1d1270fea600cf249739b297f9b29e8cca36a1ecb90de84a7fe77545d9f6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cd8545e524c049b9838925183b6058c6ca5c354cd752d4e77e28381e76be4b9d","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_relative_gap_noise","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c009-relative-gap-noise","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Gaussian-process limits and empirical correlation matrices","draft":"w712/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:tanh-gram-gap-relative-conditional-bias-variance","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C009 v1: relative conditional noise of a two-input tanh Gram gap

Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: moved, a conditional-noise component of the reviewer's named first rung. Target: T250(a). Novelty unverified. This is not a proof of the multi-layer relative gap recursion.

## Statement

Let 0<q<=1, -1<=c<=1, and n>=64. Independently across i, let (X_i,Y_i) be standard bivariate Gaussians with correlation c. Set F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2 and

    U_i=tanh(sqrt(q)X_i)/sqrt(F(q)),
    V_i=tanh(sqrt(q)Y_i)/sqrt(F(q)),
    h=E[U_i V_i], delta=1-h,
    A=mean U_i^2, D=mean V_i^2, T=mean U_i V_i,
    Dhat=1-T/sqrt(AD).

This is the uncentered empirical Gram correlation: sample means are not subtracted. The denominators are positive almost surely. There is an explicit universal rational K, defined below, such that, if c<1,

    |E Dhat-delta| <= K delta/n,
    E(Dhat/delta-1)^2 <= K/n,
    Var(Dhat) <= K delta^2/n.                         (1)

At c=1 both gaps are zero almost surely. At c=-1 both gaps equal two. The same assertions hold conditionally on any past for which the current two Gaussian marginal variances are equal to q and the fresh paired rows are independent. No independence of A and D is required.

Define M=15!!=2027025 and

    a=64(4M+1), b=64(16M+1), d=2048M,
    J=64^20 sum_{j=0}^{20} binom(20,j) product_{r=1}^j (64-2r)^(-1),
    K=(1+a+b+d+J)^12.

An empty product is one. These constants are deliberately large, but finite, rational, and independent of q,c,n. The hardest step is controlling inverse empirical norms without losing a factor of the population gap near c=1.

## 1. Gaussian increment moments relative to the population gap

The elementary tanh inequalities from C002 v2 give

    q/(1+3q)<=F(q)<=q,
    x^2/(1+x^2)<=tanh(x)^2<=x^2.

Put u(z)=tanh(sqrt(q)z)/sqrt(F(q)). Then E u(Z)^2=1, u is odd, |u(z)|<=2|z|, and its Lipschitz constant is at most two. If alpha=E[Zu(Z)], weighted Jensen for z^2 dgamma gives

    alpha >= E[Z^2/sqrt(1+qZ^2)] >= (1+3q)^(-1/2)>=1/2.

Write u(z)=alpha z+r(z), where E[Zr(Z)]=0. Gaussian conditioning gives E[Xr(Y)]=c E[Yr(Y)]=0, and likewise for the other cross terms. Consequently

    2delta=E(u(X)-u(Y))^2
       =2alpha^2(1-c)+E(r(X)-r(Y))^2 >= (1-c)/2.

Thus delta>0 when c<1 and 1-c<=4delta. Set W_i=(U_i-V_i)^2/2. For every positive integer p,

    E W_i=delta,
    ||W_i||_p <=16 delta G_(2p)^2,
    ||U_i^2-1||_p, ||V_i^2-1||_p <=4G_(2p)^2+1,
    ||U_i^2-V_i^2||_p <=16sqrt(2)G_(2p)^2 sqrt(delta),       (2)

where G_k=(E|Z|^k)^(1/k). Indeed |U-V|<=2|X-Y| and X-Y has variance 2(1-c), so ||U-V||_(2p)<=4sqrt(2delta)G_(2p). For the last line use Holder on (U-V)(U+V), with ||U+V||_(2p)<=4G_(2p). The centered variable U_i^2-V_i^2 has mean zero because the CURRENT variances are equal.

## 2. Sample mean moments, with an elementary finite count

For an even integer p and independent centered identically distributed B_i,

    ||mean B_i||_p <=p^2 ||B_1||_p/sqrt(n).                (3)

To verify this, expand the p-th power. A term with an index occurring once has zero expectation. Every remaining ordered p-tuple uses at most p/2 distinct indices. Their number is at most sum_{r=1}^{p/2} n^r r^p <=p^(p+1)n^(p/2). Holder bounds each term's absolute expectation by E|B_1|^p. Taking p-th roots gives p^(1+1/p)<=p^2. This counts an overestimate of all tuples, so needs no sign assumption.

Let w=mean W_i, x=A-1, y=D-1, and s=A-D. For p=2,4,8, (2)-(3) imply

    ||x||_p,||y||_p <=a/sqrt(n),
    ||w-delta||_p <=b delta/sqrt(n),
    ||w||_p <=(1+b)delta,
    ||s||_p <=d sqrt(delta/n).                           (4)

Here G_(2p)^2<=M for these three p, p^2<=64, and 16sqrt(2)<=32. These loose inequalities explain each integer constant in the statement.

## 3. Uniform inverse empirical norms

Pointwise,

    u(z)^2 >= z^2/(1+z^2).

For a subset I of exactly 64 samples, let A_I=mean_{i in I} U_i^2 and S_I=sum_{i in I}X_i^2. Then

    A_I >= S_I/[64(1+S_I)].

S_I has chi-square distribution with 64 degrees of freedom. Direct integration of its density s^31 exp(-s/2)/(2^32 Gamma(32)) gives, for j=0,...,20,

    E S_I^(-j)=product_{r=1}^j (64-2r)^(-1).

All integrals converge because j<=20<32. Hence E A_I^(-20)<=J. For n>=64, the average of A_I over all size-64 subsets is exactly A: each index occurs in binom(n-1,63) subsets and binom(n-1,63)/(64 binom(n,64))=1/n. Jensen for the convex function t^(-20) gives E A^(-20)<=J, and the same proof gives E D^(-20)<=J. Thus, by Lyapunov and J>=1,

    ||A^(-r)||_p,||D^(-r)||_p <=J^r whenever rp<=20.       (5)

Subset averaging is an analytic argument, not a request to enumerate subsets. No dependence assumption between the two sample norms is used.

## 4. Keep the normalization bias at order delta/n

Let k=(AD)^(-1/2) and

    t=(sqrt(A)-sqrt(D))^2/(2sqrt(AD)).

The exact Gram identity, including its factor two, is

    w=(A+D-2T)/2,
    Dhat=w k-t,
    0<=t <=(A-D)^2/(8AD).                              (6)

The last inequality uses (sqrt(A)+sqrt(D))^2>=4sqrt(AD). Holder with (4)-(5) yields

    ||t||_2 <= d^2 J^2 delta/n.                         (7)

For example, ||(A-D)^2||_4=||s||_8^2 and ||(AD)^(-1)||_4<=J^2; dropping the factor 1/8 only weakens the bound.

The identity |A^(-1/2)-1|=|x|/[sqrt(A)(1+sqrt(A))] gives

    ||k-1||_4 <=2aJ/sqrt(n).                            (8)

Indeed k-1=(A^(-1/2)-1)D^(-1/2)+(D^(-1/2)-1), followed by Holder with exponents eight and (5).

We also need the linear Taylor term, rather than just (8). For g(z)=z^(-1/2), Taylor with its integral remainder gives

    g(A)=1-x/2+r_A,
    |r_A| <=(3/8)x^2(1+A^(-5/2)).

The same holds for D,y,r_D. Set R=k-1+(x+y)/2. Algebra gives

    R=r_A g(D)+r_D-(x/2)(g(D)-1).

Holder and (4)-(5) now give

    ||R||_2 <=(a^2/n)[(3/8)(1+J^(5/2))(1+sqrt(J))+sqrt(J)/2]
             <=2a^2 J^4/n.                            (9)

The strongest inverse moment here is E A^(-20): to bound the first term, use ||x^2||_4 and ||(1+A^(-5/2))D^(-1/2)||_4, then split the latter by Holder into L8 factors. Thus no inverse moment above the proved range is used.

Since E x=E y=0 and E w=delta,

    E[w(k-1)]=-(1/2)E[(w-delta)(x+y)]+E[wR].

Equations (4),(7),(9) imply

    |E Dhat-delta| <=[ba+2(1+b)a^2J^4+d^2J^2]delta/n.   (10)

Using only Cauchy-Schwarz on E[w(k-1)] would lose a square root of n. The centered linear term above is what avoids that loss.

## 5. Relative second moment and explicit constant

From (4),(6)-(8) and n>=1,

    ||Dhat-delta||_2
      <=||w-delta||_2+||w||_4||k-1||_4+||t||_2
      <=[b+2(1+b)aJ+d^2J^2]delta/sqrt(n).               (11)

Write H=1+a+b+d+J>=2. The bracket in (10) is at most 4H^7<=H^12. The bracket in (11) is at most 4H^4, whose square is at most 16H^8<=H^12. This proves (1) with K=H^12. Variance is no larger than the mean squared deviation from the fixed value delta. At c=1, U_i=V_i; at c=-1, U_i=-V_i, proving the endpoint statements directly. All constants and estimates are uniform in q,c and therefore can be applied to a past-measurable q,c by conditioning.

## 6. What this does and does not close

At an equal-current-variance state, write delta=1-H(q,q,c). The next empirical gap has relative conditional bias at most K/n and relative conditional variance at most K/n. This proves the conditional-innovation part of the reviewer's proposed rung, uniformly even as c increases to one.

It does NOT prove a C003-type relative recursion for the original multi-layer D_l. Equal initial variances are not preserved by empirical sampling. If q_0=r_0>0 and |c_0|<1, then Q_1!=R_1 almost surely: condition on all X_i and on Y_1,...,Y_(n-1). The remaining Y_n has a nondegenerate Gaussian conditional law; tanh(sqrt(q_0)Y_n)^2 has no atoms, so its sum with the fixed other terms cannot equal the specified X-sum with positive probability. Thus applying this equal-current-variance lemma at every layer would be invalid. A coupled radial-contrast estimate, or a general unequal-current-variance extension, remains necessary. This is the FIRST missing premise in that proposed iteration.

The lower width restriction is substantive for this normalization route. For n=1, the empirical uncentered correlation is sign(XY), so E Dhat=2 arccos(c)/pi: write Y=cX+sqrt(1-c^2)Z with independent standard Gaussians X,Z. Their planar angle is uniform, and the discordant-sign sectors have total angle 2 arccos(c). The Lipschitz bound and section 1 give (1-c)/4<=delta<=4(1-c). Consequently a uniform relative bias O(1/n) all the way to c=1 fails at n=1. This observation does not refute the n>=64 claim or the eventual large-width target.

Let P be a product measure on {0,1}^n and let A and B be increasing events. Write A box B for the disjoint occurrence of A and B: the set of configurations omega for which there are disjoint index sets I and J such that every configuration agreeing with omega on I lies in A and every configuration agreeing with omega on J lies in B. Then P(A box B) <= P(A) P(B) (van den Berg and Kesten 1985). This runs in the opposite direction to the Harris-FKG inequality for the plain intersection, P(A and B) >= P(A) P(B); the two are not in conflict because A box B is a subset of A and B. In percolation the standard use is P(two disjoint open paths) <= P(open path)^2.
P is a product measure (independent coordinates)
A and B are increasing events (van den Berg-Kesten); Reimer's inequality removes this hypothesis
A box B is the disjoint-occurrence event, witnessed by disjoint coordinate sets, not the intersection

[Corollary cor:SMR_microscopic_estimate of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $Q=Q_{1/2}(t_0,x_0)$ be a parabolic cylinder with center $(t_0,x_0)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}^d$.
Fix $\mu>0$, $r\in (1,\infty)$ and $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ such that 
\begin{equation}

\frac{2}{p}+\frac{d}{q}<1.
\end{equation}
Then there exists a constant $C_0>0$ depending only on $p,q,r$ and $\mu$ such that for any local solution $(v^N,\pi^N,(\widetilde{\pi}_{k,\alpha}^N)_{k,\alpha})$ to the oscillating stochastic Stokes system (equation eq:turbulent_Stokes_microscopic of the paper) at the microscopic scale $N^{-1}Q$, it holds that 
\begin{align}

\big({\mathbf E}|v^N(t_0,x_0)|^r\big)^{1/r}
&\leq C_0
 \big({\mathbf E}\| v^N\|_{\underline{L}^2(N^{-1}Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}\\
 \nonumber
 &+C_0  \big({\mathbf E}\|\pi^N\|_{\underline{L}^2(N^{-1}I;\underline{H}^{-1}(N^{-1}B))}^r\big)^{1/r} \\
\nonumber 
 &+C_0\big({\mathbf E}\|(\widetilde{\pi}^N_{k,\alpha})_{k,\alpha}\|_{\underline{L}^2(N^{-1}Q;\ell^2)}^r \big)^{1/r}\\
 \nonumber
& +C_0 \big({\mathbf E}\|F\|_{\underline{L}^p(I;\underline{L}^q(B))}^r\big)^{1/r}+C_0 \big({\mathbf E}\|G\|^r_{\underline{L}^p(I;\underline{L}^q(B;\ell^2))}\big)^{1/r}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Localized $L^\infty$-bounds at microscopic scale -- Oscillating stochastic Stokes

[Proposition prop:boolean-no-go of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $r$ be even. Suppose a binary partial class contains distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, a concept $h_0$ that is nonstar on all of them, and, for every $B\in\binom{[r]}{r/2}$, a concept $h_B$ that is nonstar on the whole row and satisfies
\[
    h_B(x_t)
    =
    \begin{cases}
        h_0(x_t),&t\notin B,\\
        1-h_0(x_t),&t\in B.
    \end{cases}
\]
Then the class has partial VC dimension at least $r/2$.

body:
[Lemma lem:haar-residual of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $V$ be any finite-dimensional orthogonal $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-module,
let $\mathcal K_V=N^{-1}\sum_iP_{i,V}$, and let $\Pi_V$ be the
orthogonal projection onto $V^{\mathrm{SO}(n)}$.  With
$Q_V=I-\Pi_V$, for every $\ell\ge0$,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal K_V^\ell=\Pi_V+Q_V\mathcal K_V^\ell Q_V.}
\tag{3.2.10s}
\]
Consequently every empty chronological gap in a fixed reflected ribbon
child is exactly either a Haar separator or a residual gap.  Expanding
all gaps produces at most $2^h$ children when $h$ physical times are
used.  End components obey the same convention after inserting a common
auxiliary Haar conjugation in the conjugation-invariant squared-shell
scalar.

body:
[Lemma 18 (Projected total-covariance decomposition) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Fix a measurement value $r$ and $t>0$, assume
$\E[\|X_0\|^2\mid R=r]<\infty$, and let $P$ be an orthogonal projector.  With
$m_t^r(X_t)=\E[X_0\mid X_t,R=r]$,
\begin{equation}

\begin{aligned}
\Tr\!\left(P\Cov(X_0\mid r)P\right)
&=
\E\!\left[
\Tr\!\left(P\Cov(X_0\mid X_t,r)P\right)
\,\middle|\,R=r
\right]\\
&\quad+
\Tr\Cov\!\left(Pm_t^r(X_t)\mid R=r\right).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The first term is conditional variance that remains after observing the noisy
state; the second is variation of the exact posterior mean across noisy states.
Under the Gaussian noising family, the second term tends to zero as
the channel SNR tends to zero and to
$\Tr(P\Cov(X_0\mid r)P)$ as the channel SNR tends to infinity.  Thus
across-state clean-estimate dispersion is the \emph{resolved} component of a
total-covariance decomposition, not the remaining posterior covariance. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Projected total-covariance decomposition

[Proposition 4 (A bounded Brownian perturbation in a mixed equation) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $\wt\eta\in(1/\alpha,1)$, let $0<\lambda<1$, let $\kappa\ne0$, and let $r\in L^2(0,T)$ be deterministic. Consider
\[
  b(t,x)=\wt b(t,x)\equiv0,
  \qquad
  a(t,x)\equiv\kappa,
  \qquad
  \wt a(t,x)=\kappa+r(t),
\]
and
\[
  \sigma(t,x)=\wt\sigma(t,x)=1+\lambda\bigl(|x|^{\wt\eta}\wedge1\bigr).
\]
Then the baseline equation contains both the Brownian and stable terms, the perturbed equation is driven by the same two noises, and the stable coefficient is bounded, bounded away from zero, and non-Lipschitz at the origin. For any coupled solution pair satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:solutions}, the coefficient distances are
\[
  B=0,
  \qquad
  A^2=\int_0^T |r(t)|^2\dd t,
  \qquad
  S=0.
\]
Consequently, if $x_0=\wt x_0$ and $A=\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}<1$, Theorem~\ref{thm:noncritical} gives
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}
  \le C\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}}.
\]
Thus, in this mixed Brownian--stable equation, the estimate reduces to the Brownian diffusion error, while the stable coefficient is H\"older and fails to be Lipschitz.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] Let $(\gamma, \eta) = (2 + 2 \kappa, \vartheta)$ and $(\tilde{\gamma}, \tilde{\eta}) = (3/2 + 2 \kappa, - \kappa)$ where $\vartheta \in (0, 1/2 - \kappa)$. Suppose that $(\Hb, \Hp, \mathcal{W}) \in \mcD^{\gamma, \eta} \times \mcD^{\gamma, \eta} \times \mcD^{\tilde{\gamma}, \tilde{\eta}}$ is a solution of the fixed-point problem
	\begin{equs}[eq:system-in-lemma]
		\Hb &= \mathcal{P}_\gamma \mathbf{1}_+ [(\partial_x \Hb)^2 + \<b0>] + \mathcal{G} \psi
		\\
		\Hp &= \mathcal{P}_\gamma \mathbf{1}_+ [(\partial_x \Hp)^2 + \<p0>] + \mathcal{G} \psi

		\mathcal{W} &= \mathcal{P}_{\tilde{\gamma}} \mathbf{1}_+ [\partial_x \mathcal{W} (\partial_x \Hb + \partial_x \Hp) + \<0t>]

[Prop fourier-obstruction of arXiv:2606.08325, 'Digit Mixing under Polynomial Maps'] Let \(Q\in\mathbb Z[x]\) be an integer-valued polynomial of  degree $d$, say
			\[ Q(x)=a_dx^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_0, \qquad a_d\ne0.
			\]
			Then
			\begin{equation}
			\lim_{N\to\infty}
			\mathbb E\, e(2^NQ(X))=L_Q,
			\end{equation}
			where
			\[
			L_Q
			=
			\prod_{\ell=1}^{\infty}
			\exp\left(
			\lambda\bigl(e(a_dd!2^{-\ell})-1\bigr)
			\right).
			\]
			In particular, $0<|L_Q|<1$.
title: Prop fourier-obstruction of arXiv:2606.08325

[Theorem thm:main-nontriviality of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $d\geq2$, let $(\mu_\rho)_{\rho\in(0,1]}$ be a family of laws with mean $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_\rho}\sigma(0)=\rho$, and let the masses be i.i.d.\ with law $\mu_\rho$. Suppose there are $\rho_0\in(0,1)$, $\nu_0>0$, $\theta_0>0$, and $K_0<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \inf_{\rho_0\leq\rho<1}\Var_{\mu_\rho}(\sigma(0))\geq\nu_0^2
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sup_{\rho_0\leq\rho<1}\mathbb{E}_{\mu_\rho}e^{\theta_0|\sigma(0)-\rho|}\leq K_0\, .
\end{equation}
Then there is $\rho_+=\rho_+(d,(\mu_\rho))\in[\rho_0,1)$ such that $\mathcal T^{(\rho)}$ contains an infinite nearest-neighbor component almost surely for every $\rho\in(\rho_+,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21391, 'Extreme points and faces in the moment problem'] Let $(X,\mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space whose $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{F}$ contains all 
singletons in $X$. A \emph{measure} is a countably additive map $\mathcal{F}\to[0,\infty)$. 
A measure $\mu$ is \emph{concentrated} on $A\in\mathcal{F}$ if $\mu(X\setminus A)=0$.
A measure $\mu$ is a \emph{probability measure} if its total mass is $\mu(X)=1$. 
Let $P$ be the convex set of probability measures on $(X,\mathcal{F})$. The 
\emph{point measure} at $x\in X$, denoted $\delta_x$, is the measure with values 
$\delta_x(A):=1$ if $x\in A$ and $\delta_x(A):=0$ otherwise for every $A\in\mathcal{F}$. 
Let 
\[
P_1:=\{\delta_x: x\in X\}.
\]
A measure $\mu$ is \emph{$k$-atomic} [klerk-laurent19,lasserre10,nie23,schmuedgen17], 
$k\in\mathbb{N}_0$, if $\mu=\lambda_1\delta_{x_1}+\dots+\lambda_k\delta_{x_k}$ for mutually 
distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_k$ in $X$ and strictly positive real weights 
$\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k>0$. A measure is \emph{finitely atomic} if it is $k$-atomic 
for some $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Let
\[
P\!_\mathrm{fin}:=
\{\mu\in P : \text{$\mu$ is finitely atomic}\,\}.
\]
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2606.21391, 'Extreme points and faces in the moment problem'

body: [Theorem 34 (Extremality) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $\mathcal L\in\mathcal P(\mathcal G_{\bullet})$ be unimodular. Then $\mathcal L$ is extremal if and only if $\mathcal I$ is $\mathcal L$-trivial, i.e.~$\mathcal L(A)\in\{0,1\}$ for all $A\in \mathcal I$.
title: Extremality

[Dfn 86 (symmetrized classification, cf.\ Defn.~\ref{d:SDE.classification}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $q_0 = 0$. We classify the control parameters $(q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ identically as in Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification}, except for modified conditions on $p$:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\IAMPdefn{sy}\\
\BOGPdefn{sy}\\
\FAIRdefn{sy}\\
\TMPONEdefn{sy}\\
\TMPTWOdefn{sy}\\
\GOODdefn{sy}\\
\TMPTHRdefn{sy}\\
\GREATdefn{sy}\\
\SPRdefn{sy}\\
\SUPERPERFECTdefn{sy}\\
\PRFTWOdefn{sy}\\
\PRFTHRdefn{sy}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Compared to Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification}, we note that the $\sviii$, $\six$, $\sxii$, and $\sidealast$ classes are no longer present, and neither are the parameters $L_0, \epsilon_0$. 
We denote the subsets of $(q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the above conditions by
\beq
    
    \Adm^{\star,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon),\qquad
    \star \in \bigg\{
    \begin{array}{c}
    \IAMP,\BOGP,\si,\sii,\siii,\siv,\\
    \sv,\svi,\svii,\sideal,\sx,\sxi
    \end{array}\bigg\}.
\eeq
Similarly to Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification}, if either of $L,\epsilon$ does not appear in the definition of a class $\star$, then we take $\Adm^{\star,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ to be the same for all values of that parameter and sometimes omit it from the notation, writing e.g. $\Adm^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) = \Adm^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)$.
title: symmetrized classification, cf.\ Defn.~\ref{d:SDE.classification}

[Theorem thm:ci of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Under assumption~(ass:dynamics of the paper), let $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu \in
L^2(\mu)$, and let $\tilde\sigma_A^2$ and $c_A$ be sub-gamma parameters for which
Eq.~(equation eq:uq_general of the paper) holds with $\overline{A}_t \in
\{\overline{\rho}_t(V), \overline{J}_t(U)\}$. 
Fix a confidence level $1-\alpha$, with $\alpha\in (0,1)$, and define
\begin{align}
  r_A(\alpha,t)
  =
  \sqrt{\frac{2\tilde\sigma_A^2}{t}\log\left(\frac{2N_\nu}{\alpha}\right)}
  +
  \frac{c_A}{t}\log\left(\frac{2N_\nu}{\alpha}\right),
  \quad
  N_\nu \equiv \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)},
  
\end{align}
where $N_\nu$ is a prefactor encoding the initial condition with $N_\mu=1$.
Then for every $t > 0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(-r_A(\alpha,t) \leq \overline{A}_t - \E^\mu[\overline{A}_t] \leq r_A(\alpha,t)\right)
  \geq 1-\alpha ,
  
\end{align}
that is, with probability of at least $1-\alpha$, under $\mathbb{P}^\nu$, the stationary mean lies in the confidence interval
\begin{align}
  \E^\mu[\overline{A}_t]
  \in
  \left[\overline{A}_t - r_A(\alpha,t),
  \overline{A}_t + r_A(\alpha,t)\right].
  
\end{align}
Moreover, the corresponding one-sided guarantees hold with a smaller radius $r_A^{(1)}(\alpha,t)$, 
obtained from Eq.~(equation eq:ci_radius of the paper) by replacing $2N_\nu$ with $N_\nu$, i.e., 
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{A}_t - \E^\mu[\overline{A}_t]
  \leq r_A^{(1)}(\alpha,t)\right)
  \geq 1-\alpha,
  \qquad
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\E^\mu[\overline{A}_t] -  \overline{A}_t
  \leq r_A^{(1)}(\alpha,t)\right)
  \geq 1-\alpha.
  
\end{align}

Own-work draft; T419-C018 v1, proof (unaudited), known-method corollary, no novelty claimed. Let Delta be any fixed real m-by-p matrix, m>=p>=1, of exact rank p. Let n>p+3. Observe independent x_i~N(0,I_p), e_i~N(0,sigma^2 I_m), z_i=Delta x_i+e_i, with sigma>=0. Let X=[x_i], Z=[z_i], C=XX^T/n, D=ZX^T/n, W=D C^(-1). Independently initialize B0=0, A0 p-by-p with iid N(0,s^2) entries, any s>0. Almost surely C is positive definite and A0 is invertible.

For such a realization define

 lambda=lambda_min(C), c=||C||op, h0=lambda_min(A0 A0^T)>0,
 q0=||W C^(1/2)||F^2/2,
 J=||A0 A0^T||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(p)(J+2R).

Choose a measurable constant step, for example the minimum of the three displayed bounds,

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/(6Kc+||D||op),h0/[4(1+q0)]}.

Run simultaneous GD on the empirical factor loss ||BA X-Z||F^2/(2n). Then almost surely

 ||B_t A_t-W||F^2 <= (2q0/lambda) exp(-eta h0 lambda t/2),

so B_t A_t converges to W, the ordinary least-squares product. Because r=p, the rank-r reduced-rank-regression product equals W. Moreover,

 lim_(t->infinity) E ||B_t A_t-Delta||F^2
 =E||W-Delta||F^2
 =sigma^2 m p/(n-p-1).

Thus the limiting expected population excess risk equals that of rank-r reduced-rank regression, factor exactly one, for this full-input-rank family and this initialization-dependent step. The sample condition n>p+3 is more than the n>p+1 needed for the known OLS formula; the extra two samples support an elementary second-moment domination proof below. No uniform deterministic iteration count in expectation, efficiency or proper-bottleneck guarantee is claimed. This family satisfies the named target's sample-size condition whenever n is chosen large enough to satisfy that condition as well.
r=p=d_in, m>=p, fixed rank-p signal, n>p+3
Independent standard Gaussian inputs, isotropic Gaussian label noise sigma>=0, zero output factor and square iid Gaussian input factor of any positive scale
Measurable constant step depends on the data and sampled initialization and meets all displayed bounds
Expected-risk comparison is in the limit of iterations; no proper-bottleneck, explicit finite stopping or novelty assertion

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:66306f87358b8c94bfcb47780dffea9ca3362f4d33a2f0091be9cf10f969ac1c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/66/66306f87358b8c94bfcb47780dffea9ca3362f4d33a2f0091be9cf10f969ac1c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:44b7629c94b10b7214c97341b930aa357a297bef0bccb1fc92b6882943b1df65","bundle_entry_key":"full-input-risk","bundle_id":"population.t419-full-input-empirical-gd-risk-domination-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA finite-sample optimization and expected regression risk","draft":"w705/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-full-input-empirical-gd-expected-risk-gaussian-domination","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C018 v1: full-input-rank empirical GD reaches OLS with convergent expected risk

Kind: narrowed. Target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This is the full-input-rank family r=p=d_in, with output dimension m>=p. It includes arbitrary Gaussian initialization scales but uses an initialization-dependent constant step. It does not address the proper rank bottleneck r<p. The deterministic part builds on C014 and the published Du-Hu-Lee imbalance method; the OLS risk is known, not a new statistical formula.

## Statement

Let Delta be any fixed real m-by-p matrix, m>=p>=1, of exact rank p. Let n>p+3. Observe independent x_i~N(0,I_p), e_i~N(0,sigma^2 I_m), z_i=Delta x_i+e_i, with sigma>=0. Let X=[x_i], Z=[z_i], C=XX^T/n, D=ZX^T/n, W=D C^(-1). Independently initialize B0=0, A0 p-by-p with iid N(0,s^2) entries, any s>0. Almost surely C is positive definite and A0 is invertible.

For such a realization define

 lambda=lambda_min(C), c=||C||op, h0=lambda_min(A0 A0^T)>0,
 q0=||W C^(1/2)||F^2/2,
 J=||A0 A0^T||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(p)(J+2R).

Choose a measurable constant step, for example the minimum of the three displayed bounds,

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/(6Kc+||D||op),h0/[4(1+q0)]}.

Run simultaneous GD on the empirical factor loss ||BA X-Z||F^2/(2n). Then almost surely

 ||B_t A_t-W||F^2 <= (2q0/lambda) exp(-eta h0 lambda t/2),

so B_t A_t converges to W, the ordinary least-squares product. Because r=p, the rank-r reduced-rank-regression product equals W. Moreover,

 lim_(t->infinity) E ||B_t A_t-Delta||F^2
 =E||W-Delta||F^2
 =sigma^2 m p/(n-p-1).

Thus the limiting expected population excess risk equals that of rank-r reduced-rank regression, factor exactly one, for this full-input-rank family and this initialization-dependent step. The sample condition n>p+3 is more than the n>p+1 needed for the known OLS formula; the extra two samples support an elementary second-moment domination proof below. No uniform deterministic iteration count in expectation, efficiency or proper-bottleneck guarantee is claimed. This family satisfies the named target's sample-size condition whenever n is chosen large enough to satisfy that condition as well.

## Deterministic convergence, retaining the covariance metric

Subtract the constant empirical residual at W. The resulting loss is

 q(B,A)=||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2/2,

with product gradient G=BA C-D. Let E=BA-W and F_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t. C014 proves, for the first two step bounds above,

 q_(t+1)<=q_t-(eta/2)||grad q_t||F^2,
 ||F_t-F_0||F<=2eta q0,
 ||B_t A_t||F<=R.

Its proof establishes these inequalities without assuming factor boundedness in advance, and works with this anisotropic covariance, not a substituted isotropic GD. The third step bound makes

 2eta q0<=h0 q0/[2(1+q0)]<h0/2.

Hence F_t>=h0 I/2 and A_t A_t^T>=h0 I/2 for all t. The square input factor is essential. Since grad_B q=E C A_t^T,

 ||grad q||F^2 >=(h0/2)||E C||F^2
               >=h0 lambda q.

Combine this with descent to get q_(t+1)<=(1-eta h0 lambda/2)q_t. The multiplier is nonnegative: K bounds the initial factor-pair squared norm, so K>=h0, and eta<=1/(6Kc+||D||op) implies eta h0 lambda<=1/6. Iterate and use q>=lambda||E||F^2/2. If q0=0, the gradients vanish and the same conclusion is immediate.

No high-probability complement is discarded here. C and A0 meet these deterministic assumptions almost surely; the step is selected from their realized values. Defining an arbitrary measurable positive step on the null singular event has no effect on any expectation claim.

## An integrable product bound independent of the initializer

The fact that eta is allowed to depend on A0 does not itself establish expectation convergence. For every t on the almost-sure event,

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F^2<=2R^2+2||Delta||F^2.

Here R depends only on the training data, because B0=0 makes q0 independent of A0. We now prove its expectation is finite.

Conditional on X, write W=Delta+N C^(-1/2), where N has iid N(0,sigma^2/n) entries and its conditional law is independent of X. Thus

 E[||W||F^2 | X]=||Delta||F^2+(m sigma^2/n)tr(C^(-1)),
 E[2q0 | X]=||Delta C^(1/2)||F^2+mp sigma^2/n.

Since R^2<=2||W||F^2+4q0/lambda, its conditional expectation is at most

 2||Delta||F^2+(2m sigma^2/n)tr(C^(-1))
 +2||Delta||F^2 ||C||op||C^(-1)||op
 +(2mp sigma^2/n)||C^(-1)||op.

It remains to check the covariance moments used in this expression. A fully elementary bound suffices; no asymptotic random-matrix approximation is needed.

## Exact finite inverse-covariance moment check

Let G=X^T be the n-by-p standard Gaussian design. For each column j let d_j be its distance from the span of the other p-1 columns. Almost surely these spans have dimension p-1. The j-th row of the left pseudoinverse G^+ has squared norm d_j^(-2): it is the normalized residual vector of column j after orthogonal projection onto the other columns. Consequently

 sigma_min(G)^(-2)<=||G^+||F^2=sum_j d_j^(-2),
 sigma_min(G)^(-4)<=p sum_j d_j^(-4).

Conditional on the other columns, d_j^2 is chi-squared with k=n-p+1 degrees of freedom, by Gaussian orthogonal projection. Its density is t^(k/2-1)e^(-t/2)/(2^(k/2) Gamma(k/2)). Direct integration gives, for k>4,

 E[d_j^(-4)]=1/[(k-2)(k-4)].

No independence between different d_j is assumed. Therefore

 E||C^(-1)||op^2
 <= n^2 p^2/[(n-p-1)(n-p-3)]<infinity.

Also ||C||op<=tr C and the sum of np independent squared standard Gaussians gives

 E||C||op^2<=E[(tr C)^2]=p^2+2p/n.

Cauchy-Schwarz now proves E[||C||op||C^(-1)||op]<infinity. The first inverse moments are finite by the second-moment bound, and tr(C^(-1))<=p||C^(-1)||op. This proves that the data-only dominating variable 2R^2+2||Delta||F^2 is integrable, including in the zero-noise case.

## Passing to expected risk and identifying the known comparator

Pointwise product convergence and the integrable bound allow the dominated convergence theorem on the joint probability space of training data and initialization. Hence the limiting expectation equals E||W-Delta||F^2. For standard Gaussian designs the known inverse-Wishart mean is E[(XX^T)^(-1)]=I_p/(n-p-1), n>p+1; conditioning on X gives

 E||W-Delta||F^2=m sigma^2 E tr((XX^T)^(-1))
                          =sigma^2 m p/(n-p-1).

This is the standard overdetermined OLS risk, also given by Zindari-Mulayoff-Stich, arXiv:2605.19018, Theorem 1 and Proposition 3 (printed p.4; inverse-Wishart computation in Appendix IV.1). The mean formula is used only to identify the finite risk explicitly; the elementary moment argument above already proves the expectation passage.

The rank-p constraint imposes no restriction on an m-by-p regression product, so reduced-rank regression with r=p is exactly OLS. This explains the factor-one comparison and the essential limitation: there is no proper input-side rank bottleneck. C013 does not contradict this theorem because its positive step must be chosen independently of the Gaussian initializer; the present safe step uses its smallest singular value and norm. All claims remain unaudited, and novelty is not asserted.


Deterministic C014 component supplied in full:
# T419-C014 v1: empirical GD boundedness with an initialization-dependent step

Kind: bound. Target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This is an explicit anisotropic version of the published Gram-imbalance/descent method, not a solution of Target 2. It proves a trajectory component without assuming the iterates are bounded. The prior source is Du-Hu-Lee, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B, Claim B.1; its full convergence theorems have different initialization/step hypotheses. C009 already identifies the exact covariance metric and C010 the positive-noise empirical landscape.

## Statement

Let C be any real positive definite p-by-p matrix, D any real m-by-p matrix, and r>=1. Put lambda=lambda_min(C)>0, c=||C||op, ell=||D||op, W=D C^(-1), and

 q(B,A)=(1/2)||(BA-W) C^(1/2)||F^2,

with B m-by-r and A r-by-p. This is the empirical regression objective up to a constant when C=XX^T/n and D=ZX^T/n. Initialize at any finite deterministic factors B0,A0, and define

 q0=q(B0,A0), J=||A0 A0^T-B0^T B0||F+1,
 R=||W||F+sqrt(2q0/lambda),
 K=sqrt(r)(J+2R), L=6Kc+ell.

For any fixed

 0<eta<=min{1/(1+2q0),1/L},

simultaneous ordinary factor GD satisfies, for every integer t>=0,

 q_t<=q0,
 ||B_t||F^2+||A_t||F^2<=K,
 ||(A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t)-(A0 A0^T-B0^T B0)||F<=2eta q0<1,
 sum_(t>=0) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/eta.

In particular the gradient tends to zero, every accumulation point is critical, and for every integer T>=1,

 min_(0<=t<T) ||grad q(B_t,A_t)||F^2<=2q0/(eta T).

All constants are finite and computable from C,D and the initialization. There is no Gaussian assumption and no low-rank assumption on W. No iterate-convergence, saddle-avoidance or statistical-risk assertion is included.

## Exact identities and product/factor bounds

Let G=BA C-D. The two factor gradients are G_B=G A^T and G_A=B^T G. With E_t=A_t A_t^T-B_t^T B_t the first-order cross terms cancel exactly, giving

 E_(t+1)-E_t=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B),
 ||E_(t+1)-E_t||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2).

This cancellation only uses dependence on BA and does not require isotropic C. Also

 (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2
 <=r [||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2].

To verify it, write P=B^TB,Q=AA^T. Scalar trace Cauchy-Schwarz gives (tr(P+Q))^2<=r tr((P+Q)^2), and cyclicity of trace gives tr((P+Q)^2)=||P-Q||F^2+4 tr(PQ), tr(PQ)=||BA||F^2. No commutation is assumed.

When q<=q0, positivity of C gives ||BA-W||F<=sqrt(2q0/lambda), hence ||BA||F<=R. If additionally ||E-E0||F<=1, then ||E||F<=J, so the preceding trace bound implies

 ||B||F^2+||A||F^2<=sqrt(r) sqrt(J^2+4R^2)<=K.

The initialization meets these conditions and therefore has pair norm at most sqrt(K).

## Descent established before closing the boundedness induction

Suppose at the current iterate the pair norm is at most sqrt(K), and preceding steps have valid descent inequalities. Then

 ||grad q||F<=||BA C-D||op sqrt(||B||F^2+||A||F^2)
             <=(Kc/2+ell)sqrt(K).

Because eta<=1/(6Kc+ell), the proposed next point has pair norm at most 2sqrt(K). The connecting segment also lies in that ball. On that ball the Hessian quadratic form in a perturbation (dB,dA) is

 ||(dB A+B dA) C^(1/2)||F^2+2<BA C-D,dB dA>.

Its absolute value is at most

 [c(||A||op^2+||B||op^2)+||BA C-D||op]
 times (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2)
 <=[4Kc+(2Kc+ell)] (||dB||F^2+||dA||F^2).

Here the first summand uses Cauchy-Schwarz on dB A+B dA; the cross term uses |<G,dB dA>|<=||G||op||dB||F||dA||F. Thus the Hessian operator norm on the segment is at most L. Taylor's theorem along that segment proves

 q_next<=q-eta||grad q||F^2+(L eta^2/2)||grad q||F^2
        <=q-(eta/2)||grad q||F^2.

In particular q_next<=q0. Telescoping the descent inequalities, including the proposed step, and using q>=0 yields

 sum_(j=0)^t eta^2||grad q_j||F^2<=2eta q0
 <=2q0/(1+2q0)<1.

Summing the imbalance increments now proves ||E_next-E0||F<=2eta q0<1. The product/factor bound therefore puts the endpoint back in the smaller ball of pair radius sqrt(K). This closes the induction without assuming a bound before proving descent on the required larger segment. The q0=0 case is included: both gradients vanish, the sequence is constant, and all inequalities still hold.

## Consequences and exact remaining gap

Telescoping for every finite horizon gives the infinite summability bound. A nonnegative summable sequence tends to zero, so the gradients vanish. Bounded finite-dimensional factor pairs have convergent subsequences; gradient continuity makes every subsequential limit critical. The running-minimum bound follows by averaging the finite sum. These statements do not require that the entire sequence converges to one point.

For B0=0 and a Gaussian A0, this provides an allowed positive step after observing the initialization, conditional on every full-row-rank design. It does not supply a single positive step independent of the unbounded Gaussian initializer. C013 shows that unconditional expected-limit risk with such an initialization-independent fixed step can diverge even at rank one.

Combining this bound with the already verified empirical strict-saddle landscape C010 is insufficient to conclude global optimization. One must additionally show that the specified zero/Gaussian initialization does not approach a nonglobal critical point, with all hypotheses of a saddle-avoidance theorem checked for its lower-dimensional initial support and step rule. Vanishing gradients do not establish that. Even convergence almost surely would not by itself justify passing to expected population risk; a failure-tail/integrability or finite-stopping argument is separately required. The usual full-ambient absolutely-continuous random-initialization theorem cannot simply be cited for the plane B0=0.

Independent reviewer audit and any novelty assessment remain pending. Let d>=1 be an integer, p>0, Q=(-1,1]^d, and mu,nu Borel probability measures on Q. For ell>=0 let P_ell be the partition into the2^(d ell) half-open dyadic cubes of side length2^(1-ell): each coordinate interval is(-1+2k/2^ell,-1+2(k+1)/2^ell] with0<=k<2^ell. Define D_p(mu,nu)=[(2^p-1)/2]sum_{ell>=1}2^(-p ell)sum_{F in P_ell}|mu(F)-nu(F)|. This is Notation4(a)p5 ofFournier-Guillin1312.2128v1. Its normalization makes D_p<=1: each cell-discrepancy sum is at most2 and sum_{ell>=1}2^(-p ell)=1/(2^p-1). Moreover D_p=0 precisely when mu=nu, because the positive weights force equality of all dyadic cell masses, and these partitions generate the Borel sigma field of Q.

Own-work draft, claim T323-OFFAXIS-001 v2, status proof (unaudited). For three tokens x_i in S^2 under self-inclusive normalized attention dot x_i=(I-x_i x_i^T) sum_j exp(beta x_i^T A x_j)V x_j / sum_j exp(beta x_i^T A x_j), take A=V=diag(1,1/2,-2), beta=2. There is a locally asymptotically stable equilibrium x1=(-q,0,-sqrt(1-q^2)), x2=(-1,0,0), x3=(-q,0,sqrt(1-q^2)), where q is the unique root in (19/1000,191/10000) of exp(2q)+3q exp(-4+6q^2)-q exp(4-2q^2)=0. Its three directions are distinct and noncollinear, and its basin is open with positive product volume. The hyperbolic sink persists in some open neighborhood of (A,V,beta)=(V0,V0,2), with V real symmetric of signature (2,1); A may be unaligned and is realizable as Q^T K. Thus an almost-everywhere two-antipodal-cluster conclusion is false on an open family. This does not classify all initial states. Full tangent-Hessian negativity is certified by exact outward-rounded dyadic intervals; the proof and implementation still require independent audit. Clustering attractors were reported numerically by Altafini 2025; no claim that the phenomenon itself is new.
n=3 on (S^2)^3; full attention includes self-indices

For continuation: parameters sufficiently close to the base point; V symmetric
