[Conjecture conj:arithmetic_kakeya of arXiv:2609.02041, 'Sparse $k$-AP Covering Sets and the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture'] For any $\eps>0$, there exists a positive integer $\ell$ and 
$r_1,\dots,r_\ell\in\QQ\cup\{\infty\}$, none equal to $-1$, 
such that 
$$|\pi_{-1}(B)| \leq \max_{i=1}^\ell |\pi_{r_i}(B)|^{1+\eps}$$
for all finite subsets $B\subseteq \ZZ^2$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture

[Defi 9 (Classical symbols) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $m \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $p : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a classical symbol of order $m$, and we write $p \in S_{\rm cl}^m$, if $p\in S^m$ and if for all~\(j\in \Nn\) there exists $p_{m-j}\in S^{m-j}$, homogeneous of degree $m-j$ in $\xi$, smooth for $\xi \neq 0$ such that 
\[
    p - \sum_{j=0}^N\omega(\xi)p_{m-j} \in S^{m-N-1}\quad \text{for all } N\geq 0,
\] 
where $\omega \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ vanishes in a neighborhood of $0$ and equals $1$ for $|\xi| \geq 1$. 
We write $\sigma_m(p)=p_m$ and we say that $p_m$ is the principal symbol of $p$.
title: Classical symbols

 $\Psi_m(i)=\P(S_m=i)$, with the convention $\Psi_m(i)=0$ if $m<0$. Then
$$
\P(G(\mathcal T^n_{U_n})=1)
=
\frac{1}{\Psi_n(-1)}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\mathbbm{1}_{\{G(\mathcal T)=1\}}
\Psi_{n-|\mathcal T|}(0)
\right].
$$

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2607.08242, 'Convergence of random sums in non-commutative probability'] Let $\{b_i\}$ be a sequence of self-adjoint variables with $\varphi(b_i)=0$, $\varphi(b_i^2)=1$, and $\sup_{i}|\varphi(b_i^m)|<\infty$ for each $m\in\mathbb{N}$. Set $a_n=b_1+\dots+b_n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\{w_n\}$ be a sequence of positive integers increasing to infinity. Let $\{N_n\}$ be non-negative integer valued rvs such that 
    $N_n/w_n\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}1$,
    
    and $\{(\frac{N_n}{w_n})^{m}\}$ be uniformly integrable for each $m\in\mathbb{N}$. 
    
        
    
    Then the following hold. \vskip5pt
    
    \noindent (i) If $\{b_i\}$ are free then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} s$.
    

    
    \vskip5pt
    \noindent (ii) If $\{b_i\}$ are independent then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} z$.
    
    
    \vskip5pt
    \noindent (iii) If $\{b_i\}$ are half-independent then 
    $\frac{a_{N_n}}{\sqrt{w_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} r_S$.

body: Theorem 2.1 (Theorem 1 of Bubeck & Sellke (2023)). Let F be a class of functions from R^d -> [-1, 1] and let {(x_i, y_i)}_{i=1}^n be i.i.d. input-output pairs in R^d x [-1, 1]. Assume that: 1. The expected conditional variance of the output (i.e., the 'noise level') is strictly positive, denoted by sigma^2 := E[Var[y|x]] > 0. 2. F admits a J-Lipschitz parametrization by p real parameters, each of size at most poly(n, d). 3. The distribution mu of the input x_i satisfies isoperimetry (or a mixture thereof). Then, with high probability over the sampling of the data, one has simultaneously for all f in F: (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - f(x_i))^2 <= sigma^2 - eps implies Lip_{||.||_2}(f) >= Omega(eps sqrt(nd/p)).

body: [Corollary adj6 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1\leq p,q<\infty$. Suppose that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact, that $B_{Y^*}$ is relatively weakly $q$-precompact, and that $Y$ has the $\mathrm{sDPP}_{(p,q)}$. Then, the pair $(X,Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ if and only if the pair $(Y^*,X^*)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_q$ for adjoint operators. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary adj6 of arXiv:2609.03988

body:
Let r and s be probability mass functions on a finite set with total variation distance c = (1/2) sum_x |r_x - s_x|, let alpha, beta >= 0, M = max(alpha, beta), m = min(alpha, beta) and delta = M - m. Then D = (1/2) sum_x |alpha r_x - beta s_x| satisfies max(delta/2, M c - delta/2) <= D <= delta/2 + m c. Both bounds are attained for every alpha, beta >= 0 and c in [0, 1]. Writing alpha = M, beta = m: the upper bound by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (1 - c, 0, c); when m > 0, the lower bound by r = (1 - c, c), s = (1, 0) if M c <= delta, and by r = (1 - c, c, 0), s = (k, 0, 1 - k) with k = M(1 - c)/m if M c >= delta. If m = 0 then D = M/2 for all r, s.
r, s probability mass functions on one finite set
alpha, beta >= 0
total variation is half the L1 distance

[Lemma lem:ricci-internal-hard of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a complete squared-shell child through its monomer--dimer,
coefficient-pairing, ribbon, status, incidence, and Haar-residual data,
except that the complete reflection/status orbit and the complete
weak-order, equality, and finite-gap sum are retained inside the residual
component $\mathcal C_R$ containing the selected aggregate-Ricci root
$R$.  Suppose $\mathcal P_R=\varnothing$ and, after equal-time fusion,
$\mathcal C_R$ contains at least one independently token-bearing hard
resource: either a nonsingleton packet child for which the one-token
presentation has already proved a numerical factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$, or a time-indexed linear Jacobi child
$-2N^{-1}W_i$.  An unsplit mixed/full-centered hard block with only unit
or $n^{-1/2}$ relative cost is not included.  A resolved fixed-column
child whose complete closed coefficient scalar has a proved factor
$\delta_P\le N^{-1}$ relative to the bare Euler carrier is included.
Nor is a resource in a different Haar-separated component.

Let $f_R\in\{1,2\}$ be the number of fundamental $p\vee r$ circuits hit
by the four Ricci legs, let
\[
 \mathfrak e_R=\frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F,
\]
and let $\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}$ be the remaining positive,
once-normalized circuit-anchored terminal majorant.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{\text{weak orders, equality blocks, finite gaps,}\\
                  \text{and typed states inside }\mathcal C_R}}
 |\operatorname{Contr}_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}|
 \le A_L^{r_R}(r_R+1)^B
      \mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C_R}\mathfrak e_RN^{-1}.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12m}$}
\]
Consequently the complete packetless subfiber in which the Ricci
component has such a resource satisfies the shell bound on the right of
(eq:3.3.1w-12k of the paper).

[Theorem thm:first-order-score of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(A>0\) and assume (ass:standing of the paper) with \(r\geqslant r_0\) (the value of \(r_0\) is
  specified below for each expansion). Then there exists \(\sigma_0 > 0\) such that, for every
  \((y,\sigma)\in\mathcal Y_{A,\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}},\sigma_0}\), \(x=\pi(y)\), \(a = a(y,\sigma)\), it
  holds that
  \begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{s}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-1}\big(\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=2 \\
    \mathbf{H}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big( \mathsf H_0(a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma\mathscr R_{0, \mathbf{H}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3 \\
    \dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma(y) &= \sigma^{-2} \big(\dot{\mathsf S}_0 (a,x,\sigma)
    + \sigma \mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}(a,x,\sigma)\big), \qquad r_0=3.
  \end{align*}
  Here, the coefficients \(\mathsf S_0\), \(\mathsf H_0\) and \(\dot{\mathsf S}_0\) are explicitly
  given by the formulas below and have all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0+1\) in the
  variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\), uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\|
  \leqslant A\), and \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\):
  \begin{align*}
    \mathsf S_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top (a,x,\sigma)\nabla_a \mathsf L_0(a,x), \\
    \mathsf H_0 (a,x,\sigma) &= \mathbf J_\nu^\top(a,x,\sigma)
    \mathrm{D}_a^2 \mathsf L_0(a,x) \,\mathbf J_\nu(a,x,\sigma), \\
    \dot{\mathsf S}_0(a,x,\sigma) &= -\mathsf S_0 (a,x, \sigma)
    - (\mathrm{D}_a\mathsf S_0(a,x,\sigma))[a].
  \end{align*}
  The functions \(\mathscr R_{0,\boldsymbol{s}_\sigma}\), \(\mathscr R_{0,\mathbf{H}_\sigma}\) and \(\mathscr R_{0,\dot{\boldsymbol{s}}_\sigma}\) have
  all mixed derivatives up to order \(r-r_0\) in the variables \(a\), \(x\), and \(\sigma\),
  uniformly bounded for \(x\in\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{S}}\), \(\|a\| \leqslant A\), and
  \(0<\sigma\leqslant\sigma_0\). Derivatives in \(x\) are computed in the stratum coordinate
  \(\theta\), after writing \(x=\Phi(\theta,0)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): After Theorem 1 each row is h_a(x) = q_a(x_C) + lambda_a*x_j for at most one j outside C (tag 19). Call j conditionally free if for SOME realized core value X_C = c both signs of X_j occur among points of S having that same core value. If a row uses a conditionally free j, evaluating on two such points gives q_a(c)+lambda_a and q_a(c)-lambda_a both in {+-1}; since lambda_a is nonzero these are the two distinct signs, so q_a(c) = 0 and lambda_a = +-1 (tag 20). [Corollary cor:accelerated-rigidity of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Under the Chebyshev-accelerated scheme $Q_m^\ast$, the rigidity time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \le \frac{1}{m} \cdot \frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2 \log(1/\epsilon_m)} + 1, \qquad
\epsilon_m := \frac{1}{|T_m(1/\lambda_2)|}.
\]
For large $m$, $\epsilon_m \sim (1 - \sqrt{1-\lambda_2^2}/\lambda_2)^m$, yielding
\[
T_{\mathrm{rigid}}^{\mathrm{cheb}}(\delta) \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log(R_0 / (|c_2|^2 \delta))}{2(1-\lambda_2)}} = O\Bigl( \sqrt{T_{\mathrm{rigid}}(\delta)} \Bigr),
\]
a square-root speedup over the basic power iteration.

[Lemma l:time_regularity of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Fix $R,M,\mu>0$, and let $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ be such that (equation eq:condition_pq_subcritical_scaling_cutoff of the paper) holds.
For all $b\in (2,\infty)$ and $T\in (0,\infty)$, let $w_{{\rm cut}}^N$ be the unique global $(p,q)$-solution to (equation eq:navier_stokes_cutoff of the paper) provided by Lemma (l:global_cutoff of the paper) for some $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$. 
Set 
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{M}^N(t)\stackrel{{\rm def}}{=}\sum_{k,\alpha} \theta_k^N \int_0^t (\sigma_{k,\alpha}\cdot \nabla) w_{{\rm cut}}^N\,\mathrm{d} W^{k,\alpha}_s.
\end{equation}
Then there exist constants $K_T,\kappa,\gamma_0,\gamma_1>0$ independent of $u_0\in \mathcal{B}_{p,q}(M)$ and $N\geq 1$ such that 
\begin{align}

{\mathbf E} [\|\mathcal{M}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T N^{-\kappa b} (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),\\

{\mathbf E} [\|w_{{\rm cut}}^N \|_{C^{\gamma_0}(0,T;H^{-\gamma_1})}^{b}]
&\leq K_T (1+\|u_0\|_{B^{1-2/p}_{q,p}}^{b}),
\end{align}
where $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are additionally independent of $T>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:tailrl-closed-form-weights of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For every $i=1,\ldots,N$,
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{i}
\frac{r_{(k)}-r_{(k-1)}}{N-k+1}.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, all weights follow the recurrence
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\omega\bigl(r_{(i-1)}\bigr)
+
\frac{r_{(i)}-r_{(i-1)}}{N-i+1},
\qquad
\omega\bigl(r_{(0)}\bigr)=0.

\end{equation}
title: Closed-form empirical weights

[Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $\mu$   be a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the \emph{decomposability bundle} is a Borel map $T^{AM}_\mu: \mathbb{R}^n \to \Gr(\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that the following
		statements hold:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Every Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is differentiable at $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with respect to the
			linear subspace $T_\mu^{AM}$, that is, there exists a linear function $df_x^{AM}: T^{AM}_\mu(x) \to \mathbb{R}$, such that
			\[ f(x+h) = f(x) + df_x^{AM}(h) + o(\lvert h\rvert)
			\quad \text{for } h \in T^{AM}_\mu(x). \]
			\item The previous statement is sharp:  there exists a Lipschitz function $f \in \Lip(\mathbb{R}^n)$
			such that for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$ the derivative of $f$ at $x$ in the
			direction $v$ does not exist. More precisely, for $\mu$-a.e.~$x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
			\[
			\liminf_{t \to 0} \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t} < \limsup_{t \to 0}  \frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}, \quad \mbox{for all $v \not\in T^{AM}_\mu(x)$}
			\]
		\end{enumerate}
title: Definition d:am-decbundle of arXiv:2510.13659

[Lemma exp of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] The basis change formula expressing the elements of $({\mathbb A}^0)^\ast$ in terms of the elements of ${\mathbb A}^\ast$ in ${\mathbb R} {\langle}{\mathbb A}{\rangle}$ is obtained as
$$
	w^0=\sum_{(i_1, \ldots ,i_\ell)}\frac{1}{i_1!\cdots i_\ell!}(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w.
$$
where $w^0=a_1^0\cdots a_n^0$. Here, the sum runs over all multi-indices $(i_1, \ldots , i_\ell)$ such that $i_1+ \cdots + i_\ell=|w|$ where $|w|$ denotes the length of the word $w$ and  
\begin{equation*}
	(i_1, \ldots,\, i_\ell)\circ w := 
		[ a_1,\ldots , a_{i_1}]
		[ a_{i_1+1}, \ldots , a_{i_1+i_2}]\cdots
		[ a_{i_1+\cdots+i_{\ell-1}+1}, \ldots , a_{n}]
\end{equation*}
is the concatenation of the repeated bracket product of the letters in each subword as indicated. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:stein of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] For \emph{any} $\theta$, not only a minimiser, define the free score discrepancy
$\mathcal S_{t}(\theta):=\tau\big[(\widehat\xi_{t}-\xi_{\mu_{t}}(X_{t}))^{2}\big]$,
the free (Fisher-divergence-type) analogue of a Stein discrepancy between the learned
and true conjugate variable at time $t$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=\frac{1}{v_{t}^{2}}\Big(\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\Big),
  \qquad
  \mathcal L_{t}(\theta):=\tau\Big[\big(g_{\theta}(X_{t},t)-\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}
  \big)^{2}\Big],
\end{equation}
with $c_{t}$ as in (equation eq:bias-variance of the paper), exactly -- with no approximation and no
constant to be estimated. Consequently $\mathcal L_{t}(\theta)-c_{t}\ge0$ always, with
equality iff $\mathcal S_{t}(\theta)=0$.

[Lemma lm:3.7.howard.newman of arXiv:2411.02046, 'Speed of Convergence and Moderate Deviations of FPP on Random Geometric Graphs'] For any~$d \ge 2$ and~$\uppsi \in (0,1/4)$, there exists~$c_\uppsi > 0$ such that the following holds. Let~$\{q_1,q_2,\ldots\}$ be a finite or infinite sequence of elements of $\mathbb R^d$ so that there exists~$k^* \in \mathbb N$ such that the following three properties hold: first,
    \[
    \|q_{i+1}-q_i\|\le \|q_i\|^{3/4} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    second, 
    \[
    \|q_i\| \ge 3^{1/\uppsi} \text{ for all }i \ge k^*;
    \]
    and third,
    \[\mathrm{dist}(q_i,\overline{o q_j})\leq \|q_j\|^{1-\uppsi} \ \ \text{ for all $i,j$ with $j \ge k^*$ and ~$i \le j$}.\]
    Then, for all~$i,j$ with~$j > i \ge k^*$, we have
    \begin{equation*} 
        \uptheta(q_i,q_j) \le c_\uppsi~\|q_i\|^{-\uppsi}.
    \end{equation*}

body: In mathematics, a presentation is one method of specifying a group. [Definition def:delta_close of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF with values modulo a global multiple of $2\pi\chi$. Let $D$ be a bounded open set containing $0$, let $\delta > 0$ and define $D_\delta = \{z \in \mathbf{C} \colon d(z, D) < \delta\}$. For $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ let $\eta_{\theta}$ be the flow line of $h$ starting from $0$ with angle $\theta$ and for any set $A$ let $\tau_\theta(A) = \inf\{t \geq 0\colon \eta_\theta(t) \notin A\}$.
For $\theta \neq 0$, $\eta_0$ and $\eta_\theta$ are said to be \emph{$\delta$-close until $\eta_0$ exits $D$} if the following conditions hold. For all $t \in (0, \tau_0(D)]$ there exist $t_1, t_2, t'_1, t'_2$ where $0 < t_1 < t < t_2 < \tau_0(D_\delta)$ and $0 < t'_1 < t'_2 < \tau_\theta(D_\delta)$ such that for each $j = 1,2$, $\eta_0(t_j) = \eta_\theta(t'_j)$ and at this point $\eta_\theta$ hits $\eta_0$ on the \emph{left} side of $\eta_0$  (if $\theta > 0$) with angle gap $\theta$ (as defined in [ms2017ig4]). Furthermore, for any $s \in [t_1, t_2]$ and $s' \in [t'_1, t'_2]$, we have $|\eta_0(s) - \eta_\theta(s')| < \delta$. If $\theta < 0$, we replace `left side' by `right side' above.

body:
Let Omega be an open subset of R^n. A second-order operator in divergence form is Lu = -sum_{i,j} D_i(a^{ij}(x) D_j u) + sum_i b^i(x) D_i u + c(x) u, written Lu = -div(A grad u) + b.grad u + c u, where A = (a^{ij}) is a real n x n matrix-valued measurable function on Omega (not necessarily symmetric, not necessarily continuous) and b = (b^i), c are real measurable functions. L is uniformly elliptic with constants 0 < lambda <= Lambda if for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta in R^n: A(x)xi.xi >= lambda|xi|^2 and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta|; one normally also assumes b, c in L^infinity(Omega). Only the symmetric part of A enters the ellipticity condition. Sign convention: with the leading minus sign, L = -Laplacian when A = I, b = 0, c = 0, so a subsolution (Lu <= 0) generalizes a subharmonic function, and the favorable sign of the zeroth-order coefficient is c >= 0. The ratio Lambda/lambda is the ellipticity ratio; the constants in the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory depend only on n and Lambda/lambda. For u in H^1_loc the expression Lu is defined only weakly (in the sense of distributions); no differentiability of A is required.
Omega is an open subset of R^n
a^{ij}, b^i, c are real measurable functions on Omega
lambda|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta| for a.e. x and all xi, eta, with 0 < lambda <= Lambda
b, c in L^infinity(Omega)

\]

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2609.02175, '2609.02175'] Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary.
	We say that $M$ admits a strictly convex foliation if there exist
	$T>0$ and a smooth function
	\[
	\rho:M\longrightarrow [0,+\infty)
	\]
	such that, for every $t\in[0,T)$, the level set
	\[
	\Sigma_t=\rho^{-1}(t)
	\]
	is a strictly convex hypersurface, $d\rho\neq0$ on $\Sigma_t$,
	$\Sigma_0=\partial M$, and
	\[
	M\setminus\bigcup_{0\leq t<T}\Sigma_t
	\]
	has empty interior.

body: In differential geometry, the Ricci curvature tensor, named after Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro, measures how a curved space locally differs from flat space by tracking how nearby geodesics spread apart or converge. Formally, it is a symmetric rank-two tensor obtained by taking a trace of the Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metric. In Riemannian geometry, the Ricci curvature in a given tangent direction may be interpreted as an average of the sectional curvatures of planes containing that direction. A further trace of the Ricci curvature yields the scalar curvature.
title: Ricci curvature

Fix a finite alphabet Sigma, block length n, message u, and a keyed randomized code with key K and encoder output X in Sigma^n. Suppose its decoding failure is at most a for every randomized channel C, acting on the input word alone, such that d_H(x,C(x))<=p*n almost surely for every x in Sigma^n. Let E be another randomized channel Sigma^n->Sigma^n, independent of K except through its input, and suppose P(d_H(X,E(X))>p*n)<=delta under the key, encoder and channel randomness. Then the decoding failure under E is at most a+delta. In particular robustness persists if a and delta are negligible in the security parameter. If the robustness premise is restricted to efficiently sampleable channels, also assume E and the budget comparison are polynomial-time computable; the clipping preserves that property.
Robustness to every almost-sure p-substitution-bounded channel in the relevant class.
E sees the word and its own randomness, with no additional secret-key side information.
The high-probability budget is averaged over the same key/encoder/channel experiment as the decoding guarantee.

[Theorem of arXiv:2411.12522, 'Canonical insurance models: stochastic equations and comparison theorems'] Let  $(V^i)$ and  $(\bar V^i)$  be the state-wise prospective reserves of canonical insurance models $(\alpha, \Lambda, \Phi, B, b)$ and $(\bar \alpha, \bar \Lambda, \bar \Phi, B, b)$, where on each compact interval the differences {$\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ shall} have finite variation. Let $ V :=\sum_i I^i V^i $, and let $R^{ij} := b^{ij} + V^j - V^i$.
\begin{itemize}
	\item[(a)]  \textbf{Pessimistic actuarial  basis:} If the differences $\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ and $\bar\Phi - \Phi$ satisfy  
	\begin{align*}
		\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \geq 0\}} \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big) (\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big) (\mathrm{d} t)&\leq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{ V^i(t) \geq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\leq 	0,\\
		\mathds{1}_{\{V^i(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big) (\mathrm{d} t)&\geq 	0
	\end{align*}
	 for    $t \geq 0$, $i,j \in \mathcal{Z}$, $i\neq j$, then it  holds that 
	$$ \bar V^i(t) \geq  V^i(t),  \quad t \geq 0, \, i \in \mathcal{Z}.$$ 
		
	\item[(b)] \textbf{Optimistic actuarial basis:} If the differences $\bar\Lambda - \Lambda$ and $\bar\Phi - \Phi$ satisfy 
\begin{align*}
	\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \geq 0\}} \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\leq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{ R^{ij}(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Lambda^{ij}-\Lambda^{ij}\big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{ V^i(t) \geq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t) &\geq 	0,\\
	\mathds{1}_{\{V^i(t) \leq 0\}}  \big( \bar \Phi^i  -\Phi^i  \big)(\mathrm{d} t)  &\leq 	0
\end{align*}
for 	 $t \geq 0$, $i,j \in \mathcal{Z}$, $i\neq j$, then it holds that 
$$ \bar V^i(t) \leq  V^i(t),  \quad t \geq 0, \, i \in \mathcal{Z}.$$  	
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let Omega in R^n be open. H^1_0(Omega) = W^{1,2}_0(Omega) is the closure of C_c^infinity(Omega) in the norm ||u||_{H^1} = (||u||_{L^2}^2 + ||grad u||_{L^2}^2)^{1/2}; W^{1,p}_0(Omega) is the W^{1,p}-closure, 1 <= p < infinity. If Omega is bounded, the Poincare inequality ||u||_{L^2(Omega)} <= diam(Omega) ||grad u||_{L^2(Omega)} holds for u in H^1_0(Omega), so ||grad u||_{L^2} is an equivalent norm on H^1_0(Omega); and the embedding H^1_0(Omega) into L^2(Omega) is compact (Rellich), with no boundary regularity needed. If Omega is bounded with C^1 boundary there is a bounded trace operator T from W^{1,p}(Omega) to L^p(boundary), 1 <= p < infinity, with Tu = restriction of u for u in W^{1,p} continuous up to the boundary, and W^{1,p}_0(Omega) = kernel of T. Lattice facts: for u in H^1(Omega) and real k, (u - k)^+ is in H^1_loc(Omega) (in H^1(Omega) when k >= 0 or Omega is bounded) with grad (u - k)^+ = 1_{u > k} grad u a.e.; in particular grad u = 0 a.e. on every level set {u = k}. For bounded Omega and u in H^1(Omega) one says u <= k on the boundary (in the H^1 sense) if (u - k)^+ is in H^1_0(Omega), and defines sup over the boundary of u as inf{k real : (u - k)^+ in H^1_0(Omega)}; u = g on the boundary means u - g in H^1_0(Omega). These notions need no regularity of the boundary.
Omega open in R^n; bounded for the Poincare inequality, Rellich compactness and the boundary-inequality notion
C^1 boundary for the trace theorem
1 <= p < infinity for W^{1,p}_0 and the trace

body: In mathematics, especially spectral theory, Weyl's law describes the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of the Laplace–Beltrami operator. This description was discovered in 1911 (in the $d=2,3$ case) by Hermann Weyl for eigenvalues for the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on functions that vanish at the boundary of a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb {R} ^{d}$. In particular, he proved that the number, $N(\lambda)$, of Dirichlet eigenvalues (counting their multiplicities) less than or equal to $\lambda$ satisfies $$\lim _{\lambda \rightarrow \infty }{\frac {N(\lambda )}{\lambda ^{d/2}}}=(2\pi )^{-d}\omega _{d}\mathrm {vol} (\Omega )$$

[Definition of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] A \textit{positive spanning set} of a set $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^N$ is a subset $B\subseteq S$ with the property that for any $\boldsymbol s \in S$, there exist coefficients $c_{\boldsymbol b}\in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ for each $\boldsymbol b \in B$ where only a finite number of $c_{\boldsymbol b}$ are non-zero and
    $$\boldsymbol s = \sum_{\boldsymbol b \in B} c_{\boldsymbol b}\boldsymbol b.$$

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02590, 'Directional Optimal Sub-Gamma Scales for Infinitely Divisible Laws'] Fixing the quadratic proxy in a sub-gamma bound at the true variance leaves a scale to optimize, and a two-sided infinitely divisible law generally requires different scales in the two directions. For a centered law with finite nonzero variance, we normalize its Kolmogorov canonical measure and multiply the resulting variable by an independent $\operatorname{Beta}(1,2)$ variable. The signed remainder obtained in this way gives exact variational formulas for the right and left scales. We prove that a directional scale vanishes exactly when the L\'evy measure has no jumps in that direction, establish reflection, scaling, convolution, L\'evy-time, and opposite-jump perturbation rules, and recover the L\'evy triplet from the remainder law. The formulas give the two Gamma scales for bilateral Gamma laws and, for centered Skellam laws, the exact transition points $p_{\pm}=(2\pm\sqrt{3})/4$ between local and interior control; when positive jumps are rare, the right scale is asymptotic to $1/\log(1/p)$. The pair therefore records jump direction and the mechanism that controls the variance-exact sub-gamma pole.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02590: Directional Optimal Sub-Gamma Scales for Infinitely Divisible Laws

Let L be a finite lattice with bottom 0 != top 1. A cross-cut is an antichain C, containing neither 0 nor 1, that meets every maximal chain from 0 to 1. Call S inside C spanning when its join is 1 and its meet is 0, and let q_k be the number of spanning k-subsets. Then mu(0, 1) = sum_{k >= 2} (-1)^k q_k (G.-C. Rota, 1964). If 1 does not cover 0, the atoms form a cross-cut and mu(0, 1) = sum over sets S of atoms with join 1 of (-1)^|S|. The chain-meeting condition is needed: in the Boolean lattice of subsets of {1, 2}, the antichain {{1}} misses the chain empty < {2} < {1, 2}, has no spanning subset, and gives 0 while mu = 1.

body:
[Proposition 25 (Maximum principle for dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Fix a Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ that is admissible (\autoref{def-pot-admissible-triple}) and torus-adapted (\autoref{def-NS-torus-adapted}). Let $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ be a sufficiently regular dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$, and assume that the density $\mu>0$ is positive. Then the range of the function $\Sbb^1\ni x\mapsto\bigl(\Gammaunpar_\chi(t,x),\Gammazero(t,x)\bigr)$ is a subset of~$\RR^4$ that does not depend on areal time $t\in [t_0,t_1]$.  In particular, for $t\in[t_0,t_1]$ and $m=2,3$, one has 
\be

\aligned \inf_{\Sbb^1}\Gammaun_m^\chi(t_0,\cdot) & \leq\Gammaun_m^\chi(t,x)\leq\sup_{\Sbb^1}\Gammaun_m^\chi(t_0,\cdot), \\
\inf_{\Sbb^1}\Gammazero_m(t_0,\cdot) & \leq\Gammazero_m(t,x)\leq\sup_{\Sbb^1}\Gammazero_m(t_0,\cdot).\endaligned
\ee
The second line also holds at vacuum.
At vacuum, the first line is understood as the statement that if $C_1\rho_\chi\leq 2T_\chi^{0m} \leq C_2 \rho_\chi$ for some $C_1,C_2\in\RR$ at initial time then this inequality holds for all times.
The convex hull of the range of $\Gammaunpar_\chi$ is thus preserved in time, without density assumption. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximum principle for dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes flows

body: Within a BSS-type multiscale variance-halving program on Z^2 (hypothesis set: concentration envelope H1a at scale Q, anti-concentration floor H4, chaos input CH), write Q_s ~ s^alpha and the model's TRUE variance Var(X_s) ~ s^{2 chi}. Then rho_s = Q_s^2/Var(X_s) ~ s^{2(alpha-chi)} and the halving step demands chaos strength eps <~ s^{-4(alpha-chi)}. Constant-strength chaos - the only strength BSS-type constructions deliver - therefore requires alpha <= chi, while H1a (true concentration at scale Q) forces alpha >= chi: within the hypothesis set alpha = chi EXACTLY. The envelope exponent is fixed by nature, not by the theorem being chased: D in the halving lemma is the true variance (a standing assumption, not a free parameter), and the target rate n^{1-eps} is the OUTPUT of telescoping, never an input to any rung. Independent cross-check: reading D as inductive would let Efron-Stein plus one hypothesis alone deliver the conclusion with the whole apparatus idle. Refereed 2026-08-09 (two independent kills of the inductive reading). Provenance: campaign CRUX sections 2, 3b (resolved banner), 7; referee verdict iter 68.
title: Envelope-variance pinning in BSS-type multiscale FPP programs (conditional)

body:
[Theorem thm:rank-frequency of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  For every $n\in\mathcal R(h,k)$, the function
\[
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)=
 \#\left\{A\in\binom{[q]}k:|hA|=n\right\}
\]
is a quasipolynomial in $q-1$ (and hence in $q$).  Its degree is exactly
\[
 \deg F^{(k)}_{h,n}=k-r_{h,k}(n).
\]
In particular, there is an explicitly computable positive rational number
$c_{h,k,n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F^{(k)}_{h,n}(q)
 =c_{h,k,n}q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)}
  +O_{h,k}\!\left(q^{k-r_{h,k}(n)-1}\right).
\end{equation}
The possible frequency exponents therefore belong to
$\{2,3,\ldots,k\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Complete rank--frequency stratification
The existence of on/off super Brownian motion (ooSBM), Blath and Jacobi \cite{blath2023off}

[Theorem thm:kthgasket of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $D$ be a simply-connected domain, $z_1 \neq z_2$ two distinct points in $D$.
Fix $m \geq 2$ and let $E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm m^{th}}(z_1, z_2)$ denote the event that an $m$-th nested CLE$_4$ gasket in $D$ intersects both disks
$\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2)$.
We then have that 
$$(\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2)^{-1/8}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm m^{th}}(z_1, z_2))+
o(1)$$equals 
$$\frac{\pi^{3/4}}{2^{7/4}} (\mathbf{C}_{\rm{SLE}4}^{\rm loop})^2\,
\dfrac{\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}}
{\theta_2(q^{1/4})\sqrt{|\log q|}}\sum\limits_{\substack{|n| \geq m-1 \\ n = m \mod 2}}2^{m-1}(-1)^{\frac{n-m}{2}}\left( \binom{\frac{n+m}{2}}{\frac{n-m}{2}}+\binom{\frac{n+m}{2}-1}{\frac{n-m}{2}-1}\right)\hat q^{2n^2},
$$
where $\hat q$ is the complementary nome to nome $q$,
which in turn, by Lemma (lem:parametr of the paper),
is uniquely defined via 
$$\exp\Big(\pi G_D(z_1,z_2)\Big) 
= \dfrac{\theta_3(q^{1/2})}{\theta_2(q^{1/2})}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 10 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(i \in I\) and \(f(i) = j\).
  Suppose
  \[
  \Psi^{(i)}(q) \sim c q^{\alpha}K(q) \quad \text{and} \quad 
  \psi^{(j)}(q) \sim c' q^{\beta}H(q) \quad (q \to 0)
  \]
  for \(c \geq 0\), \(c' > 0\), \(\alpha,\beta \in [0,1]\), and slowly varying functions \(K,H\) at \(0\).
  Then we have
  \begin{align}    
  \Psi^{\ast,(i)}(q) \sim C q^{\alpha \beta}G(q) \quad (q \to 0), 
  \end{align}
  where 
  \[
  C := c(c')^{\alpha} \quad \text{and} \quad G(q) := H(q)^{\alpha}K(q^{\beta}H(q)).
  \]
  In particular, \(G\) is slowly varying at \(0\), and whenever \(c > 0\), the function \(\Psi^{\ast,(i)}\) is regularly varying at \(0\) with exponent \(\alpha\beta\).

[Thm main of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] Let $p \in (\lambda, 1-\lambda)$ and let $\mathcal{H}$ be a downwards closed set of nonisomorphic connected graphs with at least two vertices (in the sense of (def:downwards-closed of the paper)). Then, for every $\eps > 0$ and permissible $(y_H)_{H \in \mathcal{H}}$ (in the sense of (def:permissible of the paper)) we have
\[\abs*{\setp[\gamma_{H} = y_H\;\forall H\in \mathcal{H}] \prod_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \paren*{(p(1-p))^{e(H)/2}\sigma_{H}} - \prod_{H \in \mathcal{H}} \mathcal{N}(y_H/\sigma_{H})} \lsim_{ \mathcal{H}, \lambda, \eps} n^{-1/2+\eps},\]
where $\sigma_{H}^2 = \Var[\gamma_{H}]$ and $\mathcal{N}(z) = (2\pi)^{-1/2} e^{-z^2/2}$ is the standard normal probability distribution function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm main of arXiv:2412.09535

[Corollary 12 (leave probability and exit distribution) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] \label[corollary]{cor:leave-zero}
  Let $T_\alpha\sim\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha)$ be independent of the sticky process $u$, with $u_0=0$.
  The probability that $u_{T_\alpha}\neq 0$  is
  \[
    p_{\mathrm{leave}}
    = \frac{\mu}{\mu+\Phi},
    \qquad
    \Phi = \frac{1}{G_\alpha(0,0)},
  \]
  where $G_\alpha$ is the reflecting resolvent kernel of \cref{green-function}.
  Conditional on $u_{T_\alpha}\neq 0$, the exit position is drawn from
  the density
  \begin{equation}
    \nu_\alpha(dy) = Z_\nu^{-1}\,U(a,b,z_y)\,m'(y)\,dy,
    \qquad Z_\nu = |\mathcal{W}|/\alpha.
  \end{equation}

	\begin{align*} 
		&\sum_{\mathfrak{q=1}}^{2} E_{\kappa_{n}(s)} \big|(\widehat\sigma_{\mathfrak{q}}^{u\ell})_{tam}^{\displaystyle{n}}\big(\kappa_n(s),s,x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n},\mu^{x,N,n}_{\kappa_n(s)}\big)\big|^{p_0} \leq
		Kn^{\frac{2p_0-9}{12}} \big(1+|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n}|^{p_0}+\frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N}|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{k,N,n}|^{p_0}\big),
				\\
				& \int_ZE_{\kappa_{n}(s)}\big|(\widehat\gamma_1^u)_{tam}^{\displaystyle{n}}\big(\kappa_n(s),s,x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n},\mu^{x,N,n}_{\kappa_n(s)},\bar z\big)\big|^{p_0}\nu(d\bar z) 
				\leq Kn^{-\frac{p_0}{4}} \big(1+|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n}|^{p_0}+\frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N}|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{k,N,n}|^{p_0}\big) ,
				\\
				 &\int_Z \Big(E_{\kappa_{n}(s)} \big|(\widehat\gamma_2^{u})_{tam}^{\displaystyle{n}}\big(\kappa_n(s),s,x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n},\mu^{x,N,n}_{\kappa_n(s)},\bar z\big)\big|^{p_0}\Big)^{p_1} \nu(d\bar z)
				\leq Kn^{-p_1+\frac{1}{2}} \big(1+|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{i,N,n}|^{p_0p_1}+\frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^{N}|x_{\kappa_n(s)}^{k,N,n}|^{p_0p_1}\big)
	\end{align*}
	 where the last inequality  holds for some   $p_1\geq 1$  with  $p_0p_1\leq \bar p$.

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose the coefficient $G:=gg^\top/2$ is non-degenerate in $y$ uniformly with respect to $x$ and the drift $f$ satisfies the weak recurrence condition 
\bea\ad
\lim_{|y| \to \infty} \sup_{x\in \rr^{d_1}} \bqv{y,f(x,y)}=-\infty.
\eea 
Assume that $f,g\in C_b^{\vartheta, \dl}$ with $0< \dl \leq 1$ and $\vartheta \geq 0$. Then for every $Z\in C_p^{\vartheta, \dl}$ satisfying \eqref{cen-cond}, there exists a unique solution $u\in C_p^{\vartheta,2+\dl}$ to Poisson equation \eqref{Poi-eq} satisfying \eqref{cen-cond} given by 
\bea\ad 
u(x, y)= \int_0^\infty \EE Z(x, y_t^x)dt.
\eea
Moreover, there exists a constant $\wdh n>0$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] (Case $\vartheta=0$) for any $x\in \rr^{d_1}$ and $y\in \rr^{d_2}$,
\beq{u-der-y}
|u(x, y)|+|\nabla_y u(x, y)|+ |\nabla_y^2 u(x, y)| \leq C_0 (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eeq
where $C_0> 0$ depends only on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{0,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{0,\dl}}$;
\item[(ii)] (Case $\vartheta>0$) for any $y \in \rr^{d_2}$,
\bea
\|u(\cdot,y)\|_{C_b^{\vartheta}} \leq C_0 C_\vartheta (1+|y|^{\wdh n}),
\eea
where $C_\vartheta>0$ depends on $d_1, d_2$ and $\|f\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$, $\|g\|_{C_b^{\vartheta,\dl}}$ and $[Z]_{C_p^{\vartheta,\dl}}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 3 of arXiv:2607.03360

Claim: w718-T287-024, version 1. Kind: moved; target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). This is an elementary supporting lemma for the checked rectangular-reference route, not a claim of a new random-matrix theorem or completion of Target 2.

## Statement

Let n,p be positive integers and let delta>0, Kappa>=1+delta satisfy 1+delta <= p/n <= Kappa. Let G be an n by p real matrix of independent standard normal entries. Let S be any deterministic n by p real matrix with operator norm at most C, where C>=0. The same conclusions hold conditional on a random S independent of G. Fix 0<t_minus<=t_plus<infinity. Define

L=8 sqrt(1+Kappa),
K=max(1,C+sqrt(t_plus)L),
C0=max(1,2 sqrt(3/t_minus)),
epsilon=(6 K C0^Kappa)^(-1/delta).

For each t in [t_minus,t_plus], put Y_t=S+sqrt(t/n)G. Then

P(s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon) <= 2 exp(-n)+2^(-n).                 (1)

Here s_min is the least of the n singular values, equivalently inf_{||x||=1} ||Y_t^T x||. The bound is uniform in t and S, but is not asserted as a simultaneous event for an uncountable collection of t. If S is random independent of G without an almost sure norm bound, add P(||S||op>C) to the right side.

Consequently, suppose empirical singular-value laws of Y_t converge in probability to deterministic laws eta_t, and P(||S_n||op>C)->0 for some fixed C. Then for every t in the stated interval, eta_t([0,epsilon))=0. Thus the same epsilon is a gap for all these deterministic limiting laws. No assertion of a positive gap at square aspect ratio is made.

## Proof

1. A Euclidean unit sphere in R^d has an r-net with at most (1+2/r)^d elements, for 0<r<=1. Indeed take a maximal r-separated set. The open radius r/2 balls about its points are disjoint and lie in the radius 1+r/2 ball, so comparing their volumes gives the bound. Maximality gives coverage. This proof uses finite-dimensional Euclidean volume only.

2. Take 1/4-nets A and B in the unit spheres of R^n and R^p. For every matrix Z, approximation of both maximizing unit vectors gives

||Z||op <= 2 max_{x in A,y in B} |x^T Z y|.

For fixed x,y and Z=G/sqrt(n), x^T Z y is a centered normal of variance 1/n. The elementary normal tail bound P(|N(0,1)|>u)<=2 exp(-u^2/2), obtained by exponential Markov inequalities for both signs, yields

P(||G/sqrt(n)||op>L)
 <= 2 exp((n+p) log 9 - n L^2/8)
 <= 2 exp(-n).

The last inequality follows from p<=Kappa n, L^2=64(1+Kappa), and log 9<3. In particular, outside an event of probability at most 2 exp(-n), ||Y_t||op<=C+sqrt(t_plus)L<=K.

3. For any fixed unit x in R^n, Y_t^T x is a p-dimensional normal vector with arbitrary deterministic mean S^T x and covariance (t/n)I_p. Its density is bounded everywhere by (n/(2 pi t))^(p/2), independently of that mean. For R>0, the volume bound

vol(B_p(R)) <= (2 pi e/p)^(p/2) R^p

follows by integrating exp(-lambda ||u||^2) on R^p: the integral over the ball is at least exp(-lambda R^2) times its volume; choose lambda=p/(2R^2). Therefore

P(||Y_t^T x||<=2epsilon)
 <= (2 sqrt(e n/(p t)) epsilon)^p
 <= (C0 epsilon)^p.                                    (2)

Using the maximum density rather than a centered small-ball formula makes the arbitrary-shift hypothesis explicit.

4. Since K>=1 and epsilon<1, take an epsilon/K-net A_epsilon of the sphere in R^n, with cardinality at most (3K/epsilon)^n. If s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon and ||Y_t||op<=K, there is a unit x with ||Y_t^T x||<=epsilon, and a net point x0 at distance at most epsilon/K. The triangle inequality gives ||Y_t^T x0||<=2epsilon. A union bound and (2) give

P(s_min(Y_t)<=epsilon, ||Y_t||op<=K)
 <= (3K/epsilon)^n (C0 epsilon)^p
 <= (3K C0^Kappa epsilon^delta)^n
 = 2^(-n).

Here C0>=1, p<=Kappa n, p-n>=delta n, and 0<epsilon<1 justify each inequality. The event ||Y_t||op<=K was used only for the deterministic net approximation. It was not multiplied as an independent event with the small-ball probabilities.

5. Add the operator-norm exceptional probability from step 2 to prove (1). Conditional on an independent random S with ||S||op<=C, the same net, density bound and constants apply. Integrating the conditional inequality proves the random-input statement with the extra probability P(||S||op>C); it is unnecessary and generally incorrect to assume independence of the two exceptional events.

6. To pass to limiting laws, fix a continuous nonnegative function f supported in [0,epsilon), with f<=1. The empirical integral of f is zero unless s_min(Y_t)<epsilon. Thus its expectation tends to zero by (1) and the input-norm condition. Its convergence in probability to the deterministic integral against eta_t, together with boundedness, implies that integral is zero. Approximating indicators of [0,epsilon') for epsilon'<epsilon by such continuous tests gives eta_t([0,epsilon))=0. Constants do not depend on t, so the deterministic conclusion holds for each t with the same gap. This does not exchange a probability bound with an uncountable union.

## Gaussian-product application and limitations

For S=UV^T/n with independent standard normal U (n by M) and V (p by M), and bounded positive ratios M/n and p/n, apply the same two-sphere Gaussian net argument to U/sqrt(n) and V/sqrt(n). Their operator norms are bounded by fixed constants with exceptional probability tending to zero. The deterministic inequality ||UV^T/n||op<=||U/sqrt(n)||op ||V/sqrt(n)||op supplies the required C. The noise matrix is independent of both factors. Hence any deterministic limiting singular laws supplied by the already checked real population-Wishart theorem have this gap on compact intervals t>0 whenever p/n stays bounded away from one.

This lemma supplies no density regularity, no entropy differentiation, and no MMSE limit by itself. Its constants are deliberately crude. The least trusted step of the larger route remains algebraic boundary regularity and the singular-logarithm chain rule, not the elementary union bound above.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:965a7f6569046bdab574a5d8dade402280c470a6610623c9409c56ed763549bc","revision_digest":"sha256:762ffbc60d1a44b7d6b7b9f148692dce3f8fd290c35553753083c63fc18fcacf","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:shifted-rectangular-gaussian-smoothing-gap-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 w718-T287-024 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In multivariable calculus, the implicit function theorem is a theorem that provides sufficient conditions under which a planar curve specified by an equation F(x, y) = 0 can also be specified as the graph of a function y = g(x), so that for each point (x, y) on part of the curve, one has y = g(x). An example is the unit circle, whose points satisfy x^2 + y^2 = 1, which can locally be solved by y = sqrt(1 - x^2), expressing the top semicircle as a graph. It is not always possible to solve the equation for y algebraically, and the implicit function theorem gives analytic conditions under which there exists a function g whose graph belongs to the given curve, and, in some formulations, also gives a way of constructing approximations to g.

[Defn 11 (Majority rule) of arXiv:2606.22960, '2606.22960'] Let \((T_n,(B_v)_{v\in[n]})\) be the broadcast-coloured tree of size \(n\), where
	\(B_v\in\{-1,1\}\) denotes the colour of vertex \(v\).
	The {\it majority rule} estimator is the \(\{-1,1\}\)-valued random variable
	\[
	\widehat B_{\mathrm{maj},n}
	:=
	\begin{cases}
		1, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v > 0,\\
		-1, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v < 0,\\
		\xi_n, & \sum_{v=1}^n B_v = 0,
	\end{cases}
	\]
	where \(\xi_n\) is independent of the broadcasting process and satisfies
	\[
	\mathbb P(\xi_n=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_n=-1)=\frac12.
	\]
	Its error probability is defined by
	\[
	R_{\mathrm{maj}}(n,q):=\mathbb P\!\left(\widehat B_{\mathrm{maj},n}\neq B_1\right),
	\qquad
	R_{\mathrm{maj}}(q):=\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_{\mathrm{maj}}(n,q).
	\]
title: Majority rule

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1 > 0$ and $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we have $S_\star(\lambda,\mu) \subseteq S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_1)$.
\begin{proof}
    Let $\YY \in S_\star(\lambda,\mu)$.
    Then for any $i \in [r]$,
    \[
        \lambda_i \BBb_i
        \le \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
        \le \Budget(\YY;\mu)
        = \frac{1}{\alpha}
        \bigg(
            \sum_{j=1}^s
            \mu_j
            (\www_j)^{1/2}
        \bigg)^2
        \le \frac{1}{\alpha}
        (\mu,\www)
        = \frac{1}{\alpha}\,,
    \]
where the last equality uses that $\www \in \cW_\mu$. Since $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, this implies $\BBb_i \le 1/(\alpha \iota)$. It follows that
    \[
        \epsilon_1 \alpha^2 \iota^3 \sum_{i=1}^r (\BBb_i)^2
        \le \epsilon_1 \iota r
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:r-s-bd}}{\le} \epsilon_1\,,
    \]
and the conclusion follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 9 of arXiv:2608.29416

body: In commutative algebra and algebraic geometry, localization is a formal way to introduce the "denominators" to a given ring or module. That is, it introduces a new ring/module out of an existing ring/module R, so that it consists of fractions such that the denominator s belongs to a given subset S of R. If S is the set of the non-zero elements of an integral domain, then the localization is the field of fractions: this case generalizes the construction of the field of rational numbers from the ring of integers.
title: Localization (commutative algebra)

    $$I_J(f) \coloneqq \int_{\Delta^k(t)} f(t_1,\dots,t_k)\prod_{j=1}^k \tilde z_{J_j}(t_j)\,dt_k\cdots dt_1 \,,$$
    and we also overload this notation to apply to $\mathbb{R}^n$-valued $f$.
    When $k = 0$ this should be interpreted as $I_0(f) = f$, where $f$ is a constant.

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] Let \(p\ge2\).  For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let $F_i\in C^2(\R)$ satisfying that $F_i''' \geq 0$ and $|F_i(x)|\le K_i(1+|x|^p)$ for some constant $K_i$. Assume further
    $\int_0^\infty t^{p/2}\,\mu_n(\mathrm dt)<\infty$,
then, for every $\rho\in\mbox{ConsStop}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n)$ and every
$i=1,\ldots,n$,
\begin{equation}
    \E[F_i(X_{\sigma_i})]
    \ge
    \E[F_i(X_{\rho_i})].
\end{equation}
In particular,
$$
    \E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n F_i(X_{\sigma_i})\right]
    \ge
    \E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n F_i(X_{\rho_i})\right].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

If phi is convex on an interval I containing the range of an integrable random variable X with values in I, then phi(E X) <= E phi(X), where E phi(X) always exists in (-infinity, +infinity]. For concave phi the inequality reverses. Finite form: for points x_1, ..., x_n in I and NONNEGATIVE weights w_i summing to 1, phi(sum w_i x_i) <= sum w_i phi(x_i); nonnegativity is essential (signed weights summing to 1 break the inequality, e.g. phi(x) = x^2, weights 2 and -1 at points 0 and 1).

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Assume that $\domO$ is a bounded and sufficiently smooth domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$. 
Assume that $\nu$ and $\kappa$ are positive constants.  Assume that the functions $\sigma_k$ and $\bg_k$ are measurable and sufficiently regular w.r.t. the 3rd variable. Assume that $\psi: \mathbb{R}    \to \mathbb{R}$ is the Landau potential. Assume that  $(\Omega,\mathscr{F},\mathbb{P})$ is a probability space with a right-continuous filtration $\mathbb{F}=(\mathscr{F}_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ 
 such that on this probability space two i.i.d. copies of  $\ell^2$-cylindrical $\mathbb{F}$-adapted  Wiener processes are defined.
Then, there exist an $\ell^2$-cylindrical $\mathbb{F}$-adapted Wiener process $W=(w_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}}$, progressively measurable processes $\bu$, $\phi$, $p$, and a sequence $(p_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}}$, whose trajectories belong to suitable functional spaces, such that the tuple $(\bu,p,\phi,(p_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N} \setminus\{0\}})$ is a weak solution of the following problem:
\begin{equation}
\left\{\begin{aligned}
&\d \bu + [\diver(\bu \otimes \bu) - \nu \Delta \bu + \nabla p + \newK \diver(\nabla \phi \otimes \nabla \phi)]\,\d t \\
&\hspace{0.5 truecm} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}  \left[(\sigma_k(t,x) \cdot \nabla) \bu -\nabla p_k + \bg_k(t,x,u) \right]\d w_k &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO,
\\
&\diver \bu= 0 &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO,
  \\
&\d \phi + \diver(\phi \bu) \,\d t= 
\,\Delta \left(-  \Delta \phi(t) + \,\psi^\prime(\phi(t)) \right)\d t &\mbox{ in } (0,T) \times \domO.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.10486

[Proposition ei4LUE of arXiv:2605.12777, 'Mesoscopic Rates of Convergence for Complex Wishart Matrices at the Leftmost Spectrum Edge'] [log-gas]
   Suppose $a\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $X$ be an $(N+a)\times N$ matrix with i.i.d.\ complex standard Gaussian entries, then the joint distribution of the eigenvalues of $L_{a,N}:=X^*X$ has the following probability density function:
    \begin{equation}
        p_{L_{a,N},2}(x_1,x_2,...,x_N)=\frac{1}{C_{L_{a,N},2}}\prod_{1\le j< k\le N}\chi_{\{x_j\ge0\}}|x_j-x_k|^2\sum_{j=1}^N x_j^a\exp(-x_j)
    \end{equation}
    for $C_{L_{a,N},2}$ appropriate normalization constant.
    
    In addition, an $N$-dimensional nonnegative random vector $(x_1,x_2,..,x_N)$ with the joint probability density function as (equation J4LUE of the paper) is called a \textbf{Laguerre Unitary Ensemble (LUE)} with parameter $a$.
   For convention, we say the Wishart matrix $L_{a,N}$ belongs to the LUE. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition ei4LUE of arXiv:2605.12777

[Defn radial link pattern of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Given $\boldsymbol{z}=\{z_1,z_2,...,z_n\}$ on the unit circle, a radial link pattern is a homotopically equivalent class of non-intersecting curves connecting pair of boundary points (links/arcs) or connecting boundary points and the origin (rays).

The link pattern in the unit disk with one interior point is known as the standard module $W_{n,m}$ over the affine Temperley-Lieb algebra $aTL_n$. The link patterns with $n$ boundary points and $m$ links are called $(n,m)$-links, denoted by ${\rm LP}(n,m)$. 

The number of radial $(n,m)$-links is given by $|{\rm LP}(n,m)|=C_{n}^{m}$.
title: Radial link pattern

body: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.48(a) is answered in the negative: tau_1 <= tau_0 fails. Here tau_1 is Aldous and Fill's variation threshold, the first t at which the two-point distance max_{i,j} ||P_i(X_t in .) - P_j(X_t in .)||_TV is at most 1/e, and tau_0 = sum_j pi_j E_i T_j is Kemeny's constant. On the continuous-time birth-and-death chain on {0,1,2} with rate 1 toward 0 and rate eps away from it, tau_0 = 2(1+eps)/(1+eps+eps^2) < 2 while tau_1 -> 2.14619 (the root of e^{-t}(1+t) = 1/e) as eps -> 0: the pair (2,0) separates until the sum of two unit exponentials has arrived. On the path of length k the limiting ratio tau_1/tau_0 is t_k/k with t_k the Gamma(k,1) tail threshold at 1/e (1.0731, 1.0861, 1.0880 at k=4, 1.0868, ...), so sup tau_1/tau_0 lies in [1.0880, 66]. Exact 30-digit check: k=2, eps=0.1 gives tau_0 = 1.981982, tau_1 = 2.010072. At eps=0.1 the two-point distance matters: measured against the stationary law, max_i ||P_i(X_t in .) - pi||_TV, the same chain reaches 1/e at t = 1.946386, below tau_0. For eps <= 0.05 both distances give tau_1 > tau_0 (at eps=0.05, 2.079327 and 2.051467 against tau_0 = 1.995249).

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2606.17859, 'Full $\Gamma-$expansion for the level-two large deviation rate functionals of non-reversib'] Let $m\in C^2(\bb T)$ be the density of a probability measure
($m\ge 0$, $\int_{\bb T} m(x)\, dx =1$). Suppose that there exists
$c>0$ such that $m(x) \ge c$ for all $x\in\bb T$.  Let
$H\colon \bb T \to \bb R$ be given by
\begin{equation}

H(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \, \log \big( \mss a(x)\, m (x) \big)
\;+\; \frac{1}{2\epsilon} 
\frac{\<\mss b/\mss a\>}{\<1/(\mss a\,m)\> }  \,
\int_0^x \frac{1}{\mss a(y)\, m (y)} \, dy  \,-\,
\frac{1}{2\epsilon} 
\int_0^x \frac{\mss b(y)}{\mss a(y)} \, dy \;,
\end{equation}
where, recall, $\<h\> = \int_{\bb T}h(y)\,dy$. Then, $H$ belongs to
$C^2(\bb T)$ and $m$ is the unique stationary state for the diffusion
induced by the generator $\ms L_{H,\epsilon}$.
title: Lemma 6 of arXiv:2606.17859

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): Let $E_1,\dots,E_k$ be the selected witness rows in deletion order; from each witness pair choose one pivot $p_s\in E_s$. The pivots are distinct and $E_s$ contains no later pivot $p_t$ ($t>s$), so $(h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1}^k$ is triangular with nonzero diagonal. \[
        \lambda_n=n\left(\frac{n-m_n}{n}\right)^{k_n}\longrightarrow \lambda\in(0,\infty),

        b_n=n-m_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Then
\[
        E_n\Rightarrow \Poisson(\lambda).
\]
Equivalently, for every fixed integer $u\ge0$,

        \Pbb(E_n=u)\longrightarrow e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^u}{u!}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm restate of limiting profile of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $c\in\mathbb{R}$ be an absolute constant. Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(m_N)_{N\ge 1}$ and $(l_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers, such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $m_N,l_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}l_N=\infty$.
\item $n_N=m_Nl_N$ for all $N\ge 1$.
\end{enumerate}
For all $N\ge 1$, let $t_N=\frac{n_N}{2}(\log n_N-\frac 12\log l_N+c)$. Let $\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N}$ be defined as in (defi: Pnk and its convolution of the paper), and let $\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}}$ be defined as in (defi: quotient of space of the paper). Then, we have
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}})=2\Phi\left(\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1$$
when $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}m_N=\infty$, and 
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}})=2\Phi\left(\sqrt{1-\frac 1m}\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1$$
when $m_N=m\ge 2$ is fixed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm restate of limiting profile of arXiv:2604.23890

[Dfn of arXiv:2603.13873, '{Solvability of BSDEs with possibly unbounded stochastic coefficients \\ on a general weig'] A continuous function $u:\bar {G}\rightarrow{\mathbb R}^k$ is a viscosity sub-solution (super-solution) of PDE (equation PDE-1 of the paper) if for any $1\leq i\leq k$ and any function $\phi\in C^2(\bar {G};{\mathbb R})$, it holds that
$$
\begin{array}{c}
\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0))\geq 0\ (\leq 0), \ x_0\in G;\\
\max\{\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0)),
h_i(x_0)-u_i(x_0)\}\geq 0, \ x_0\in \partial G\\
(\min\{\mathcal{\bar L}\phi(x_0)+g_i(x_0,u(x_0),(\nabla\phi\sigma)(x_0)),
h_i(x_0)-u_i(x_0)\}\leq 0, \ x_0\in \partial G),
\end{array}
$$
as long as $u_i-\phi$ has a local maximum (minimum) at point $x_0\in \bar {G}$. A continuous function $u$ is a viscosity solution of PDE (equation PDE-1 of the paper) if it is both a viscosity sub-solution and a viscosity super-solution.

\item[(ii)] Let $h\in(0,1)$ be such that $\tfrac{h}{2}\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}
> (1-h)\ln 3$. Then for any $x\in H_0$
\[

\geq 1 - C\exp\big(-\tfrac{1}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{9(1-\theta)}\big)
-C'N^2 \exp\big((1-h)N\ln 3-\tfrac{hN}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}\big).
\]
\item[(iii)] 

For any $B\subset H_0$ with $|B|\geq N/2$,
we have
\[
{\mathbb P}[\xi_{KN}^B \text{ is $(1-h)$-good}]
\geq 1 - 2C'N^2 \exp\big((1-h)N\ln 3-\tfrac{hN}{2}
\ln\tfrac{1}{1-\theta}\big).
\]

Own-work draft, claim w733-T363-013 v2, proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4) have labels+1. Train both hidden/output weights of a bias-free two-layer ReLU network by continuous gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss. Exactly k>=1 live neurons have w_j=(u_j,y_j), v_j>0 and min_j y_j(0)>4 sqrt(sum_j u_j(0)^2); every remaining neuron is strictly dead on both points, with arbitrary output. These activation sets and positive live outputs persist, the loss tends to zero, and the entire normalized parameter direction converges to a vertical KKT family of normalized margin1/8. Its unit-margin representative is v_j=y_j=r_j>0, u_j=0, sum r_j^2=4, with all other parameters zero. For k<m this representative is not a local minimum of parameter norm subject to the two unit-margin constraints. For k=m only the direction/margin conclusion is asserted. Under iid hidden/output N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, any sigma>0, put p=atan(1/4)/pi and h_k=2^(-k) E[(1-Phi(4R))^k] for a chi_k radius R and standard Gaussian CDF Phi. The exact probability that exactly k neurons satisfy the collective live condition and all others are dead is binom(m,k) h_k p^(m-k). Summing k=1..m-1 gives a sufficient nonlocally-optimal bad-KKT family probability at widths2..6. The k=1 event is the source's known one-live family; multiple-live terms are an additional classified subcone here. This does not classify every initialization with the same activation labels or give the full Gaussian basin probability. No kink solution selection is used; all finite-time trajectories lie in smooth activation regions.
two given positive-labelled inputs, no biases, fully trained hidden/output weights
continuous summed exponential or logistic gradient flow
strict collective barrier with k positive-output both-active neurons and all others dead
k<m for failure of local optimality; iid isotropic Gaussian coordinates only for event probability

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9502cb1d9dbe80a3309fc0373c93056de22651850f0863f652c3e37bcd745b77","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/95/9502cb1d9dbe80a3309fc0373c93056de22651850f0863f652c3e37bcd745b77.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:32463912994d58c86c87c8ace8204ff60a90bc2309274e71c8ba0b0d2e2bd745","bundle_entry_key":"collective-positive-both-active-barrier","bundle_id":"population.relu-collective-horizontal-energy-bad-kkt-barrier","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:relu-two-point-collective-horizontal-energy-bad-kkt-barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T363: collective horizontal-energy barrier for a bad KKT family
Claim w733-T363-013 v2. Target 2; kind narrowed. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

## Statement and scope
Use x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels +1, f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j dot x), no biases, with both layers trained by gradient flow for the sum of exponential or logistic losses. Exactly k neurons have v_j>0 and w_j=(u_j,y_j) satisfying

    min_j y_j(0) > 4 sqrt(sum_j u_j(0)^2).                 (H)

Every other neuron is strictly dead on both points; its output is arbitrary. The sum in (H) is over the k live neurons. For any k>=1, these activation patterns persist, loss tends to zero, and the parameter direction converges to a vertical, margin-1/8 KKT family. When k<=m-1, the unit-margin representative is not a local minimum of squared parameter norm. The multiple-live case k>=2 extends the source's one-live-neuron sufficient event; it does NOT classify every initialization with the same activation pattern. It does not assert a full Gaussian basin probability.

## 1. Barrier and existence
While the activation sets persist let a_i=-ell'(f_i)>0, A=a1+a2, d tau/dt=A, and g=(a1-a2)/A. Set b_x=sum v_j u_j, b_y=sum v_j y_j. Then f1=b_y/4+b_x and f2=b_y/4-b_x. The derivative magnitude a(f) is strictly decreasing for both losses, so b_x*g<=0 and |g|<=1. In the tau clock:

    u_j'=v_j*g,  y_j'=v_j/4,  v_j'=u_j*g+y_j/4.

For U=sum u_j^2, U'=2 b_x*g<=0. Write M=sqrt(U(0)). As long as the sector and positive outputs persist, y_j increases, and v_j'>=y_j/4-|u_j|>=y_j(0)/4-M>0. Thus v_j stays positive, y_j>=y_j(0)>4M>=4|u_j|. A first-exit argument closes the strict invariant region: no finite-time exit is possible. Dead neurons remain constant since their ReLU values and derivatives vanish at the two data points.

The physical-time vector field grows at most linearly in parameters: all live contributions are positive, hence f_i>0 and a_i<=1. Consequently the solution exists for all physical times. The tau clock is unbounded: if tau had a finite limit, the displayed linear-coefficient system (|g|<=1) would keep parameters bounded, hence f_i bounded and A bounded away from zero, contradicting bounded tau as t tends to infinity. All these arguments take place strictly inside smooth activation regions and invoke no convention at a ReLU kink.

## 2. Direction and margin
Let s_j=v_j+y_j and d_j=v_j-y_j. Their equations are

    s_j'=s_j/4+u_j*g,  d_j'=-d_j/4+u_j*g.

Since |u_j*g|<=M, e^(-tau/4)s_j has an integrable derivative and converges to c_j. Moreover c_j>=s_j(0)-4M>0. The variation-of-constants formula gives |d_j(tau)|<=|d_j(0)|+4M, while |u_j|<=M. Thus

    e^(-tau/4) v_j -> c_j/2,  e^(-tau/4) y_j -> c_j/2,
    e^(-tau/4) u_j -> 0.

All dead parameters become zero after normalization. With N the total squared parameter norm and C=sum c_j^2>0, N/e^(tau/2)->C/2, b_y/e^(tau/2)->C/4, and b_x/e^(tau/2)->0. Therefore f_i/N->1/8 and f_i->infinity. In particular the entire parameter direction converges, not merely its margin. Its unit-margin representative has live v_j=y_j=r_j>0, u_j=0, sum r_j^2=4; dead neurons are zero. Both margins equal 1 and N=8.

## 3. KKT and strict local suboptimality
For minimizing N/2 under f_i>=1, multipliers lambda1=lambda2=2 certify KKT stationarity: at each live neuron the vertical and output derivatives of 2f1+2f2 are r_j and r_j, respectively, and the horizontal derivatives cancel. At a zero neuron the output-hidden product ReLU has derivative zero at the origin, so its first-order stationarity equation holds as well. Constraints are active and multipliers positive.

For k<=m-1 select a zero neuron and one live coefficient r>0. Put a=||x1||=sqrt(17)/4. For delta>0 small, change the selected live parameters to

    v=r, u=-delta/(2r), y=r-2delta/r.

It remains active on both points if delta<r^2/4. Its prediction changes are (-delta,0). At the zero neuron introduce w=t*x1/a and v=t, where t=sqrt(delta/a)>0. Since x1 dot x2=-15/16<0, this adds (delta,0). Both constraints therefore remain exactly equal to one. The total squared norm change is

    Delta N = (-4+2/a)*delta + (17/4)*delta^2/r^2.

Here 2/a<4 because sqrt(17)>2. For sufficiently small delta the change is strictly negative; all perturbations tend to zero with delta. This proves failure of local optimality. For k=m there is no spare zero neuron and this local argument is NOT claimed, though the margin/direction conclusions still hold.

For comparison a feasible network at this width can use x1-only and x2-only directions: two neurons w_i=s*x_i/a, v_i=s with s=1/sqrt(a). Each point has margin one and squared norm 4/a=16/sqrt(17)<8. Its normalized margin is sqrt(17)/16>1/8. This is only a witness of suboptimality; no global optimality proof is needed here.

## 4. Exact Gaussian event probability
Let all hidden and output coordinates be independent N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. Write p=atan(1/4)/pi, the hidden dead-sector probability. For a specified set of k live neurons, the probability of (H) and all positive outputs is

    h_k = 2^(-k) E[ (1-Phi(4 R))^k ],  R~chi_k,
        = 2^(-k)/(2^(k/2-1) Gamma(k/2))
          integral_0^infinity r^(k-1) exp(-r^2/2) [1-Phi(4r)]^k dr.

Indeed, after dividing by sigma the k horizontal coordinates are independent standard Gaussians; conditionally on their radius R each vertical coordinate must exceed 4R, independently; output signs contribute 2^(-k). For k>=1 this integral is strictly positive. The exact probability of exactly k barrier-live neurons and all others dead, with arbitrary placements, is

    P_{m,k} = binom(m,k) h_k p^(m-k).

These placement events, and the events for different k, are disjoint since live and dead sectors are disjoint. For widths2..6 the sufficient non-local-minimum bad-family probability is sum_{k=1}^{m-1} P_{m,k}. The k=1 term is the already known source family, since h_1=p/2. The additional terms k=2..m-1 (ten width/k pairs for m=3..6) are the new part of this slice. For widths2..6 the coefficient rows multiplying h_k p^(m-k) are respectively [2], [3,3], [4,6,4], [5,10,10,5], [6,15,20,15,6]. These are exact event masses, not certified numerical approximations to h_k and not total bad-basin probabilities. The cone condition is scale-invariant, so these formulas apply in particular to sigma=1e-6.

The most delicate step for review is closing the all-neuron barrier using U'=2 b_x*g and then passing to the normalized parameter direction.

[Corollary cor:bipartite of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$. Let $G^{(n)}$ be a sequence of bipartite graphs on $n$ vertices satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$. Let $\mathsf{x}_\mathrm{alt} = \mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}^{(n)}$ denote the alternating condition on $G^{(n)}$ as in (eq:alternatingbipartite of the paper). Then, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, the binary noisy voter model on $G^{(n)}$ with noise $\theta$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}}(\varepsilon) = \frac{1+o(1)}{\min\{4-2\theta,4\theta\}}\log n\,,
\end{equation}
where the $o(1)$-term is $ O\big(\log^{-\upalpha/2} n\big)
$ with a constant depending on $\varepsilon,\theta,\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$ (but not on $G^{(n)}$).
Furthermore, if $\mathsf{x}_0=\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}$ is any arbitrary sequence of initial conditions, we have
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty}\frac{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(\varepsilon)}{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}}(\varepsilon)} \geq 1\,,
\]
thus $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition on $G^{(n)}$. In particular, for Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}_n$ (the case $G^{(n)}=\mathbb{Z}_n$) at any inverse temperature $\beta>0$, the alternating initial condition $\mathsf{x}_{\mathrm{alt}}$ is the asymptotically fastest initial condition. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2604.24664, 'Absolute continuity of Rosenblatt measures'] Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and $f: [0, T] \to \Rbb$. The \emph{left} and \emph{right Riemann--Liouville fractional derivatives of $f$ of order $\alpha$} are defined by
	\begin{align*}
		(I^{-\alpha}_{0+} f)(x) &= \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)} \frac{\d{}}{\d{x}} \int_0^x (x-y)^{-\alpha} f(y) \d{y},
		\\
		(I^{-\alpha}_{T-} f)(x') &= \frac{1}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)} \frac{\d{}}{\d{x'}} \int_{x'}^{T} (y-x')^{-\alpha} f(y) \d{y},
	\end{align*}
	for almost all $x,x' \in [0, T]$.

[Proposition prop:chi2 of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Under the pseudo-wave map the semigroup acts by
$\psi_{\pi_t}=D^{-1}T_tD\,\psi_{\pi_0}=e^{\Lambda t(A-\mathrm{I})}\psi_{\pi_0}$ with
$A=A^{T}$, so $T_t$ is self-adjoint in $L^{2}(1/\nu)$. The stationary law maps to
the unit vector $\psi_\nu=\sqrt\nu$, and the $\chi^{2}$ divergence is the
corresponding squared distance to it,

\begin{equation}
\chi^{2}(p\,\|\,\nu)=\sum_i\frac{(p_i-\nu_i)^{2}}{\nu_i}=\|\psi_p-\psi_\nu\|^{2}.

\end{equation}

Consequently, with $\gamma$ the spectral gap of the chain,
$\chi^{2}(\pi_t\,\|\,\nu)\le e^{-2\gamma t}\,\chi^{2}(\pi_0\,\|\,\nu)$.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] There exists a constant \(C=C(\eps,\sfT,K_0)>1\) such that the following
holds for all \(0\le r\le t\le\sfT\), provided \(n\) is sufficiently
large. Fix \(x\in\mathcal F_t\) and \(u\in D_0^{(t,x)}\), and set
\[
  q_r(u):=\Re z_r(u),
  \qquad
  \eta_r(u):=\Im z_r(u),
  \qquad
  d_r(u):=\dist\bigl(q_r(u),S_r\bigr),
\]
\[
  v(u):=\Im m_0(u)=\Im m_r(z_r(u)).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
  C^{-1}\eta_*\le v(u)\le C\eta_*,
  \qquad
  C^{-1}\eta_*\le \eta_r(u)\le C\eta_*,
  \qquad
  |q_r(u)|\le C.
  
\end{equation}

[Theorem Informal; bounded-disorder coexistence of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:intro-coexistence}
For every \(p\ge3\), there is a symmetric, compactly supported law
\(\mu\) with a \(C^\infty\) density, matching the standard Gaussian moments through
order \(2p\), for which the following hold simultaneously.  Every fixed
admissible incoherent-frame regularization has expectation asymptotic to
its Gaussian counterpart, whereas for some compact interval
\(B\subset(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 >
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\]
The count on the left is unregularized and unrestricted in space.  The
same dichotomy holds in the standard symmetric-coordinate model. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Informal; bounded-disorder coexistence

[Definition def:graph_event_E_reg of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $K^{\mathcal{E}}$ be a large constant. Define $\mathcal{E}$ to be the collection of graphs $H$ on the vertex set $[n]$ which satisfy the following inequalities (where $A$ denotes the adjacency matrix of $H$):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\sum_{1\leq i\leq n} |A_{s_1i}-p|\cdots |A_{s_ki}-p|\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}p^k n, \quad \text{ which implies}\quad
    \sum_{1\leq i\leq n} |\lambda_{s_1i}\cdots \lambda_{s_ki}| \leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}} z_p^k p^k n).\]

    \item  For $k\in \{1, 2\}$, any interval $I\subseteq [n]$ and any distinct $s_1, \dots, s_k\in [n]$ we have
    \[\Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} (A_{s_1i}-p)\cdots (A_{s_ki}-p)\Big|\!\leq\! K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{p^k n\log n}, \text{ which implies } \Big|\!\sum_{i\in I} \!\!\lambda_{s_1i}\cdots \lambda_{s_ki}\Big|\!\leq \!O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p^k \sqrt{p^k n\log n}).\]

    \item  We have $\|A-pJ\|_{op}\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}\sqrt{np}$. If the $n\times n$ matrix $\Lambda$ is defined by $\Lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}$, this also implies $\|\Lambda\|_{op}\leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}}z_p\sqrt{np})$.

    \item  For any $s\in [n]$ we have \[\sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\big|(A_{si}-p)(A_{sj}-p)(A_{ij}-p)\big|\leq K^{\mathcal{E}}p^3 n^2, \text{which implies} \sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\big|\lambda_{si}\lambda_{sj}\lambda_{ij}\big|\leq O(K^{\mathcal{E}}n^2p^3z_p^3).\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:graph_event_E_reg of arXiv:2607.22480

Let psi_X be the cumulant generating function of a random variable X. The Cramer transform, in the one-sided convention used for upper-tail (Chernoff) bounds, is psi_X^*(t) = sup_{lambda >= 0} (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)). For t >= E X it equals the Fenchel-Legendre dual (convex conjugate) sup over all real lambda of (lambda * t - psi_X(lambda)), which is Cramer's rate function; for t < E X the one-sided transform is 0, while the conjugate is in general positive (for a standard normal X the conjugate is t^2/2 for every t).

Own-work draft. Status: proof (unaudited); independent review outstanding; wider literature novelty unverified. Let X be standard Gaussian in R^d, u any unit vector, teacher y=sigma(u dot X), and student f_rho(X)=integral sigma(w dot X)rho(dw) for probability rho on the unit sphere. Outer coefficients are fixed at +1; the prior and initialization are uniform on the sphere. R is E(f_rho-y)^2 with no factor 1/2, and MFLD is partial_t rho=div_S(rho grad_S(delta R/delta rho))+lambda(t)Delta_S rho. [Proposition 20 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $\varepsilon>0$, let $A, B$ be two bounded self-adjoint operators
on a separable Hilbert space, and $\Pi$ be a projection let ${\rm C}>0$. 
Define for $t\in\R$, 
\[
\mathcal U_t(A) : =  e^{it(\Pi A\Pi)} - \Pi e^{it A}\Pi  . 
\]
Suppose that the following conditions hold:
\[
1)\quad \|\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le {\rm C}\, ,
\qquad
2)\quad \|[A,B]\| \le \varepsilon\, ,
\qquad
3)\quad
\| \Pi(A-B) (1-\Pi) \|_{\rm tr} \le \varepsilon \, ,
\]
\begin{equation} 
4)\quad \| \Pi B(1-\Pi)  (A-B) \|_{\rm tr}\leq \varepsilon\,,  \qquad  \|(A-B)\Pi B(1-\Pi)\|_{\tr} \le \varepsilon   \, .
\end{equation}
Then,  for any $t\in\R$, 
\[
\|\mathcal U_t(A)- \mathcal U_t(B)\|_{\tr}  \leq  \varepsilon |t| (1+ |t|+{\rm C}t^2 )  .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (e_1, e_2, e_3, ...) be a finite or countable orthonormal sequence in an inner product space H. Then for every x in H, the sum over n of |<x, e_n>|^2 converges and satisfies sum over n of |<x, e_n>|^2 <= ||x||^2. [Theorem thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let $G=(\Lambda,E)$ be a connected undirected graph without self-loops
  and take $l,r\in{\mathbb N}_0$ with $l\le r$.
  Let $(X,T)$ be vrjp in exchangeable time scale on the subdivided graph $G_r$ with
  starting point $\rho\in\Lambda$ and random weights $W_e>0$, $e\in E_r$, with
  respect to some probability measure with corresponding expectation ${\mathbb E}$. Its restriction
  $(X^{\Lambda_l\neq},T^{\Lambda_l\neq})$ to $\Lambda_l$
  with self-loops removed is again a mixture of vrjps on $G_l$ with random
  weights denoted by $W^{(l)}=(W_e^{(l)})_{e\in E_l}$. If the family $W=(W_e)_{e\in E_r}$ is
  independent or i.i.d., then so is the family $W^{(l)}$. Given $W$, the conditional
  law of $W^{(l)}$ can be described in terms of the restriction
  $\beta_{\Lambda_r\setminus\Lambda_l}$ of a $\nu_{\Lambda_r}^W$-distributed
  random field $\beta$. 
  For any finite subgraph $\tilde G$ of $G$ and the corresponding subdivision
  $\tilde G_l=(\tilde\Lambda_l,\tilde E_l)$, the restriction of $W^{(l)}$ to
  $\tilde E_l$ equals $W^{\tilde\Lambda_l}$ given in (equation def:W-J of the paper) with $J=\tilde\Lambda_l$
  and $I=\tilde\Lambda_r\setminus\tilde\Lambda_l$, and
  fulfills the recursion equations described in 
  Lemma (le:aux-W-l-1 of the paper), below. In particular, one has 
  \begin{align}
    
    &P_\rho^{W,\Lambda_r}((X^{\Lambda_l\neq},T^{\Lambda_l\neq})\in\cdot)=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{\Lambda_r}}
      P_\rho^{W^{(l)\neq}(\beta),\Lambda_l}((X,T)\in\cdot)\,
      \nu_{\Lambda_r}^W(d\beta).
  \end{align}
  Assume that the vertex degree of $G$ is bounded by $d$. Moreover, assume
  that the weights $W_e$, $e\in E_r$, are i.i.d.\ and satisfy
  ${\mathbb E}[W_e^\alpha]\le{c_1} 2^{\alpha(r-l)}$ for some $\alpha\in (0,\tfrac14]$
  with the 
  constant ${c_1}(d,\alpha)$ from Fact (fact:sabot-tarres-recurrence of the paper). 
  Then, the process $X^{\Lambda_l\neq}$ is a mixture of positive recurrent
  reversible Markov chains. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Vrjp on subdivided graphs

[Theorem thm:list-robustification of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $s\ge1$, put $r=b+s$ and $t=\lfloor(n+b)/r\rfloor$, and perform the same
padding and random partition. Run an ordinary learner independently on each
group and output the pointwise list of its $r$ predictions. If the base
learner has population risk at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least
$1/2$ on a clean group, then the resulting list has risk greater than
$\varepsilon$ with probability at most $2^{-s}$. Consequently, if
$d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d$, taking $s=\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil$ gives list size
$b+O(\log(1/\delta))$ using
$O((d/\varepsilon)(b+\log(1/\delta)))$ clean examples.

[Cor fixedfactor of arXiv:2607.00311, 'Thermal Concentration and Poisson--Dirichlet Edge Statistics for Random-Lattice Gibbs Ense'] Let $L_n$ be distributed according to $\mu_n$ on $\mathbb X_n$.
Let $\gamma>1$ and let $0<c<1$.
Define the primitive Gibbs mass of the $\gamma$--approximate shortest-vector window by
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L)=
\frac{
\sum_{\bm u\in L_{\operatorname{prim}}^\sharp,\ \|\bm u\|\le\gamma\lambda_1(L)}
 g_{n,c}(\tau_n(\bm u))}
{B_{n,c}(L)}.
$$
Then
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L_n)\to0
$$
in probability if $c<\gamma^{-2}$, while
$$
\Pi_{n,c}^{\lambda}(\gamma,L_n)\to1
$$
in probability if $c>\gamma^{-2}$ and $c<1$.
This probability is taken with respect to the primitive Gibbs ensemble; the shortest length 
$\lambda_1(L)$ is the usual shortest length of the full lattice, but the sampling measure is primitive.

body:
Let U ⊂ C be open and F a family of holomorphic functions on U. F is normal (in the finite sense) if every sequence in F has a subsequence converging uniformly on every compact subset of U; the limit is then automatically holomorphic, and it need not belong to F. F is normal in the extended sense if every sequence in F has a subsequence which, on each connected component of U, either converges uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function or tends to ∞ uniformly on compact subsets (equivalently, the reciprocals tend to 0 uniformly on compact subsets). For families of meromorphic functions, normality means that every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets with respect to the chordal metric of the Riemann sphere; restricted to holomorphic families this coincides with the extended sense, because a spherical limit of zero-free reciprocals is, by Hurwitz's theorem, either holomorphic or identically ∞ on each component. Normality is a local property: F is normal on U if and only if every point of U has a neighborhood on which F is normal. Normality asserts the existence of convergent subsequences only; it does not assert convergence of the family itself, and the limit function may leave the family (for instance the limit of injective functions may be constant).
U ⊂ C is open
all members of the family are holomorphic (respectively meromorphic) on the same open set U
