{"artifact_digest":"sha256:508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a3ae660870fdea8f35c824f25dc15528839b10e28ddcb8627fdccfcc527d9ad7","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c025","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c025-c026-relative-schur-and-rare-features","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and Gaussian conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:relative-schur-sampling-whitened-fourth-moment-gaussian-coupling","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C025 v1: relative Schur sampling bound via whitened fourth moments

Kind: moved (one restricted stochastic covariance step). Target: 4.
Status: proof (unaudited); novelty unverified. Standard Schur monotonicity and sample-moment identities are used, not claimed as new.

## Statement and scope
Let d=r+k with r>=0 and k>=1. Let X_1,...,X_n be iid real d-vectors, n>=1, with positive definite UNCENTERED second-moment matrix G=E[XX^T]. No zero-mean assumption is imposed. Suppose

kappa=E[(X^T G^(-1)X)^2]<infinity.

Set S=n^(-1) sum_i X_i X_i^T. Partition the first r and last k coordinates. Write B(M) for the generalized Schur complement of the first block of a PSD matrix M: if M=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], set B(M)=C-D^T A^+ D. For r=0, B(M)=M. Put B=B(G)>0.

Then, including singular empirical S,

E || B^(-1/2) B(S) B^(-1/2) - I_k ||_op^2 <= (kappa-d)/n.       (1)

There is a coupling, with the correct conditional Gaussian law N(0,B(S)) given S, to an unconditional N(0,B) vector, with expected squared Euclidean cost at most

tr(B) (kappa-d)/n.                                            (2)

After whitening both output vectors by B^(-1/2), the cost is at most k(kappa-d)/n. Thus the W2 distance between the Gaussian covariance mixture E[N(0,B(S))] and N(0,B) is at most sqrt(tr(B)(kappa-d)/n). Constants do not explicitly involve lambda_min(G); the distribution-dependent parameter kappa can nevertheless be large.

This addresses the covariance-noise part of source equation (4.9) for an iid feature block only. It does not prove that every reused-weight parent block is iid, control its deviation from the infinite-width population G, control the conditional mean error, or prevent accumulation over program lines. It is not a complete Target 1 or Target 4 theorem. Prior literature/novelty and independent review remain open.

## 1. Deterministic relative Schur stability
For a PSD block matrix M and every v in R^k,

v^T B(M) v = inf_{u in R^r} (u,v)^T M (u,v).                  (3)

This is the usual variational characterization of the generalized Schur complement. To see the singular case directly, PSD implies each column of D lies in range(A): for w in ker(A), positivity of (tw,v)^T M(tw,v) for all real t forces w^T Dv=0. Complete the quadratic square with u+A^+Dv; its infimum is v^T(C-D^TA^+D)v. In particular B is monotone for Loewner order and positively homogeneous on PSD matrices. This is standard matrix algebra, included to fix the rank-deficient convention of source equation (3.1).

Let delta=||G^(-1/2)(S-G)G^(-1/2)||_op, which is finite. Always S<=(1+delta)G. If delta<=1 then S>=(1-delta)G as well. Applying (3) gives

B(S)<=(1+delta)B;
B(S)>=(1-delta)B when delta<=1.

When delta>1, the trivial B(S)>=0 supplies the lower bound needed instead. Hence, for all delta>=0, all eigenvalues of

C_S=B^(-1/2)B(S)B^(-1/2)

lie in [max(0,1-delta),1+delta]. Therefore

||C_S-I||_op<=delta,
||sqrt(C_S)-I||_op<=delta.                                  (4)

The latter follows from |sqrt(t)-1|=|t-1|/(sqrt(t)+1)<=|t-1| for t>=0. No good-event cutoff, inverse sample Gram, or rank assumption on S is needed.

## 2. Exact sampling identity
Set Y_i=G^(-1/2)X_i, so E[Y_iY_i^T]=I_d. Define E_i=Y_iY_i^T-I_d. They are independent, mean-zero matrix-valued variables with finite second moment. Thus cross inner products have zero expectation and

E || n^(-1) sum_i E_i ||_F^2
= n^(-1) E ||YY^T-I||_F^2
= n^(-1) [E||Y||^4 - 2E||Y||^2+d]
= (kappa-d)/n.                                             (5)

This uses independence of distinct iid rows, not independence of a Gram matrix and its Schur complement. Since operator norm is at most Frobenius norm, (4)-(5) prove (1). Cauchy-Schwarz gives kappa>=d^2, so the displayed nonnegative bound is consistent even for n<d.

## 3. Conditional Gaussian coupling
Take Z~N(0,I_k) independent of the whole sample, and define

U=B^(1/2) sqrt(C_S) Z,    V=B^(1/2) Z.

Given S, U is centered Gaussian with covariance B^(1/2) C_S B^(1/2)=B(S), and V has the fixed target covariance B. The factor for U need not be the symmetric square root of B(S); it gives the correct conditional Gaussian law. Conditional expected squared distance equals

tr[B (sqrt(C_S)-I)^2] <= tr(B) delta^2,

using (4) and PSD trace monotonicity. Equation (5) proves (2). Whitening U and V yields sqrt(C_S)Z and Z, with cost <=k E delta^2. Taking infima gives the W2 conclusions. No assumption that B commutes with C_S is used.

## 4. Conditional version and dependence warning
The same proof applies conditionally on a sigma-field F if the rows are conditionally iid, G=E[XX^T|F] is positive definite almost surely, and kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2|F] is finite. With an independent fresh Gaussian Z, the conditional cost is <=tr(B)(kappa-d)/n. Its unconditional expectation is

E[tr(B)(kappa-d)]/n,

provided this is finite. It is NOT replaced by a product of expectations without an additional justification. Past-measurable mean errors can be added to U and V; the mean/noise cross term then vanishes by the centered fresh Z, not by assuming means and covariance errors are independent.

## 5. Checks, literature status, and unpaid source hypotheses
For Gaussian X~N(0,G), the usual Gaussian fourth moments give kappa=d(d+2), so (2) is tr(B)d(d+1)/n regardless of conditioning of G. This is only a simple corollary and is not claimed to improve the classical Wishart Schur-complement distribution.

The full source proof still needs a bound on whitened moments for its actual nonlinear parent-feature blocks, an appropriate conditional-iid/martingale replacement where rows are dependent, population-kernel transport, mean stability, and accumulation over lines. Merely bounding coordinate fourth moments or marginal kernel variances does not supply a bound on kappa. A separate rare-feature construction tests that missing implication.

[Theorem thm:plurality of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Assume that the adversary adds at most $b$ examples. Put $r=4b+1$ and
$t=\lfloor(n+b)/r\rfloor$. After padding to the declared final length with
correctly labeled duplicates, select $rt$ positions uniformly if necessary,
partition them randomly into $r$ groups of size $t$, run an ordinary improper
learner on every group, and output their pointwise plurality. Then
\[
    R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})
    <
    4 \, R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{iid}}(t;\mathcal{H}).
\]
Consequently, if $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d$, then
$R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})=O(d(b+1)/(n+b))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [LITERATURE CHECK 09-08 10:1x, answering his novelty question] Read Solomyak's survey directly. CONFIRMED: 2/3 is open and the survey states verbatim that the only known singular parameters are reciprocals of Pisot numbers, so this session's control-set hole is real. Salem 1944 already gives muhat -> 0 at any non-Pisot parameter, so all our work concerns the RATE. Solomyak Thm 2.7(i) gives an L^2 density for a.e. lambda in (1/2, 2^-1/2), an interval CONTAINING 2/3 - so the L^2 route is the classical route and 2/3 is simply not covered as an individual point. Garsia does not apply since 3/2 is not an algebraic integer. Transversality is the named crucial idea behind the a.e. results, so our finding that Erdos-Kahane collapses at fixed lambda because transversality fails is the expected reason, not a discovery. HONEST VERDICT: no theorem; the reformulations are the subject's standard instruments; the one plausibly novel item is the parity obstruction (any relaxation dropping parity returns the trivial bound identically), which is a negative result about a criterion we built and still needs checking against the computer-assisted-bounds literature

[Corollary cor:tailrl-binary-recovery of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Suppose $r_i\in\{0,1\}$ and let
$M:=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbbm{1}\{r_i=1\}$. If $M>0$, then every successful
rollout receives weight $1/M$ and every unsuccessful rollout receives weight
zero. Hence the uncentered TailRL{} estimator reduces to
\begin{equation}
g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
=
\frac{1}{M}
\sum_{i:r_i=1}S_i,

\end{equation}
which is the MaxRL estimator. After mean-centering, successful rollouts have
weight $1/M-1/N$ and unsuccessful rollouts have weight $-1/N$. If $M=0$,
all uncentered and centered weights are zero.

\begin{itemize}
 \item the scale $(z,r)$ is $M$-good for $h$, and
 \item the event $G$ above occurs for the (scaled and translated) field $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$.

body: Fermat's Last Theorem: There are no three positive integers a, b, c satisfying a^n + b^n = c^n for any integer exponent n > 2. (By contrast, for n = 1 and n = 2 the equation has infinitely many positive integer solutions; for n = 2 these are the Pythagorean triples, e.g. 3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2.) The statement was conjectured by Pierre de Fermat in 1637 and proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994, using a result obtained jointly with Richard Taylor, via the modularity of semistable elliptic curves.
title: Fermat's Last Theorem

body:
[Definition def:openpath of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $\lambda\in(0,\infty]$, $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ and $\mathfrak r\in\{\mathrm{u},\mathrm{i}\}$. An \emph{open
path} from $(u_0,t_0)$ to $(u_n,t_{n+1})$ consists of particles $u_0,\dots,u_n$, such that
consecutive particles are distinct, and times $t_0<t_1<\dots<t_{n+1}$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item for $1\le j\le n$ there is an active transmission mark from $u_{j-1}$ to $u_j$ at time
  $t_j$; when $\lambda=\infty$ this says that $u_{j-1}$ and $u_j$ are in contact at $t_j$;
\item for $0\le j\le n$ there is no effective recovery mark of $u_j$ in $(t_j,t_{j+1}]$.
\end{enumerate}
Its \emph{trace} is the c\`adl\`ag path $\gamma$ on $[t_0,t_{n+1}]$ given by $\gamma(t)=X_{u_j}(t)$
for $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$ and $0\le j\le n-1$, and by $\gamma(t)=X_{u_n}(t)$ for
$t\in[t_n,t_{n+1}]$. Its jumps have size at most $2r$. The path is \emph{contained} in a
space-time region $D$ if $(\gamma(t),t)\in D$ for every $t\in[t_0,t_{n+1}]$.
title: Open path

body: [Definition Pareto optimality of arXiv:2608.22945, 'A Momentum-Based Variance-Reduced Algorithm for Federated Multiobjective Optimization'] For any two solutions $x, y\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$, we say $x$ \emph{dominates} $y$ if and only if $f_s(x)\leq f_s(y), \forall s\in[S]$ and $f_s(x)<f_s(y), \exists s\in[S]$. A solution $x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ is \emph{Pareto optimal} if it is not dominated by any other solution. A solution $x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$ is \emph{weakly Pareto optimal} if there does not exist a solution $y$ such that $f_s(y)< f_s(x), \forall s\in[S]$.
title: Pareto optimality

[Corollary 33 (Phase transition for Poisson-Voronoi percolation) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Fix $\lambda>0$. Then 
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (1)}] for every $p\in [0,p_c(\lambda))$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ does not have an unbounded cluster a.s.
\item[{\rm (2)}] for every $p\in (p_c(\lambda),p_u(\lambda))$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ has infinitely many unbounded clusters a.s.
\item[{\rm (3)}] for every $p\in (p_u(\lambda),1]$, $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ has a unique unbounded clusters a.s.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Phase transition for Poisson-Voronoi percolation

[Lemma 18 (Differentiation formula for a finite-intensity Poisson process) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \((\mathsf X,\nu)\) be a finite measure space, and for \(t\ge 0\) let \(\Pi_t\) be
a Poisson point process on \(\mathsf X\) with intensity measure \(t\nu\). Then, for
every finite counting measures, the map
\(t\mapsto \Ebb[F(\Pi_t)]\) is differentiable on \((0,\infty)\), and its right
derivative at \(t=0\) is given by
\[
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ebb[F(\Pi_t)]
=
\int_{\mathsf X}\Ebb\!\left[F(\Pi_t+\delta_z)-F(\Pi_t)\right]\nu(\dd z).
\]

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9ca88b61ebe1e7f7cf0e7ac35f5189ec97863a1c1cfd824d5d340d63cffe3dd2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/9c/9ca88b61ebe1e7f7cf0e7ac35f5189ec97863a1c1cfd824d5d340d63cffe3dd2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7fe8c274286a5325c95ba2b9daa57a9addb1442faed2ef66e0c6dd06926607f3","bundle_entry_key":"2604-20514-lemma-17-differentiation-formula-for-a-","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s3_017","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-20260907/bundle_s3_017.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2604-20514-lemma-17-differentiation-formula-for-a","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: If \(\nu(\mathsf X)=0\), then \(\Pi_t\) is almost surely empty for every \(t\), and
both sides vanish identically. Thus assume \(\nu(\mathsf X)>0\).

Fix \(t\ge 0\), and let \(\Xi_h\) be an independent Poisson point process on
\(\mathsf X\) with intensity \(h\nu\), \(h>0\). Then
\[
\Pi_{t+h}\overset{d}{=}\Pi_t+\Xi_h,
\]
and therefore
\[
\Ebb[F(\Pi_{t+h})]-\Ebb[F(\Pi_t)]
=
\Ebb\!\left[F(\Pi_t+\Xi_h)-F(\Pi_t)\right].
\]
Since \(\nu(\mathsf X)<\infty\), the total number \(N_h:=\Xi_h(\mathsf X)\) is
Poisson with mean \(h\nu(\mathsf X)\). In particular,
\[
\Pbb(N_h=0)=1-h\nu(\mathsf X)+O(h^2),
\qquad
\Pbb(N_h=1)=h\nu(\mathsf X)+O(h^2),
\qquad

[Lem generator-for-SPDE of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Let $\mathcal{A} = \mathcal{M}$ or $\mathcal{A} = \mathcal{M}_+ \coloneqq \mathcal{M}_0^c$ and $f: \mathcal{A} \to \mathbb{R}$, $b: \mathcal{A} \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, and $\sigma: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{L}_2(\mathcal{U}, \mathbb{R}) \cong \mathcal{U}$ be measurable functions such that $df(r,v,z) = b(r,v,z)dt + \sigma(r,v,z) dW_t$ holds, meaning that for all $(r_0,v_0,z_0) \in \mathcal{A}$

        f(r_t,v_t,z_t) = f(r_0,v_0,z_0) + \int_0^t b(r_s,v_s,z_s)ds + \int_0^t \sigma(r_s,v_s,z_s)dW_s

    \end{enumerate}

Let (M,tau) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state tau(1)=1. Let X=(X_1,...,X_n) be an algebraically free tuple of bounded selfadjoint elements, with n a fixed positive integer. On noncommutative polynomials in X, define the free difference quotient partial_j by partial_j X_i=delta_ij*(1 tensor 1) and the Leibniz rule, with the usual bimodule action on the tensor product. The conjugate variable J_j belongs to the L2(tau) closure of the polynomial algebra and, if it exists, satisfies tau(J_j P(X))=(tau tensor tau)(partial_j P(X)) for every polynomial P. Equivalently J_j is the adjoint of partial_j applied to 1 tensor 1. Define Phi_star(X)=sum_{j=1}^n ||J_j||_2^2 when all conjugate variables exist, and Phi_star(X)=+infinity otherwise. This is conjugate-variable, non-microstates free Fisher information relative to the scalar algebra C. It is not the Fisher information of a classical parametric likelihood.
Normalized faithful normal tracial state on a finite von Neumann algebra.
Fixed finite algebraically free bounded selfadjoint tuple, so the difference quotients on its polynomial algebra are well-defined.
Conjugate variables, when present, lie in the L2 closure of that polynomial algebra.

Every separable real Banach space X is isometrically isomorphic to a closed linear subspace of C[0, 1], the space of continuous real functions on [0, 1] with the supremum norm. (The complex version holds with complex-valued C[0,1].) Consequently C[0,1] is universal for the class of separable Banach spaces up to isometry, and every separable metric space embeds isometrically into C[0,1] as well (Banach-Mazur, via the Kuratowski embedding x -> d(x, .) - d(x_0, .)). In contrast, no separable Banach space is isomorphically universal for the class of separable REFLEXIVE spaces with a separable dual of the same kind (Szlenk), and the universality fails in an essential way for spaces of continuous functions on countable compacta (Bessaga-Pelczynski, Milutin: C(K) for uncountable metrizable compact K is isomorphic to C[0,1], while C(K) for countable K is not).
X separable (the separability is essential: a non-separable space cannot embed into the separable space C[0,1])
real scalars in the statement; the complex case is identical with complex-valued functions

[Proposition BBSTAB of arXiv:2411.04590, 'Singular stochastic delay equations driven by fractional Brownian motion: Dynamics, longti'] Assume that \( A \) and \( \pi \) satisfy the same conditions as in Lemma (PII of the paper), and let \( G \in {L}(\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n, {L}(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^n)) \). Consider the following linear stochastic differential equation:
			\[
			\begin{aligned}
				\mathrm{d}y_t &= A\left( y_t, \int_{-r}^{0} y_{\theta+t} \, \pi(\mathrm{d}\theta) \right) \mathrm{d}t + \epsilon G(y_t, y_{t-r}) \, \mathrm{d}B_t(\omega), \\
				y_{\theta} &= \xi_{\theta} \quad \text{for} \quad \theta \in [-r, 0], \quad \xi \in C([-r, 0], \mathbb{R}^n),
			\end{aligned}
			\]
			where \( y^{\xi, \epsilon}_t \) denotes the solution. Let \( \lambda_1 \) be as defined in (equation TRFVV of the paper), and assume \( \lambda_1 < 0 \). Then, there exists \( \epsilon_0 > 0 \) such that for every \( 0 < \epsilon < \epsilon_0 \), there exists \( \lambda^\epsilon < 0 \) such that for any \( \xi \in C([-r, 0], \mathbb{R}^n) \), the following holds:
			\[
			\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log | y^{\xi, \epsilon}_t(\omega) |\leq \lambda^\epsilon, \quad \text{almost surely}.
			\]
			This yields in particular a pathwise stability result on $C([-r,0],\mathbb{R}^n)$

[Definition 43 ($\mathrm{RCD}(K, \infty)$ condition) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $(X,d,\mu)$ be a Polish measure space. We say that it is an $\operatorname{RCD}(K, \infty)$-space if it satisfies the $\mathrm{CD}(K, \infty)$-condition and if its Cheeger energy is quadratic, i.e., for all $f,g\in L^2(X,\mu)$ such that $0<\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(f)\operatorname{Ch}_\mu(g)<\infty$, one has
\[

[Thm 41 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] For any real numbers $q_0>0, \delta > 0$, there exist constants $r = r(q_0) \in (0, 1)$ and $\mC = \mC(q_0, \delta) > 1$ such that the following holds. 
 Define
  \[
     i_{max}=\left\lfloor\frac 9{10}\frac{\log N}{\log(1/(1-r))}\right\rfloor
    \] and
  the sequence
\[
  N_i=\lfloor N (1-r)^i\rfloor,\quad 0\le i\le i_{max}\] that
decreases from $N_0=N$ to $N_{i_{max}}\asymp N^{1/10}$. Define also
the sequence \[
\epsilon_i=10^{-i}N^{-100},\quad 0\le i\le i_{max}
.\]
 For every $i\le i_{max}-1$, we have
   \begin{flalign}
     \tmix^{N_i}(\epsilon_i) \le \mC{N_i}^{2+\delta} + t_{\rm mix}^{N_{i+1}}(\epsilon_{i+1})+t^{\mq_0,N_i}_{\rm mix}\left(\frac   {\epsilon_i}4\right).
   \end{flalign} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $k, n\in \mathbb{N}$, $n\ge k$, let $\nu_{k,n}$ be the normalized Haar measure on the Grassmannian
$Gr(k,n)$ of all $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb R^n$. Then there
exists a constant $C(k,n)>0$ such that, for every $k\times n$ matrix $J$,
one has
\[
\int_{Gr(k,n)}(\det J^H)^2\,\nu_{k,n}(dH)
=
C(k,n)\det(JJ^*),
\]
where $J^H:=JU_H$ and $U_H$ is the $n\times k$ matrix whose columns form an

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.16733, 'Concentration Inequalities for Sample Cross-Covariances'] Let \((X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered random vector
\((X,Y)\in\mathbb R^{d_X+d_Y}\). Assume that \(X\) and \(Y\) are
sub-Gaussian random vectors with covariance matrices \(\Sigma_X\) and
\(\Sigma_Y\), and sub-Gaussian constants \(K_X,K_Y\). Set
\[
r_{X}:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_X)}{\|\Sigma_X\|},
\qquad
r_{Y}:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_Y)}{\|\Sigma_Y\|}.
\]
For every \(u\ge 1\), it holds with probability at least \(1-\exp(-u)\) that
\[
\bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y_i^{\top}-\E X Y^{\top}\bigg\| \lesssim K_{X}K_{Y}(\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}+u}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{(r_{X}+u)(r_{Y}+u)}}{N}\bigg).
\]
As a corollary,
 \begin{align*}
\E \bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y^{\top}_i-\E X Y^{\top}\bigg\| \lesssim K_{X}K_{Y} (\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{r_{X}r_{Y}}}{N}\bigg).
 \end{align*}
Moreover, if $(X,Y)$ is jointly Gaussian, then
\begin{align*}
\E \bigg\|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i Y^{\top}_i-\E XY^{\top}\bigg\| \asymp (\|\Sigma_{X}\|\|\Sigma_Y\|)^{1/2} \bigg(\sqrt{\frac{r_{X}+r_{Y}}{N}}+ \frac{\sqrt{r_{X}r_{Y}}}{N}\bigg).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.16733

[Corollary 33 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $0<t\le\sigma<2$ and $p\in(1,\infty)$. For
    $T\in\Lambda^{t-\sigma,p}(\R^n)$ with
    $T\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}$, define
    \[
      \big\langle(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}T,\,w\big\rangle
      :=\big\langle T,\,(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}w\big\rangle,
      \qquad w\in\Lambda^{\sigma,p'}(\R^n),
    \]
    the right-hand side being unambiguous because
    $(-\triangle)^{\frac{t}{2}}w$ is defined modulo
    $\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}$ (Proposition~\ref{scale_isom} with
    $(s,p)$ replaced by $(\sigma,p')$) and $T$ annihilates this space.
    Then
    \[
      (-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}:\
      \Lambda^{t-\sigma,p}(\R^n)\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-t-n/p']}
      \longrightarrow
      \Lambda^{-\sigma,p}(\R^n)\perp\mathcal P_{[\sigma-n/p']}
    \]
    is an isomorphism, reducing to Theorem~\ref{dual_isom} when $t=\sigma$,
    and
    \begin{equation}
      (-\triangle)^{\tfrac{t}{2}}\circ(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{\sigma-t}{2}}
      =(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{\sigma}{2}}
      \qquad\text{on }L^p(\R^n),
    \end{equation}
    where $(-\triangle)^{\frac{\sigma-t}{2}}$ and
    $(-\triangle)^{\frac{\sigma}{2}}$ are the operators of

body:
[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2604.07207, 'Mixing times of step-reinforced random walks'] Assume that $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $L \geq 120$. There exist positive constants $C_1=C_1(\alpha)$, $C_2=C_2(\alpha)$ and $H_0=H_0(\alpha)$ such that if $n\geq H_0 L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}$, then for any $k= 1,2,\dots, \lfloor L/40 \rfloor$, one has
$$
\PP\left(  \left|\left\{1\leq j \leq n: \frac{L}{96k} \leq |\CalC_{j,n}|<\frac{L}{2k}\right\}\right| \leq \frac{  C_2 k^{\frac{1}{\alpha}} n}{L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}} \right)  \leq 7\exp\left(- \frac{ C_1  k^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}n}{L^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}}\right).
$$
In the case $\alpha=1/2$, if $L/\sqrt{\log L} \geq 120$, then for any $n\geq  H_0 L^{2}/\log L$ and any integer $k \in [\sqrt{\log L}, \lfloor L/40 \rfloor]$, one has,  
$$
\PP\left(  \left|\left\{1\leq j \leq n: \frac{L}{96k} \leq |\CalC_{j,n}|<\frac{L}{k}\right\}\right| \leq \frac{  C_2 k^{2} n}{4 L^{2}} \right)  \leq 7\exp\left(- \frac{ C_1  k^{2}n}{4 L^{2}}\right).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 15 of arXiv:2604.07207

[Proposition prop:mode of arXiv:2607.19844, 'Binomial probabilities at a fixed distance from the mode:\\ size-biasing and the complete '] The upper mode of $\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)$ is
	\[
		\lfloor(N+1)p\rfloor=\nu+\lfloor p-h\rfloor

	\]

[Definition 12 (Quantum triangles with  {possibly} thin vertices) of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Fix $W_1, W_2, W_3>0$. Let $I:=\{i\in\{1,2,3\}:W_i<\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\}$. Let $\tilde W_i = W_i$ if $i \not \in I$ and $\tilde W_i = \gamma^2 - W_i$ if $i \in I$. Sample $(S_0, (S_i)_{i \in I})$ from 
 \[\QT(\tilde W_1, \tilde W_2, \tilde W_3) \times \prod_{i\in I } (1-\frac{2W_i}{\gamma^2}) \Md_2(W_i).  \]
 Embed $S_0$ as $(\tilde D, \phi, \tilde a_1, \tilde a_2, \tilde a_3)$, for each $i \not \in I$ let $a_i = \tilde a_i$, and for each $i \in I$ embed $S_i$ as $(\tilde D_i, \phi, \tilde a_i, a_i)$ in such a way that the $\tilde D_i$ are disjoint and $\tilde D_i \cap \tilde D = \tilde a_i$. Let $D = \tilde D \cup \bigcup_{i \in I} \tilde D_i$ and let $\QT(W_1, W_2, W_3)$ be the law of $(D, \phi, a_1, a_2, a_3)/{\sim_\gamma}$.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try a direct cluster-expansion (Mayer-type) argument for the susceptibility at fixed p (2d) in the d -> infinity limit. Result: At p = lambda/(2d) the expected cluster size chi(p) has, for fixed lambda < 1, a convergent expansion as d -> infinity in powers of 1/d obtained by comparing the cluster to a branching process with Poisson(lambda) offspring and counting cycles: the first correction is the non-backtracking one: an exploration with s - 1 = 2d - 1 new neighbours per vertex has critical point 1/(s-1) = s^-1 + s^-2 + s^-3 + ..., which already gives a_1 = a_2 = 1 with s = 2d; the cycles of Z^d first change the expansion at order s^-3, where the 4-cycles move the coefficient from 1 to the known 7/2. This direct route reproduces a_1, a_2 by hand; a_3 = 7/2 is the first coefficient the cycles change, and getting it requires the 4-cycle corrections together with the self-avoidance of the exploration; I did not complete it. Existence of the expansion to all orders without the lace expansion would need a general theorem that the non-backtracking cycle corrections form an asymptotic series, which is a version of the lace expansion in disguise (the lace expansion IS the systematic bookkeeping of these corrections); a Mayer-type expansion at fixed lambda < 1 converges for the subcritical susceptibility, and p_c is then the divergence point of the series in lambda, whose location in powers of 1/d is obtained by inverting the series, which is a purely algebraic step if the expansion of chi is known to all orders with uniform error terms. So: an alternative derivation exists in principle via the convergent subcritical cluster expansion plus inversion, but the uniformity of the subcritical expansion up to lambda near 1 is exactly the difficult point. Computing a_4 by hand would require the next order of cycle corrections; not done. Obstruction: Uniformity of the subcritical cluster expansion up to the critical point; a_4 requires third-order cycle corrections.

[Lemma lem:hill-scc of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Under the conditions stated previously, if $i \in \overline{Z}$, then $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, so that $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$ has one terminal SCC, which must include $u$.

\proof If $i = u$, then, by definition, $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$. If $i \not= u$, then $i \leadsto_G z$ for some $z \in Z$. By Definition~(def:hill of the paper).2 and 3, the last edge on any path from $i$ to $z$ in $G$ is rerouted to $u$ in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$, so that $i \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$, as claimed. The final assertion follows in consequence. \hfill \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem AnalyticStraightLine of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:\left[0,K\right]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$
be a continuous BV path with unit speed parametrisation. Let $s$ be a point at which
$\gamma$ is differentiable. Let $T\in(s,K]$ be chosen such that \[
\big|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}-\gamma'_{s}(t-s)\big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}(t-s),\ \Big|\Big|\frac{\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}}{t-s}\Big|-1\Big|\leqslant\frac{1}{6}
\]for all $t\in(s,T]$ and
\[
\left|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}\right|<\left|\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{s}\right|
\]for all $t\in(s,T)$. Suppose that $\log S\left(\gamma\right)$ has infinite R.O.C. on
the interval $\left[s,T\right]$. Then the following two statements hold true.

[Theorem theorem1 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{all} the new observed coupons. Let $T_{N,d}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=\binom{N}{d} \sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(-1\right)^{k+1}\binom{N}{k}\Bigg(\binom{N}{d}-\binom{N-k}{d}\Bigg)^{-1}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Express the escape probability through the branching-process representation for the one-cookie deterministic case. Result: In the deterministic environment with one cookie of strength p at each site (M = 1, delta = 2p - 1... transient iff delta > 1 which needs more than one cookie; take M = 2 cookies of strength p each, delta = 2(2p - 1) > 1 iff p > 3/4). The event of never returning to 0 after the first step: the walk must never come back, which in the branching-process picture (right excursions counted by the number of down-crossings of each edge) means the branching process with migration started from the edge (0,1) never produces a down-crossing of (0,1) into 0... the escape probability equals the probability that the total number of down-crossings of the edge (0,1) is zero, which is P(the branching process with migration started at 1 individual at level 1 has zero descendants at level 0) - not directly a standard extinction probability but a hitting probability of the time-reversed process. For the source's example [Zer05, Th. 18] the closed form exists; for general bounded stacks the escape probability is the solution of a finite-dimensional fixed-point equation obtained by conditioning on the first cookie stack at sites 1, 2, ...: define q_k = P(never return to 0 | walk currently at k, all cookies at sites >= k intact, cookies at sites < k in their post-visit states); the states of the sites already visited matter only through the remaining cookie counts, which for M bounded is a finite vector, and the walk's returns to 0 require descending through all visited sites; the escape probability then equals the probability of survival of a Markov chain on finite cookie-count vectors, computable numerically for given (M, p) but with no closed form in general. Recorded: reduction to a finite-state escape problem; closed form only in special cases. Obstruction: No closed form beyond special cases; the reduction gives a numerical procedure only.

[campaign status: unreviewed - author-checked against the source's exact wording; verification unreviewed] For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator the ITINERARY of a trajectory is the sequence of fixed-point neighbourhoods it visits; Rozikov (2009, p. 4) asks whether some trajectory has a periodic itinerary. CLAIM, in two halves. (i) YES at m = 3, by an example already in the literature: for the cyclic Volterra operator with a = b = c = 1, matrix A = [[0,1,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,-1,0]], whose leading 2x2 minor is 1 so the operator is transversal and whose fixed-point set - the three vertices and the centre - is finite, the itinerary of every non-fixed interior point is periodic, 1 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> ..., with sojourns 12, 51, 1073, ... growing geometrically by the heteroclinic-cycle mechanism of Ganikhodzhaev and Zanin (2004). (ii) NO in general: at m = 4, Ganikhodjaev and Zanin (arXiv:1205.3841, Theorem 5) show the trajectory moves along the routes 1-4-3-2-1, 1-4-2-1 or 1-4-3-1, and a simulated cyclic-type m = 4 map produces the MIXED itinerary 1,4,3,2,1,4,2,1 - so itineraries need not be periodic. THE SHARP OPEN QUESTION, which is what the source presumably meant: is every itinerary eventually periodic, or which matrices A force it? The 2012 route analysis is the starting point. A periodic ITINERARY is a symbol sequence, not a periodic ORBIT: periodic orbits are typically absent while periodic itineraries need not be.
transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator with a finite fixed-point set

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $a, \eta>0$, $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and $d\ge2$. There exists
a constant $C:=C(a,\eta,k,d)>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every
log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, and every polynomial mapping
$
f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)
$
satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\mu}(f_j)\ge a
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \eta,
\]
one has
\[
\mu(f\in A)
\le
C\bigl(\lambda_k(A)\bigr)^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+1}}
\]
for every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb R^k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 89 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$ and $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$ as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip} and \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym}, and the symmetrization operation $\sym$ as defined by \eqref{e:symmetrize.set.of.measures}, we have \[\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha) = \sym(\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha))\,.\]
Similarly, for $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)$ and $\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)$ as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.sym} and \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}, we have
	\[\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)
	=\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))\,.\]

\begin{proof}
   By the definitions of these sets, we have
    \[
        \sym(\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha))
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip}}{=} 
        \sym\bigg(
            \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0}
            \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)
        \bigg)
        \subseteq 
        \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \sym\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)\Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym}}{=} \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)\,.
    \]
Similarly, we have
	\begin{align*}
	&\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}}{=}\sym\bigg(
	\bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L > 0} \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\bigg)\\
	&\qquad\subseteq
	\bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L > 0} \sym\Big(\cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\Big)
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.sym}}{=}
	\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.
	\end{align*}
Therefore it suffices to show the reverse inclusions.

    Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$ and a sequence $\epsilon_n\downarrow0$.
    By the definition \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym} of $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$, for any $\epsilon_n$ there exists $L_n$ and a sequence of $L_n$-Lipschitz algorithms $\cA_{n,j}$ (acting in $N_j$ dimensions) such that

            \sym(\mu(\cA_{n,j})),\mu

        \bigg\} \le \epsilon_n\,.
    \]
This implies the existence of $\tilde{\mu}_{n,j} \in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$ such that
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_{n,j},\tilde{\mu}_{n,j})
	=\max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(
            \mu(\cA_{n,j}),
            \tilde{\mu}_{n,j}
            \Big),
       \bbW_2\Big(\mu^\Ising(\cA_{n,j}),\cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon_n\,.
	\]
    In light of Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.sym.preimage.compact}, by passing to a subsequence of the $j's$, we can ensure that
 $\tilde{\mu}_{n,j}$ converges in $\bbW_2$ to some $\tilde\mu^n \in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$ as $j\to\infty$.
    Then
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{n,j}),
        	\tilde{\mu}_n\Big) \le \epsilon_n + \bbW_2\Big(\tilde{\mu}_{n,j},\tilde{\mu}_n\Big) \le 2\epsilon_n\,,
    \]
    where the last inequality holds after omitting finitely many $j$'s.
    By passing to a subsequence of the $\epsilon_n$ we can ensure that as $n\to\infty$, $\tilde\mu^n$ converges in $\bbW_2$ to $\tilde\mu \in \sym^{-1}(\mu)$.
    Then
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{n,j}),\tilde \mu\Big) \le \tilde\epsilon_n \equiv 2\epsilon_n + \bbW_2(\tilde{\mu}_n, \tilde\mu)\,.
    \]
Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip} of $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$, it follows that
    \[
        \tilde\mu 
        \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L_n,\tilde\epsilon_n) 
        \subseteq \bigcup_{L>0} \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\tilde\epsilon_n)\,.

    This shows $\mu \in \sym(\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha))$, and thus $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha) \subseteq \sym(\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha))$. This proves the first assertion of the lemma.

[Proposition eq:sparse-profile-net-bound of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:sharp-profile-energy}
Suppose that the random field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\).
Put
\[
 \pi_N(a):=
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1)}
 \mathbb P\{\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a\}.
\]
Put
\[
 \mathcal S_{N,k}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
       \abs{\operatorname{supp}x}\le k\},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_p=\frac{p^{p+1}}{p!}.
\]
For \(1\le k\le N\), \(a>0\), and
\(0<\delta<\Lambda_p^{-1}\),
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert\ge a
 \right\}\notag\\
 &\qquad\le
 \binom Nk\left(1+\frac2\delta\right)^k
 \pi_N\bigl((1-\Lambda_p\delta)a\bigr).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, if \(1\le k_N\le N\), \(k_N=o(N)\), and
\(a_N\to a>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb P\left\{
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal S_{N,k_N}}\left\lverth_N^J(x)\right\rvert
 \ge a_N\right\}
 \le-\frac{a^2}{2}.
\end{equation}
The same conclusions hold for the standard symmetric-coordinate model
whenever its field satisfies \(({\rm PT})_p\); the profile MGF and
orbit-coordinate joint bounds described above are sufficient.

[Thm 16 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For $\calX_n=(X_n,d^{X_n},\rho_{X_n},\mu_{X_n}),\;\calX=(X,d^X,\rho_X,\mu_X)\in\frK_{\bullet}(\tau)$,
the following conditions are equivalent to each other.
\begin{itemize}
  \item [$\mathrm{(i)}$]There exist a compact metric space $(M,d^M,\rho_M)$ and root-preserving isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Hausdorff topology, and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ weakly.  
  \item [$\mathrm{(ii)}$]There exist a compact metric space $(M,d^M)$ and isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Hausdorff topology, $f_n(\rho_{X_n})\to f(\rho_X)$ in $M$,
  and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ weakly.
  \item [$\mathrm{(iii)}$]$d^{\tau,\BL^{\kappa}}_{\frK_{\bullet}}(\calX_n,\calX)\to 0$
\end{itemize}
In particular, $d^{\tau,\BL^{\kappa}}_{\frK_{\bullet}}$ induces the rooted compact Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov topology.

STATUS: proof (unaudited), own-work draft. Exact normal linear-stability classification of every finite fixed point of joint-head factored-attention GD at every eta>0: the stationary curve v=0,kq=p_bar has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers 1-eta lambda_+/- with lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2(k^2+q^2)))/2. One normal direction is always repelling; the other attracts exactly when k^2+q^2<(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2, is neutral at equality, and repels beyond. Every positive fixed step loses the attracting normal direction at sufficiently unbalanced factorizations.

# Target 1: exact normal stability of the factored GD stationary curve

Version 1, proof unaudited. This is a linearized stability classification;
it does not claim a nonlinear flip bifurcation or a full-space GD basin theorem.

Assume precisely the n-example factored model of claim 010:
0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0, logistic average loss of
v h_i(kq), h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), and simultaneous Euclidean GD
with any fixed eta>0. Let p_bar<0 be the unique mean root and define

 A=mean_i h_i(p_bar)^2/4>=0,
 B=mean_i h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

All finite stationary points, equivalently all GD fixed points, form the
curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar}. At such a point write S=k^2+q^2>=2|p_bar|.
The GD Jacobian has tangent multiplier 1 and normal multipliers

 mu_-=1-eta lambda_-, mu_+=1-eta lambda_+,
 lambda_+/-=(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2 S))/2.

Here lambda_-<0<lambda_+, hence mu_->1 everywhere: no point of E is
linearly attracting in all normal directions. The other normal direction is

* strictly attracting in the linearization when eta lambda_+<2;
* neutral with multiplier -1 when eta lambda_+=2;
* strictly repelling with multiplier less than -1 when eta lambda_+>2.

Let
 J_eta=(4/eta^2-2A/eta)/B^2.

The first case is EXACTLY S<J_eta, the middle case exactly S=J_eta,
and the last exactly S>J_eta. Equivalently, with C=k^2-q^2,
S=sqrt(C^2+4p_bar^2): there is an attracting normal direction only if
J_eta>2|p_bar|, and then precisely at

 |C|<sqrt(J_eta^2-4p_bar^2).

Equality gives neutral normal points when J_eta>=2|p_bar|. If J_eta
is smaller than 2|p_bar|, every point is repelling in both normal directions.
In particular, for EVERY eta>0, sufficiently unbalanced factorizations on
E are normally repelling in both directions. There is no positive constant
step that preserves the flow's one attracting normal direction uniformly
along the entire stationary curve. This does NOT imply an open basin of
cycles or disprove a full-space almost-everywhere GD endpoint theorem.

## Proof

The fixed-point condition is gradient L=0, classified in proof 008.
Its loss Hessian at E is
 [[A,-Bq,-Bk],[-Bq,0,0],[-Bk,0,0]].
The tangent vector (0,k,-q) is in its kernel. In the orthonormal basis
e_v=(1,0,0), e_s=(0,q,k)/sqrt(S) of the normal plane, the Hessian is
 [[A,-B sqrt(S)],[-B sqrt(S),0]].
The quadratic characteristic polynomial is lambda^2-A lambda-B^2 S,
which yields lambda_+/- and their signs. The GD Jacobian is I-eta Hessian,
proving the multipliers and their linear classifications.

For equivalence with J_eta, consider the polynomial
f(z)=z^2-Az-B^2 S, whose positive zero is lambda_+ and negative zero
lambda_-. Since 2/eta>0, lambda_+<2/eta is equivalent to
f(2/eta)>0, or S<J_eta; equality and the reverse inequality follow likewise.
This avoids squaring a potentially negative expression 4/eta-A.
Finally S^2=C^2+4p_bar^2 by algebra, and S is unbounded along E by
taking k->infinity, q=p_bar/k. All asserted threshold statements follow.

## Scope of the obstruction

The obstruction is to a PARTICULAR transfer from flow to GD: retaining
one attracting normal direction uniformly on every imbalance leaf at fixed
step. It is not an obstruction to every possible discrete-time proof.
The imbalance leaves themselves are not invariant under GD:
C_+=(1-eta^2 v^2 G^2)C. Both facts must be accounted for in further work.
Normal multipliers on the unit circle require separate nonlinear analysis;
no attracting two-cycle is claimed. Scalar genuine self-attention embeddings
of this family are supplied in claim 008.
Coupled n>=2 scalar h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), 0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0; logistic average loss; simultaneous Euclidean GD. A=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2, mean h_i(p_bar)=0. Linear normal stability only.

[Lemm 8 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (closeness in $d_{BL}$ implies closeness of mixed moments, bounded case)
Let $X_1,...X_4,X_1',...,X_4'$ be random variables such that
\[
d_{BL}\big( (X_1,...,X_4),\ (X_1',...,X_4') \big) \leq \alpha,
\]
where $\alpha \geq 0$. 
Assume that there exists $L \in [1,\infty)$ such that $|X_i|,|X_i'|\leq L$ for all $i=1,...4$. Then for all non-negative integers $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ with $q=p_1+p_2+p_3+p_4 > 0$ it is the case that
\[
| \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i^{p_i} - \E \Pi_{i=1}^4 X_i'^{p_i}| \leq 2q L^q \alpha.
\]

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: the Hoelder exponent satisfies 0 < alpha < 1 strictly, and the Lebesgue exponent satisfies 1 < p < infinity strictly. The reason is that the second derivatives of the Newtonian potential are given by a singular integral operator, which is bounded on C^{0,alpha} and on L^p only in the open ranges. Failure at alpha = 0 (continuous right-hand side does not give a C^2 solution): in the plane put u(x) = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) (log(1/r))^{1/2} for 0 < r = |x| < 1/2, u(0) = 0. A computation with u = p g, p = r^2 cos(2 theta) harmonic and g = (log(1/r))^{1/2}, using Laplacian(p g) = 4 p g'/r + p (g'' + g'/r), gives Laplacian u = -cos(2 theta) ( 2 (log(1/r))^{-1/2} + (1/4)(log(1/r))^{-3/2} ), which extends continuously by 0 at the origin, while D_{11}u = 2(log(1/r))^{1/2} + o(1) blows up. Since u is C^1 and C^infinity off the origin, it solves Laplacian u = f distributionally on the ball with f continuous; no C^2 solution of Laplacian v = f exists near 0, because v - u would be harmonic hence smooth. (Consistently, this f is continuous but not Dini continuous, and Dini continuity is the correct substitute hypothesis.) Failure at alpha = 1: with q = x_1^3 - 3 x_1 x_2^2 and g = log(1/r), the function u = q g has Laplacian u = -6 q/r^2 = -6 r cos(3 theta), which is Lipschitz, while D_{111}u = 6 log(1/r) + O(1) is unbounded, so u is not in C^{2,1}. Failure at p = infinity: u = (x_1^2 - x_2^2) log(1/r) has Laplacian u = -4 cos(2 theta) in L^infinity while D_{11}u = 2 log(1/r) + O(1) is not bounded, so Laplacian u in L^infinity does not give u in W^{2,infinity} = C^{1,1}; the correct endpoint statement is Laplacian u in L^infinity implies D^2 u in BMO. Failure at p = 1: let f_k = rho_{1/k} be standard mollifiers and u_k = Gamma convolved with f_k, so Laplacian u_k = f_k with ||f_k||_{L^1} = 1 and ||u_k||_{L^1(B_2)} bounded; on B_1 minus the origin D_{12}u_k converges pointwise to D_{12}Gamma, whose size is comparable to |x|^{-n} and hence not integrable near 0, so by Fatou ||D^2 u_k||_{L^1(B_1)} tends to infinity. No estimate of the form ||D^2u||_{L^1} <= C(||Laplacian u||_{L^1} + ||u||_{L^1}) can hold; the correct endpoint statements are weak-L^1 bounds and the Hardy space result Laplacian u in H^1 implies D^2u in L^1. Practical consequence: from f merely continuous (or bounded) one gets u in W^{2,p}_loc for every finite p and u in C^{1,alpha}_loc for every alpha < 1, but not, in general, u in C^2 - the first example above is exactly the obstruction (for particular right-hand sides, a smooth f say, the solution is of course C^2).
title: Pitfall: Schauder and Calderon-Zygmund Estimates Fail at the Endpoints (C^0, L^1, L^infinity)

For n servers, Poisson jobs of rate lambda*n/k routing to uniform k-subsets, and k tagged arrival streams observed exactly on [0,T], let H count tagged servers hit per job and beta=(lambda*n/k)*P(H>=2). Their joint path total variation from independent rate-lambda Poisson streams is at least 1-exp(-beta*T). If k tends to infinity with k=o(sqrt(n)), beta~lambda*k^3/(2*n). At k/n^(1/3)->c>0, the liminf is at least 1-exp(-lambda*T*c^3/2). Conversely k=o(n^(1/3)) gives path TV tending to zero by the delete-and-restore coupling. This proves a path-coupling obstruction, not a necessary threshold for a stationary queue vector at a single time.
Poisson jobs with independent uniform routing
lambda,T fixed and positive
Exact continuous arrival paths
For the asymptotic formula: k tends to infinity and k=o(sqrt(n))

abla u) = f$ in $\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$. (Stampacchia, Ann. Inst. Fourier 1965.) (I) $L^\infty$ estimate. If $f \in L^m(\Omega)$ with $m > N/2$ (so $f \in H^{-1}$ and the weak solution $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ exists and is unique), then $u \in L^\infty(\Omega)$ and $\|u\|_{L^\infty} \leq C\,\|f\|_{L^m}$ with $C = C(N, \lambda, m, |\Omega|)$. Sharp edge: the exponent is sharp - for $N \geq 3$ there are $f \in L^{N/2}(\Omega)$ (even for $A = I$) whose solution is unbounded, e.g. $u = \log|\log|x||$ near the origin, whose Laplacian lies in $L^{N/2}$ but $u 
otin L^\infty$; for $f \in L^{N/2}$ one only gets $u$ in the Orlicz class $\exp L$ (and $u \in L^q$ for all $q < \infty$). (II) $L^1$ and measure data. If $f \in L^1(\Omega)$ (or more generally $f = \mu$ is a bounded Radon measure on $\Omega$), there exists a unique DUALITY solution: a function $u \in L^1(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega u\,g\,dx = \int_\Omega w_g\,d\mu$ for every $g \in L^\infty(\Omega)$, where $w_g \in H_0^1(\Omega) \cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ is the weak solution of the adjoint problem $-\operatorname{div}(A^{T}
abla w_g) = g$ (bounded by part (I), which is all that is needed to pair with $f \in L^1$); for MEASURE data one needs $w_g$ continuous on $\overline\Omega$ so that $\int w_g\,d\mu$ makes sense - interior continuity is De Giorgi-Nash-Moser, continuity up to the boundary requires a mild regularity of $\partial\Omega$ (e.g. Lipschitz, or an exterior cone condition), which is then an extra hypothesis in the measure case. This $u$ satisfies: $u \in W_0^{1,q}(\Omega)$ for EVERY $q < N/(N-1)$ with $\|u\|_{W_0^{1,q}} \leq C(N,\lambda,\Lambda,q,\Omega)\,\|\mu\|_{\mathcal{M}}$ ($= \|f\|_{L^1}$ for $L^1$ data); $|
abla u|$ lies in the Marcinkiewicz (weak-$L$) space $M^{N/(N-1)}(\Omega)$ and, for $N \geq 3$, $u \in M^{N/(N-2)}(\Omega)$; $u$ is the strong $W_0^{1,q}$ limit of the weak solutions $u_n$ with smooth data $f_n 	o f$ in $L^1$ (or $f_n 	o \mu$ weakly-* with $\|f_n\|_1$ bounded); $u$ solves the equation in the sense of distributions, $\int A
abla u\cdot
abla\varphi = \int \varphi\,d\mu$ for $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; and $T_k(u) \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ for every $k$ with $\lambda\int|
abla T_k(u)|^2 \leq k\|\mu\|$. Sharp edges: (a) $q = N/(N-1)$ is excluded and cannot be reached - for $\mu = \delta_0$ and $A = I$ the Green function has $|
abla u| \sim |x|^{1-N}$, which is in $L^q$ near 0 iff $q < N/(N-1)$; (b) uniqueness holds among DUALITY solutions (equivalently among limits of approximations, or entropy/renormalized solutions), NOT among all distributional solutions in $W^{1,q}$, $q < N/(N-1)$: for merely measurable uniformly elliptic $A$ Serrin (1964) constructed, for any $1 < q < 2$, a nonzero $u \in W^{1,q}(B)$ on a ball $B$ with $\operatorname{div}(A
abla u) = 0$ distributionally and $u 
otin H^1_{loc}$ (a 'pathological solution'), so a distributional $W^{1,q}$ solution is not determined by its data without a selection principle such as duality, approximation, or the entropy/renormalized formulation; (c) with $L^1$ data the solution is in general NOT in $H_0^1$ (its energy is infinite), so the Lax-Milgram framework does not apply directly - the estimates are obtained on approximations via the truncation method and passed to the limit.

For $h > k$, $(h-k)|A_h|^{1/2^*} \\leq \\|G_k(u)\\|_{2^*}$, so $\\phi(h) := |A_h|$ satisfies $\\phi(h) \\leq C\\|f\\|_m^{2^*}(h-k)^{-2^*}\\phi(k)^{\\theta 2^*}$. The exponent $\\theta 2^* > 1$ exactly when $m > N/2$; Stampacchia's real-variable lemma on such recursive inequalities then forces $\\phi(d) = 0$ for a finite $d = C\\|f\\|_m|\\Omega|^{(\\theta 2^* - 1)/2^*}$, i.e. $\\|u\\|_\\infty \\leq d$. At $m = N/2$ the exponent equals 1 and the lemma gives only exponential integrability, matching the counterexample. (II) Approximate $\\mu$ by $f_n \\in C_c^\\infty$ with $\\|f_n\\|_1 \\leq \\|\\mu\\|$ and let $u_n \\in H_0^1$ be the weak solutions. Testing with $T_k(u_n)$: $\\lambda\\int|\\nabla T_k(u_n)|^2 \\leq \\int f_n T_k(u_n) \\leq k\\|\\mu\\|$. Sobolev on $T_k(u_n)$ gives $|\\{|u_n| \\geq k\\}| \\leq C k^{-N/(N-2)}$ ($N \\geq 3$), and splitting $\\{|\\nabla u_n| \\geq h\\} \\subset \\{|u_n| \\geq k\\} \\cup \\{|u_n| < k, |\\nabla u_n| \\geq h\\}$, the second set has measure $\\leq h^{-2}k\\|\\mu\\|/\\lambda$; choosing $k = h^{(N-2)/(N-1)}$ gives $|\\{|\\nabla u_n| \\geq h\\}| \\leq C h^{-N/(N-1)}$, uniformly in $n$. Hence $(u_n)$ is bounded in $W_0^{1,q}$ for each $q < N/(N-1)$ (weak-$L^{N/(N-1)}$ embeds in $L^q$ on a bounded set), so a subsequence converges weakly in $W_0^{1,q}$ and strongly in $L^1$ to some $u$; by linearity $A\\nabla u_n \\to A\\nabla u$ weakly in $L^q$ and the distributional equation passes to the limit. Duality: for $g \\in L^\\infty$ and $w_g$ the continuous adjoint solution, $\\int u_n g = \\int A\\nabla u_n\\cdot\\nabla w_g = \\int f_n w_g \\to \\int w_g\\,d\\mu$, so $u$ is a duality solution; the same identity with $\\mu = 0$ shows a duality solution of the homogeneous problem is orthogonal to $L^\\infty$, hence zero - uniqueness - and then the whole sequence converges. Strong convergence in $W_0^{1,q}$ and the entropy inequality for $T_k(u)$ follow from uniqueness plus the linear estimates applied to $u_n - u_m$.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:8c779e94860ee87f795e1934b4a0484ee72529f37aa5326b6bd8499bda726e53","revision_digest":"sha256:7bba34209aa1de121daefe005a5bb783e1eb800331b4e677d6dbdf6096168f4d","source_id":"wikipedia:Sobolev_inequality","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: Let (mu_eps) be probability measures on a topological space X satisfying a large deviation principle with good rate function I as eps -> 0+, and let phi: X -> R be bounded and continuous. Varadhan's lemma states that the limit as eps -> 0 of eps times the log of the integral over X of exp(phi(x)/eps) mu_eps(dx) equals sup_{x in X} (phi(x) - I(x)). The boundedness hypothesis on phi can be relaxed to a mild exponential tail (moment) condition. This is a Laplace-type asymptotic for LDP-obeying measures, generalizing Laplace's method for integrals. Due to S. R. S. Varadhan.
title: Varadhan's lemma

Consider binary classifiers obtained by thresholding the scalar output of feedforward ReLU networks with at most W scalar parameters, each encoded using at most B bits, where W,B are positive integers. Use the finite graph-description convention in the proof of Theorem 6.1: all edge endpoints can be indexed among U<=W named neurons, so the architecture is encoded by specifying the two endpoint indices for every parameter. No additional uncharged choice of input-coordinate names is allowed. Then the number of distinct classifiers is at most 2^{O(W B + W log(W+1))}, and their VC dimension is O(W B + W log(W+1)). For a fixed architecture the simpler bound VCdim <= W B follows. The variable-architecture term is the cost of describing the graph, not extra numerical precision.

(Decoupling lemma, Lemma 4.7) For random variables X, Y with independent copies X', Y' and any event E(X,Y): P(E(X,Y)) <= P(E(X,Y) and E(X',Y) and E(X,Y') and E(X',Y'))^{1/4}. Let z_1,...,z_n be i.i.d. with P(z_i = 0) = P(z_i = 1) = 1/2 and Q = sum_{1<=i,j<=n} c_ij z_i z_j. (Cor 4.4) If there is U with |U| >= m >= 2 such that each i in U has at least m indices j with |c_ij| >= 1, then P(Q in I) = O(m^{-1/8}) for every interval I of length 1, absolute constant. (Cor 4.5) If at least m indices i each have at least m indices j with c_ij != 0, then P(Q = 0) = O(m^{-1/8}). (Thm 1.3) A random symmetric matrix with i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) entries on and above the diagonal is singular with probability O(n^{-1/8+delta}) for every delta > 0.

Assumes: z_i i.i.d. {0,1}-valued (the paper notes extensions to other distributions, constants then depend on the law); many rows with many large (or nonzero) coefficients

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is the proved attraction-domain extension of the partial answer to Problem 3.11 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution, the distribution of a sum of freely independent self-adjoint variables with the indicated laws, and * for classical convolution of independent real variables. A law lambda is freely strongly unimodal when lambda boxplus nu is unimodal for every unimodal nu. Let lambda be a nondelta probability law on R and suppose there are b_n>0 and a_n in R such that the image of lambda^{boxplus n} under x -> x/b_n+a_n converges weakly to C_1, the Cauchy law with density 1/[pi(1+x^2)]. Here lambda^{boxplus n} is its n-fold additive free convolution. Then lambda is not freely strongly unimodal. For the proof, D_c(mu) denotes the image of mu under x -> c x; unimodal measures are preserved by positive dilations and translations and are closed under weak convergence. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The affine-scaled free convolution powers converge weakly to C_1.
Free convolution is weakly continuous, and unimodal measures are weakly closed.

body:
[Proposition 20 (Particle and mixed-stress factorization) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider a torus-adapted Navier--Stokes potential~$\chi$.
The orthogonal components of the particle-number current, and the mixed parallel-orthogonal stress-tensor components, take the following form, for some scalar functions~$\Numb_\chi,U_\chi$:
\be
\vNumb_\chi^a = \Numb_\chi(s_\perp, s_\parallel, \xi_\perp, \xi_\parallel) u^a ,
\qquad
T_\chi^{am} = \frac{1}{2} U_\chi(s_\perp, s_\parallel, \xi_\perp, \xi_\parallel) u^a u^m , \qquad
a=0,1 , \quad m=2,3 .
\ee

for $(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$: 

\medskip

\noindent \underline{\textbf{Top-order integral inequalities for $\mastercontroltop$}.}
We have the following estimates for the $L^2$-controlling quantity $\mastercontroltop(\ubar,u)$

\begin{align}
		\begin{split}

			& \ \ + (1+\varsigma_1^{-1}) \fluxcontrolVort(\ubar,u) + (1+\varsigma_1^{-1}) \bulkcontrolVort(\ubar,u) + \bulkcontrolVortVort_N(\ubar,u) +  \bulkcontrolDivGradEnt_N(\ubar,u)  \\

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Put $V_+=\sup_\Omega V$ and $V_-=\inf_\Omega V$. Then $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ is concave, $\Lambda_V^\Omega(0)\ge0$ and
\[
|\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma_1)-\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma_2)|\le\|V\|_\infty|\gamma_1-\gamma_2|,
\qquad
\Lambda_V^\Omega(\gamma)=-\gamma V_\pm+o(|\gamma|)\quad(\gamma\to\pm\infty).
\]
Assume in addition that $\Omega$ is bounded, $q\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ and $V\in C(\overline\Omega)$. Then $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ and $\Lambda_D^\Omega$ are real analytic on $\R$ and $(0,\infty)$, respectively. With $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$,
\[
(\Lambda_V^\Omega)'(\gamma)=-\int_\Omega V\phi_\gamma\phi_\gamma^*,\qquad
(\Lambda_D^\Omega)'(\alpha)=-d\int_\Omega\phi_\alpha^*(J*_\Omega\phi_\alpha-\phi_\alpha).
\]
Moreover,
\[
(\Lambda_V^\Omega)'(\gamma)=-V_\pm+o(1)\quad(\gamma\to\pm\infty),
\]
and $\Lambda_V^\Omega$ is strictly concave if $V$ is nonconstant. No sign is imposed in general on $(\Lambda_D^\Omega)'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.02416

body: [Lemma 93 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\mu$ be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-content, $C\in D_\mu$, and $V$ be a neighbourhood of $\mu(C)$ in $\mf A$. Let $A,B\in \sigma_0(D_\mu)$ be such that $C\subset A\cup B$. Then there are $A',B'\in D_\mu$ such that $A'\subset A\cap C$, $B'\subset B\cap C$, and $\mu(A') + \mu(B') \in V$.

\[
 \mathfrak{d} = \sum_{e=1}^{\mathfrak e}\big(|r_e^{\textnormal{I}}-r_e^{\textnormal{II}}\bigr| + \sum_{h=1}^H \Big( \big(|\theta^{\textnormal{I}}_{h,h}- \theta^{\textnormal{II}}_{h,h}\bigr| + \big(|\hat{a}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{I}}-\hat{a}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{II}}\bigr| + \big(|\hat{b}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{I}}-\hat{b}_{h}^{\prime\,\textnormal{II}}\bigr|\Big).
\]
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{Lemma_continuity_varyinf_ff} there exists $C>0$ (depending only on the constants in Assumptions \ref{Assumption_A_prime} and \ref{Assumption_B}) and two measures $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{I} \rightarrow \textnormal{II}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{II} \rightarrow \textnormal{I}}$, such that:
\begin{align}
&\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{I} \rightarrow \textnormal{II}}\in \mathscr{P}_\star^\textnormal{II}, \qquad \sum_{h=1}^H \int_{\hat a'_h}^{\hat b'_h}\left|\mu^{\textnormal{I} \rightarrow \textnormal{II}}_h(x)- \mu^{\textnormal{I}}_h(x)\right|\dd x < C \cdot \mathfrak{d},\\
&\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\textnormal{II} \rightarrow \textnormal{I}}\in \mathscr{P}_\star^\textnormal{I}, \qquad \sum_{h=1}^H \int_{\hat a'_h}^{\hat b'_h} \left|\mu^{\textnormal{II} \rightarrow \textnormal{I}}_h(x)- \mu^{\textnormal{II}}_h(x)\right|\dd x < C \cdot \mathfrak{d},

body: Every real (or complex) m by n matrix A factors as A = U Sigma V^T with U, V orthogonal (unitary) and Sigma diagonal with nonnegative entries sigma_1 >= sigma_2 >= ... >= 0, the singular values. The columns of U and V are left and right singular vectors; the rank equals the number of nonzero singular values, and truncating Sigma gives the best low-rank approximation in operator and Frobenius norms (Eckart-Young).

Among all Cartan geometries of type \((G,H)\) on a manifold $N$ whose Cartan connections share the same \(\mathfrak m\)-part \(\vartheta\), there exists a unique one whose Cartan connection is normal. body:
Let S be a fair all-or-none selector on three terminals a,b,c, and let T be a three-arm star whose arms are mutually independent Bernoulli(1/sqrt(2)). Every pair connection probability is 1/2 in both S and T. Add identical deterministic exterior wiring joining a to c, and ask whether b is connected to that wired pair. The crossing probability is 1/2 for S and 1-1/(2sqrt(2)) for T, differing by (2-sqrt(2))/4>0. Equal terminal-pair marginals therefore do not suffice for an exact gadget transfer in arbitrary exterior connectivity events.
Three distinct labeled terminals.
The star arms are mutually independent with probability 1/sqrt(2).
The selector is one Bernoulli(1/2) hyperedge.
Exterior wiring a~c is deterministic and crossing means b connected to a or c.

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,d)$ be a quasi-metric space and let $\mu$ be a measure on some $\sigma$-algebra on $\XX$.
    Let $s\ge 0$.
    We say that $\mu$ satisfies the \emph{small-ball condition with parameter $s$}, if there exist constants $c,r_0>0$ (depending on $s$) such that
    \begin{equation}
      \mu^\ast \bigl(\ball(x,r)\bigr)
      \leq \exp\bigl( -c \cdot (1/r)^s \bigr)
      \qquad \forall \, x\in \XX \text{ and } 0 < r < r_0
      .
      
    \end{equation}

[Proposition 47 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] There exists an isomorphism of graded $S_n$-modules:

$$H^\ast(\mathsf{gr}_1(\mathsf{FT}_\Gamma))(n)\cong \bigoplus_\lambda  \Sigma^{|\lambda|+2} p_\lambda\Phi[n,\lambda^\ast] $$
where $p_\lambda$ is non-zero only if $\lambda$ is of the form $\lambda=(a,b)$, in which case:
	$$
	p_{(a,b)} = \begin{cases}
		(a-2)/2	&	a\equiv_2 b\equiv_2 0 \text{ and } b=0\\
		(a-b)/2	&	a\equiv_2 b\equiv_2 0 \text{ and } b\neq 0 \\
		(a-b)/2+1	&	a\equiv_2 b \equiv_2 1 \\
		0	&	a \not\equiv_2 b
	\end{cases}
	$$

body: In probability theory and information theory, the mutual information (MI) of two random variables is a measure of the mutual dependence between the two variables. More specifically, it quantifies the "amount of information" obtained about one random variable by observing the other random variable. The concept of mutual information is intimately linked to that of entropy of a random variable, a fundamental notion in information theory that quantifies the expected "amount of information" held in a random variable.
title: Mutual information

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), claim w725-T329-002 v1. This is an optimization of a published upper-bound certificate, not an optimal-capacity theorem. In Vardi?Yehudai?Shamir Theorem 6.2 (arXiv:2110.03187v1 p.9), let n>=4, d,C be positive integers, and let x_i in R^d have norms <=r, pairwise distances >=delta>0, and labels in {1,...,C}; normalize r>=1 and delta<=1. Put h=log_2(d*n*C*r/delta)>0 and M=floor(sqrt(n)). Fix source constants A,K>0 such that for every integer 2<=s<=M the source certifies weight precision <=A*h*f(s) and depth <=K*e(s), where f(s)=s/sqrt(log_2 s) and e(s)=n*h/f(s). For a bit budget beta>0 define t=beta/(A*h), and call s certified if f(s)<=t. The certified set is nonempty exactly when t>=2; if nonempty it is {2,...,S}, with S the largest certified integer, and e(S) minimizes the displayed depth expression. If t>=f(M), then S=M and e(S)=n*h/f(M). If 2<=t<f(M), then n*h/t<=e(S)<(3/2)*n*h/t, equivalently A*n*h^2/beta<=e(S)<(3*A/2)*n*h^2/beta. The inequalities concern e(S), not the actual network depth; the actual theorem supplies an upper bound K*e(S). For beta=c*log_2 n, the exact certificate threshold is c>=2*A*h/log_2 n. With fixed feasible c and h=Theta(log n), the unsaturated expression is Theta(n log n), so the constant-width parameter guarantee is O(d+n log n). All source constants are unspecified. For n=4 only s=2 is legal, so every feasible budget is saturated. Independent review is pending; no Lean certification is claimed.

Let X take values in {-1, 1}^n, n >= 1, under any law, fix a coordinate i, and let X_i' be a replacement sign which, given X_{-i}, is independent of X_i; X^(i) is X with coordinate i replaced by X_i'. Put D_i u(x) = (u(x with x_i = 1) - u(x with x_i = -1))/2, m = E[X_i | X_{-i}] and m' = E[X_i' | X_{-i}]. For every real u on the cube, (1/2) E[(u(X) - u(X^(i)))^2] = E[(1 - m m') (D_i u(X))^2], with the weight 1 - m m' in [0, 2]. Hence (1/2) E[(u(X) - u(X^(i)))^2] = E[(D_i u(X))^2] for every u if and only if m m' = 0 almost surely: at each value of X_{-i} of positive probability, X_i or X_i' is conditionally fair, and the law of the other sign is then arbitrary (X_i' = 1 always is allowed when X_i is conditionally fair). If X_i' is a fresh draw from the conditional law of X_i (m' = m, the heat-bath step), the left side is E[Var(u(X) | X_{-i})] = E[(1 - m^2) (D_i u)^2]. Under the uniform law and for u with values +-1, E[(D_i u)^2] is the influence of coordinate i.

[Theorem 53 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $k$ be a perfect field and $X$ a del Pezzo variety over $k$.
Then for every simple normal crossings divisor $D$ on $X$, the pair $(X,D)$ is log HT-split.
In particular, we have
\[
F_*\Omega^{\bullet}_X(\log D) \simeq \bigoplus_{i=0}^{\dim X} \Omega_X^i(\log D)[-i]
\]
and Akizuki--Nakano-type vanishing for $(X,D)$ as in \Cref{vanishing}.

[Proposition 8 ({\cite[Corollary~5.6) of arXiv:2609.00936, 'Extended Abstract of Counting Divisorial Contractions with Centre a $cA_n$-Singularity'] {Pae24Counting}}] 
Let $U = \operatorname{Spec} (\mathbb C[x_1, \ldots, x_n] / I)$ be an affine variety properly containing the origin. Assign positive integer weights $w_1, \ldots, w_m$ to the variables $y_1, \ldots, y_m$ of $\mathbb C^m$ and assign the weights $1, \ldots, 1$ to $x_1, \ldots, x_n$. Let superscript ``an'' denote analytification. Let $\psi\colon (U^{\mathrm{an}}, \bm 0) \to (Z, \bm 0)$ be a biholomorphic map germ to a complex space subgerm $(Z, \bm 0)$ of $(\mathbb C^m, \bm 0)$. Define the variety $\hat U$ by
\[
\hat U := \operatorname{Spec} \frac{\mathbb C[x_1, \ldots, x_n, y_1, \ldots, y_m]}{I + (\psi_1^{<w_1} - y_1, \ldots, \psi_m^{<w_m} - y_m)},
\]
where $\psi_j^{<w_j}$ denotes the truncation of the $j$-th coordinate power series of $\psi$ up to order $w_j - 1$. Note that $\hat U$ is isomorphic to~$U$ and let $\theta\colon (\hat U^{\mathrm{an}}, \bm 0) \to (Z, \bm 0)$ be the composition of the map germs of $\hat U^{\mathrm{an}} \to U^\mathrm{an}$ and $U^{\mathrm{an}} \to Z$. Then, both of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\theta$ lifts to a biholomorphism around the exceptional loci of the weighted blowups, and
\item every proper birational morphism locally analytically equivalent to the weighted blowup of $Z$ is given by the weighted blowup of $\hat U$ for some local biholomorphism~$\psi\colon U \to Z$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

STATUS: proof (unaudited); own-work draft; no novelty assertion. Complete implicit parametrization of all balanced opposite-head two-cycles across scalar logistic tanh factored-attention models with 0<a<b, plus exact transverse multiplier 5-2r-2/r; no factor sign flip is possible. One strictly increasing scalar equation determines the unequal negative margins. A 576-case full-Jacobian scan found no attracting candidates, as numerical evidence only.
ASSUMPTIONS: Single signed link h(s)=a+b tanh(kappa s), 0<a<b, kappa>0, eta>0, simultaneous Euclidean joint GD in (v,k,q), k^2=q^2 on the cycle, v0*v1<0. Explicit necessary and sufficient parametrization across model parameters given in proof.
SCOPE/GAP: Independent audit pending. Uniform instability of the balanced Jacobian block for unequal head magnitudes remains open; 576 floating-point samples do not settle it.

# Balanced opposite-head two-cycles: complete implicit parametrization

T328-W698-017 v1, Target 1, proof (unaudited).

Consider L(v,k,q)=log(1+exp(-v h(kq))), h(s)=a+b*tanh(kappa*s),
0<a<b, kappa>0 and simultaneous Euclidean GD with fixed eta>0.
For this scalar signed link, every balanced period-two orbit whose heads have
opposite signs is covered by the following construction, up to interchanging
the two phases and simultaneously negating both factors. The construction
parametrizes cycles across the data/step parameters; for prescribed a,b,kappa,
eta these parameter equalities are necessary and sufficient, not a claim that
every prescribed model has such a cycle.

## Construction from four positive parameters

Choose 0<r<1 and T,y0,kappa>0. Define

    A=tanh T, B=tanh(r^2*T),
    D=cosh(T)^2/cosh(r^2*T)^2,
    sig(y)=1/(1+exp(-y)), f(y)=y*sig(y)^2.

There is a unique y1>0 solving

    f(y1)=f(y0)/(r*D).

Indeed f'(y)=sig(y)^2*[1+2y*(1-sig(y))]>0 on y>0,
and f increases continuously from 0 to infinity. Put

    g0=sig(y0), g1=sig(y1), c=g0/g1,
    t=y1/(y0*c),
    v0=sqrt((1-r)*(A-B)/((1+t)*(1+c)*kappa*sech(T)^2)),
    H0=y0/v0, H1=c*H0,
    b=H0*(1+c)/(A-B), a=b*A-H0,
    eta=v0*(1+t)/(g0*H0), w=sqrt(T/kappa).

All denominators are strictly positive. Also a/b=(c*A+B)/(1+c) lies
strictly between B and A, hence 0<a<b. These parameters give the exact
period-two orbit

    (v0,w,-w) <-> (-t*v0,r*w,-r*w).

The two signed margins are -y0 and -y1. In particular the logistic factors
are exactly g0 and g1, not factors obtained from a limiting approximation.

## Verification

h(-w^2)=-H0 and h(-r^2*w^2)=H1. Thus g0*H0=g1*H1 and
the two head increments are respectively -v0*(1+t) and v0*(1+t).
Let d0=b*kappa*sech(T)^2, d1=b*kappa*sech(r^2*T)^2=D*d0.
The first factor coefficient is

    delta0=eta*v0*g0*d0
          =v0^2*(1+t)*(1+c)*kappa*sech(T)^2/(A-B)=1-r.

For the second coefficient, the scalar equation gives

    t*(g1/g0)*D = y1*g1^2*D/(y0*g0^2)=1/r.

Consequently delta1=eta*(-t*v0)*g1*d1=-(1-r)/r=1-1/r.
On k=-q the factor multipliers 1-delta0=r and 1-delta1=1/r
return the factors exactly. The head changes sign, so the orbit is nonfixed.

## Completeness within the stated class

Balance means k^2=q^2. If k=q, the product is nonnegative, h(kq)>0,
and the head strictly increases at every finite point, so there is no finite
cycle. If k=q=0 the same argument applies. Thus a balanced cycle must lie
on k=-q with nonzero k. Interchange phases so v0>0>v1 and simultaneously
negate both factors so k0=w>0. Since delta_j=eta*v_j*g_j*h'_j,
delta0>0>delta1. The returning-factor equation is

    (1-delta0)*(1-delta1)=1.

The second factor is >1; therefore 0<1-delta0<1. Write this number r.
It follows that k1=r*w and delta1=1-1/r. In particular no factor sign flip
is possible for an opposite-head balanced two-cycle in this class.
The head update v1-v0<0 forces h0<0, and the reverse update forces h1>0.
Set H0=-h0, H1=h1, t=-v1/v0, T=kappa*w^2,
y0=v0*H0, y1=t*v0*H1. These are positive. The equal and opposite
head increments imply H1/H0=g0/g1=c, whence t=y1/(y0*c).
Dividing the two factor coefficients gives r*D*f(y1)=f(y0).
The identities h1-h0=b*(A-B), delta0=1-r and the head increment then
recover precisely the formulas for b,a,v0,eta above. This proves completeness.

## Full Jacobian test and its present limit

The normal two-step multiplier is exactly

    mu_U=(1+delta0)*(1+delta1)=(2-r)*(2-1/r)=5-2r-2/r.

It satisfies |mu_U|<1 precisely for (3-sqrt(5))/2<r<1,
equals -1 at the left endpoint, and is <-1 below it. It is zero at r=1/2.
The other two multipliers are exactly the eigenvalues of J1*J0, using
the general balanced Jacobian given in proofs/014_opposite_head_cycles.md.
This is an exact formula for the full spectrum, but no uniform inequality
for that balanced block has been proved for unequal head magnitudes.

The reproducible script scripts/asymmetric_cycles.py sampled 576 choices:
r in {.1,.2,.35,.4,.5,.65,.8,.9,.98}, T in {.1,.3,.6,.9,1.3,2,3,5},
y0 in {.01,.1,.4,1,2,4,8,16}, with kappa=1. It solved the monotone
equation by floating-point bisection and differentiated the full 3D loss.
It found zero attracting candidates; the smallest observed full spectral
radius was approximately 8.9666956. The largest relative cycle residual was
approximately 2.56e-13. These are numerical evidence, not rigorous bounds,
and cannot establish instability throughout the parametrization.

Claim 016 proves full instability and the complete second-multiplier phase
diagram on the equal-head-magnitude subfamily r=1/2,
cosh(T)^2=2cosh(T/4)^2. The SINGLE remaining hard step for upgrading
the wider numerical finding to a theorem is a rigorous spectral-radius
inequality for J1*J0 throughout (r,T,y0)>0 with 0<r<1. This proof
does not claim that step or almost-everywhere factored-GD convergence.

[Lem 10 of arXiv:2609.00719, 'On the Aleksandrov--Bakelman--Pucci estimates for the weighted $1$-Laplacian'] Let $u\in \mathrm{USC}(\R^n)$ and $u_j\in C(\R^n)$ be nonnegative. Assume that, for every $x\in\R^n$,
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[(I)] there exist $x_j\to x$ such that $u_j(x_j)\to u(x)$;
            \item[(II)] for every sequence $x_j\to x$,
            \[
            \limsup_{j\to\infty}u_j(x_j)\leq u(x).
            \]
        \end{enumerate}
        Then
        \[
        \limsup_{j\to\infty}\Theta(u_j)
        \subseteq \Theta(u).
        \]

body: If A is a square matrix with every entry strictly positive, then A has a real eigenvalue r > 0, the Perron root, that is strictly greater in absolute value than every other eigenvalue of A. This r is a simple root of the characteristic polynomial and has an eigenvector with all entries strictly positive, unique up to positive scaling; no other eigenvalue admits a nonnegative eigenvector. If A is merely nonnegative and irreducible, r > 0 still exists as an eigenvalue of maximal absolute value with a positive eigenvector, though other eigenvalues may tie it in absolute value. Proved by Oskar Perron (1907) and Georg Frobenius (1912).
title: Perron-Frobenius theorem

Consider the Gaussian network and empirical FIM F_M specified in assumptions,with fixed depth L,sample count T>=1 and output dimension C>=1. Write g_(k,t)=grad_theta f_k(x_t),P=dim(theta),and F_M=(1/T)*sum_(k,t) g_(k,t)g_(k,t)^T. Let alpha>0 satisfy P/M^2->alpha,and assume explicitly that <g_(k,s),g_(kprime,t)>/M->delta_(k,kprime)*alpha*K_st,where K has diagonal kappa1 and off-diagonal kappa2,with kappa1>=kappa2>=0. All these finitely many limits hold jointly almost surely,or jointly in probability. Then lambda_max(F_M)/M -> (alpha/T)*(kappa1+(T-1)*kappa2),in the same convergence mode. The source defines kappa1 and kappa2 by the same-sample and distinct-sample order-parameter sums: kappa_j=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_(j,l)*qhat_(j,l-1),where qhat_(1,l)=lim ||h_l(x_t)||^2/M_l,qtilde_(1,l)=lim ||grad_(u_l)f_k(x_t)||^2;for j=2 replace each squared norm by the corresponding inner product at distinct inputs s,t. The backward-weight decoupling is Assumption1 of the source;the explicit gradient Gram convergence is an additional hypothesis here. The output multiplicity C does not multiply this largest-eigenvalue coefficient. Fixed C,T and kappa2>=0 are essential to this stated version. No conclusion about nonzero lower-order eigenvalues when the leading coefficient vanishes,or about a growing sample count,is asserted. Draft,independent review pending.
Fixed L>=2 and fixed positive integers C,T. Widths M_l/M->alpha_l>0 for l=0,...,L-1; M_L=C. Hidden layers h_l=phi(u_l), u_l=W_l*h_(l-1)+b_l; output f=u_L is linear.
Independent Gaussian initialization W_l[i,j]~N(0,sigma_w^2/M_(l-1)) and b_l[i]~N(0,sigma_b^2), sigma_w>0 and sigma_b>0. Inputs are iid standard Gaussian. Parameters theta include all weights and biases.
phi and phi_prime have finite squared Gaussian integrals at each recursively occurring preactivation variance. The empirical FIM normalization is F=(1/T)*sum_(t=1)^T sum_(k=1)^C grad_theta f_k(x_t)*grad_theta f_k(x_t)^T.
C,T,L are fixed as M tends to infinity. P is the total number of weights and biases,alpha=sum_(l=1)^(L-1) alpha_l*alpha_(l-1),and P/M^2->alpha>0.
Explicit additional hypothesis: for every fixed k,kprime in1..C and s,t in1..T,the inner product of parameter gradients divided by M converges to delta_(k,kprime)*alpha*(kappa1 if s=t else kappa2). Convergence is either almost surely throughout,or in probability throughout.
The finite constants satisfy kappa1>=kappa2>=0. Forward and backward same-sample and distinct-sample order parameters entering the source formulas have finite deterministic limits common to each sample or sample pair. These convergence and output-decoupling statements are premises,not consequences proved here from Assumption1.

body:
[Theorem thm-intro-main of arXiv:2605.24627, 'A 4/7-limit law for the largest interpoint distance in a rotational ellipsoid'] Let $0<a<1$. Then
\[
n^{4/7}(2-M_n) \stackrel{{\cal D}}{\longrightarrow} Z,
\]
where $\stackrel{{\cal D}}{\longrightarrow}$ denotes convergence in distribution, and 
\[
\mathbb{P}(Z>t) = \exp\{-\Lambda_{a}t^{7/2}\}, \qquad t\ge 0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Lambda_{a} = \frac{9}{64\pi}I_{a},
\]
where
\[
I_{a} = \int_A \mathbf 1 \{G(s,s',y,y',\tau)\le 1\}
\,{\rm d}s\,{\rm d}s'\,{\rm d}y\,{\rm d}y'\,{\rm d}\tau,
\]
\[
G(s,s',y,y',\tau) = \frac{s+s'}{2} + \frac{\tau^2}{4} 
- \frac{a^2}{4}(y-y')^2,
\]
and
\[
A = \{(s,s',y,y',\tau): s,s'\ge 0,\ y^2\le s,\ (y')^2\le s'\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-intro-main of arXiv:2605.24627

\]
