[Definition 16 (Factor of i.i.d.) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Consider a locally finite transitive graph $G=(V,E)$
    (with respect to some group $\Theta\subset\operatorname{Aut}(G)$).
    Let $S$ denote a measurable space,
    and let $\mu$ denote the distribution of a $\Theta$-stationary random field on $S^V$.
    Let $(T,\lambda)$ denote a probability space, and consider $\P:=\lambda^V$.
    A \emph{factor of i.i.d.}\ (FIID) is a map $\phi:T^V\to S^V$
    with the following properties:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\phi$ is measurable with respect to the product $\sigma$-algebras on $T^V$ and $S^V$,
        \item $\phi$ is equivariant with respect to $\Theta$,
        \item If $X\sim\P$, then $\phi(X)\sim\mu$.
    \end{itemize}
title: Factor of i.i.d.

body: [Theorem rep theorem of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ are smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks, and there is a representable contraction morphism $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ whose exceptional $\mathcal{E}$ is a smooth Cartier divisor. Moreover, suppose there is a smooth closed Deligne--Mumford substack $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq \mathcal{Z}$, such that $f^{-1}(\mathcal{Y}) \simeq \mathcal{E}$ set-theoretically, and $f : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z} \setminus \mathcal{Y}$. Then $f$ is an ordinary blowup with reduced center $\mathcal{Y}$, in particular $f|_{\mathcal{E}} : \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is a projective bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathcal{E})|_{\mathcal{E}} \simeq \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{E}}(-1) \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}$ for some line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{Y}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:gamma of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Let $\phi$ be a
		$\mathbb Z$-valued height function on the vertices of a connected domain $V\subset \mathbb Z^2$. Associate to each bond $e\in (\mathbb Z^2)^*$, dual to some edge $(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2$, the gradient $(
abla \phi)_e := \phi_x - \phi_y$, where $x$ is taken to be the 	extsc{north} vertex if $(x,y)$ is vertical and the 	extsc{west} vertex if $(x,y)$ is horizontal. We say the bond $e$ is a \emph{disagreement bond} of $\phi$ if $(
abla\phi)_e
eq 0$ (including when $\phi_x$ or $\phi_y$ are specified by the boundary conditions). A \emph{disagreement polymer}~$\gamma$ is a (maximal) connected component of the disagreement bonds of $\phi$, and we let $\ensuremath{\mathcal P}_\phi$ denote the disagreement polymers in $\phi$. For such a polymer, let $D_i$ be the connected components of $V \setminus \gamma$, noting that by the maximality of $\gamma$, within each $D_i$, all the vertices that are $*$-adjacent to $V\setminus D_i$ must have the same height $h_i$ in~$\phi$. Call the triple $(\gamma, \{D_i\}, \{h_i\})$ a \emph{labeled disagreement polymer}. For brevity,  we denote labeled disagreement polymers by $\gamma$ (omitting the $\{h_i\}$ from the notation).
title: Disagreement polymer

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] Let \(\bm f=(f_1,f_2)^\top\in\mathscr S^\dagger \). The sequence of martingales $ \left\{
	\bm M_t^n(\bm f):0\le t\le T \right\}_{n\in \mathbb{N} }$ converges in 
	the topology of  $ \mathcal D([0,T], \mathbb{R})$, as $ n  \to \infty $, towards a mean-zero Gaussian process \(W_t(\bm f)\) with quadratic variation given by
	\[
	\Phi_{11}+\Phi_{12}+\Phi_{21}+\Phi_{22},
	\]
	where, for \(k=1,2\),
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\Phi_{kk}
		&=
		\int_0^t
		\Bigg\{
		\int_0^1
		2\rho_k(s,u)
		\left(
		1-\rho_k(s,u)
		\right)
		\left(
		\partial_u f_k(u)
		\right)^2
		\,\mathrm du                                     
		+
		\int_0^1
		\left(
		\gamma_1\rho_1(s,u)
		+
		\gamma_2\rho_2(s,u)
		\right)
		f_k(u)^2
		\,\mathrm du                                      \\
		&\quad
		+
		\left(
		\alpha_k\rho_0(s,0)
		+
		\alpha_0\rho_k(s,0)
		\right)
		f_k(0)^2                                  
		+
		\left(
		\beta_k\rho_0(s,1)
		+
		\beta_0\rho_k(s,1)
		\right)
		f_k(1)^2
		\Bigg\}
		\,\mathrm ds,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	and, for \(k\neq l\),
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\Phi_{kl}
		&=
		-
		\int_0^t
		\Bigg\{
		\int_0^1
		2\rho_1(s,u)\rho_2(s,u)
		\partial_u f_1(u)
		\partial_u f_2(u)
		\,\mathrm du                                      \\
		&\quad
		+
		\int_0^1
		\left(
		\gamma_1\rho_1(s,u)
		+
		\gamma_2\rho_2(s,u)
		\right)
		f_1(u)f_2(u)
		\,du
		\Bigg\}
		\,\mathrm ds .
	\end{aligned}
	\]

Let u: {-1, 1}^n -> R under the uniform measure, with Fourier coefficients u^(S) = E[u chi_S], derivatives D_i u(x) = (u(x with x_i = 1) - u(x with x_i = -1))/2 and total influence I(u) = sum_i E[(D_i u)^2]. Then I(u) - Var(u) = sum over |S| >= 2 of (|S| - 1) u^(S)^2. Hence Var(u) <= I(u) (the Poincare inequality of the cube), with equality iff u is affine, u^(S) = 0 for |S| >= 2. With Pi u = u^(empty) + sum_i u^({i}) x_i the affine part, ||u - Pi u||_2^2 = sum over |S| >= 2 of u^(S)^2 <= I(u) - Var(u), with equality iff u^(S) = 0 for every |S| >= 3.

Then for the BPVEI $(Y_n)$ defined in (equation eq:Y of the paper),

\end{equation*}
define a homogeneous standard honest transition function of a Markov branching 
process with immigration.

[Lemma lem:mmean of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let $z_i\in\mathbb{R}^m$ carry weights $p_i>0$ with $\sum_ip_iz_i=0$, and let
$E=\sum_ip_i\lVert z_i\rVert^2$. Then some convex combination $\delta$ of at most
$m$ of the points satisfies $\Wnorm\delta^2\le E/m^2$. The constant is
attained by the uniformly weighted regular simplex.

DRAFT; author proof, independent mathematical review pending. For n>=81 put t=floor(sqrt(n)), a=t, b=2t+1, k=t+1, and m=floor(n/2). Let D_n be the interior of the union of the rectangles [0,a/n]x[0,1], [b/n,1]x[0,1], and [a/n,b/n]x[(m-1/2)/n,(m+1/2)/n]. Each D_n is a simply connected Jordan polygon with fixed corner marks A=(0,1), B=(0,0), C=(1,0), D=(1,1). Its closure Hausdorff distance from the closed unit square is <=k/(2n), its boundary Hausdorff distance is <=b/n, its area loss is k(n-1)/n^2, and its unmarked Caratheodory kernel at (1/2,1/2) is the open unit square. Yet in the induced nearest-neighbor graph on mesh-1/n vertices in its closure, independent bonds p=1/2 give P(AB connects CD)<=2^-k, tending to zero: only the row y=m/n joins the chambers. Canonical square crossings are uniformly positive by classical RSW. The missing marked-prime-end convergence is essential; this example refutes an overstrong approximation bridge, not the properly marked C0017 target.

Let X be a Banach space, Y a normed space, and {T_i : i in I} a family (of any cardinality) of bounded linear operators from X to Y. If the family is pointwise bounded, meaning sup over i of ||T_i(x)|| is finite for every x in X, then it is uniformly bounded: sup over i of the operator norms ||T_i|| is finite. Consequently, if a sequence of bounded operators on a Banach space converges pointwise, the limit operator is bounded. Completeness of the domain is essential.

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.09248, '\bfseries Limit laws for longest edges in empty region graphs'] Suppose that the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:PoisConvAbstract} are satisfied and that $\log(t)+\tau+b>0$. Then, for the point process $\xi_t|_{W \times [b,\infty)\times\LL^d}$, the quantities $E_2$, $E_3$, and $E_4$ in Theorem \ref{thm:BSY} {with $S_{(x,y)}:=S(x,y)\cup\{x,y\}$ for $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$} are bounded by
    \[
    E_2 \le C_2 \frac{1+ b+ \log(t) + \tau}{e^{2b}t}, \quad E_3 \le \frac{C_3}{e^b(b+\log(t)+\tau)^{\max\{d-2, 1/2\}}},\quad
    E_4 \le \frac{C_{4,1}}{e^b(b+\log(t)+\tau)^{d-1}}+\frac{C_{4,2}}{e^{2b}t}.
    \]
    Here, $C_2$, $C_3$, $C_{4,1}$, and $C_{4,2}$ are constants in $(0,\infty)$ depending only on $d$ and $W$ as well as the constants $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ in Theorem \ref{thm:PoisConvAbstract}. Possible choices are
    \[
    C_2 := \frac{2^{d+1} \kappa_d \alpha^d}{\gamma}\vol(W),\quad C_3 := \begin{cases}
        \frac{4 d \kappa_d^2 M_{d-1}\gamma^{d-2}}{\beta^d(d-2)}\vol(W), & d \ge 3,\\
        {\frac{16\sqrt{2} \pi^{5/2}}{\beta^2\sqrt{\gamma}}\vol(W),} & d = 2,
    \end{cases}\quad
    C_{4,1} := \frac{2^{d+4} d \kappa_d M_{d-1}\gamma^{d-1}}{\beta^d} \vol(W), 
    \]
and $C_{4,2}:=16\vol(W)$, where $M_{d-1} := (2(d-1)/e)^{d-1}$.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2604.25336, 'Central limit theorem for slow-fast system under mixed fractional Brownian motion'] Under assumptions \textbf{H1}-\textbf{H3}. Define \(\hat g(x,y):=g(x,y)-\bar g(x)\) and 
\begin{equation}
\Psi(x,y) =\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathcal{P}_t^x \hat g(x, Y_t^x) \dd t.
\end{equation} 
The \(\Psi(x,y)\) is the solution to the Poisson equation \eqref{Poisson_eq} where \(h\) is replaced by \(\hat g\).
Moreover, \(\Psi(x,y)\in C^2\). For all \((x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}^m\), \(D_x\Psi(x,y)\) and \(D^2_{xx}\Psi(x,y)\) are linear growth. Specially,
\(D_y\Psi(x,y), D^2_{xy}\Psi(x,y), D^2_{yy}\Psi(x,y)\) are globally bounded. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: The all-one-ended event is not automatically a tail event Result: Take two disjoint one-ended infinite trees and add one edge joining them. Before the addition every component has one end; afterwards the connected tree has two ends, since deleting the joining edge separates two infinite pieces. Check: The added edge creates no cycle and the change is finite. Thus the property can change within the class of spanning forests under a finite edge modification. Obstruction: Uniform-forest tail triviality cannot be invoked until a separate tail representation of the event is proved. The example is a logical obstruction, not a uniform-forest counterexample.

body:
[Lemma lem:universal-root of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $X,Z\in\operatorname{End}(W)$ be arbitrary, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N$ be the Kac
orthonormal basis of $W=\mathfrak{so}(n)$, and put $A_i=\operatorname{ad}_{a_i}$.
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_i(X,Z)&=\{X,[A_i,Z]\}a_i,&
 U_i(X,Z)&=\{X,Z\}a_i,\\
 E_i(X,Z)&=\{[A_i,X],Z\}a_i,&
 \bar E(X,Z)&=\frac1N\sum_iE_i(X,Z).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.10a}
\]
Put $\Psi(T)=\sum_jA_jTa_j$.  Then, with no projection onto curvature
summands,
\[
 \mathcal R_i=A_iU_i-(E_i-\bar E)-\bar E,
 \qquad
 \bar E=\frac1N\sum_jA_jV_j+H(X,Z),\qquad V_j=XZa_j,
\tag{3.2.10b}
\]
where
\[
 H(X,Z)=\frac1N\{-X\Psi(Z)+Z\Psi(X)\}.
\tag{3.2.10b$'$}
\]
Moreover, writing $\|\cdot\|_2$ for Hilbert--Schmidt norm,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac1N\sum_i\|U_i\|^2
 &\le\frac4N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_j\|V_j\|^2
 &\le\frac1N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2,\\
 \frac1N\sum_i\|E_i-\bar E\|^2
 &\le\frac{16(n-2)}N\|X\|_2^2\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.2.10c}
\]
The residue satisfies
\[
 \|H(X,Z)\|
 \le\frac{\sqrt{n-2}}N
 \bigl(\|X\|_\mathrm{op}\|Z\|_2+\|Z\|_\mathrm{op}\|X\|_2\bigr).
\tag{3.2.10e}
\]
If $X$ and $Z$ are symmetric, then $\Psi(X)=\Psi(Z)=0$, so $H=0$.
The identities and estimates remain valid when all maps are tensored by
an ancillary identity and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm is taken on the
amplified space.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] For every integer $n\geqslant 1$ and every $\kappa>0$, there are $
 \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\kappa)>0$ and $
 C=C(n,\kappa)>0$
with the following property. Let $(X,\ensuremath{\mathrm d},\mathcal H^n,x)$ be a pointed
$\operatorname{RCD}(-\eta,n)$ space, where $0\leqslant\eta\leqslant1$, and let
\[
 u=(u^1,\ldots,u^n):B_2(x)\to \mathbb R^n
\]
have harmonic components. Denote by $I$ the $n\times n$ identity matrix and put
\begin{equation}
 G_u:=\left(\langle\nabla u^i,\nabla u^j\rangle\right)_{i,j=1}^n,
 \qquad
 D:=\fint_{B_1(x)}|G_u-I|\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^n.
\end{equation}
If $D+\eta\leqslant \varepsilon$, then
\begin{equation}
 \fint_{B_r(x)}|G_u-I|\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal H^n
 \leqslant Cr^{-\kappa}(D+\eta)
 \qquad\forall 0<r<\frac14.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01464

[Lemma lem:interior-dirichlet-gmc-comparison of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $M_{h_D}^{\rm can}$ and $M_{h_U}^{\rm can}$ be the canonical GMC measures
obtained from the construction of Lemma~(lem:canonical-borel-gmc of the paper) on $D$
and $U$, respectively.  Under the coupling above, for every fixed $V\Subset U$,
almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 M_{h_D}^{\rm can}|_V
 =w_{D,U}\,M_{h_U}^{\rm can}|_V,
 \qquad
 w_{D,U}(z)
 :=\exp\!\left(
   \gamma\chi_{D,U}(z)
   -\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb E[\chi_{D,U}(z)^2]
  \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 w_{D,U},\ w_{D,U}^{-1}\in C_b(V).
\end{equation}
In particular, the two measures in
(equation eq:interior-dirichlet-gmc-comparison of the paper) have the same null sets on $V$.

[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\). For every \(x>0\), there exists a unique
\(\theta_a(x)\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
        \Lambda_a'(\theta_a(x))=x,
        \qquad
        J_a(x)=\theta_a(x)x-\Lambda_a(\theta_a(x)).
\]
Moreover, \(J_a\) is differentiable and strictly convex on \((0,\infty)\), with
\(J_a'(x)=\theta_a(x)\) and
\(J_a''(x)=1/\Lambda_a''(\theta_a(x))\). Finally, \(J_a\ge0\) on
\([0,\infty)\), and it vanishes uniquely at
\(\lambda_a=\frac{1}{4\pi}(1-\frac{1}{a})\).

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $\chi$ is injective. Let $V$ be a $k[G]$-module with $\ell_V$ constant. Let $a\in C_m$ and $W:=U(a,1)$. We assume that $V$ is constant-indecomposable and we consider a direct sum decomposition into indecomposable $k[G]$-modules $V=\oplus_{i=1}^{\imath_V} U(a_i,b_i)$. Let 
$$J:=\{a_i+\epsilon|i\in\llbracket1,\imath_V\rrbracket\}.$$
Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have an identity
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Hom_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr)=\begin{cases}1\quad\textup{if}\quad a\in J\\0\quad\textup{if}\quad a\notin J.\end{cases}$$

{\bf (2)} Let $(c,b)\in\mathbb J_{m,p^s}$. Then 
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Ext^1_{k[G]}(U(c,b),W)\bigr)=\begin{cases}1\quad\textup{if}\quad  a=c+\epsilon\;\textup{and}\;b<p^s\\0\quad\textup{if}\quad a\neq c+\epsilon\;\textup{or}\;b=p^s.\end{cases}$$

{\bf (3)} Suppose that $\jmath_V=0$. Then 
$$\dim_k\bigl(\Hom_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr)=\dim_k\bigl(\Ext^1_{k[G]}(V,W)\bigr).$$
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.03191

[Definition def:inf-free-mom-cum of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $(\mathcal{A}, \varphi^{(0)}, \varphi^{(1)}, \ldots,
  \varphi^{(\nu)})$ be an infinitesimal non-commutative probability space of
  order $\nu$. The infinitesimal free cumulants of order $\nu$ are
  multilinear maps $(\kappa_n^{(0)}, \ldots, \kappa_n^{(\nu)} : \mathcal{A}^n
  \rightarrow \mathbb{C})$ uniquely determined by the following relation: For
  every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $i = 0, \ldots, \nu$ and $(a_1, \ldots, a_k) \in
  \mathcal{A}^k$,
  \begin{equation}
    \varphi^{(i)} (a_1 \ldots a_k) = \sum_{\pi = \{V_1, \ldots, V_p \} \in
    \ensuremath{\operatorname{NC}} (k)} \sum_{\lambda_1 + \cdots + \lambda_p = i}
    \frac{i!}{\lambda_1 ! \ldots \lambda_p !} \prod_{i = 1}^p \kappa_{|V_i
    |}^{(\lambda_i)} (a_1, \ldots, a_k |V_i) . 
  \end{equation}
title: Definition def:inf-free-mom-cum of arXiv:2412.09290

[Lem 31 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] There exists a constant $C > 1$ such that the following holds, whenever $q \in (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ and $a, b, c \in (1-\varepsilon, 1 + \varepsilon)$, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon \in (0, C^{-1})$. Fix $z_0 = (x_0,y_0) \in \mathfrak{L}_{q;a,b,c}$, and assume that $x_0\ge x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}$ and that $\ell_{z_0}$ is the southwest edge of $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$. 
	 
	 \begin{enumerate} 
	 	\item We have that $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le -\partial_x \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$. 
	 	\item We have that $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{-1} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le \partial_y \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{-1} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$. 
		\item We have that $C^{-1} \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{1/2} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q}^{3/2} \le \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^{1/2} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q}^{3/2}$. 
		\item Assume that $z_0 = (x_0,y_0) \in \mathfrak{L}_{q;a,b,c}$ and $\ell_{z_0}$ is the southwest edge of $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$, but now $ x_0\le x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}$. Then $C^{-1} (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2} \le -\partial_x \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C (\mathfrak{d}_{z_0} \mathfrak{e}_{{z_0};q})^{1/2}$ remains valid, but now $C^{-1} \le \partial_y \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C$ and $C^{-1} \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^2 \le \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} ({z_0}) \le C \mathfrak{d}_{z_0}^2$. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For fixed k>=2, the kth cumulant of M_t=exp(-5t/2+sqrt(5t)*Z) has coefficients A_ks=(1/s!)*sum_partition w_pi*(sum_blocks 5*|B|*(|B|-1)/2)^s. For every m>=0 and 0<=t<=c, its Taylor error is at most W_k*exp(a_k*c)*(a_k*t)^(m+1)/(m+1)!, where W_k=sum_r Stirling(k,r)*(r-1)! and a_k=5*k*(k-1)/2. The coefficients below k-1 vanish. Multiply by (2k-1)!!*q0^k for the scalar Gaussian-mixture output cumulant of order2k. Assumptions: Fixed k,m,c; Z and final xi standard normal independent; q0 deterministic nonnegative; finite-moment cumulants. This concerns the settled limiting law evaluated at t=L/n, not exact finite-width cumulants. Complete definitions: Pi_k partitions [k], w_pi=(-1)^(|pi|-1)(|pi|-1)!, H_pi=sum_B 5*|B|*(|B|-1)/2, and A_ks=sum_pi w_pi*H_pi^s/s!. For each fixed k the cumulant is entire in t; this does not reconstruct the probability law from moments.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:893e2ba5914650d9ec8a1cb35ef6b7328e3b412018d8b1499cd824c6398054e4","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/89/893e2ba5914650d9ec8a1cb35ef6b7328e3b412018d8b1499cd824c6398054e4.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:119ecb8fe3c8d07319122c7e554ceeb9ab679c0efb1b4fa92796c07f5682ec90","bundle_entry_key":"lognormal-cumulant-uniform-taylor","bundle_id":"population.t244-explicit-uniform-cumulant-remainders-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks; cumulant expansions","draft":"w691/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:lognormal-cumulants-explicit-fixed-order-taylor-remainder","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C018: explicit all-order cumulant remainders for the limiting scalar law

Version 1, Target 2; proof (unaudited). This supplies the named explicit remainder, not a new lognormal law. No novelty claim is made for the partition or connected-graph identities. The law itself is settled in the dossier and prior literature.

Fix k>=2 and c>=0. Let M_t=exp(-5t/2+sqrt(5t)Z), where Z is standard normal, 0<=t<=c. Set a_j=5j(j-1)/2, and let Pi_k denote partitions of [k]. For pi in Pi_k define

    w_pi=(-1)^(|pi|-1)(|pi|-1)!,
    H_pi=sum_(B in pi) a_|B|,
    W_k=sum_(r=1)^k S(k,r)(r-1)!,
    A_(k,s)=(1/s!) sum_(pi in Pi_k) w_pi H_pi^s.

Here S(k,r) is the Stirling number of the second kind and H^0=1 also at H=0. Define cumulants by the finite partition formula, not by an assumed finite moment-generating function. Then for every integer m>=0,

    |kappa_k(M_t)-sum_(s=0)^m A_(k,s)t^s|
       <= W_k exp(a_k c) (a_k t)^(m+1)/(m+1)! .       (1)

All constants are explicit finite sums. In particular, (1) is uniform over all integer L,n with 0<=L<=cn upon setting t=L/n. This is a statement about the limiting-law cumulant evaluated at that t, not a claim that it equals the exact finite-width cumulant.

Proof: E M_t^j=exp(a_j t). Finite moment-cumulant inversion gives

    F_k(t)=kappa_k(M_t)=sum_pi w_pi exp(H_pi t).

Since 0<=H_pi<=a_k, the exponential Taylor remainder for t>=0 is at most exp(a_k c)(a_k t)^(m+1)/(m+1)! termwise. Summing absolute weights proves (1). Every operation is on a finite partition set, so no analyticity of a probability MGF or interchange of an infinite moment series is used.

The coefficients of t^s vanish for s<k-1. To see this, put v=exp(5t)-1. The moment exp(a_jt)=(1+v)^(j choose 2) is the sum of v^|E| over all simple graphs on a fixed j-element set. Each graph uniquely decomposes into connected components. The finite partition moment-cumulant recursion therefore identifies F_k with the sum of v^|E| over connected simple graphs on [k]. Such a graph has at least k-1 edges. The first coefficient is 5^(k-1) times the number of labeled trees (equivalently k^(k-2), by the usual Prüfer encoding). This known identity explains cancellations; inequality (1) does not need tree enumeration.

For a scalar final preactivation Y_t=sqrt(q0 M_t) xi, q0>=0 deterministic and xi an independent standard Gaussian, all odd cumulants vanish and

    kappa_(2k)(Y_t)=(2k-1)!! q0^k F_k(t).

The same factor multiplies (1). This relation follows by substituting the finite-order formal moment series of q0 M into the Gaussian even-moment series; it does not require the actual series to converge.

Scope: for each fixed k, F_k is a finite sum of exponentials and is entire as a function of t; (1) is therefore stronger than a merely asymptotic fixed-k statement. It is not uniform in k and does not reconstruct a law from its moments. In particular no all-cumulant convergent distributional expansion, tail bound, or lognormal moment determinacy follows. C019 supplies the separate finite-width comparison needed if (1) is applied to an actual finite network.

Prior sources: Hanin-Nica, arXiv:1812.05994, Theorem 1 Eq.(6), printed p.2, already gives depth-uniform moment estimates (implicit order-dependent constants); Hanin arXiv:2204.01058 Theorem3.1 supplies fixed-depth cumulant order estimates. Neither observation is represented here as a new scalar law. General partition inversion and the warning about the nonexistent positive lognormal MGF were returned by brain cards claim_3d1bead33c1ed66849b25263fccb642613a580bd05af0aad53e23ee32049a474 and claim_012141e53f5181bec890d1421b14aba76f07b48847ee96c90a73338fb6a8c3fd.

body: Let g be a norm on R^2 that is even in the first coordinate (g(-h, m) = g(h, m)), as every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm is. For fixed m, the map h -> g((h, m)) is even and convex, hence minimized at h = 0, so g((h, m)) >= g((0, m)) = |m| g(e_2). Consequently, for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) with j = r + m, m > 0 (longitudinal overshoot past the far endpoint): g(v) + g((0,r) - v) - g((0,r)) >= (r + m) g(e_2) + m g(e_2) - r g(e_2) = 2 m g(e_2), and symmetrically for j = -m < 0. The dogleg excess grows at least LINEARLY in the overshoot, with the explicit constant 2 g(e_2), using convexity and symmetry alone - no curvature hypothesis of any kind. The bound is tight as h -> 0. Use: in localization arguments it kills union sites with longitudinal overshoot at a rate no curvature assumption needs to fund, letting curvature windows be quoted only where they are literally assumed. Numerical attack: 0 violations in 300,000 trials on an anisotropic convex norm, worst ratio 1.000019.

[Theorem 1 (Inverse Riffle Shuffle with Concentrated Pile-Size Law) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Let $f_n$ be a probability distribution on $[n]$, and consider the inverse riffle-type shuffle which chooses $K_n$ with law $f_n$, then moves a uniformly chosen set of $K_n$ cards to the top. Put $Y_n:=K_n/n$, and assume that $Y_n\to\alpha$ in probability for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$, with
$\operatorname{Var}(Y_n)=o\left(\frac1{\log n}\right).$
Define
$$q_{2,n}:=\sum_{k=1}^n f_n(k)\frac{\binom{k}{2}+\binom{n-k}{2}}{\binom{n}{2}}.$$
If $t_n$ is any sequence of integer times such that
$$t_n=\frac{2\log n+c+o(1)}{-\log q_{2,n}},$$
then
$$s_n(t_n)\to 1-\exp\left(-\frac12e^{-c}\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Inverse Riffle Shuffle with Concentrated Pile-Size Law

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e171fa8587e4f09c53cdb48e0409d988c2e40c0c495318429a1a1a79d7447480","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e1/e171fa8587e4f09c53cdb48e0409d988c2e40c0c495318429a1a1a79d7447480.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d298801d9e87ef8068b4206b4c0b86e44d799755f7a27d4b0928954567b699e8","bundle_entry_key":"li-zhang-arora-theorem54-norm-correct-replacement","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-norm-correct-theorem54-replacement","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-norm-correct-source-theorem54-replacement-envelope","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Norm-correct replacement bound for the source quadratic regression problem

Status: proof (unaudited). This is a standard rank argument specialized to repair the source normalization, not a novel sample-complexity result. It makes explicit the expected-risk specialization already implicit in JOINT-005 and its queued brain card.

Let d>=1, D=d(d+1)/2, and P consist of x~N(0,I_d) with noiseless target q_alpha(x)=sum_i alpha_i x_i^2, alpha in R^d. The source expected complexity uses E_samples ||A(S)-q_alpha||_L2^2 <=epsilon ||q_alpha||_L2^2 uniformly in alpha.

For every orthogonally equivariant measurable learner A and 0<=epsilon<1, any n satisfying that guarantee necessarily obeys

    n >= ceil(D(1-epsilon)).

There exists an orthogonally equivariant learner that achieves zero error at n=D. Separately, a one-filter square-activation CNN with d scalar patches and only its d readout coefficients trained recovers every q_alpha at n=d. Thus the candidate replacement envelope is

    ceil(D(1-epsilon)) <= inf_(equivariant A) N_star(A,P,epsilon) <=D,
    inf_(specified CNN readout learners) N_star(A,P,epsilon) <=d.

The upper statement is existence of a learner, not an upper bound on every algorithm. No claim is made that the worst-case minimax risk curve equals1-n/D for intermediate n.

## Use the prediction norm, not the faulty source identity

For a real symmetric M, let q_M(x)=x^T M x. The true Gaussian inner product is

    <q_M,q_N>_L2 =2tr(MN)+tr(M)tr(N).

This follows by polarization of the corrected identity in SOURCE-011 (or direct fourth-moment expansion). It is positive definite on Sym(d), so the homogeneous quadratic subspace V has dimension D. Select any orthonormal basis phi_1,...,phi_D in this Hilbert space. The target q_theta=sum_j theta_j phi_j has prediction norm1 for every theta on S^(D-1). No ratio of expectations or uncertain source normalization is used.

Orthogonal equivariance under the Gaussian marginal transfers the learner's uniform normalized guarantee from diagonal targets to every homogeneous symmetric quadratic: diagonalize M and rotate inputs. Source Definition3.2 is sufficient, including for randomized algorithms. Hence a uniform prior on theta in S^(D-1) is a valid lower-bound prior, with exactly unit target prediction norm throughout its support. This transfer is used BEFORE averaging targets.

## Pair targets by a reflection fixing every observed label

Condition on the n input locations, independently of theta. Their evaluation matrix L has entries L_ij=phi_j(x_i) and rank r<=min(n,D). Let P be the Euclidean projection onto its row span, Q=I-P, and T=P-Q=2P-I. Then T is orthogonal, T^2=I and LT=L. The uniform spherical prior is invariant under T. This remains valid for D=1, where S^0 is the uniform two-point law.

Fix the learner's independent random coins. Targets theta and Ttheta produce identical labels and therefore exactly the same output h. If its L2 risk is infinite the lower bound is immediate. Otherwise orthogonally project h onto V, with coefficient vector gamma; projection cannot increase its squared distance from either target. Since theta=Ptheta+Qtheta and Ttheta=Ptheta-Qtheta,

    [||gamma-theta||^2+||gamma-Ttheta||^2]/2
       =||gamma-Ptheta||^2+||Qtheta||^2
       >=||Qtheta||^2.

Averaging over the spherical prior pairs theta and Ttheta without changing their law. Thus conditional average prediction risk is at least E_theta||Qtheta||^2=tr(Q)/D=(D-r)/D. The last equality uses E theta theta^T=I/D, valid also for D=1. Then average over inputs and coins. Since r<=n, the Bayes average risk is at least(1-n/D)_+. The uniform guarantee, transferred to every unit-norm quadratic, bounds that same average by epsilon, so n>=D(1-epsilon); integrality gives the ceiling. All integrands are nonnegative; Tonelli justifies averaging. No independence of conditional labels, posterior density formula, or product of conditional probabilities is assumed.

## Exact interpolation upper bounds

For the equivariant upper, minimize least-squares residual over Sym(d), choosing the unique minimum-Frobenius-norm minimizer. This is defined on every data set and commutes with orthogonal conjugation. At n=D its quadratic design is invertible almost surely: the D inputs e_i and e_i+e_j for i<j give an invertible evaluation matrix, first determining diagonals and then off-diagonals. Therefore its determinant is a nonzero polynomial in the sample coordinates; IID Gaussian inputs avoid its zero set almost surely. Exact recovery holds for every fixed quadratic target, yielding zero normalized expected risk. The zero target causes no division issue: the source guarantee is an inequality against epsilon times its squared norm.

For the CNN, one scalar shared filter w=1 with square activation and d independent readout weights represents sum_i alpha_i x_i^2. At n=d the design of squared coordinates is invertible almost surely, since inputs e_i give identity as a polynomial witness. Solving the readout linear system yields exact recovery for each fixed target. This is a readout-only upper, not a new claim about arbitrary joint-GD initialization. Joint-training candidates remain JOINT-005 and GD-006 v2.

## Verification and scope

The hardest imported source premise is only its model/algorithm definition, not its erroneous LemmaD.8 constant. The reflection identity is a finite algebraic identity and holds for any vector gamma, so it includes improper learners after Hilbert projection. If equivariance is removed, the lower transfer to all homogeneous quadratics fails: the coordinate-aware d-feature learner above is a counterexample to a universal D lower on diagonal targets. If inputs depend on theta, the independent fixed-input reflection prior argument fails. Noisy labels are not covered by the exact interpolation upper.

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2608.11637, '\bf Uniform Local Asymptotics for L\'evy Processes with Subexponential Jumps'] For any constants $\theta>0$, $ K\geq 0$ and
 	$\delta_1\geq \delta_0>0$, we have as $t\to\infty$, 
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{0<s\leq t} \sup_{x\geq \theta t} \sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)} \sup_{\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_1]} 
 	\bigg| 	\frac{ \mathbf P\big( Z_s\in x-y+\Delta_\delta \big)}{s\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)} -1 \bigg| \to 0.
 	\eeqlb
 	Moreover, there exist some constants $C,t_0>0$ such that for all $t\geq t_0$,
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{0<s\leq t} \sup_{x\geq \theta t} \sup_{y\leq Kb(x)} \sup_{\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_1]}
 	\frac{ \mathbf P\big( Z_s\in x-y+\Delta_\delta \big)}{s\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)}  \leq C.

 \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
 \item 
  The correlation functions
$\rho^{(p)}, p \in \mathbb{N}$, 
 of $\mathcal{P}$ are {\em mixing} if for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$
there exists an increasing-decreasing family of functions $\omega_k : [0, \infty)
\to [0, \infty)$ such that  for all $p,q \in \mathbb{N},
x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have
\begin{equation} 
\left| \rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q}) - \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1p)\rho^{(q)}(\bk x{p+1}{p+q}) \right| \leq \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{equation}
where $s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q})$  is at (equation defs of the paper).
Denote 
$C_k:= \sup_s \omega_k(s)$ and observe 
that $(C_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ is non-decreasing.

\item  $\mathcal{P}$ has  {\em fast mixing  correlations} if 
$\omega_k$ is fast decreasing  for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$. 
\end{enumerate}

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Fix n>=1 integer, T>0, s in (0,1], c0 in [-1,1]. Start a two-input Gram chain with Q0=R0=s and C0=s*c0. Given each completed past, draw n iid centered Gaussian pairs (Ai,Bi) of covariance [[Ql,Cl],[Cl,Rl]], independently of previous layers, and update Qnew=mean tanh(Ai)^2, Rnew=mean tanh(Bi)^2, Cnew=mean tanh(Ai)tanh(Bi). Put Dl=1-Cl/sqrt(Ql*Rl), el=Ql-Rl, Hl=sum(j=1..l)1/j, H0=0; these variances are positive almost surely. Define K=32768*exp((105/2)*(4+T)), A=K*s*exp(3*T), B=264*exp(264*T)*A. For every integer 0<=l<=T*n: ||Ql*Rl*Dl||_2<=A*D0/(l+1), E(el^4)<=B^2*D0^2*Hl^2/n^2, E(el^2*Ql*Rl*Dl)<=A*B*D0^2*Hl/(n*(l+1)), and E(Ql^2*Rl^2*Dl^2)<=A^2*D0^2/(l+1)^2. Consequently sum(l=0..L-1)||el||_4^2<=B*D0*L*HL/n for 1<=L<=T*n. Norms are probability Lp norms. This uses the independently checked finite-width marginal bound T244-w691-C027 v1 and unaudited one-step lemma T250-w712-C013 v1. It closes the two radial mixed sources, not the stochastic angular gap or the full Tensor Programs rate. No Lean certificate is claimed.

Deterministic equal initial variances s in (0,1], arbitrary c0 in [-1,1], n>=1 and l<=Tn

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6438d50a85b4b0f985c1662c224b717d72d855a1551f851cd14c541d5ec9331c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/64/6438d50a85b4b0f985c1662c224b717d72d855a1551f851cd14c541d5ec9331c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3a6490416b848b395f2baa9a7aed9d2f464c9bebbf32e151bc41dc071efbb6b1","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_radial_mixed_source_closure","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c014-radial-mixed-source-closure","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and stochastic two-input Gram propagation","draft":"w712/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-two-input-radial-mixed-source-fourth-moment-closure","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C014 v1: closing the radial fourth-moment mixed sources

Kind: moved. Target: 1 (two-input critical tanh chain).
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This closes a component of
C013, not the full Tensor Programs target or the stochastic angular error.

## Model and statement

Fix n>=1, horizon T>0, and deterministic initial Gram entries
Q_0=R_0=s in (0,1], C_0=s c_0, -1<=c_0<=1. Set D_0=1-c_0.
At each update the n Gaussian pairs (A_i,B_i), conditional on the past,
are iid with covariance matrix [[Q_l,C_l],[C_l,R_l]]. Define
Q_(l+1)=mean tanh(A_i)^2, R_(l+1)=mean tanh(B_i)^2,
C_(l+1)=mean tanh(A_i)tanh(B_i). All layers use fresh rows.
These matrices are positive semidefinite. Marginal variances are strictly
positive almost surely at each finite layer, and bounded by 1.
Write c_l=C_l/sqrt(Q_l R_l), D_l=1-c_l, e_l=Q_l-R_l,
H_l=sum_(j=1)^l 1/j, H_0=0. Norms below are probability Lp norms.

Use the following conservative explicit constants:

    K_T=32768 exp[(105/2)(4+T)],
    A_T=K_T s exp(3T), B_T=264 exp(264T) A_T.

For every integer 0<=l<=Tn,

    ||Q_l R_l D_l||_2 <= A_T D_0/(l+1),                  (1)
    E[e_l^4] <= B_T^2 D_0^2 H_l^2/n^2,                  (2)
    E[e_l^2 Q_l R_l D_l]
       <= A_T B_T D_0^2 H_l/[n(l+1)],                   (3)
    E[Q_l^2 R_l^2 D_l^2] <= A_T^2 D_0^2/(l+1)^2.       (4)

The constants are not claimed sharp. All expectations refer to the actual
coupled chain; Q and R, and their angular gap, are not independent.

## 1. Settled marginal input

We use T244-w691-C027 v1, equations (11)-(12) of
urn:mb-local:70868895e24d4cc2
The exact version has reviewer urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS in its CLAIMS record;
the proof file retains its historical unaudited heading. Only its
unconditional finite-width moment bound is used, not its conditional
limiting-law consequence. It applies separately to both marginals here:
their shared rows across inputs do not change either marginal kernel.

For order 4, its nonsingleton partition constant is
C_4=6*3+3*3^2+4*15+105=210, and its c=1/2048.
Equation (12) gives, for 2<=l<=Tn,

    ||Q_l||_4 <= [8/(c l)] exp[C_4(4+T)/4]
                <= K_T/(l+1),

because (l+1)/l<=2. At l=0 and 1 the same last bound follows from
Q_l<=1 and K_T>=2. Identical bounds hold for R_l. We take this audited
scalar result as ground; the argument below concerns the coupled gap.

## 2. Unnormalized distance retains its initial-gap scale

Set P_l=Q_l+R_l-2C_l. This is the empirical squared distance and

    P_l=(sqrt(Q_l)-sqrt(R_l))^2+2sqrt(Q_l R_l)D_l >=0.

Given the past, A_i-B_i are iid N(0,P_l). Since tanh is 1-Lipschitz,

    P_(l+1) <= mean (A_i-B_i)^2.

For any integer p>=1, conditionally on the past,

    E[P_(l+1)^p | past]
       <= P_l^p product_(k=0)^(p-1)(1+2k/n)
       <= P_l^p exp[p(p-1)/n].                         (5)

The product is the exact pth moment of chi-square_n divided by n^p:
it follows from the Gaussian-square mgf (1-2t)^(-n/2), differentiating
p times at zero. When P_l=0 the difference is identically zero and (5)
continues to hold. Iterated conditional expectation, not independence of
states at distinct layers, proves

    E P_l^4 <= P_0^4 exp(12l/n),
    ||P_l||_4 <= P_0 exp(3T)=2sD_0 exp(3T).            (6)

## 3. The second mixed source

Let M_l=||Q_l R_l D_l||_2. The nonnegative distance identity gives
2sqrt(Q_l R_l)D_l<=P_l. Hence, pointwise,

    (Q_l R_l D_l)^2 <= Q_l R_l P_l^2/4
                        <= (Q_l+R_l)^2 P_l^2/16.

Cauchy-Schwarz and the triangle inequality now give

    M_l <= (1/4)||Q_l+R_l||_4 ||P_l||_4
          <= K_T s exp(3T)D_0/(l+1).

This proves (1) and (4), without separating dependent factors.

## 4. Closing C013 and the first mixed source

Use C013 v1 equation (1), with its B=e_l^2+8Q_lR_lD_l and a<=1.
C013 is an explicitly identified unaudited dependency; its finite
one-step estimate is not re-proved here. Put z_l=(E e_l^4)^(1/2).
Cauchy-Schwarz bounds E[e_l^2 Q_lR_lD_l]<=z_l M_l.
Expand C013's B and B^2 and take total expectations to obtain

    z_(l+1)^2 <= (1+18/n+1079/n^2)z_l^2
                  +(144/n+17264/n^2)z_l M_l
                  +69056 M_l^2/n^2.                  (7)

All coefficients and variables on the right are nonnegative. Since
528>=18, 69696>=1079, 528>=144, 139392>=17264, and 69696>=69056,
the right side is at most [(1+264/n)z_l+264M_l/n]^2. Thus

    z_(l+1) <= (1+264/n)z_l+264M_l/n.                 (8)

The equal initial variances give z_0=0. Iterating the deterministic
inequality (8), then applying (1), yields for l<=Tn

    z_l <= (264/n) sum_(j=0)^(l-1)
                    (1+264/n)^(l-1-j) M_j
         <= 264 exp(264T) A_T D_0 H_l/n.

Squaring proves (2). The same Cauchy-Schwarz estimate with (1) gives
(3). At l=0 these statements hold directly. If D_0=0 the paired features
coincide at every layer and all four inequalities hold with zero sides.
The case c_0=-1 is permitted and does not require a positive lower gap.

## Scope and remaining obstruction

The two mixed sources named at the end of C013 are now bounded entirely
in terms of the deterministic initial gap and explicit constants.
For L>=1, sum_(l=0)^(L-1) z_l <=B_T D_0 L H_L/n.
In particular H_L<=1+log L. For 0<eps<1 and L<=n^(1-eps),

    (L/n)(1+log L)
       <= [1+2/(exp(1) eps)] sqrt(L/n),

because sqrt(L/n)<=n^(-eps/2), log L<=log n, and
x exp(-eps x/2)<=2/(exp(1)eps) for x>=0.
Thus this accumulated radial source fits the requested sqrt(L/n)
scale, with eps-dependent constants. It does not by itself prove the
angular recursion, a readout Wasserstein bound, or all of Target 1.
The remaining hard step is the stochastic angular-gap recursion with
predictable products and their inverses: a final product depends on
future innovations, so its moment bound cannot simply be multiplied by
a martingale variance. A valid higher-moment martingale argument (or a
different coupling) is still required. No independence shortcut is used

[Prp 2 of arXiv:2506.12755, '{\bf Stochastic intrinsic gradient flows on the Wasserstein space}\footnote{Supported in p'] Assume $(C_1)$. Let $\Lam$ be as in \eqref{eq:Lam}, $\gamma:\RR^d\times\scr P\to (0,\infty)$ be measurable such that $c^{-1}\leq\gamma(\cdot,\cdot)\leq c$
	for some constant $c\in(0,\infty)$ and $\Gamma$ be as in \eqref{eq:Gammadef}.
	
	
	(i) The bilinear form $(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam},C_b^1(\scr P_p))$, defined 
	\begin{equation*}\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}(u,v):=\int_{\scr P_p}\Gamma(u,v)(\mu)\LL(\d\mu),\qquad u,v\in C_b^1(\scr P_p),
	\end{equation*} 
	has a closed extension in $L^2(\scr P_p,\LL)$. Its minimal closed extension yields a quasi-regular, strongly local Dirichlet form $(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam},\D(\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}))$.
	In particular, there exists a non-terminating diffusion $(\Omega, \scr F,$ $(\mu_t)_{t\geq 0}, (\P^\mu)_{\mu\in \scr P_p})$ on $\scr P_p$ which is associated with $\EE^{\gamma,\Lam}$.
	
	(ii) There exist $\phi_{\mu,k}\in L^2(\RR^d\to\RR^d,\mu)$, $k=\N$, $\mu\in\scr P_p$, such that $D_{\phi_{\mu,k}}u:\scr P_p\to\RR$ is measurable for $u\in C_b^1(\scr P_p)$ and 
	\begin{equation*}
		\Gamma(u,v)(\mu)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty D_{\gamma_\mu\phi_{\mu,k}} u(\mu)D_{\phi_{\mu,k}}v(\mu)
	\end{equation*}
	for $\Lam$-a.e.~$\mu\in\scr P_p,$ $u,v\in C_b^1(\scr P_p)$.

[Lemma lem:sinbound of arXiv:2606.08325, 'Digit Mixing under Polynomial Maps'] For all \(u\in\mathbb R\),
			\[
			\sin^2(\pi u)\ge 4\|u\|^2.
			\]
			Consequently, for \(0\le a\le1\),
			\[

body:
Every continuous map f from the closed unit ball B^n in R^n to itself has a fixed point: some x with f(x) = x. Convexity and compactness are what matter: the theorem holds for any nonempty compact convex subset of R^n in place of the ball.

In particular any continuous map of a nonempty closed interval [a,b] into itself has a fixed point. The hypotheses cannot be dropped in general: on S^1 in R^2, the half-turn f(x)=-x is continuous and has no fixed point although S^1 is compact; on R^n for n>=1, f(x)=x+v with v nonzero is continuous and has no fixed point although R^n is convex.

Then the map sending x to the point where the ray from f(x) through x exits the ball is a continuous retraction of the ball onto its boundary sphere. But no such retraction exists: it would induce, on the level of homology (or the fundamental group for n = 2), a factorization of the identity of the sphere through the trivial group of the contractible ball, a contradiction. Hence a fixed point exists. For the interval, g(x)=f(x)-x satisfies g(a)>=0 and g(b)<=0, so the intermediate value theorem gives a zero (the singleton case is immediate). The half-turn fixed-point equation x=-x forces x=0, outside S^1; the translation equation x+v=x forces v=0, a contradiction. To justify the general compact-convex case already stated by the keeper, choose a closed ball containing K and its nearest-point projection P onto K: existence follows from compactness, uniqueness from strict convexity of squared distance, and the projection variational inequalities give ||P(x)-P(y)||<=||x-y||. body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\mathbf a_*\in D$ be a strict local minimum point of $H$, and choose
$\rho>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)\Subset D,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  H(\mathbf b)>H(\mathbf a_*)
  \quad
  \bigl(
  \mathbf b\in\overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)}
  \setminus\{\mathbf a_*\}
  \bigr).
\end{equation}
Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\mathbf a_*,\rho,\kappa,M$, and $R$, such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$\mathbf a_\varepsilon\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_*)$, and let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_\varepsilon).
\]
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper).  If
\begin{equation}
  \eta_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\mathcal D(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})
  +\kappa^2[H(\mathbf a_\varepsilon)-H(\mathbf a_*)]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}

body: The Feynman–Kac formula, named after Richard Feynman and Mark Kac, establishes a link between parabolic partial differential equations and stochastic processes. In 1947, when Kac and Feynman were both faculty members at Cornell University, Kac attended a presentation of Feynman's and remarked that the two of them were working on the same thing from different directions. The Feynman–Kac formula resulted, which proves rigorously a real-valued analogy to Feynman's path integrals. The complex case, needed in quantum mechanics, is still an open question.
title: Feynman–Kac formula

[Theorem 24 (Uniform convergence in probability) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:baseline}--\ref{ass:solutions} and suppose $B,A,S<1$. Then there exists a constant $C>0$, independent of $h$, such that, for every $h>0$, if $\wt\eta\in(1/\alpha,1]$, then
\[
\Pbb\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}>h\right)
\le \frac{C}{h}\left[|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}
+\max\left\{
B^{\frac{\alpha\wt\eta-1}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+1}},
A^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}},
S^{\alpha-1/\wt\eta}
\right\}\right].
\]
If $\wt\eta=1/\alpha$ and $\Theta=\max\{B,A,S\}\in(0,1)$, then
\[
\Pbb\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}>h\right)
\le \frac{C}{h}\left[|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}
+\left(\log\frac1\Theta\right)^{-1}\right].
\]
When $\Theta=0$, the right-hand side is interpreted as $C|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}/h$.

Let Z_t=sum b_n W_t^n. If v is a deterministic Navier-Stokes solution, u(t,x)=v(t,x+Z_t) solves the corresponding stochastic equation by Ito-Wentzell. The Leray projection commutes with constant translations. Obstruction: For spatially varying coefficients the flow is not a translation, the transformed Laplacian has random variable coefficients, and the pressure projection no longer simply commutes. No general endpoint estimate or optimality proof is obtained. The2026 high-probability global result uses chosen noise and smoother initial spaces, so its abstract does not settle this question.

Let X be a variety over a number field k. The set of rational points X(k) diagonally embeds into the Brauer-Manin set X(A_k)^{Br}. Consequently, if X(A_k) is non-empty but X(A_k)^{Br} is empty, then X(k) is empty, providing a Brauer-Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle.

Under (IID)+(UE) transience in direction l gives the Sznitman-Zerner regeneration structure with tau_1 < infinity a.s.; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 2.20). Under (UE) a trap of diameter r holds the walk at most exponentially long in r, so sub-ballistic behaviour needs polynomially rare traps of logarithmic size along the path, which i.i.d. environments do allow; the question is whether the tail P(tau_1 > n) can be as heavy as n^{-1+eps}. The Guerra-Ramirez theorem (T) <=> (T') (2018) settles Open Question 3.28 but neither of these. Recorded as the moment-self-improvement reformulation.

Hence this is the Fourier expansion. There is no constant coefficient. [Proposition 22 (Isotropic range evolution) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] At level $t$, conditionally on
$(L_t,R_t)=(\ell,r)\in\N^2$, the proposed graft rate is
$\ell+r+1$. If $U$ is uniform on $\{-\ell,\ldots,r\}$ and
$(L_t',R_t')$ is an independent copy of $(L_t,R_t)$, then the proposed
update is
\begin{equation}

        (\ell,r)
        \longmapsto
        \bigl(\max\{\ell,L_t'-U\},\max\{r,R_t'+U\}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Null updates are allowed.

body:
[Thm 27 of arXiv:2607.03924, 'Tree Coordinates and Range Martingales for Positive Operator-Valued Measures'] Let $X=\left\{ X_{w}\right\} $ be a bounded self-adjoint
range martingale. Then 
\begin{equation}
Q_{n+1}\left(X\right)-Q_{n}\left(X\right)=\sum_{\left|w\right|=n}E^{1/2}_{w}\Gamma_{w}\left(X\right)E^{1/2}_{w}
\end{equation}
for every $n\geq0$. In particular, $\left\{ Q_{n}\left(X\right)\right\} _{n\geq0}$
is an increasing sequence of positive operators. If 
\[
M=\sup_{w}\left\Vert X_{w}\right\Vert ,
\]
then 
\[
0\leq Q_{n}\left(X\right)\leq M^{2}I
\]
for every $n$. Hence $Q_{n}\left(X\right)$ has a strong limit.

[Proposition of arXiv:2604.17253, 'Large Deviations for the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation with Randomized Quasi-Periodic Ini'] The domain ${\mathrm D}^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}$ admits a canonical identification with
\begin{align*}
{\mathscr D}^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}=
\begin{cases}
\prod_{j=1}^d \mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j}, & \gamma^{(k)}=0,\ k\ge1;\\
\prod_{j=1}^d (\mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j})^3, & \gamma^{(1)}=1;\\
\prod_{j=1}^3 {\mathscr D}^{(k-1,\gamma_j^{(k-1)})}, & \gamma^{(k)}\in(\Gamma^{(k-1)})^3,\ k\ge2.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
This identification is induced by coordinate-wise projection.

More precisely, for each $j=1,\dots,d$, we define the projection
\[
\iota_{x_j}:\left(\prod_{j=1}^d \mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j}\right)^s \to (\mathbb{Z}^{\nu_j})^s,
\quad
\iota_{x_j}\big((q_1^1,\dots,q_d^1),\dots,(q_1^s,\dots,q_d^s)\big)
= (q_j^1,\dots,q_j^s).
\]
The full map $\iota=(\iota_{x_1},\dots,\iota_{x_d})$ induces the above identification. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Given a parametric family {f(.;theta): theta in Theta} and data X, a statistic T(X) is sufficient for theta if the conditional distribution of X given T(X) = t does not depend on theta, for (almost) every value t in the range of T. Equivalently, by the Fisher-Neyman factorization criterion, T is sufficient for theta if and only if the density or pmf factors as f(x;theta) = g(T(x), theta) * h(x) for some functions g >= 0 and h >= 0, where h does not depend on theta.
title: Sufficient Statistic

[Theorem thm:FDT of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] For each mode $i \ge 2$, define $C_i(k) = |c_i|^2 \lambda_i^{2k}$ and $R_i(k) = c_i \lambda_i^k$. Then
\[
\frac{C_i(k+1) - C_i(k)}{C_i(k)} = \lambda_i^2 - 1 = -2\mu_i + \mu_i^2, \qquad
C_i(k) = |R_i(k)|^2,
\]
and summing over $i$ recovers the exact dissipation law (equation eq:modewise-dissipation of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spectral fluctuation-dissipation theorem

[Lemma 12 (Kneser) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $A,B$ be subsets of a locally compact, abelian group $G$ and let $\mu$ 
denote (a version of) the Haar measure on $G$. If there exists an open 
subgroup $H$ such that 
$$
A+B+H=A+B \quad\text{and}\quad \mu(A+B+H) = \mu(A+H) + \mu(B+H)-\mu(H),
$$
then 
$$
\mu(A+B) \geq \mu(A)+\mu(B)-\mu(H).
$$
Otherwise, 
$$
\mu^*(A+B) \geq \mu(A)+\mu(B),
$$
where $\mu^*$ denotes the inner measure induced by $\mu$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Choose positive integers n,L,M,D and D'>=0, parameter bound B>0, token clipping radius R>0, a label bound B_y>=1, and confidence 0<xi<1. Consider fixed-length in-context prediction instances Z=(H,y), with |y|<=B_y almost surely, drawn independently from one meta-distribution. In the paper's setting one first draws a task distribution P, then draws the context and query example iid from P. A transformer has L residual blocks, each consisting of normalized ReLU attention followed by a residual two-layer ReLU MLP; it has token dimension D, at most M attention heads per block, and MLP hidden width at most D'. For S tokens, attention sends h_i to h_i+(1/S) sum_m sum_j ReLU(<Q_m h_i,K_m h_j>) V_m h_j. The MLP sends h to h+W_2 ReLU(W_1 h). Project every input token and every block's output token onto the Euclidean radius-R ball. Read out the designated label coordinate of the final query token and clip it to [-B_y,B_y]. Restrict parameters to the class Theta with norm max_block(max_m{||Q_m||op,||K_m||op}+sum_m ||V_m||op+||W_1||op+||W_2||op)<=B. Write L(theta)=E[(y-prediction_theta(H))^2/2] and let hat theta be any exact empirical minimizer of the same loss over Theta on n independent instances. There is a universal C such that, with probability at least 1-xi, L(hat theta)<=inf_(theta in Theta) L(theta)+C B_y^2 sqrt((L^2(M D^2+D D') log(2+max{B,R,B_y})+log(1/xi))/n). This is an expected loss over the meta-distribution. Source: arXiv:2306.04637, Section 5.1 and Theorem 20, PDF pages 14–15; proof Appendix J.2, PDF page 89. The harmless choice B_y>=1 is stated explicitly here; any smaller valid label bound may be enlarged to one.
n,L,M,D positive integers; D'>=0; B,R>0; B_y>=1; 0<xi<1
The n pretraining instances are iid from the same meta-distribution and the query label is bounded by B_y
Normalized ReLU attention, residual ReLU MLP, input and hidden-token Euclidean projection at radius R, and prediction clipping at B_y
The specified transformer parameter norm is at most B and hat theta is an exact constrained empirical risk minimizer

Own-work draft; status independently checked proof. For iid finite nonnegative tooth heights with P(H_0>t)~C t^(-1/3), C>0, two independent discrete-time simple random walks started together at the backbone origin have infinitely many backbone collision times almost surely for almost every environment. The candidate proof counts only collisions at the positive-density good roots of I0012-L1 v1. Source Lemma 4.9 supplies a constant first moment in a scale-N time window of order N^3; the good-root collision Green sum gives E[Z_N^2]<=E[Z_N] O(1+log N), hence P(Z_N>0)>=c/(1+log N). Adapted geometric exit blocks and an explicit conditional product argument yield infinitely many successes. No independence of different blocks is assumed. The result is conditional on source Lemmas 4.9 and 4.10 and Proposition 4.11 at gamma=1/3 and on a nonempty Lemma 4.9 time window; Lemma 4.8, on which that window rests, prints an impossible unrestricted time range (see the Lemma 4.8 caveat card). Complete proof: proofs/I0012-C1_v1.md. Audit dispositions: w667 PASS on version 1; w668 PASS on version 1.

body: In first-passage percolation on Z^2 with edge weights confined to [a, b] with a > 0, any geodesic from the origin to (0, r) satisfies a DETERMINISTIC bound on its transversal excursion: it never attains transversal level D > r(b - a)/(2a). The proof is elementary counting: reaching transversal level D forces at least r + 2D edges, each of weight at least a, giving passage time at least a(r + 2D), while the straight path gives at most b r; the two are incompatible beyond the stated level. No probabilistic input is used, so the bound holds for every realisation.

body:
Agresti and Veraar, Nonlinear parabolic stochastic evolution equations in critical spaces (journal version 2025, p. 130), Problem 4 asks whether in the variational setting of their Theorem 6.4 there is a constant C_T with E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 <= C_T (1 + E ||u_0||_H^2) for all u_0 in L^2(Omega; H). Our result (id P0266, 2026-09-08): the bound FAILS, on the authors' own named unresolved example - Allen-Cahn on the one-dimensional torus with one-dimensional quadratic noise, du = (Laplacian u + u - u^3) dt + gamma u^2 dW, at the critical gamma^2 = 2. With deterministic constant data u_0 = a > 0 the solution stays spatially constant, and the substitutions Y = 1/U, Y = e^{-t} V, time change s = (e^{2t} - 1)/2 and R = V / sqrt 2 turn the SDE into R being a four-dimensional Bessel process started at R_0 = 1/(sqrt 2 a), with U_t = e^t / (sqrt 2 R_s). Since sup_{t <= T} U_t^2 >= 1/(2 inf_{s <= S} R_s^2) and a BES(4) enters a ball of radius x with probability of order x^2 (Newtonian capacity), P(sup U^2 > y) is of order 1/y - tail index one - so E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 = infinity for every T > 0 while E ||u_0||_H^2 = a^2 is finite. Verification as the source words it: checked in the reverse direction by Ito as well; and an instrument note - a first simulation appeared to contradict the x^2 scaling, but refining the steps at fixed x drives P/x^2 toward the exact constant 2.0 (1.204, 1.579, 1.697 at x = 0.2 and 0.725, 1.285, 1.455 at x = 0.1), so the scaling is real. NOT Lean-checked: this one has no finite arithmetic core, being Ito calculus plus a capacity estimate. Prior art not cleared; the source is a year old, so the memo rates this among the likeliest to be genuinely new.

[Corollary cor:iterated-suspension of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$ and put $A^{(0)}=A$.  For each $1\leq i\leq t$, choose an
integer $\ell_i\geq2$ and a specified $c_i$ having a length-$\ell_i$
representation by points of $A^{(i-1)}$ with $\gcd(c_i,\ell_i)=1$, and set
$A^{(i)}=\Sigma_{\ell_i,c_i}A^{(i-1)}$.  Put
$R=\prod_{i=1}^t\ell_i$, with the empty product equal to one.  Then, for
$q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H_{A^{(t)}}(z)
 &=\mathcal H_A(z)\prod_{i=1}^t[\ell_i]_z,
 \\
 |qA^{(t)}|
 &=\sum_{\substack{0\leq j_i<\ell_i\\
                    j_1+\cdots+j_t\leq q}}
   |(q-j_1-\cdots-j_t)A|,
 \\
 \mathcal K_{A^{(t)}}(z)
 &=\mathcal K_A(z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1-z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \mathcal B_{A^{(t)}}(\xi,z)
 &=\mathcal B_A(\xi,z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1+\xi z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \operatorname{ndiam}(A^{(t)})&=R\operatorname{ndiam}(A).
 
\end{align}
If every $\ell_i\leq q$, then
\[
 r_q(A^{(t)})=r_q(A)+t,\qquad
 \operatorname{fdim}_q(A^{(t)})=\operatorname{fdim}_q(A).
\]
If the starting projective coordinate ring is ACM, then the ACM property
and Cohen--Macaulay type are preserved.

Kind: route-failure. Target1. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unresolved.

For every 0<mu<1, rank r=2 and p=3, the C029 reduced weighted-Stiefel flow has an open positive-Gaussian-probability set of initially full-rank signal overlaps whose determinant crosses zero at a finite positive time. The construction embeds into every r>=2,p>r and any unequal pair of positive target singular values. This is not a counterexample to eventual convergence; it blocks quantitative arguments that require signal overlap to remain invertible or its determinant to stay positive throughout the reduced trajectory.

Take H=diag(1,mu^2,0), M=[[2,-1],[-1,2]], M^(-1)=(1/3)[[2,1],[1,2]], and

Y_*=[[3/5,4/5,0],[0,0,1]].

This is an exactly row-orthonormal frame. Its two-by-two target-signal block S_* is [[3/5,4/5],[0,0]], so det(S_*)=0. Let v=(3/5,4/5), x=(-4/5,3/5), and follow the smooth autonomous flow

Y'=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^TY).

The signal block obeys S'=M^(-1)S diag(1,mu^2)(I-S^TS). At Y_*, the derivative of its determinant is the component of the second row derivative along x:

D'(0) = (1/3) v diag(1,mu^2) x^T
      = (4/25)(mu^2-1) <0.

Compactness of St ensures that the flow through Y_* exists both forward and backward in time. Since D(0)=0 and D'(0)<0, for all sufficiently small delta>0 its determinant is positive at time -delta and negative at time +delta. Start instead at the full-signal-rank frame Y(-delta): it crosses zero after a finite positive time. Strict signs at the two endpoints persist under perturbations of both the initial frame and the SPD parameter M, by continuous dependence on initial conditions and parameters. Thus the crossing is present on an open subset of SPD_2 times St(2,3).

The smooth polar map G=M^(1/2)Y takes this to an open set of full-row-rank 2-by-3 matrices. Every nonempty open subset has positive iid-Gaussian probability. The initial signal block of G is invertible because both M^(1/2) and S_initial are invertible. This is therefore an obstruction on a positive-probability Gaussian set, rather than just a specially chosen measure-zero initialization.

For an exact algebra fixture mu=1/2, the derivative is -3/25. A nearby rational full-signal-rank frame is obtained by keeping the first row v and replacing the second by (a x_1,a x_2,b), with a=2q/(1+q^2), b=(1-q^2)/(1+q^2), q=1/10^6. Its determinant is a>0 and its instantaneous determinant derivative is strictly negative by exact rational arithmetic. This fixture checks the local derivative; the analytic transverse-crossing argument above proves existence of a crossing. No floating-point trajectory or interval integration is used.

For r>2, append signal-aligned orthonormal rows, identity blocks to M, and arbitrary additional positive diagonal target singular values; add zero input columns if p>r+1. Those aligned rows are stationary and the two-by-two crossing is unchanged. The open-set argument again gives positive probability in the full-dimensional Gaussian model. For unequal positive values lambda_i>lambda_j, the derivative scales to (4/25)(lambda_j^2-lambda_i^2)<0. Output dimensions m>=r only require embedding the target's positive output coordinates.

If M is scalar, or the two positive singular values coincide, the displayed transverse derivative vanishes. This explains why the flat-spectrum arguments do not supply this unequal-spectrum barrier automatically. C029's convergence proof does not require signal overlap to stay nonsingular, so C030 does not contradict that claim.

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p_0 < p_1 <= infinity, and let T be a SUBLINEAR operator defined on L^{p_0}(mu) + L^{p_1}(mu) with values in the measurable functions on Y, which is of WEAK type (p_0, p_0) with constant A_0 and of weak type (p_1, p_1) with constant A_1 (for p_1 = infinity this means ||Tf||_infinity <= A_1 ||f||_infinity). Then for every p with p_0 < p < p_1, T is of strong type (p,p): ||Tf||_{L^p(nu)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(mu)} for all f in L^p(mu), where one may take C = 2 (p/(p - p_0) + p/(p_1 - p))^{1/p} A_0^{1-theta} A_1^{theta} with 1/p = (1-theta)/p_0 + theta/p_1, and the term p/(p_1 - p) is read as 0 when p_1 = infinity. The constant blows up as p tends to p_0 or to p_1, and the conclusion genuinely fails at the endpoints. Off-diagonal version: if T is of weak types (p_0, q_0) and (p_1, q_1) with p_0 not equal to p_1, q_0 not equal to q_1, and p_i <= q_i for i = 0,1, then T is of strong type (p_theta, q_theta) for 0 < theta < 1, with 1/p_theta and 1/q_theta the interpolated exponents.

[Lemma lem:fromboxestointegrals of arXiv:2609.01825, 'On everywhere locally soluble varieties \\ in families over toric bases'] Let $\vec W = (\log (B/X_1), \dots, \log (B/X_k)) = (\log \theta) \vec U_{\!-}$ and $1< \theta \leq 2$. Then for $\gamma > \max_{1\leq l\leq k} \sum_{i=1}^s \frac{\varpi_{li}}{\alpha_i}$ we have
	\begin{multline*}
		\sum_{\vec j \in \cal P(\vec U_{\!-})} \sum_{\vec x \in \cal B_{\vec j}} f(\vec x)
		= c_f \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^s \alpha_i^{-\ell_i}\Bigr) \int_{\cal P(\vec W)}  \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (1+t_i )^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t\\
		+ O\biggl(
		C_f (\log \theta)^{-s} \int_{\cal P(\vec W)} \bigl(1 + \min\nolimits_i t_i\bigr)^{-\delta} \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (1 + t_i)^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t
		\biggr)\\
		+ O\biggl(
		C_f \int_{\Xi'} \prod_{i=1}^s \mathrm e^{t_i} (1 + t_i)^{\ell_i} \,\mathrm d\vec t
		\biggr),
	\end{multline*}
	where
	\begin{equation*}
		\Xi' = \cal P(\vec W) \setminus \cal P(\vec W - (\gamma \log \theta, \dots, \gamma \log \theta)).
	\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 11 of arXiv:2512.19063, 'Sharp Decoupling Inequalities for the Variances and Second Moments of Sums of Dependent Ra'] With the same setting as Theorem 6, we have a Chebyshev-type inequality for any $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(|S_{n}-\mathbb{E} S_{n}|>t\right)\leq\frac{2\operatorname{Var}(S^{\prime}_{n})}{t^{2}}.$ (15) If in addition $S_{n}\geq 0$ a.s., we have a Paley-Zygmund-type inequality for any $0<\theta<1$, $\mathbb{P}(S_{n}>\theta\,\mathbb{E} S_{n})\geq(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}-(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}=(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{1}{\frac{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}}{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}-1}.$

[Lemma 2 (Theorem 7.11, \cite{Fen10}) of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] Suppose $\bm{X} = (X_1, X_2, \ldots) \sim \PD(\alpha, \theta)$. Let 
\bal
\tilde{H}_m(\alpha, \theta) = \sqrt{\theta}\left( \frac{\theta^{m-1}}{(1 - \alpha)_{(m-1)}}  \sum_{i = 1}^\infty X_i^m - 1 \right), \qquad m \geq 2,
\eal
be the scaled $m$th order homozygosity. Then
\bal
(\tilde{H}_2(\alpha, \theta), \tilde{H}_3(\alpha, \theta), \ldots) \xrightarrow{D} (H_2(\alpha), H_3(\alpha), \ldots)
\eal
as $\theta \to \infty$, where $\bm{H} = (H_2(\alpha), H_3(\alpha), \ldots)$ is a $\R^\infty$-valued random vector such that for all $r \geq 2$, $(H_2(\alpha), \ldots, H_r(\alpha))$ has a multivariate normal distribution with zero mean and covariance matrix
\bal
\cov(H_i(\alpha), H_j(\alpha)) = \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(i+j-1)}}{(1 - \alpha)_{(i-1)}(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}} + \alpha - ij, \qquad i,j = 2, \ldots, r.
\eal (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7.11, \cite{Fen10}

body: [Corollary adj8 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1\leq p<\infty$. Suppose that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact and that $Y$ is a Banach space with the $\mathrm{DP}^*\mathrm{P}_p$ such that $B_{Y^*}$ is weak$^{*}$ sequentially compact. Then $(X,Y)$ has the $\mathrm{SMP}_p$ if and only if $(Y^*,X^*)$ has the weak$^*$-to-weak$^*$ maximizing property. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. For 0 <= rho <= 1, (1 - rho) Var(f) <= D_rho(f) <= (1 - rho^n) Var(f). For 0 < rho < 1 and nonconstant f, equality on the left holds iff all the nonconstant Walsh mass is at level 1, and on the right iff it is at level n; at rho = 0 and rho = 1 both bounds are equalities for every f. If 0 <= rho < sigma <= 1 then D_rho(f) >= D_sigma(f), strictly when f is not constant. No such monotonicity holds on [-1, 1]: D_rho(x_1 x_2) = 1 - rho^2 increases on [-1, 0].

Let N=N(n) with N/n->c in (0,infinity). For all n,i,j let X_ij^(n) be real independent identically distributed random variables with mean zero, variance one, and E|X_ij^(n)|^(4+epsilon)<infinity for some epsilon>0. Let sigma_ij(n) be deterministic real numbers uniformly bounded in absolute value. Let A_n be deterministic real N-by-n matrices whose row Euclidean norms and column Euclidean norms are uniformly bounded over all n and all rows and columns. Put (Y_n)_ij=sigma_ij(n) X_ij^(n)/sqrt(n) and Sigma_n=Y_n+A_n. For the relevant N,n, write A=A_n and sigma_ij=sigma_ij(n), D_j=diag(sigma_1j^2,...,sigma_Nj^2), and Dtilde_i=diag(sigma_i1^2,...,sigma_in^2). Let S_plus consist of the functions z->integral_[0,infinity) (lambda-z)^(-1) nu(dlambda) for probability measures nu on [0,infinity), analytically continued to C minus [0,infinity). Define the unique S_plus-valued solution psi_i,psitilde_j by psi_i(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(Dtilde_i Ttilde(z))/n)] and psitilde_j(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(D_j T(z))/n)], where Psi=diag(psi_i), Psitilde=diag(psitilde_j), T(z)=[Psi(z)^(-1)-z A Psitilde(z) A^T]^(-1), and Ttilde(z)=[Psitilde(z)^(-1)-z A^T Psi(z) A]^(-1). Both trace terms in these canonical equations use division by n. Let P_n be the empirical eigenvalue probability measure of Sigma_n Sigma_n^T and pi_n the deterministic probability measure with Stieltjes transform tr(T_n(z))/N. Then, for every n, E integral lambda P_n(dlambda) = integral lambda pi_n(dlambda) = (1/(N n)) sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^n sigma_ij(n)^2 + tr(A_n A_n^T)/N. In particular both first moments are bounded uniformly in n by sigma_max^2+a_max^2, where sigma_max bounds all |sigma_ij(n)| and a_max bounds all row and column Euclidean norms of A_n. The empirical first moment appears under expectation in this equality; the deterministic first-moment identity is exact, not merely asymptotic.

uniformly bounded deterministic variance profile sigma_ij
deterministic real means A_n with uniformly bounded Euclidean row AND column norms
noise normalization Y_ij=sigma_ij X_ij/sqrt(n)
P_n is the N-normalized empirical spectral measure

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.26084, 'Localic Esakia Duality\\via Conic Frames'] Let~$(X,\leq)$ be a Priestley space. A subset~$C\subseteq X$ is called a \emph{clopen upper set} if~$C$ is clopen and~$\up C= C$. The collection of clopen upper sets is denoted~$\ClopUp(X)$, and forms a distributive lattice under set-theoretic intersections and unions.

	If~$(X,\leq)$ is an Esakia space, then~$\ClopUp(X)$ moreover forms a Heyting algebra, with implication given for clopen upper sets~$A,B\subseteq X$ by~(\cite[\S 2]{bezhanishvili2023FrametheoreticPerspectiveEsakia}):
	\[
	A\to B
	:=
	X\setminus \down (A\setminus B).
	\]
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2608.26084

[Lemma 4 (Stopped physical-state stability) of arXiv:2608.19151, 'Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning for Controlled Hawkes Jump-Diffusions'] Suppose that Assumption~\ref{ass:standing}(S1) holds. Fix
$K\geq1$ and $a\in\mathcal A$. Let
\[
    (X^a,N^a,\lambda^a)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    (X^{K,a},N^{K,a},\lambda^{K,a})
\]
be constructed with the same Brownian motion, the same Poisson random
measures, the same initial condition, and the same admissible control
process $a$. For $R\geq1$, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_R^{K,a}
:=
\inf\Bigl\{
t\in[0,T]:\;&
\norm{N_t^{K,a}}_1+\norm{N_t^a}_1>R
&\text{or }\norm{X_t^{K,a}}>R
\text{ or }\norm{X_t^a}>R
\Bigr\}
\wedge T.
\end{aligned}
\]
Set
\[
D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
:=
\E\left[
    \sup_{0\leq u\leq t}
    \norm{
        X_{u\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}^{K,a}
        -
        X_{u\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}^a
    }
\right],
\]
and
\[
D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t)
:=
\E\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_R^{K,a}}
\norm{\lambda_s^{K,a}-\lambda_s^a}_1\,\dd s.
\] Then, for every $R\geq1$, there exists
$C_{T,R}<\infty$, independent of $K$ and
$a\in\mathcal A$, such that
\begin{equation}

D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
\leq
C_{T,R}\int_0^tD_{X,R}^{K,a}(s)\,\dd s
+
C_{T,R}D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t),
\qquad
0\leq t\leq T.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}

D_{X,R}^{K,a}(t)
\leq
C_{T,R}D_{\lambda,R}^{K,a}(t),
\qquad
0\leq t\leq T.
\end{equation}

body: [Lemma 6 (Bennett's integral \citep{bennett1948spectra}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] For a high-resolution quantizer with local step $\Delta(x)$ and input density $p$ whose overload distortion is negligible, as holds in particular when $p$ is supported within the quantizer's granular range, the distortion is $D=\tfrac{1}{12}\int \Delta(x)^2 p(x)\,dx$, the integral taken over that range. For a uniform quantizer ($\Delta$ constant, overload negligible) this reduces to the additive-white-noise model $D=\Delta^2/12$, with quantization error approximately uniform on $[-\Delta/2,\Delta/2]$ and decorrelated from the signal. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bennett's integral \citep{bennett1948spectra}

Let (X_n) be a martingale for (F_n) and let (H_n)_{n >= 1} be PREDICTABLE, meaning H_n is F_{n-1}-measurable. Define the transform (H . X)_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} H_k (X_k - X_{k-1}), with (H . X)_0 = 0. If each H_n is bounded (or, more generally, if H_n (X_n - X_{n-1}) is integrable for every n), then (H . X) is a martingale. If (X_n) is a SUPERMARTINGALE and in addition H_n >= 0 for every n, then (H . X) is a supermartingale; the same with submartingale. Predictability is the load-bearing hypothesis: H_n may depend on everything known strictly before time n but not on the outcome at time n. Without it the conclusion is false - taking H_n = sgn(X_n - X_{n-1}) gives (H . X)_n = sum |X_k - X_{k-1}|, which is nondecreasing and not a martingale unless the increments vanish. The nonnegativity requirement in the supermartingale case is also necessary, since multiplying by -1 turns a supermartingale into a submartingale. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Section 10.6]

[Theorem 4 (Local-in-time theory) of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Under Assumption~\ref{Hypo-Q}, let
		\[
		s>\frac{3}{2}+\max\{2\delta_{\mathcal Q},1\}.
		\]
		For every $H^s$-valued $\mathcal F_0$-measurable random variable $v_0$,
		the Cauchy problem \eqref{Target problem SCCF} admits a pathwise unique maximal
		$H^s$ classical solution $(v,\tau^*)$ in the sense of
		Definition~\ref{Def : solution}.
		Moreover,  the maximal lifetime $\tau^*$ is independent of the Sobolev index $s$: if $v_0$
		belongs to two admissible Sobolev spaces, then the corresponding maximal
		lifetimes coincide; and
		the following blow-up criterion also holds:
		\begin{equation}
			\limsup_{t\uparrow\tau^*}
			\left(
			\|\partial_xv(t)\|_{L^\infty}
			+
			\|\Lambda v(t)\|_{L^\infty}
			\right)
			=\infty\quad
			\text{a.s. on}\ \left\{\tau^*<\infty\right\},
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem teo_fey_kac of arXiv:2605.07832, 'A Bismut -Elworthy formula for BSDEs with degenerate noise'] Let hypotheses (ip_forward of the paper), (ip_forward_agg of the paper) and (ip-psiphi of the paper)
hold true.  Moreover assume that $\phi$ is G\^ateaux differentiable with bounded derivative and that $\psi$ is G\^ateaux differentiable with respect to $x$, $y$ and $z$ \textcolor{red}{with bounded derivatives}. The nonlinear Kolmogorov equation ((Kolmo of the paper)) has a unique mild solution $v$ given by the formula
$$v(t, x) = Y_t^{t,x} ,\qquad     (t, x) \in [0, T ] \times H,$$
where $(X^{t,x},Y ^{t,x} , Z^{ t,x} )$ is the solution to the FBSDE (equation fbsde of the paper). Moreover, we
have, $\mathbb P$-a.s.,
\begin{align}

Y_s^{t,x} = v(s, X_s^{t,x} ),\quad       Z_s^{t,x} =\nabla_x v(s, X_s^{t,x} )\nabla_x  X_s^{t,x}G(s)
\end{align}
and, under our assumptions, there exists a constant $C$, that may depend also on $\nabla_x\phi$,
$\nabla_x\psi$ and $L_\psi$, such that
\begin{equation}
\vert Z_s^{t,x}\vert \leq C.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:from-r-to-l of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let the graph $G$ be finite and take $0\le l\le r$. We endow the subdivided graph $G_r$
  with i.i.d.\ edge weights $W_e>0$, $e\in E_r$. Consider the family $W^{(l)}$ of
  corresponding random weights
from Theorem (thm:vrjp-on-G-r-pos-rec of the paper), all realized on the same probability space
with expectation operator ${\mathbb E}$. We abbreviate
$C_\alpha:=2^{-\alpha}\Gamma(\tfrac12-\alpha)/\sqrt{\pi}$
for $0\le\alpha<\frac12$ and ${c_2}:=\gamma+\log 2=1.27036\ldots$, where 
\begin{align}
  
  \gamma=-\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\log t\, dt=0.57721\ldots
\end{align}
denotes the Euler Mascheroni constant. 
For all $\bar e\in E_l$ and $e'\in E_r$, one has
  \begin{align}
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
    &\le (2^{-\alpha})^{r-l}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]
    &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,1],\\
    
    {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]
     &\le \frac{1}{C_\alpha}\min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}\left(C_\alpha 
       (2^{-\alpha})^{r-m}{\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha]\right)^{2^{m-l}}
     &\hspace{-1cm}\text{ for } \alpha\in[0,\tfrac12),
    \\
      
    {\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{\bar e}]
    &\le \min_{m\in\{l,\ldots,r\}}
      2^{m-l}\left({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]-(r-m)\log 2+{c_2}\right)-{c_2}.
  \end{align}
  Set $m_0:=r-2-\lfloor\alpha^{-1}\log_2(C_\alpha {\mathbb E}[W_{e'}^\alpha])\rfloor$
  and $m_1:=r-2-\lfloor(\log 2)^{-1}({\mathbb E}[\log W_{e'}]+{c_2})\rfloor$.
  If $m_0\in\{l,\ldots,r\}$, a minimizer in (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper)
  is given by $m=m_0$. If $m_0<l$ or $m_0>r$, it is given by
  $m=l$ or $m=r$, respectively. The analogous statement holds for $m_1$
  with (equation eq:combined-alpha of the paper) replaced by (equation eq:combined-log of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Decay of the effective weights by restriction

[Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $f\in \mathcal D_I$.
  \begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item 
      The  {\em extended graph} of $f$ is defined as
      $$
        \mathbb G(f)
         := \bigcup_{t\in I}\big(\{t\} \times [\min(f(t-),f(t)), \max(f(t-),f(t))]\big).
      $$
      Thus, in  words from~[K23], the extended graph  ``contains the graph together with the straight lines connecting the two ends of a jump discontinuity''.
    \item 
      A~{\em parametric representation} of (the extended graph of) $f$ is a mapping $\phi$ which maps $[0,1]$ onto $\mathbb G(f)$ and for which $u \mapsto \phi(u)$ is increasing with respect to the total order $\preceq$ on $\mathbb G(f)$ defined by
      $$
        (t_1,x_1)\preceq (t_2,x_2) :\Longleftrightarrow t_1\le t_2
          \mbox{ and } \left(t_1=t_2 \Rightarrow |x_1 - f(t_1-)| \le |x_2 - f(t_1-)|\right).
      $$
  \end{enumerate}
title: Definition defextgraph of arXiv:2605.10617

[Lem mass-from-high-to-low of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] For every $(\tilde z_0,\tilde v_0) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times S^{n-1}$ and $\eta \in (0, \eta^*(\tilde z_0))$ there is some $\delta, C > 0$ such that for all $(z_0,v_0)$ with $$\|\tilde z_0 - z_0\| + \|\tilde v_0 - v_0\| \leq \delta$$

    $$\mathbb{P}\Big(\sup_{t \leq C\ln\epsilon^{-1}} \|P_\eta(z_0)v^\epsilon(t)\| \geq \delta \Big) \geq \delta$$
    (where the process $(z^\epsilon(t), v^\epsilon(t))$ is defined as in (equation eq:zv-def of the paper) with initial condition $(z_0,v_0)$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 3 of arXiv:2601.22205, 'Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares'] A Latin square is based on a group if it is isotopic to a Cayley table of a group. A set of cells meeting each row and each column exactly once, whose entries are all distinct, is a transversal of a Latin square. Suppose L = {lij} is the Cayley table of a quasigroup Q = {q0, . . . , qn−1} and T = {(0, j0), . . . , (n −1, jn−1)} is a transversal of L. Then the map θ: Q →Q defined by θ(qi) = qji is a bijection.
title: Definition 3 of arXiv:2601.22205: Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares
