[Lemma 13 (Boundary repair) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $d,K,M,N,L\in\N^+$ and $0<\delta\le1/(3K)$.
Let $\widetilde\Phi$ be a $d$-input architecture in $\Arch(N,L)$ and
$\widetilde\calA\in\aff(M,P_{\widetilde\Phi})$ be given.  There are
$\Phi\in\Arch(3^d(N+4),L+2d)$ and
$\calA\in\aff(M,P_\Phi)$, constructed solely from
$(\widetilde\Phi,\widetilde\calA,K,\delta)$, with the following property.
For every $f\in C([0,1]^d)$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, and
$\bmxi_f\in\R^M$, set
$\widetilde{\bmtheta}_f:=\widetilde\calA(\bmxi_f)$.  If
\[
 \lvert f(\bmx)
 -\widetilde\Phi_{\widetilde{\bmtheta}_f}(\bmx)\rvert
 \le\varepsilon,\qquad
 \bmx\in[0,1]^d\setminus\Omega_{K,\delta},
\]
then, with $\bmtheta_f:=\calA(\bmxi_f)$,
\begin{equation*}
 \lvert f(\bmx)-\Phi_{\bmtheta_f}(\bmx)\rvert
 \le\varepsilon+d\omega_f(\delta),\qquad \bmx\in[0,1]^d.
\end{equation*}

    $$

body:
Own work method record, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C015 v1. Standard Gaussian-conditioning technique; no specialist novelty asserted. For real A with iid N(0,1) entries, deterministic unit x_*, independent x_0, fixed eta>0 and quartic phase-retrieval GD x_(t+1)=x_t-(eta/m)A^T r_t, r_t=((Ax_t)^2-(Ax_*)^2) elementwise times Ax_t, let Q_t=[x_*,x_0,...,x_t], Y_t=AQ_t, M_t=[r_0,...,r_(t-1)], e_t=P_(M_t)^perp r_t and k_t=d-rank Q_t. Conditional on the chronological transcript through Ax_t, A^T r_t=(Q_t^dagger)^T Y_t^T r_t+||e_t||P_(Q_t)^perp z_t for fresh standard Gaussian z_t. When e_t!=0, K_t=||P_(Q_t)^perp A^T r_t||^2/||e_t||^2 is conditionally chi-square_(k_t). After revealing A^T r_t, with q=x_(t+1), the next forward query equals in conditional law Y_t Q_t^dagger q-(eta/m)K_t e_t+||P_(Q_t)^perp q||P_[M_t,r_t]^perp u_t, with fresh standard Gaussian u_t. If e_t=0 the next query is already known and the reaction term is zero. For deterministic finite T and delta in (0,1), L=log(2T/delta), all nondegenerate t<T satisfy |K_t-k_t|<=2sqrt(k_t L)+2L simultaneously with probability at least 1-delta. For m=ceil(alpha*d), the scalar reaction coefficient obeys |eta*K_t/m-eta/alpha|<=(eta/m)(2sqrt(d L)+2L+T+2+1/alpha). The history projection and cubic residuals are retained, not controlled; no escape or convergence theorem is proved. Proof idea: conditional Gaussian matrices are their minimum-norm constrained mean plus P_M^perp G P_Q^perp. Every earlier backward image belongs to span Q through the GD update, so the backward mean simplifies. After the next backward query, the minimum-norm dual of the new residual direction is e_t/||e_t||^2. Its projection onto the next GD query gives the displayed reaction term. Gaussian chi-square tails are conditioned on each chronological transcript and union-bounded over the deterministic horizon; no independence of adaptive K_t is assumed. No stopped Gaussian list is called iid. The full-history projection and residual-correlation bounds needed for escape remain unproved.
real standard Gaussian matrix; deterministic unit signal; x_0 independent of A
fixed positive GD step and the stated quartic normalization by 1/(4m)
chronological forward/backward linear-query transcript, enlarged by the signed Ax_* only for analysis; no conditioning on future events
orthogonal projectors and Moore-Penrose inverses; dependent query columns allowed; deterministic finite horizon cap
title: Draft: Adaptive Gaussian matrix conditioning for phase-retrieval GD and its chi-square reaction coefficient

body:
[Theorem th:gamma of arXiv:2411.06838, 'Generalized Wasserstein Barycenters'] Let $(\lambda_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\lambda$ be signed measures on $\mathcal{P}_2(H)$, satisfying (equation eq:hypotheses of the paper). Assume that
\begin{align}
	\lim_{k\to \infty} \int_{\mathcal{P}_2(H)}\varphi(\nu)\,{\rm d}\lambda^{\pm}_k(\nu) &= \int_{\mathcal{P}_2(H)}\varphi(\nu)\,{\rm d}\lambda^{\pm}(\nu) \qquad \forall \varphi \in C^0_b(X),\\
	\lim_{k\to \infty} \int_{\mathcal{P}_2(H)}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d} |\lambda_k|(\nu) &= \int_{\mathcal{P}_2(H)}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d} |\lambda|(\nu).
\end{align}
Let $\mathcal{E}_k:\mathcal{P}_2(H) \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as
\[
	\mathcal{E}_k(\mu):= \int_{\mathcal{P}_2(H)} W_2^2(\nu,\mu){\rm d}\lambda_k(\nu).
\]
Then

(i) $\mathcal{E}_k$ $\Gamma$-converges to $\mathcal{E}$ in $\mathcal{P}_2(H)$, with respect to the convergence induced by the 2-Wasserstein distance, and also with respect to the weak topology of $\mathcal{P}_2^w(H)$;

(ii) If $\mu_k$  is a minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_k$ for all $k\in \mathbb{N}$, the sequence $(\mu_k)_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ is precompact with respect to the weak topology of $\mathcal{P}_2^w(H)$;

(iii) As a consequence of (i) and (ii),  if $\overline{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_2(H)$ is a limit point in $\mathcal{P}_2^w(H)$ of a subsequence of minimizers $(\mu_{k_j})$, then
	\[
		\lim_{j \to \infty} \mathcal{E}_{k_j}(\mu_{k_j}) = \mathcal{E}(\overline{\mu})=\min_{\mu \in \mathcal{P}_2(H)}\mathcal{E}(\mu).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:gamma of arXiv:2411.06838

body:
[Lemma le:divisibility of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] Let $\mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{asym}}$ be the subspace of $\mathcal{H}_n$ of
  antisymmetric elements of $\mathcal{H}_n$. Then
  \begin{equation}
    \mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{asym}}=V_n\mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{div}}
    \quad\text{where}\quad
    \mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{div}} = \{h\in
    L^2(\mu_n):V_nh\in\mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{asym}}\}.
  \end{equation}
  Equivalently, for every antisymmetric holomorphic $g\in L^2(\gamma_n)$, we have
  $g=V_nf$ for a symmetric holomorphic $f\in L^2(\mu_n)$. Moreover, for every
  symmetric $f\in L^2(\mu_n)$,
  \begin{equation}
    \operatorname{dist}_{L^2(\gamma_n)}(V_nf,\mathcal{H}_n)^2
    =
    c_n'\operatorname{dist}_{L^2(\mu_n)}(f,\mathcal{H}_n^{\mathrm{div}})^2.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Divisibility

body: Ross's second conjecture (the mean workload of an M/G/1 queue in a Markov-modulated random environment is non-increasing in the environment's speed c) is false. With a 64-state cyclic environment (rates d = tan(pi/m) + eta, m = 64, covariance 4 + (1/2) e^{-dt} cos t), arrival modulation g injective over 64 values in (1,3) with mean 2, and service law U[0.99, 1.01], the second-order coefficient satisfies Delta = I_d(3 pi) - I_d(2 pi) = +0.0044 > 0 (2.64 times the required 1/600), so the mean workload increases between speeds 2 pi and 3 pi for arrival intensity eps below about 3.3e-4; the effect is about 1e-11 in absolute workload. The expansion E[V] = eps a b2/2 + eps^2 b1 (Int k_B) a^2 + R with R <= eps^3 M^3 b1^2 b2 / (2 (1 - eps M b1)) reproduces Pollaczek-Khinchine exactly in a constant environment with the remainder bound attained, and an exact QBD (exponential service) confirms it uniformly in c. The construction escapes Bauerle-Rolski (not reversible: detailed balance violated by 0.159) and Chang-Chao-Pinedo (row rates take two distinct values). Service criterion: a reversal needs H_B(s) = E[1 - cos(sB)]/s^2 non-monotone (Erlang-20 gives none; U[0.99, 1.01] does).

body:
[Lemma lem:component_boundary_intersection of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $z,w \in \mathbf{H}$ distinct points and let $U_1$ (resp.\ $U_2$) be the connected component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus {\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ containing $z$ (resp.\ $w$).  Then we have that:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item On the event that $\partial U_1 \cap \partial U_2 \neq \emptyset$ and $U_1 \neq U_2$, we have that the left (but not the right) side of $\partial U_1$ intersects the right (but not the left) side of $\partial U_2$ or vice-versa. 
\item $\partial U_1$, $\partial U_2$ can only intersect if their angle difference $|\theta(U_1) - \theta(U_2)|$ is below the critical angle.
\item On the event that $\partial U_1 \cap \partial U_2 \neq \emptyset$, we have that the Hausdorff dimension of $\partial U_1 \cap \partial U_2 \neq \emptyset$ is a.s.\ equal to~(equation eqn:flow_line_intersection_dimension of the paper) with $\rho = \frac{1}{\pi}|\theta(U_1)-\theta(U_2)|\left(2-\frac{\kappa}{2}\right) - 2$.
\item On the event that $\partial U_1 \cap \mathbf{R}_+ \neq \emptyset$ and that the right boundary of $U_1$ does not contain any open interval of $\mathbf{R}_+$, we have that the Hausdorff dimension of $\partial U_1 \cap \mathbf{R}_+$ is equal to~(equation eqn:boundary_flow_line_dimension of the paper) with $\rho = -1 +\frac{b + \theta(U_1)\chi}{\lambda}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:component_boundary_intersection of arXiv:2411.13133

body:
[Proposition prop:bounded of arXiv:2608.30166, 'Square Functions and Rectifiability\\ under Monotone Transformations of the Density'] Let $\mu$ be $n$-AD-regular with constant $c_0$ and $\mu(\mathbb{R}^d)<\infty$, and let
$F\colon(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel function and bi-Lipschitz on
$J_1=[2^{-n}c_0^{-1},c_1]$ with constant $\lambda_1$, where $c_1=5^dc_0$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If (equation eq:carlesonF of the paper) holds for some constant $c$, then $\mu$ is uniformly
$n$-rectifiable. No hypothesis on $F$ near $0$ is required.
\item[(b)] Conversely, if $\mu$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable and in addition
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0<\varepsilon\le c_1}\ \varepsilon\int_\varepsilon^{c_1}
\bigl|F(t)-F(2^{-n}t)\bigr|^2\,\frac{dt}{t}\;<\;\infty,
\end{equation}
then (equation eq:carlesonF of the paper) holds. Condition (equation eq:tail of the paper) is satisfied whenever
$t\mapsto F(t)-F(2^{-n}t)$ is bounded on $(0,c_1]$, and for $F$ continuous on
$(0,\infty)$ this is the same as being bounded near $0$; in particular (equation eq:tail of the paper)
holds for $F=\log$, for which $F(t)-F(2^{-n}t)\equiv n\log 2$.
\end{itemize}

[Thm optimali of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] {\bf (P-2)}
Consider the secretary problem
with the  Mallows distribution with $q=q_n\in(0,1)$ in the case that the largest number is  of highest rank..

\noindent i. Let $q_n=1-\frac cn$, where $c>0$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim n\Big(\frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)\Big),
\end{equation}
 and the corresponding  limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
Also, $\lim_{c\to\infty} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)=1$ and $\lim_{c\to0} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{e^c-1}e\big)=\frac1e$.

\noindent ii.
Let $q_n=1-\frac c{n^\alpha}$, where $c>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
n-M_n^*\sim\frac{n^\alpha}c,
$$
 and the corresponding limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent iii. Let $q\in(0,1)$.  Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
M_n^*=n-L, \ \text{where}\ L \ \text{satisfies}\ \frac q{1-q}\le L<\frac 1{1-q}.
$$
The corresponding limiting probability of success is given by
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=(1-q)q^{L-1}L>\frac1e.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm optimali of arXiv:2605.10452

[Defn def:smc of arXiv:2604.20629, 'Rates of forgetting for the sequentially Markov coalescent'] Let $(Y_{\ell})_{\ell\ge0}$ be a Markov
jump process on $(0,\infty)$ with the following dynamics. When $Y_{\ell}=y$,
the process waits an exponential time $r(y)=y$ before jumping,
at which time the process takes on
the new value $Y'=Uy+Z$, where $U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$ is the
recombination time on the current tree expressed as a fraction of
the tree height, and $Z\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ is the additional coalescence
time after the recombination event. 

Equivalently, one may construct $(Y_{\ell})$ from its embedded jump
chain and holding times as follows. Let $(X_{n})_{n\ge0}$ be the
jump chain and let $(E_{n})_{n\ge0}$ be i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$,
independent of the chain. Given $X_{n}$, define the holding time
\[
\Delta\ell_{n}:=\frac{E_{n}}{X_{n}}\ \sim\ \mathrm{Exp}(X_{n}),
\]
and jump locations $\ell_{0}:=0$, $\ell_{n+1}:=\ell_{n}+\Delta\ell_{n}$.
Then define 
\begin{align}
Y_{\ell} & :=X_{n}\quad\text{for }\ell\in[\ell_{n},\ell_{n+1}),\nonumber \\
X_{n+1} & :=U_{n}X_{n}+Z_{n},
\end{align}
where $(U_{n},Z_{n})$ are i.i.d.\ with $U_{n}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$
and $Z_{n}\sim\mathrm{Exp}(1)$. In particular, $(Y_{\ell})$ is almost surely
piecewise constant.
title: Sequentially Markov coalescent process

body:
[Lemma 30 (Finite--infinite volume coupling) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] For every $N\geq2$ and $t\geq0$, the finite- and infinite-volume
$\gamma$-avalanches may be coupled so that
\[
        r_N^\gamma(t)=r_\infty^\gamma(t)\wedge N.
\]
Consequently,
\[
        R_N^\gamma(t)
        =\mathbb{E}[r_\infty^\gamma(t)\wedge N]
        \uparrow R_\infty^\gamma(t),
        \qquad
        P_N^\gamma(t)
        =\mathbb{P}(r_\infty^\gamma(t)\geq N)
        \downarrow P_\infty^\gamma(t).
\]
On $\{r_\infty^\gamma(t)<N\}$ the two avalanches have the same duration.

[Theorem thm:MET of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Under the same conditions in Theorem (thm:FK theorem of the paper), there exists $\tilde{\Omega}\in\mathcal{I}$ with $V(\tilde{\Omega}^c)=0$ such that for any $\omega\in\tilde{\Omega}$,
	\begin{longlist}
		\item	The limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}(\Phi(n,\omega)^*\Phi(n,\omega))^{1/2n}:=\Psi(\omega)$ exists.
		\item Let $e^{\lambda_{p(\omega)}(\omega)}<\ldots<e^{\lambda_{1}(\omega)}$ be the different eigenvalues of $\Psi(\omega)$, where $p(\omega)$ is the number of  the different eigenvalues of $\Psi(\omega)$, and let $U_{p(\omega)}(\omega),\ldots,U_{1}(\omega)$ be the corresponding eigenspaces with multiplicities $d_i(\omega):=\operatorname{dim}U_i(\omega)$. Then
		\[p(T\omega)=p(\omega),\lambda_i(T\omega)=\lambda_i(\omega),\text{ and }d_i(T\omega)=d_i(\omega)\text{ for all }i\in\{1,2,\ldots,p(\omega)\}.\]
		\item Put $V_{p(\omega)+1}(\omega):=\{0\}$ and for $i=1,2,\ldots,p(\omega)$
		\[V_i(\omega):=U_{p(\omega)}(\omega)\oplus\ldots\oplus U_i(\omega)\]
		such that 
		$$
		V_{p(\omega)}(\omega) \subset \ldots \subset V_i(\omega) \subset \ldots \subset V_1(\omega)=\mathbb{R}^d.
		$$
		Then for each $x \in \mathbb{R}^d \backslash\{0\}$ the Lyapenov exponent
		$$
		\lambda(\omega,x):=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \left\|\Phi(n,\omega) x\right\|
		$$
		exists as a limit and
		$$
		\lambda(\omega,x)=\lambda_i(\omega) \Leftrightarrow x \in V_i (\omega)\backslash V_{i+1}(\omega)
		$$
		equivalently 
		\[V_i(\omega)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\lambda(\omega,x)\le\lambda_i(\omega)\}.\]
		\item For all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}$
		\[\lambda(T\omega,L(\omega)x)=\lambda(\omega,x),\]
		whence 
		\[L(\omega)V_i(\omega)\subset V_i(T \omega)\text{ for all }i\in\{1,\ldots,p(\omega)\}.\]
		\item If $V$ is ergodic then the function $p$ is constant on $\tilde{\Omega}$, and the functions $\lambda_i$ and $d_i$ are constant on $\{\omega\in\tilde{\Omega}:p(\omega)\ge i\}$, $i=1,2,\ldots,d$.
	\end{longlist}

[Defi 22 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let us assume that we are given
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\bs{X}^N=(X^N_1,\dots, X^N_d)$ a $d$-tuple of independent GUE matrices,
        \item $(x^m_i)_{i\in [1,d], m\in \N }$ free semicircular variables,
        \item $I = (I_1,\dots,I_{2n})\in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}^{2n}$ a collection of $2n$ integers,
        \item $T_n = (t_1,\dots,t_{2n})$ a sequence of non-negative real numbers.
    \end{itemize}
    Then with $\widetilde{t}_0=0$ and $\widetilde{t}_1\le \dots\le \widetilde{t}_{2n}$ the elements of $T_n$ sorted in increasing order, we set 
	$$ X_{i,I}^{N,T_{n}} = \sum_{l=1}^{2n} (e^{-\widetilde{t}_{l-1}} -e^{-\widetilde{t}_l})^{1/2} x^{I_{l}}_i + e^{-\widetilde{t}_{2n} /2} X_i^N , \qquad 1\le i\le d\,,$$
	$$ x_{i,I}^{T_{n}} = \sum_{l=1}^{2n} (e^{-\widetilde{t}_{l-1}} -e^{-\widetilde{t}_l})^{1/2} x^{I_{l}}_i + e^{- \widetilde{t}_{2n}/2} x_i^0 \,,\qquad 1\le i\le d. $$
    Note that we used Lemma \ref{lem:bigspace} to define $X^{N,T_n}_{i,I}$.

Given an outer measure mu* on X, call a set E measurable (in Caratheodory's sense) if it splits every test set additively: mu*(A) = mu*(A ∩ E) + mu*(A ∩ E^c) for all A subset X. The collection of measurable sets is a sigma-algebra, and mu* restricted to it is a complete (countably additive) measure. Consequently a premeasure on an algebra extends to a measure on the generated sigma-algebra (used to build Lebesgue measure).
mu* an outer measure on X

    \[

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:06bdf48cee34086f60bc0c9383563e692549d4b18552ade27d28fc71c00ee29c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/06/06bdf48cee34086f60bc0c9383563e692549d4b18552ade27d28fc71c00ee29c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:df3997f0310034279a485959cec33d2de0603a4e53a05f4c1618f49dd2d73aeb","bundle_entry_key":"full-column","bundle_id":"population.t419-lora-all-scale-square-input-and-expected-risk-scope-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA factor gradient descent","draft":"w705/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-full-column-population-gd-all-gaussian-scales","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C012 v1: population GD at every scale for full-column-rank targets

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.
This covers an entire dimension family and initialization interval, but it is the full-input-rank subfamily; the low-rank case r<d_in at moderate/large scale remains open in this work. The techniques are elementary imbalance and descent estimates. Related primary initialization results were consulted; the Springer 2024 source was inaccessible beyond its landing response, so literature coverage and novelty are unresolved. The result must not be advertised as a new published theorem or a solution of the whole row.

## Statement

Let Delta be an m-by-r real matrix, m>=r>=1, of exact rank r and ||Delta||op=1. Let 0<rho<1, c=10r/rho, and let s>0 be arbitrary. Initialize B0=0 of size m-by-r and A0 of size r-by-r with iid N(0,s^2) entries. Define

 h=s^2/(c^2 r), H=4c^2 r^2 s^2,
 K=2 sqrt(r) H+4r,
 0<eta<=min{h/(4r), 1/(6K+1)}.

For simultaneous constant-step GD on f(B,A)=(1/2)||BA-Delta||F^2, with probability at least 1-rho over A0, for every integer t>=0,

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F <=sqrt(r) exp(-eta h t/4).

Thus for 0<eps<1 it suffices to take

 t>=ceil[(4/(eta h)) log(sqrt(r)/eps)].

Unlike C003 this statement places no upper or lower restriction on s. It requires d_in=r, so it does not address learning a proper input-side rank-r subspace. The bound has no dependence on sigma_r(Delta) after normalization; fitting a full-column-rank product with an invertible square input factor does not require resolving an unobserved input subspace. For an unnormalized target with lambda=||Delta||op, use s_bar=s/sqrt(lambda), eta_bar=eta lambda, and error eps_bar=eps/lambda in the normalized statement.

## Initial event

Use only the square-Gaussian part of C004, not its optional small-scale Loewner comparison. With probability at least 1-rho,

 sigma_min(A0)>=2s/(c sqrt(r)),
 ||A0||F<=2crs.

Consequently, with D0=A0 A0^T,

 D0>=h I, ||D0||F<=||A0||F^2<=H.

These inequalities hold for every s>0. The Gaussian density/column-distance and Markov argument in C004 is scale-independent. Fix this event for the rest of the proof.

## Exact imbalance identity and a factor-size bound

Put E=BA-Delta, G_B=E A^T and G_A=B^T E. Simultaneous GD gives the exact cancellation

 D_next-D=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B),
 D=A A^T-B^T B.

Hence ||D_next-D||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2).

For arbitrary factors let P=B^TB and Q=AA^T, both r-by-r positive semidefinite. The trace Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and direct expansion give

 (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2
 =tr(P+Q)^2 <= r tr((P+Q)^2)
 =r [||P-Q||F^2+4||BA||F^2].

Here tr(P+Q)^2 means the square of the scalar trace, whereas tr((P+Q)^2) is the trace of the squared matrix. This identity does not require P and Q to commute.

Whenever f<=f0 and ||D-D0||F<=h/4, one has ||BA||F<=||Delta||F+sqrt(2f0)<=2sqrt(r), and

 ||B||F^2+||A||F^2
 <=sqrt(r) sqrt[(H+h/4)^2+16r]
 <=2 sqrt(r) H+4r=K.

The last inequality uses h<=H and sqrt(x^2+y^2)<=x+y for nonnegative x,y. The initialization satisfies this factor bound as well.

## Descent without a circular boundedness assumption

Inductively suppose the factor-pair norm is at most sqrt(K), and preceding steps have the descent inequality. At the current point,

 ||grad f||F<=||E||op sqrt(||B||F^2+||A||F^2)
             <=(K/2+1)sqrt(K).

Therefore eta<=1/(6K+1) makes the proposed next point have pair norm at most 2sqrt(K). The entire connecting segment lies in that ball. Throughout that ball,

 ||B||op^2+||A||op^2<=4K,
 ||BA-Delta||op<=2K+1,

so the factor Hessian has norm at most 6K+1. This follows by expanding its quadratic form as ||dB A+B dA||F^2+2<E,dB dA>. Thus ordinary smooth descent along this segment yields

 f_next<=f-(eta/2)||grad f||F^2.

Summing the valid descent inequalities, including this proposed step, gives

 sum_(j<=t) eta^2||grad f_j||F^2<=2eta f0<=eta r<=h/4.

The exact imbalance identity then gives ||D_next-D0||F<=h/4. The next point also has f_next<=f0, so the preceding factor-size bound shows its pair norm is actually at most sqrt(K), closing the induction. This argument justifies the required segment bound before using the resulting factor bound at its endpoint.

## Uniform gradient domination and rate

For every iterate,

 D>=D0-(h/4)I >=(3h/4)I,
 AA^T=D+B^TB >=(3h/4)I.

Since A is square, right multiplication by A^T is bounded below on every residual matrix:

 ||grad f||F^2>=||E A^T||F^2
               >=(h/2)||E||F^2.

Combining this with descent gives

 ||E_next||F^2 <=(1-eta h/2)||E||F^2.

The factor is nonnegative because h<=H<=K and eta<=1/(6K+1). Since ||E0||F^2=||Delta||F^2<=r, iteration and 1-x<=exp(-x) prove the statement.

## Essential scope and boundaries

For a rectangular A of size r-by-p with p>r, AA^T positive definite does not imply ||E A^T||F>=sqrt(h/2)||E||F for arbitrary m-by-p residual E. Residual directions orthogonal to A's row space can be annihilated. This is the precise point where this proof fails for genuinely low-rank input adaptation, so the argument must not be extended to that case silently.

The scale s=0 is excluded: both factors would remain zero. The result includes r=1, m=r, all positive scales, and every full-column-rank target condition number. No finite precision, asymptotic random-matrix formula, probability multiplication or independence among iterates is used. Only the original Gaussian initial event is probabilistic; everything after it is deterministic. Independent audit and prior-work novelty checks remain pending.

For any metric D on X and 0<a<1, D^a is a metric with the same topology and dim_H(X,D^a)=dim_H(X,D)/a. If D_{h+c}=exp(xi*c)D_h for constant c, then D_{h+c}^a=exp(a*xi*c)D_h^a, so the product xi*dim_H is unchanged. This shows that constant-shift covariance alone cannot determine metric dimension. It is not a second LQG metric: every continuous path from 0 to 1 in the snowflaked Euclidean interval has infinite D^a-length, by the first hitting times of levels k/n and partition sums n^(1-a). Thus the LQG length-space and pathwise Weyl axioms are outside this countermodel.

body: In complex dynamics, the Julia set and the Fatou set are two complementary sets defined from a function. Informally, the Fatou set of the function consists of values with the property that all nearby values behave similarly under repeated iteration of the function, and the Julia set consists of values such that an arbitrarily small perturbation can cause drastic changes in the sequence of iterated function values. Thus the behavior of the function on the Fatou set is "regular", while on the Julia set its behavior is "chaotic".
title: Julia set

Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{T})$ be an arbitrary Borel mark space equipped with a probability measure $\Theta$. Let $\Phi$ be a Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{A}$ with intensity measure $\gamma \lambda_d \otimes \Theta$, where $\gamma > 0$ and $\lambda_d$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$. The Random Connection Model (RCM) simplicial complex $\Delta$ is constructed inductively: (0) The vertex set is the set of points of $\Phi$; (1) For each pair of points $x, y \in \Phi$, the edge $\{x, y\}$ is added independently with probability $\varphi_1(x, y)$; (k) For $j \in \{2, \dots, \alpha\}$ and any $(j+1)$-tuple $\{x_0, \dots, x_j\} \subset \Phi$ all of whose proper subsimplices have been added to $\Delta$, the $j$-simplex $\{x_0, \dots, x_j\}$ is added independently with probability $\varphi_j(x_0, \dots, x_j)$.

$\rho^{E}_0$ equals the nonzero spectrum of the weighted overlap matrix
$G=\mathsf{w}^{1/2}\mathcal{G}\,\mathsf{w}^{1/2}$. Moreover the entire characteristic
polynomial of $\rho^{E}_z$, and every power trace $\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho^{E}_z)^{k}]$, is

body: In mathematics, the Laplace transform, named after Pierre-Simon Laplace (/ləˈplɑːs/), is an integral transform that converts a function of a real variable (usually $t$, in the time domain) to a function of a complex variable $s$ (in the complex-valued frequency domain, also known as s-domain or s-plane). The functions are often denoted using a lowercase symbol for the time-domain function and the corresponding uppercase symbol for the frequency-domain function, e.g. $x(t)$ and $X(s)$.

Let (X, d) be a metric space. The space of unparametrized curves P(X) consists of equivalence classes of continuous curves gamma: [0, 1] -> X modulo orientation-preserving reparametrizations, equipped with the uniform metric d_P(gamma_1, gamma_2) = inf_{phi} sup_{t in [0, 1]} d(gamma_1(t), gamma_2(phi(t))), where phi ranges over increasing homeomorphisms of [0, 1]. The collection space Pi(X) consists of countable collections Gamma = {gamma_i} subset P(X) having only finitely many curves of diameter exceeding any positive threshold, equipped with the Hausdorff-type metric on macroscopic curves.

[Proposition prop:time-change-SCI of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let \(G=(X,w,\kappa,\mu)\) be a graph. Define
\[
    \widetilde\mu:=\mu+\kappa
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    \widetilde G:=(X,w,0,\widetilde\mu).
\]
Then,
\[
    G\text{ satisfies }\hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \widetilde G\text{ satisfies }\hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{}.
\]
Moreover, if \((X,w,0,\mu)\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{}, then
\((X,w,\kappa,\mu)\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{} for every
killing term \(\kappa\ge0\).

Let X be a nearest-neighbor walk on Z^d, d>=1, started at 0, in a static environment with all transition probabilities at least kappa>0 under its original quenched or annealed law P. Let T in N union {infinity} be any random time and R_T=sup_{0<=n<=T}||X_n||_infinity. Let Q=P or Q=P(.|A) for a specified event A with P(A)>0. If Q(R_T>r)<=C exp(-lambda r) for every integer r>=0, with C finite and lambda>log(1/kappa), then E_Q[T]<infinity. This is a sufficient condition; no necessity or implication from directional transience is asserted.
d is an integer >=1; X starts at 0 on Z^d
nearest-neighbor transitions in a fixed or randomly sampled static environment
every transition probability is at least a deterministic kappa in (0,1/(2d)] under the original law P
T takes values in N union {infinity}; it need not be a stopping time
Q is P or a conditioning on an event of positive P-probability
Q(R_T>r)<=C exp(-lambda r) for all integer r>=0
C is finite and lambda>log(1/kappa)

[Theorem th:deficit1 of arXiv:2608.19358, 'An optimal Poincaré inequality\\for the complex Ginibre log-gas'] For all symmetric $f\in\mathcal{C}^\infty_c(\mathbb{C}^n_{\neq},\mathbb{R})$, 
  \begin{align}
    \mathcal{E}_{\mu_n}(f,f)
    -2\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_n}(f)
    &=2\|r\|_{L^2(\mu_n)}^2
    +4\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}(m-1)\|g_m\|_{L^2(\gamma_n)}^2\\
    \|A_nf\|_{L^2(\mu_n)}^2-2\mathcal{E}_{\mu_n}(f,f)
    &=
    \|(A_n+2)\widetilde f\|_{L^2(\mu_n)}^2
    +4\|r\|_{L^2(\mu_n)}^2
    +8\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}(m-1)\|g_m\|_{L^2(\gamma_n)}^2
  \end{align}
  where
  \begin{itemize}
  \item $\widetilde f=f-\int_{\mathbb{C}^n}f\mathrm{d}\mu_n$
  \item $g=\sum_{m=0}^\infty g_m$ is the Hermite expansion of
    $g=U\widetilde f$ in $L^2(\gamma_n)$, with $m=|q|$
  \item $r=\widetilde f-h-\overline{h}$
  \item
    $h=U^{-1}g_0=U^{-1}\operatorname{proj}_{\mathcal{H}_n}(U\widetilde{f})$,
    $\overline{h}$ denotes the pointwise complex conjugate of $h$
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sum of squares for the Poincaré and $\Gamma_2$ deficits

[Corollary t:cltspindisag1 of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] (CLT for sum of spins on Poisson-Boolean model)
Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a stationary Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ of intensity \(\rho\) and $K$ be a compact set containing the origin and with a non-empty interior. Let  \(\Psi = \Psi(\cdot)\) be the Poisson-Boolean graph induced by the Poisson-Boolean model on \(\mathcal{P}\), as described above. Consider a spin configuration model with the Gibbs distribution given by (equation eqn:gibbs of the paper), defined on the graph~\(\Psi\) and with finite spin space $\mathbb{K}$.
Assume that for some \(\epsilon > 0\), the maximum influence (equation defq of the paper) satisfies
\[
q(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n)) < \min \{1, \rho_c / \rho\} - \epsilon
\]
almost surely for all $\mathcal{P}_n$, for all large enough $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and where $\rho_c$ is the critical intensity for percolation of the Poisson-Boolean model.
Under these conditions, the spin model \(\{V_x(\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n))\}_{x \in \mathcal{P}_n}\) satisfies the central limit theorem as stated in Theorem~(spinmain of the paper), provided that the moment and variance conditions specified in the theorem are also met. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary t:cltspindisag1 of arXiv:2605.28430

For Q = 2 Y (L + beta) + lambda (V - v_c(L, P))^2 + F(L, P) with such a hub, L, V, P orthonormal projections of independent coordinates with densities at most 1, t = l + beta, c = 2 sqrt 2 |lambda|^{-1/2} and a(l, p) = sup_v rho_{L,V,P}(l, v, p): ||p_Q||_inf <= 1/2 + int int_{|t| <= 1} min(rho_{L,P}(l, p), c a(l, p) |t|^{1/2}) dl dp/(2|t|). Proof: given X' the form is affine in Y; for fixed (l, p) the bathtub step of Proposition S bounds int f(y|p) dv/(2|t|) by sqrt 2 (|lambda| |t|)^{-1/2}; |t| > 1 contributes at most 1/2. Windowed corollary: 1/2 + int r(p)(2 + 2 log_+(c a(p)/r(p))) dp with r, a the suprema over |l + beta| <= 1. This covers the single hub with no hub or light diagonal and linear terms in span(w, v, q^), uniformly in eps. The windowed form is NOT bounded under the (0.1) leverage condition alone: w = (e1+e2)/sqrt2, q^ = (e1-e2)/sqrt2, v = (e3+e4)/sqrt2 and two combs with incommensurate spacings of order N^{-1/2} give int r = 3.9, 7.5, 22.6, 83.7 at N = 64..4096, while the sharp form stays bounded (V independent of (L, P)) and Proposition 3.15 covers that configuration. [Lemma last two rows are equal of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $p_{n-1,j}=p_{n,j}$ for all $1\leq j\leq n$.
    \begin{proof}
        We present a combinatorial argument. Card $n$ is drawn first and placed by itself. Now card $n-1$ goes on top, respectively on the bottom, of card $n$ with probability $1/2$. Hence, cards $n$ and $n-1$ move as a block in the shuffle with both orderings equally likely. Therefore, given a position, they are equally likely to end up there. One can also argue by computing the transition probabilities and using Pascal's identity and symmetry.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma last two rows are equal of arXiv:2507.10294

[Lemma prob0 pure of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Assume that $\xi$ is pure $p$-spin. Let $\varepsilon>0$. Let $u\in(0,1)$, $q\in(0,1)$, $f\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\zeta\in \mathrm{Prefix}_2(u,q)$ where $\mathrm{Prefix}_2$ is as in Definition (def:nprefix of the paper).
		
		Let $\delta\in[\varepsilon,1)$ and $\mathbf{m}\in[-1+\delta,1-\delta]^N$. Suppose moreover that $q_\mathbf{m}\in (q-\varepsilon,q+\varepsilon)$ and
		$\mathrm{dist}\!\bigl(\zeta_\mathbf{m},\,\zeta|_{(q,1]}+\zeta([0,q])\,\delta_q\bigr)<\varepsilon$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  The gradient $\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})$ is a non-degenerate Gaussian vector in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Its log-density at $0$, tilted by
			\[
			u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right),
			\]
			satisfies
			\begin{multline}
				\log \varphi_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
				+u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right)
				\\
				=
				\frac{1}{2}N\xi(q)u^2
				-\frac{1}{2}N\xi''(q)\!\left(\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t\right)^{\!2}
				-\frac{1}{2\xi'(q)}
				\Vert \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})-u\xi'(q)\mathbf{m}\Vert^2
				\\
				-\frac{N}{2}\log(2\pi \xi'(q))
				+\frac{N(p-1)}{2p\,\xi'(q)\,q}
				\!\left(
				\frac{1}{N}\langle \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m}),\mathbf{m}\rangle
				-\xi'(q)\int_0^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				\right)^{\!2}
				\\
				-u\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)+N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)+Nf\right)
				+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right).
			\end{multline}
			
			\item  Suppose moreover that
			\begin{equation}
				\langle \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m}),\mathbf{m}\rangle
				=
				N\xi'(q)\int_0^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t+O(N\varepsilon)
			\end{equation}
			and
			\begin{equation}
				\sum_{i=1}^N\bigl(h_\zeta(q,m_i)-\partial_m h_\zeta(q,m_i)m_i\bigr)
				+N\int_0^q t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				+\frac{N}{2}\int_q^1 t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				=
				-Nf+O(N\varepsilon).
			\end{equation}
			Then the squared term in (equation eq:pure-prob0-main of the paper) is $O(N\varepsilon)$, so that 
			\begin{multline}
				\log \varphi_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
				+u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right)
				\\
				=
				\frac{1}{2}N\xi(q)u^2
				-\frac{1}{2}N\xi''(q)\!\left(\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t\right)^{\!2}
				-\frac{1}{2\xi'(q)}
				\Vert \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})-u\xi'(q)\mathbf{m}\Vert^2
				\\
				-\frac{N}{2}\log(2\pi \xi'(q))
				-u\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)+N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)+Nf\right)
				+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right),
			\end{multline}
			and, on the event $\{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0\}$,
			\begin{equation}
				F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=Nf+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right).
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate}

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked; reduction plus asserted conditional, not a solution] Svante Janson's Problem 18.39 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510, asks whether Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability is possible in the condensation regime 0 < nu < lambda. Janson conjectures that it is not possible for the full sequence and, more strongly, that there are always epsilon > 0 and a subsequence along which Y_(1) >= epsilon n w.h.p. (Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. Let m_n/n -> lambda > nu. (Y_1,...,Y_n) is n i.i.d. pi variables conditioned on sum m_n, Y_(1) = max_i Y_i, and M = (lambda-nu)n. Heuristic rate: carrying M in r = M/a boxes of size a has class weight binomial(n,r) pi_a^r up to the bulk's fluctuation, giving log P = M Lambda(a) + o(M) with Lambda(a) = [log pi_a + log(a/(lambda-nu)) + 1]/a. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j). The record asserts, as author-checked and with no proof given beyond reference to an analogous step for Problem 18.40 in a companion memo, the following Proposition: if for some epsilon > 0 and every C, along infinitely many records, Lambda(a_j) - max_{a <= epsilon a_j} Lambda(a) > C a_j^(-1/2), then along n_j = a_j/(lambda-nu), P(Y_(1) >= ((lambda-nu)/2) n_j) -> 1, so the conjecture holds. Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. The record poses the open Question whether, for every law pi on Z_{>=0} with radius one and finite mean, [log pi_a + log a]/a has infinitely many records with gap exceeding a_j^(-1/2) below max_{a <= epsilon a_j} for some fixed epsilon > 0. This is not a proved equivalence with the conjecture. A negative answer would only give a candidate counterexample, still requiring proof that the allocation spreads. The Question's normalisation and fixed threshold also differ from the Proposition's hypothesis. The problem remains open. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The allocations are defined along sizes with positive conditioning probability.
0 < nu < lambda and the boundary-tilted law pi has generating-function radius one.

Then for any compact set $K\subset E$, the restricted measure $1_K\mu$ is of finite energy integral; that is, $1_K\mu \in \mathcal{S}_0$.

In particular, if $\mu(E) < \infty$, then $\mu$ itself belongs to $\mathcal{S}_0$, which further implies that $\mu \in \mathcal{S}_{00}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Denote by $\hat{\pi}$ the estimator given by Theorem \ref{possible}. Then, for any $k > \frac{2}{2\alpha - 1}$, $ov(\hat{\pi}, \pi^*) \geq \frac{|\Ker_k(I)|}{n}(1 - o_\Proba(1))$.

    In particular, if $\ds\min_{u \in V} \left( \sum_{v \in V}  (p_{\{ u, v\}}s^2)\right) \goesto{n \to +\infty} +\infty$, then $ov(\hat{\pi}, \pi^*) = 1 - o_\Proba(1)$: almost exact alignment is feasible. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 3 (Regeneration at a level) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] Suppose that the $t$-avalanche has finite range $I$. Conditionally on
$\mathcal H_t$, its terminal fitnesses are independent and have the form
\[
        F_x=t+E_x,\qquad x\in I,
\]
where the $E_x$ are independent $\operatorname{Exp}(1)$ variables,
independent of $\mathcal H_t$. Consequently, when the threshold is raised
above $t$, the next triggering level occurs at rate $|I|$, its location is
uniform on $I$, and the subavalanche attached there is independent of
$\mathcal H_t$ and has the law of an avalanche at the triggering level.

[Lemma 8 (A uniform exponential envelope) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] Fix \(p\ge1\), and assume $\lambda_n=nq_n^{k_n}$ is bounded. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every integer $u\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
        \Pbb(E_n=u)u!p^u\le (p\lambda_n)^u.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if $\lambda_n\to\lambda$, there is a constant $B\ge1$ such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and all integers \(u\ge0\),
\[
        \Pbb(E_n=u)u!p^u\le B^u.
\]

body: Publication record. Problem 11 of N. N. Ganikhodzhaev and U. A. Rozikov, Quadratic stochastic operators: results and open problems (2009), asks whether their Theorem 6 (a strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on three types has a unique fixed point, and it is not attractive) extends to more types. Y. Shmalo, Fixed points of strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators in four or more types (September 2026) shows that it does not extend to four or more types; uniqueness at four types is left open and reduced to one determinant inequality by an index count. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/strictly-nonvolterra-qso-fixed-points (commit 0526854748f5); ResearchGate record 414323511. Not refereed.
title: Ganikhodzhaev-Rozikov Problem 11 answered: the fixed-point theorem for strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators does not extend to four or more types (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/strictly-nonvolterra-qso-fixed-points)

[Theorem lucesec of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] Consider the secretary problem for a
$P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}$-type Luce
  distribution in the case that the smallest number is of highest rank.
For  $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M))=
\begin{cases}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M\theta_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i}\sum_{j=M+1}^n
\frac{\theta_j}{\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\theta_i},\ M\in\{1,\cdots, n-1\};\\
\frac{\theta_1}{\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i},\ M=0.\end{cases}

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:finite-profile-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $H\geq1$ and $k\geq2$, and let $G$ be a nontrivial torsion-free abelian
group.  The following four collections of truncated profiles are identical:
\[
 \bigl\{(|jA|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:A\subset G,\ |A|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(|jB|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
\[
 \bigl\{(|P^{\times j}|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       P\subset\mathbb Z_{>0},\ |P|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(H_{C_B}(j))_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
where $P^{\times j}$ is the $j$-fold product set and $C_B$ is the projective
monomial curve attached to $B$ over an arbitrary field.  More strongly,
equip the subgroup generated by an additive realization with a
translation-invariant linear order.  Its complete equality-and-order table
through degree $H$ then has an integer exponent representative.  The
resulting sumset, product-set, and monomial-curve exponent models have
identical ordered tables, active ranks, and relation-birth degrees through
$H$.

Every such table has a primitive integer representative
$B=\{0=b_0<\cdots<b_{k-1}\}$ with
\begin{equation}
 b_{k-1}\leq dH^{d-1}\prod_{i=1}^r p_i
 \leq(k-1-r)H^{k-2},
 \qquad d=k-1-r,
\end{equation}
where $r$ and $p_i$ are its active rank and birth degrees through $H$.
The universal exponent $k-2$ for preserving the complete truncated table is
best possible.

body:
[Proposition tightness condition of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] For a sequence of c\`adl\`ag stochastic processes $\{X^{(n)}\}_{n\geq 1}$ defined on a common probability space with $\sup_{n \geq 1}  \mathbf{E} \big[|X^{(n)}(0)|^q\big] < \infty$ for some $q>0$, it is $C$-tight if the following two conditions hold for any $T\geq 0$ and some constant $\beta>2$.
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(1)] 
  There exist some constants $C>0 $, $p\geq 1$ and $\rho,\alpha>0$ such that for any $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $n\geq 1$,
  \begin{eqnarray*}
   \sup_{t\in[0,T]} \mathbf{E}\Big[\big| X^{(n)}(t+\delta)-X^{(n)}(t)\big|^{p}\Big] 
   \leq C\cdot \Big(  \delta^{1+\rho}+ \frac{\delta}{n^\alpha}\Big).
  \end{eqnarray*}
 		
  \item[(2)] 
  $\displaystyle\sup_{k=0,1,\cdots,[Tn^\beta]} \sup_{\delta\in[0,1/n^{\beta}]} \big|  X^{(n)}(k/n^\beta+\delta) -X^{(n)}(k/n^\beta)\big|  \overset{\rm p}\to 0$  as $n\to\infty$. 
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition tightness condition of arXiv:2411.15485

[Corollary c1 of arXiv:2411.19433, 'Singular mean-field backward stochastic Volterra integral equations in infinite dimensiona'] Let condition $(A_{2})$ satisfy. Then, for every \( \Psi(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{b}}(r, \delta; H) \), the stochastic Fredholm-type integral equation (equation 3.6 of the paper) admits a unique adapted solution

\[
(\Psi_{\delta}(\cdot), \aleph(\cdot, \cdot)) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{\delta}}(r, \delta; H) \times L^2(r, \delta; L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(\delta, b; L_0^2)).
\]

The second special case of (equation f3.4 of the paper) is as follows: Let \( r = \delta \), and define

\[
X(t) := \lambda(t, t), \quad t \in [\delta, b], \quad \aleph(t, s) := \mu(t, s), \quad (t, s) \in [\delta, b]^2.
\]

Then equation (equation f3.4 of the paper) becomes

\begin{align}
X(t) = \Psi(t) + \int_t^b \eta(t, s, \aleph(t, s), \mathbb{E}[\aleph(t, s)]) \, ds - \int_t^b \aleph(t, s) \, dB_{s}, \quad t \in [\delta, b].
\end{align}

This is a specific case of a singular MF-BSVIE (equation r3 of the paper), where the generator \( \eta \) is independent of \( X(s) \) and \( \aleph(s, t) \). We can define \( \aleph(t, s) \) for \( (t, s) \in [\delta, b]^2 \) by using the martingale representation theorem:

\[
X(t) = \mathbb{E}[X(t) | \mathcal{F}_{\delta}] + \int_{\delta}^t \aleph(t, s) \, dB_{s}, \quad t \in [\delta, b].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Its Gaussian displacement variance involves integral_0^1 k^(-1-s)dk, finite for every s<0 at any fixed temperature. body: Consider an autonomous C^1 planar vector field dx/dt = f(x) on an open subset of R^2, and a forward trajectory that stays inside a compact set for all t >= 0. The Poincare-Bendixson theorem states that its omega-limit set is nonempty, compact, connected, and is either a fixed point, a periodic orbit, or a union of finitely many fixed points joined by homoclinic or heteroclinic orbits; in particular, if the omega-limit set contains no fixed point, it is a single periodic orbit. The result is specific to the plane and fails for flows in dimension 3 or higher. Due to Henri Poincare and Ivar Bendixson.
title: Poincare-Bendixson theorem

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] [\textbf{Convergence of the Dynkin martingale}]
Let $H \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$. The sequence of martingales $\big\{ \big(  \mathcal{M}_t^n(H)  \big)_{0 \leq t \leq T}, \; n \in \mathbb{N}_+\big\}$ converges with respect to the Skorohod topology of $\mathcal{D}([0, T], \mathbb{R})$ to a mean zero Gaussian process $\mathcal{M}(H)$, as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{M}(H)$ is a continuous martingale on $[0, T]$ whose quadratic variation is $\langle \mathcal{M}(H) \rangle_t = t D_3 \mathcal{P}^{ \gamma} H$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.03777

[Theorem 1 (Pfaffian identity for the representation defect) of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Let $n$ be a positive squarefree integer and suppose that $s_2(n)$ is even.  For any
basis $\mathcal B$ of $\Sel_2'(E_n)$, let $C_{\mathcal B}(E_n)$ be the Gram matrix of
the Cassels pairing.  Then
\[
2\sigma_Q(n)2^{s_2(n)/2}\mid \Delta_Q(n)
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\mathcal D_Q(n)=\Pf\bigl(C_{\mathcal B}(E_n)\bigr)\in\F_2.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the two sides are equal to $1$ if and only if
\[
\rk E_n(\Q)=0,
\qquad
\Sha(E_n)[2^\infty]\cong(\Z/2\Z)^{s_2(n)}.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30875, 'A Decomposition Theorem for Topological Semi-small Maps'] Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper surjective semi-small map .
   	Let $Y= \bigsqcup_{\alpha}S_{\alpha}$ be a Whitney stratification of $Y$ with respect to which $f$ is stratified, and denote by $Y_{\mathrm{rel}} \subset Y$ the set of relevant strata of $f$.
   	For each $S \in Y_{\mathrm{rel}}$, let $\mathcal{L}_S$ be the corresponding local system defined above.
   	There is a canonical quasi-isomorphism
   	\begin{align*}
   	Rf_* \mathbb{Q}_X[\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(X)] \simeq \bigoplus_{S \in Y_{\mathrm{rel}}} IC_{\overline{S}}(\mathcal{L}_S).
   	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematical analysis, the Weierstrass approximation theorem states that every continuous function defined on a closed interval [a, b] can be uniformly approximated as closely as desired by a polynomial function. Because polynomials are among the simplest functions, and because computers can directly evaluate polynomials, this theorem has both practical and theoretical relevance, especially in polynomial interpolation. The original version of this result was established by Karl Weierstrass in 1885 using the Weierstrass transform.
title: Stone–Weierstrass theorem

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof} Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$.
Recall the notation \eqref{e:lam.mu.delta.ball}, and suppose
$(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda$ and 
 $(\lambda,\mu)\in B_\delta(\lambda',\mu')$. Given $\YY'\in S_\star(\lambda',\mu';\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$, we will construct $\YY\in S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ which is $o_\delta(1)$-close to $\YY'$. We set $\vwww$ as in Lemma~\ref{l:D.mu.continuity.w}, so that we have the bound $\|\vwww-\vwww'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2$. Recalling Lemma~\ref{l:p.polytope.bd.local.aux}, we see that
 $\vwww,\vwww'$ are confined to a compact domain $[0,9/\iota_0]^s$.
The $\Budget$ function is uniformly continuous on the compact domain
$[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}\times\Lambda$, so
	\[\sup\bigg\{
	\begin{array}{l}
	|\Budget(\YY;\mu)
	-\Budget(\YY';\mu')|
	:\YY,\YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s},
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\mu-\mu'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\|\YY-\YY'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2
	\end{array}
	\bigg\} \le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\]
where $o_\delta(1)$ denotes an error tending to zero as $\delta\to0$. 
For the purposes of this proof, let us abbreviate
	\begin{align*}
	c(\YY;\lambda)
	&\equiv \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
	+ \epsilon_1\alpha^2\iota^2(\|\vBBb\|_2)^2\,,\\
	g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	&\equiv c(\YY;\lambda) - \Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2\,.
	\end{align*}
Then we can similarly bound
	\[\sup\bigg\{\begin{array}{l}
	|c(\YY';\lambda)
	-c(\YY';\lambda')|
	: \YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}, 
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\end{array}
	\bigg\}
	 \le o_\delta(1)\,.
	\]
Combining the above bounds gives
	\beq
	c(\YY';\lambda)
	-\Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2
	\le g (\YY';\lambda',\mu') + o_\delta(1)
	\le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\eeq
uniformly over 
$(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')$ in $\Lambda$ within distance $\delta$,
and
$\YY,\YY'\in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$ within distance $\delta/\iota^2$.
If the above left-hand side is in fact $\le0$ then we are done, since we can then set
$\YY=(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
 to achieve
$g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$. If the above left-hand side is
 strictly positive, then it remains to choose 
 $\YY=(\vBBb,\vvvv,\vUUu,\vwww)$
 close to 
 $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$ to make $g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$.
In this case, consider the path in $\cD_\mu$ given by the line segment joining $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
to $\YY(1)\equiv(\vec{0},\vvvv'-\vUUu',\vec{0},\vwww)$. If we parametrize this segment as a linear function $\YY(t)$ of $t\in[0,1]$, then along the segment we have
	\[\Cost(\YY(t);\lambda)
	-\Cost(\YY(0);\lambda)
	=-(\lambda,\vBBb'+\vUUu')t
	\equiv -A(\YY')t\,.
	\]
Recall from \eqref{e:surplus.small.error.bound} that at the start of the line segment we have $g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu) \le o_\delta(1)$.  Let $\eta = g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu)$. We then divide into several cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item If  $A(\YY')\ge\eta^{1/2}$, then we can choose $t_0= \eta / A(\YY') \le \eta^{1/2}$ such that
	\[
	g(\YY(t_0);\lambda,\mu) 
	\le  \eta^{1/2} - A(\YY') t_0 
	\le 0\,,
	\]
and (since $\YY,\YY' \in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$) $\|\YY(t_0)-\YY(0)\|_2 \lesssim \eta^{1/2}$. In this case, we can conclude by setting $\YY = \YY(t_0)$.
\item Otherwise, if 
$A(\YY')\le \eta^{1/2}$, then
assumption~\eqref{e:def-Lambda} implies that 
\[
    \max\Big(\|\vBBb'\|_1,\|\vUUu'\|_1\Big) \le \frac{\eta^{1/2}}{\iota}\,,
\]

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $T:Z\to Z$ be a Borel automorphism of a standard Borel space.
There is a Borel family of sets
\[
    z\longmapsto P_z\subset\mathbb R
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $P_z$ are uniformly Delone;

\item
\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z);
\]

\item
if $z,w\in Z$ and $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
    P_w=P_z-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^u z;
\]

\item
for every $z\in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1)
\]
in the sense of tempered distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-dimensional coding theorem

body:
Aldous and Janson, The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II (arXiv:2303.02529), Open Problem 14 (pp. 54-55) asks to prove that L_n, the expected drawn length of DTCS(n) under their recursion (73) l(chi_m) = l(chi_i) + l(chi_{m-i}) + 2 + |h(chi_{m-i}) - h(chi_i)|, grows roughly like n log^4 n. Our result (id P0340, 2026-09-08): the drawn length is Theta(n), so the conjecture is FALSE. For every full binary tree the drawn length is at most the sum of all leaf depths, because the increment 2 + |h_R - h_L| is at most n_L + n_R (a full binary tree with k leaves has height at most k-1); with the authors' own Theorem 3 (the expected depth of a random leaf is asymptotic to (1/(2 zeta(2))) log^2 n = 3 pi^-2 log^2 n) this gives E[drawn length] <= n E[leaf depth] ~ (3/pi^2) n log^2 n = o(n log^4 n). The heuristic's error is a missing factor m: their heuristic (75) uses n a(n,m) as the mean count of size-m subclades where the correct count is (n/m) a(n,m); with the wrong count the conjecture is reproduced exactly, with the right one the scale sum converges (sum log^3 m / m^2) instead of diverging (sum log^3 m / m). Verification as the source words it: machine-checked in P0340.lean, together with the exact decomposition drawn(T) = sum of internal subtree heights + height(T); simulation gives L_n/n = 4.71, 4.78, 4.84, 4.83, 4.86 at n = 10^3 to 4 x 10^5 - flat across a 400x range while log^4 n grows 12x - with the sampler validated first against the paper's own clade counts and leaf-depth law. Prior art not cleared.
DTCS(n), the discrete critical beta-splitting tree of Aldous and Janson
drawn length defined by their recursion (73)

body: [Lemma reduction of arXiv:2607.24528, 'On Feige's conjecture'] Let $\delta>0$, let \(F\) be a merger, and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). Suppose that \[ F(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\leq\alpha \] whenever \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\geq 0\) and \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\geq n+\delta. \] Then, for any independent nonnegative random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with expectation one, \[ \mathbb P\left(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i<n+\delta\right)\geq 1-\alpha. \]

body:
[Corollary 34 (Conditional convergence) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let either $W(\mu):=\mu(\varphi_0)$, with $\varphi_0\in\Cc$, $\varphi_0\not\equiv0$, fixed
and $\eps$ admissible in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:restricted} and small
enough that $\bN(\mu(\varphi_0)>\eps)>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:PZ}); or
$W(\mu):=\mu(\R^d)$, with $\eps>0$ arbitrary --- every $\eps$ being admissible
here, since $\mu(\R^d)$ has no atoms under $\bN$ and
$\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)\in(0,\infty)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:totalmass}). Then
\[
\bP\bigl(\mu_n\in\cdot\;\big|\;W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)
\;\xRightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\;
\bN\bigl(\,\cdot\,\big|\;W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)
:=\frac{\bN(\,\cdot\,;\,W(\mu)>\eps)}{\bN(W(\mu)>\eps)}
\]
weakly as probability measures on $\cM$, and
$n^{2}\,\bP\bigl(W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)\to\bN\bigl(W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)\in(0,\infty)$.

[Theorem 6 (Information-theoretic lower bound for exact quantile regret) of arXiv:2608.22227, '\fontsize{18pt}{20pt}\selectfont \bf Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with Smoothed Q'] Fix a target quantile level \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and assume \(A\ge2\) and \(H\ge2\). Then there exist constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), depending at most on the fixed target level \(\tau\), such that for every \(\rho\in(0,\frac{\min\{\tau,1-\tau\}}{8}]\), every
\(T\ge c_0\,\frac{A}{\rho^2}\), and every possibly randomized learning algorithm that, at each episode \(t\),
outputs a deterministic history-dependent policy
\(\pi^t\in\Pi_{\mathrm{det}}\), there exists a finite-horizon episodic MDP \(\mathcal M=(\mathcal S,\mathcal A,H,P^\star,r)
\) with deterministic rewards \(r_h(s,a)\in[0,1]\),
\(
|\mathcal S|=2\), \(|\mathcal A|=A\), such that the root-level plateau constant of this instance satisfies $\rho_\tau=\rho$, and 
$\mathbb E\!\left[\Reg_\tau(T)\right]
\ge c_1\,\frac{H} {\rho_\tau}\sqrt{AT}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Information-theoretic lower bound for exact quantile regret

body: [Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.03171, 'Factorization patterns and fields of definition of $\ell$-torsion points on the Jacobians '] Suppose that $\tilde{P}(X)\in\mathbb{F}_{\ell}[X] $ has linear irreducible factors of the form $(X-\alpha)^3(X-\beta)^2$, for some nonzero $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{F}_{\ell}$. [Lemma lem:ineqs of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $H_n$ be integer-valued and let $N_n(h),L_n(h)$ be nonnegative random
variables such that
$$
\{H_n\ge h\}=\{N_n(h)\ge1\},
\qquad
\{L_n(h)\ge1\}\subseteq\{H_n\ge h\}.
$$
If $\mathbb{E}[N_n(h_n)]\to0$, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to0$. If
$L_n(h_n)\to\infty$ in probability, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:ineqs of arXiv:2607.22291

[Theorem eqWellposed of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] Assume that $A$ is a self-adjoint, negative definite   linear  operator on $H$. Then, the equation (eqSEE of the paper) admits a unique mild solution $X(\cdot) \in L_{\mathbb{F}}^2(\Omega ; C([0, T] ; H)) \cap L_{\mathbb{F}}^2 (0, T ; D((-A)^{\frac{1}{2}} ) $. Moreover,
\begin{align*}
    & |X(\cdot)|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^2(\Omega ; C([0, T] ; H))}+|X(\cdot)|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^2 (0, T ; D((-A)^{\frac{1}{2}} )} \\
    & \leq \mathcal{C}\big(\left|X_0\right|_{L_{\mathcal{F}_0}^2(\Omega ; H)}+|F(\cdot, 0)|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^2 ( 0, T ; H)}+|\widetilde{F}(\cdot, 0)|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^2 ( 0, T ; H)}\big)
    .
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Openproblem 13 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Do suitable analogues of Theorem \ref{Theorem: Main} and Corollaries \ref{Corollary: Spectral Geometry},
\ref{Corollary: Fractal Dimension}, and \ref{Corollary: Variance} still hold if one or several of the following changes are made?
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $D$ is replaced by a compact Riemannian manifold of any dimension.
\item $\xi$ is replaced by a more general singular noise
(e.g., $\xi$ could be Gaussian with covariance $\mbf E[\xi(x)\xi(y)]=\mf K(x,y)$
for the Riesz kernel $\mf K(x,y)=|x-y|^{-\om}$, $\om>0$, or the fractional
kernel $\mf K(x,y)=\prod_{i}|x_i-y_i|^{-\om_i}$, $\om_i>0$).
\item Assuming there is a boundary, the Dirichlet boundary condition is replaced by
another boundary condition (e.g., Neumann, Robin, or mixed).
\end{enumerate} (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Problem 13 of arXiv:2507.06186

body:
Let mu and nu be laws of countably many zero-one indicators X_i, pairwise negatively correlated under each law. Suppose delta_i=E_mu X_i-E_nu X_i>=0 and sum_i delta_i^2=infinity. Then mu and nu are mutually singular. The criterion needs no common invariant group action. Its application to distinct free and wired spanning-forest laws requires checking the ordered-marginal, negative-correlation and divergent-squared-gap hypotheses; that divergence is not proved for arbitrary networks here.

        \end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:t0-asymptotics of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Fix $\lambda_*>0$.  Uniformly for all $\lambda\geq\lambda_*$ and all
admissible solutions $(f,g)$ at $t=0$, with $u=\log g$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \lambda\|f\|_{C^0}=O(\alpha^{-1}),
 \qquad \|u\|_{C^0}\leq C,
 \qquad
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C} f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}=o(1)
 \quad (\alpha\to\infty).
\end{equation}
More precisely,
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\geq\lambda_*}
 \sup_{(f,g)\in\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}}
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{as }\alpha\to\infty,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}\) denotes the set of admissible
solutions at \(t=0\).

[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}

More generally, if \(r_n,s_n\to\infty\), both are of the same order, and
\(\Phi(s_n)-\Phi(r_n)\to y\), then
\(\Psi(s_n)-\Psi(r_n)\to y\).

Garg, Gunn and Wang, arXiv:2506.01854v2, Corollary 4: relative to any crypto oracle, there are no statistically secure pseudorandom codes robust to any constant rate of independent random binary errors. This already holds for secret-key zero-bit PRCs with negligible soundness and completeness errors and polynomial query complexity. Their noise parameter rho is correlation: N_rho refreshes each bit independently with probability 1-rho, equivalently flips each bit with probability (1-rho)/2; constant positive noise means rho is bounded away from 1. Section 1.1 interprets this as a fully black-box separation from primitives implemented by crypto oracles; footnote 3 specifies the additional PSPACE oracle used in that interpretation. The statistical oracle impossibility must not be read as an unconditional impossibility from existence of one-way functions.
Binary channel with a constant positive independent bit-flip rate below one half
Statistical security in the oracle model of the source
Polynomially many oracle queries and polynomial block length
Negligible completeness and soundness errors

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p < infinity, and F: X x Y -> [0, infinity] measurable for the product sigma-algebra. Then ( int_Y ( int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) )^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} <= int_X ( int_Y F(x,y)^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} dmu(x), both sides in [0, infinity]. Consequently, for complex measurable F with the right-hand side (computed with |F|) finite, int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) converges absolutely for nu-a.e. y and its L^p(nu)-norm is at most the right-hand side. In words: the L^p norm of an integral is at most the integral of the L^p norms. (For p = infinity the analogous statement with ess sup holds for F >= 0.)
(X, mu) and (Y, nu) are sigma-finite measure spaces
F is measurable with respect to the product sigma-algebra
F >= 0 (or the right-hand side is finite when F is complex)
1 <= p < infinity

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy' (prob environment labelled eq:tuple-of-Phis).] When $\phi$ is unital, Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) says that the value $E_n$ gives the rate function in the large deviations principle obeyed by the random element
\[(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n] \in \S^\rm{u}_k(B_n).\]
The values $E_n'$ should have an analogous interpretation, but this time for the random $S$-tuples
\begin{equation}
\big((\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n\cup sB_n]:\ s \in S\big)
\end{equation}
taking values in the space
\[\Big\{(Q_s:\ s \in S) \in \prod_{s \in S}\S^\rm{u}_k(B_n\cup sB_n):\ (Q_s)[B_n]\ \hbox{is the same for all $s$}\Big\}.\]
If this is true, then both inequalities in Lemma~(lem:1-2-ineqs) become instances of the contraction principle.

I believe one can prove this along the same lines as Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) without any really new ideas, but working with the the tuples in~(eq:tuple-of-Phis) is sure to be more complicated than working with $(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n$ alone. (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)

[Lemma lem:LG-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.

\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{E}[W\log_2^+W]<\infty

Own work draft, status independently checked proof, E0018-C3 v1 (w667 PASS, w668 PASS). For symmetric-rate switching of real 2x2 matrices Ai, set Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I. The exponent obeys L_A(r)=L_B(r)+(tr A0+tr A1)/4. If one traceless part has nonzero imaginary eigenvalues +-i omega, a fixed real similarity and time scaling transform the traceless pair into J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] and eta H+sJ, H=diag(1,-1), eta>=0, s real; normalized rate rho=r/omega and the original traceless exponent equals omega times the normalized exponent at rho. For unscaled traceless matrices with spectral abscissae ki=sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)), there exist scalar shifts Ai=Bi-ai I making both individually Hurwitz with prescribed damping average abar iff abar>(k0+k1)/2. This places no requirement on the averaged matrix. No rate monotonicity or unimodality is asserted.
Real 2x2 matrices
Symmetric switching rate r>0
A nonzero traceless elliptic part for the canonical-form clause

Status: proof (unaudited), 2026-10-14.

Let symmetric-rate switching alternate two real 2x2 matrices Ai. Put
Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I, so Bi is traceless. Let tau=(tr A0+tr A1)/4.
The top Lyapunov exponent satisfies L_A(r)=L_B(r)+tau whenever one exists.
This is an exact pathwise scalar factorization plus the two-state occupation law.
If B0 has purely imaginary nonzero eigenvalues +-i omega, omega>0, then after a
single fixed real similarity and time scale omega the pair is
B0/omega=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],
B1/omega=eta H+s J=[[eta,-s],[s,-eta]], eta>=0, s real, H=diag(1,-1).
The transformed switching rate is rho=r/omega. Thus (after removing traces) every
pair with a nonzero elliptic matrix reduces to two real parameters eta,s.

Proof of trace shift. Let c_i=tr Ai/2 and C(t)=integral_0^t c_{I_s}ds.
The fundamental matrix equals exp(C(t)) times the one for Bi: differentiate on
sojourns and use the commuting scalar factor and continuity at jumps.
The two-state symmetric occupation law gives C(t)/t->(c0+c1)/2=tau almost surely.
Fixed similarity preserves exponential norm growth since its condition number is
constant. Rescaling time t'=omega t divides both matrices and rate by omega and
scales the original exponent by omega.

Proof of elliptic canonical form. Cayley-Hamilton for a traceless real B0 gives
B0^2=-omega^2 I. Choose any real nonzero vector v; vectors v, B0v/omega are linearly
independent, since dependence would give a real eigenvalue. In that basis B0=omega J.
Every real traceless B1 in this basis decomposes uniquely into s0 J+R, where
s0=(B1_21-B1_12)/2 and R is symmetric traceless, R=[[a,b],[b,-a]].
Any real symmetric traceless R has eigenvalues +-eta0 with eta0=sqrt(a^2+b^2)>=0.
There is a determinant-one orthogonal matrix O (a plane rotation) with
O^T R O=eta0 H: select an orthonormal eigenbasis, flip its second eigenvector if
necessary to make determinant one. Every plane rotation commutes with J, so the
same O leaves B0 unchanged. Divide by omega to obtain eta=eta0/omega,s=s0/omega.
This transformation is fixed, independent of r, so preserves the full rate curve.

Exact diagnostic identities. Half the trace of (B1/omega)^2 equals eta^2-s^2;
half the trace of ((B0+B1)/(2omega))^2 equals [eta^2-(1+s)^2]/4.
Let k1=sqrt(max(eta^2-s^2,0)), kavg=(1/2)sqrt(max(eta^2-(1+s)^2,0)).
The symmetric occupation average of the individual spectral abscissae is k1/2.
Comparing these algebraic endpoints, kavg>k1/2 is possible only for s<-1/2
and eta>|1+s|; those two conditions are also sufficient. This statement compares
spectral abscissae only; it does not assert a stochastic slow/fast limit theorem.
For any traceless real Bi its eigenvalue spectral abscissa is sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)).
A scalar shift Ai=Bi-ai I is Hurwitz exactly when ai exceeds that abscissa.
Consequently a fixed scalar damping average abar can make BOTH Ai Hurwitz if and
only if abar>(k0+k1)/2: necessity by summing ai>ki; sufficiency choose
ai=ki+abar-(k0+k1)/2. No condition on the averaged matrix is required.

Non-result: the two-parameter curve is not proved unimodal. This reduction helps
separate an actual Hurwitz-only search from an unnecessarily stable-average search.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:383fff664b083531fd9875bbc9b5c71c0f80d084bc72a1271d76e6a30ea40474","revision_digest":"sha256:c800e2e5ac4a159efd0bbfbb4710f53f8c474e0744d25c16014a6e5d0f200358","source_id":"own-work:w658:E0018-C3-v1","source_revision":"owner-work://brain_workers/w658/proofs/E0018_C3_v1.md; exact v1 independently audited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: The number of primes up to x satisfies pi(x) ~ x / log x, equivalently pi(x) ~ Li(x), as x grows. Proved independently by Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin (1896) by showing zeta(s) has no zeros on the line Re(s) = 1; elementary proofs (Erdos, Selberg 1949) avoid complex analysis. The error term in the theorem is governed by the zero-free region - under the Riemann hypothesis the error is O(sqrt(x) log x).
title: Prime Number Theorem

[Lemma lem:prime-deleted-character-sum of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $X\geq2$ and $1\leq Y\leq X$.  Let $m,w,D\geq1$, and let $q,t\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $(t,D)=1$ and $wt\equiv q\pmod D$.
Let $P$ be a prime with $P\nmid D$, and put $\chi_m(\cdot)=(\frac{\cdot}{m})$.
Define
\[
\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)
=
\{\ell\mid m:\ \ell\text{ odd},\ v_\ell(m)\text{ odd},\
\ell\nmid q,\ (D,w,\ell)=1\}
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak m
=
\frac{m}{\displaystyle
\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)}(\sqrt\ell/2)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{M\in[X,X+Y]\\M\equiv t\ (\bmod D)\\P\nmid M}}
\mu^2(M)\chi_m(M)
\chi_m\left(\frac{wM-q}{D}\right)
&\ll
\sqrt X+\frac{\mathfrak mY}{mD}
+\frac{\log(2X)\sqrt{\mathfrak mY}}{\sqrt D},
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
with an absolute implied constant.

In the Gaussian linear-regression setting y=<x,theta*>+z, with independent x~N(0,diag(v_1,...,v_d)) and z~N(0,sigma^2), let n,d be positive integers, v_i>0, sigma^2>0, and theta*_i nonzero. Put a_i=v_i(theta*_i)^2 and b=sigma^2/n. For coordinate learning rates 0<=eta_i<=1/v_i define the deterministic surrogate risk of equation (2), Rbar_eta(t)=sigma^2+sum_i [a_i(1-eta_i v_i)^(2t) +b(1-(1-eta_i v_i)^t)^2], for integer t>=1. For any prescribed integer t_*>=1, choose eta_i=[1-(b/(a_i+b))^(1/t_*)]/v_i. Then each coordinate summand attains its minimum at t=t_*, and Rbar_eta(t_*)=sigma^2+sum_i a_i b/(a_i+b), the global minimum over all admissible coordinate rates and integer stopping times. These are oracle rates using the true signal coefficients and feature variances. This statement optimizes the source surrogate; approximating the random finite-sample prediction risk requires the separate hypotheses and conclusion of Theorem 1.

[Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564, 'Power-law and log-periodic degree tails for a family of probability generating function eq'] There exist $\theta>0$ and $M<\infty$, depending only on $p$, such that
\[
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M,
  \qquad
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D^*_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M^{j}.
\]
Consequently there are constants $C,c>0$ with
\[
  \mathbb{P}(D_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad
  \mathbb{P}(D^*_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad n\ge0,\ x\ge0 .
\]
title: Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564

body:
[Defi 15 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] A {\bf Ginibre Brownian motion} of size $N$ is an $\M_N(\C)$-valued diffusion process $Z^N(\cdot)$ of the form
    \[ Z^N(t) \equaldist \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(X^N(t) + \i Y^N(t) ) \]
    where $X^N,Y^N$ are independent Hermitian Brownian motions of size $N$.  Entrywise, this can be described simply: for $1\le i,j\le N$, 
    $\{\sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Re}Z_{i,j}^N, \sqrt{2N}\,\mathrm{Im}Z_{i,j}^N\}_{t\ge 0}$ are all independent standard Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}$.

    The random matrix $Z^N(1)$, whose entries are all i.i.d.\ complex normal random variables, is called a {\bf Ginibre Ensemble} first introduced in \cite{Ginibre1965}. Equivalently, the law of $Z$ has a density with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\M_N(\C)$ which is proportional to $Z\mapsto \exp(-N\mathrm{Tr}_N[Z^\ast Z])$.  Note that this density is invariant under $Z\mapsto UZV^\ast$ for any deterministic unitary matrices $U,V\in\mathrm{U}(N)$; thus, the law of the Ginibre ensemble is unitarily bi-invariant.
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2511.10535

At a fixed parameter theta, let a single-example gradient g have finite second moment, mean G=grad L(theta) and covariance Sigma=E[(g-G)(g-G)^T]. Let H=grad^2 L(theta), and assume G^T H G>0. McCandlish et al. define B_noise=tr(H Sigma)/(G^T H G). When G!=0, they also define B_simple=tr(Sigma)/||G||_2^2. These are different statistics in general. They coincide when H is a positive scalar multiple of the identity. For the mean of B independent identically distributed gradients, the gradient covariance is Sigma/B. Interpreting B_noise as a local quadratic turning-point scale requires the one-step quadratic model; identifying it with a global empirically optimal critical batch size is an additional modeling step. In particular a common scalar step size does not make curvature isotropic.

H is the loss Hessian; positive G^T H G for B_noise

[Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Consider  $\alpha>0$ and the following Hilbert space of space-time functions:
\begin{align}
\mathcal{H}_\alpha=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+, \mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)),  
\end{align}
    where $\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)$ is the Sobolev space introduced in Definition (sobo_def of the paper). On a complete probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{G},\mathbf{P})$ we define a centered Gaussian family $\{W(\phi); \phi\in \mathcal{H}_\alpha\}$, whose covariance is given by 
\begin{align}
\mathbf E\left[ W(\varphi) W(\psi)\right]
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+}\ \left\langle \varphi (t,\cdot) , \psi (t,\cdot)\right\rangle_{\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)}  dt \notag\\
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+} \int_{M^2} \varphi (t,x)  \psi (t,y)G_{2\alpha}(x,y)dxdy dt
\, ,
\end{align}
for $\varphi$, $\psi$ in $\mathcal{H}_\alpha$. This family is called the fractional Gaussian fields on $M$.
title: Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614

\frac{|F_{n,l}(\tau)|-l}{\sqrt{(1-1/m)l}}

\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal N(0,1).
$$

\[
|F_{n,l}(\tau)|=\sum_{i=1}^n c(i,\tau(i)).
\]
Thus $|F_{n,l}(\tau)|$ is a permutation statistic of the form considered by Hoeffding
[hoeffding1951combinatorial]. For every fixed $i$, there are exactly $l=n/m$ values of $j$ such that $i\equiv j \pmod m$.
Hence
\[
\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n c(i,j)=\frac1m,
\qquad
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n c(i,j)=\frac1m,
\qquad
\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^n c(i,j)=\frac1m.
\]
Therefore the centered array $d(i,j)$ in Hoeffding's notation is simply
\[
|d(i,j)|=\left|c(i,j)-\frac1m\right|\le 1.
\]
By Hoeffding's variance formula ...","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:f1f07be4859a77c40931acb6d683abdeb0f843b5a8f94943f80f582411bd771c","revision_digest":"sha256:c82c9f12432358c7e9b08a303814e263c05b86d0f4e9d527bf9a52437d150855","source_id":"arxiv:2604.23890","source_revision":"tex-as-downloaded-2026-09-07","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] For any~$s\in \{0,1\}$ we have the following inequalities.
    \begin{align}
        \phi[L_k(s)] &\les \pi_4(y/\delta,2^k y/\delta)\pi_1(\ep/\delta,y/\delta)^2, 
        && \text{for } k\in\{0,1,\dots,K\},  \\
        \phi[L_k(s)] &\les \pi_4(y/\delta,x/\delta)\pi_4(2^{2K-k}y/\delta,y/\delta)\pi_1(\ep/\delta,y/\delta)^2, 
        && \text{for } k\in\{K+1,\dots,2K\}. 
    \end{align}
    The above inequalities also works for~$R_k(s)$.
