[Definition 5 (Discrete Hessian and the $\De_i$ on $T_n$) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] Let $f: T_n \ra \R$ be a function.
\bit
\item Let $E_0(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_0\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +2, v_2 + 1)\}.$

\item Let $E_1(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_1\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 1)\}.$ 
\item Let $E_2(T_n)$ be the set of all parallelograms $e_2\subseteq T_n$ whose vertices are $\{(v_1, v_2),  (v_1 + 1, v_2+1),  (v_1, v_2 + 1),  (v_1 +1, v_2 + 2)\}.$ 
\eit

We define the discrete Hessian $\hess(f):E(T_n) \ra \R$ to be a  real-valued function on the set $E(T_n) = E_0(T_n) \cup E_1(T_n) \cup E_2(T_n)$ and the $\De_i$ from $\R^{T_n}$ to $\R^{E_i(T_n)}$ by 
\beq\lab{eq:A}
\hess f(e_0) := \De_0 f(e_0) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2) - f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 +2, v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_1) := \De_1 f(e_1) :=  - f(v_1, v_2) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2) + f(v_1, v_2 + 1) - f(v_1 + 1,  v_2 + 1).\nonumber\\
\hess f(e_2) := \De_2 f(e_2) :=  f(v_1, v_2) - f(v_1+1, v_2+1) - f(v_1, v_2 + 1) + f(v_1 + 1, v_2 + 2).\nonumber\\
\eeq
title: Discrete Hessian and the $\De_i$ on $T_n$

body: [Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{stationary} if for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ the law of the weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ is the same as the law of the translated weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega+z,\mathcal E_\omega+z,\sigma_\omega(\cdot - z),\theta_\omega(\cdot - z))_{\omega\in\Omega}$. We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{ergodic} if all events $A\in \mathcal{A}$ that are invariant under translations in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ have probability $\mathbb{P}(A)\in\{0,1\}$.
title: Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157

The approximate-error identity in Zeng--Lee arxiv2310.17513v3 detailed Lemma9 (PDF25-26), f_adapt(x)-f_target(x)=ReLU((LR_(RL)(E)-E)x), is false under its stated assumptions. A counterexample has width D=2, depth L=1, rank budget R=1, base W1=I, target W=diag(2,3), target bias0, and bounded input set X={(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}. Here E=diag(1,2), LR1(E)=diag(0,2), all required nonsingularity assumptions hold, yet no rank-at-most-one update and any choice of output bias can satisfy the displayed identity on all X. This refutes that identity, not Lemma2's exact-realization conclusion at its larger sufficient rank, Theorem3's exact expressivity theorem, or by itself every version of the separate quantitative bound.

Additive weight update rank at most1; arbitrary freely trainable bias
Target weights diag(2,3), target bias0, base weights I

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e47893a1d804d56f7bc3f4e254d7cbe4ca75d4d70b06dc24db8de738f8648886","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e4/e47893a1d804d56f7bc3f4e254d7cbe4ca75d4d70b06dc24db8de738f8648886.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:37558d05512a6be08552041d4732873e645041d66d1b9cfe7f9a5c858fd97486","bundle_entry_key":"draft-chebyshev-gp-transformer","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-chebyshev-gp-predictive-001","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"transformer approximation; Gaussian-process prediction","draft":"w727/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-chebyshev-relu-attention-gp-predictive-uniform-kl-w727","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"CURRENT AUDIT STATUS: independently checked proof, T336-w727-C002 v1; urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28 PASS in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. Exact proof SHA256 f367eed1f9fb01baee0dabd6f699b418c16bcc3a5ecdfc7182dae660291f3339. No novelty or Lean certification is claimed. The following original submission text retains historical pre-audit status notices.

# Target 1: accelerated finite-feature GP prediction

Claim T336-w727-C002 v1. Rung: proof (unaudited), subject to recorded checks. The full theorem is not Lean-checked and no independent audit or novelty certification is claimed.

The hardest step is realizing both Chebyshev recurrences in normalized ReLU attention, including the previous-iterate registers and variance readout. Section 4 specifies every head.

## 1. Statement

Fix integers p>=1 and n>=0, reals s>0, B>=0, R>0, eps>0, and a feature map z:X->R^p with ||z(x)||<=R. The zero-mean GP prior has kernel k(x,x')=z(x)^T z(x'). Observations have independent N(0,s) noise. A prior scale tau^2 is absorbed into z. The prediction concerns a new **noisy observation**, not the latent function value.

Input tokens supply any t<=n context pairs (z_i,y_i), |y_i|<=B, and one query q=z(x_*). Zero padding fixes N=n+1 tokens. The supplied feature encoding is specified in Section 4. Its computation from arbitrary raw inputs is not included in the size bound.

Use the bidirectional residual normalized ReLU-attention architecture of Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1, PDF page 5, Eq. (1):

    h_i^+ = h_i + (1/N) sum_heads sum_j ReLU(<Q h_i,K h_j>) V h_j.

Q,K,V are real D-by-D matrices. There is no softmax, layer normalization, or causal mask. Feed-forward blocks are identities. Define

    n_+=max(1,n), L=s+n_+R^2, kappa=L/s, M=nR^2B/s,
    delta=min(1/2, s/(2R^2), sqrt(s eps)/(1+M), s sqrt(eps)/R^2),
    T=ceil((sqrt(kappa)/2) log(2/delta)).

An attention-only transformer of width D=7p+4, depth T+2, and at most five heads per layer outputs (mhat,vhat) with vhat>=s and

    KL(N(m,v) || N(mhat,vhat)) <= eps

uniformly over all these contexts and queries. Here (m,v) are the exact posterior noisy predictive mean and variance. A dense parameter bound is 15(T+2)D^2+2D, including a linear readout. All weights depend only on the fixed bounds, never the observed inputs or labels. They are explicit in Section 4.

If R=0, (mhat,vhat)=(0,s) is exact and the formulas dividing by R are unnecessary. No training, ERM generalization, arbitrary raw-feature complexity, softmax approximation, or infinite-rank truncation theorem is asserted.

## 2. Posterior and spectral interval

Set A=s I+sum_i z_i z_i^T and b=sum_i z_i y_i. Completing the square in the standard-normal weight prior and Gaussian likelihood gives posterior weight mean A^{-1}b and covariance s A^{-1}, hence

    m=q^T A^{-1}b, v=s+s q^T A^{-1}q.

For every r, s||r||^2<=r^T A r<=(s+nR^2)||r||^2<=L||r||^2. Thus A is symmetric positive definite, spec(A) is contained in [s,L], v>=s, and

    ||A^{-1}b||<=nRB/s, ||A^{-1}q||<=R/s.

These are deterministic bounds and use no independence among context features.

## 3. Accelerated iteration and its error

Put c=(L+s)/2, d=(L-s)/2, a=c/d. Since n_+>=1 and R>0, d>0,a>1. Define Chebyshev polynomials C_0(x)=1,C_1(x)=x,C_{j+1}(x)=2xC_j(x)-C_{j-1}(x).

For a right-hand side f start x_0=x_{-1}=0. Let eta_0=1/c,beta_0=0 and, for j>=1,

    eta_j=2C_j(a)/(d C_{j+1}(a)), beta_j=C_{j-1}(a)/C_{j+1}(a).

Take T updates

    x_{j+1}=x_j+beta_j(x_j-x_{j-1})+eta_j(f-Ax_j).

Every denominator is positive: for zeta=a+sqrt(a^2-1)>1 the polynomial recurrence gives C_j(a)=(zeta^j+zeta^{-j})/2>0.

For x*=A^{-1}f, induction gives

    x*-x_j=r_j(A)x*,
    r_j(lambda)=C_j((c-lambda)/d)/C_j(a).

At j=0 this is the identity; at j=1 it is 1-lambda/c. For the induction, C_{j+1}(a)+C_{j-1}(a)=2a C_j(a) gives 1+beta_j=eta_j c. Substitution in the error recurrence then gives exactly the recurrence for C_{j+1}. All coefficients are fixed independently of A and f.

For lambda in [s,L], (c-lambda)/d is in [-1,1]. By the cosine addition formula and induction, C_j(cos theta)=cos(j theta); thus |C_j(x)|<=1 there. Also

    zeta=(sqrt(kappa)+1)/(sqrt(kappa)-1), rho=zeta^{-1} in (0,1).

Orthogonal spectral decomposition gives ||r_T(A)||_op<=1/C_T(a)<=2rho^T. With u=1/sqrt(kappa) in (0,1),

    log((1+u)/(1-u))=integral_0^u 2/(1-x^2) dx>=2u.

The denominator is positive throughout the integration interval. Hence 2rho^T<=2exp(-2T/sqrt(kappa))<=delta by the stated T.

Apply the iteration simultaneously to f=b and f=q, with final iterates w_T,u_T. It follows that

    ||w_T-A^{-1}b||<=delta nRB/s,
    ||u_T-A^{-1}q||<=delta R/s.

Furthermore u_T=g_T(A)q, where g_T(lambda)=(1-r_T(lambda))/lambda. Since |r_T(lambda)|<=delta<=1/2 and lambda>=s>0, g_T(lambda)>0, so q^T u_T>=0.

## 4. Explicit attention heads

Each token contains seven p-dimensional registers

    (z_c,z_q,qbar,w,u,w_old,u_old)

and four scalars (y,one,mout,vout), for D=7p+4. Every token has one=1. Context i has z_c=z_i,z_q=0,y=y_i. The query has z_c=0,z_q=q,y=0. Padding has z_c=z_q=0,y=0. All working registers and mout start at zero; vout=s. This is a fixed role-dependent feature encoding with no query label.

Specifying linear Q and K coordinate lists of equal length and a linear V output defines ordinary D-by-D matrices, with all unspecified coordinates zero. Constant scores use the register one.

**Broadcast layer, one head:** Q=one,K=one, and V writes N z_q into qbar. Exactly one token supplies z_q, so after the normalized sum qbar=q on every token.

The four iterate registers are identical on all tokens at initialization. The following layers preserve that invariant.

**Solver layer j, five heads:** All expressions below use pre-layer registers; eta=eta_j,beta=beta_j.

1. Q=(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes N eta z_c into w. Its score is y_j-z_{c,j}^T w_i.
2. Q=-(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes -N eta z_c into w.

Together these write eta sum_i z_i(y_i-z_i^T w), by ReLU(r)-ReLU(-r)=r.

3. Q=u,K=z_c. V writes -N eta z_c into u.
4. Q=-u,K=z_c. V writes N eta z_c into u.

Together these write -eta sum_i z_i z_i^T u.

5. Q=one,K=one. V writes the following, with **no N factor**:

       beta(w-w_old)-eta s w        into w,
       beta(u-u_old)+eta(qbar-s u)  into u,
       w-w_old                     into w_old,
       u-u_old                     into u_old.

The normalized sum in head 5 is the average of identical registers and equals the displayed expression. The residual connection makes the old registers equal to the pre-layer w,u. Summing all five heads produces exactly the recurrences of Section 3 for f=b,q. Context, feature, label, constant, and output registers are unchanged. Query and padding contribute zero to the data sums because z_c=y=0. This proves the invariant and exact implementation by induction.

**Readout layer, four heads:** Q=qbar,K=w,V writing one into mout, and Q=-qbar,K=w,V writing -one into mout, together produce q^T w_T. The factors 1/N cancel the sum over N identical w registers. Likewise Q=qbar,K=u,V writing s one into vout, paired with Q=-qbar,K=u,V writing -s one into vout, produces s q^T u_T. The preexisting vout=s supplies the noise floor. Thus the query token outputs are exactly

    mhat=q^T w_T, vhat=s+s q^T u_T>=s.

This is T+2 layers and at most five heads. Counting three D-by-D matrices per head gives the parameter bound. There is no nonlinear readout computing products or inverses outside the transformer.

## 5. Uniform forward KL

The errors obey

    |m-mhat|<=M delta<=sqrt(s eps),
    |v-vhat|<=R^2 delta<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)).

For the mean inequality use M/(1+M)<=1, also when M=0. Both variances are >=s. Put h=(v-vhat)/vhat, so |h|<=1/2 and 1+h>0. The exact Gaussian formula is

    KL=(h-log(1+h))/2+(m-mhat)^2/(2vhat).

For h in [-1/2,1/2], h-log(1+h)=integral_0^h x/(1+x) dx<=h^2. If h>=0, use x/(1+x)<=x. If h<=0, reverse the integral and use |x/(1+x)|<=2|x| on [h,0]. All denominators remain >=1/2. Consequently

    KL<=|v-vhat|^2/(2s^2)+|m-mhat|^2/(2s)<=eps.

All estimates hold for every admissible context and query. There is no conversion from a prior-averaged loss to uniform KL.

## 6. Prior work and boundaries

Bai et al., arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1 (PDF page 5), supplies the architecture. Theorem 4 (PDF page 7) and Appendix D.1 supply known GD ridge point prediction with three heads and depth proportional to the condition number. Those facts are settled and are not claimed anew. The construction here combines classical Chebyshev iteration with exact attention operations to obtain simultaneous mean/variance and an explicit uniform KL budget. Novelty remains subject to literature and independent review.

The feature-input qualification is essential. A bounded finite-rank kernel on a compact set alone imposes no continuous or efficiently computable feature map on the raw inputs. A raw-input theorem needs additional regularity and an explicit feature-computation cost. Assume $0<c<1$ and put
$$
y_c=\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{c}.
$$
For $t\in\mathbb R$, define
$$
H(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{t}e^{-x^2}dx.
$$
This is the distribution function of the centered Gaussian law with density
$\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^2}$, or equivalently of a normal random variable with
variance $1/2$.
Then
$$
\frac{
B_{n,c}((-\infty,y_c+t/\sqrt{n}],L_n)
}{
B_{n,c}(L_n)
}
\longrightarrow H(t)
$$
in probability as $n\to\infty$.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6dc21933118a9f085b795fb1aaf07524e88fe68721ab07b9b0e6059ed44e0498","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6dc21933118a9f085b795fb1aaf07524e88fe68721ab07b9b0e6059ed44e0498.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e5ef2edc6a2a6f3d1c5d6d828a2d52998c13cb4090f1de47795cb241700acbaa","bundle_entry_key":"relu-degeneracy","bundle_id":"population.t244-relu-angle-localization-001","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:gaussian-relu-atomic-degeneracy-path-coupling","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Exact atomic degeneracy and coupling over linearly many layers

Status: independently checked proof; reviewer PASS on the listed claim version. Target 1, technical support: removes the atomic degeneracy obstacle to a stopped/conditioned-kernel diffusion argument. This is one technical step, not a proof of the proposed SDE.

Assume a zero-bias width-n network with independent Gaussian weight matrices and ReLU, n>=2. Initial inputs are nonzero with angle theta_0 in (0,pi). Given nonzero nonproportional inputs with angle theta, define q=(pi-theta)/(2*pi). Let D be the event that one output vector is zero, or both output vectors are nonzero and have zero angle.

**One-step identity.**

    p_n(theta) = P(D|theta) = 2^(1-n) + (n-1) q^n <= (n+1) 2^-n.

Proof. P(X=0)=P(Y=0)=2^-n, and their intersection has probability q^n. Thus extinction contributes 2^(1-n)-q^n. Conditional on any fixed pattern of strict signs, the positive coordinates have an absolutely continuous density. Two nonzero nonnegative vectors can be proportional only if their positive supports agree. If that common support has size >=2, proportionality is a nontrivial polynomial equality (for two coordinates, X_i Y_j-X_j Y_i=0) and has probability zero. If the support is a singleton, proportionality is automatic. There are n such sign patterns, each with probability q^n. Add these disjoint probabilities. The bound uses q<=1/2. After the first surviving layer the angle is in (0,pi/2].

**Conditioned-kernel coupling.** Let P_n(theta,.) be the exact kernel, sending D to an absorbing cemetery state. Let Q_n(theta,.) be P_n conditioned on D not occurring, well-defined for n>=2 and theta in (0,pi). For any integer L, the path laws of P_n and Q_n started at the same angle satisfy, in the convention d_TV=sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|,

    d_TV(path_0:L(P_n), path_0:L(Q_n)) <= min(1, L (n+1) 2^-n).

Construct a step coupling while the chains agree: sample the P_n step. If it survives, use the same value for Q_n. If it dies, draw Q_n independently from its conditioned kernel and count a disagreement. The Q_n marginal is correct since its law is (1-p)Q_n+pQ_n. Each agreeing step disagrees with conditional probability at most (n+1)2^-n. The union bound proves the assertion. This is a per-step conditioned chain; it is not asserted to equal the original path law conditional on survival through L.

For L<=Tn the bound is T n(n+1)2^-n. Thus proving a weak path limit for Q_n is sufficient to prove the same weak path limit for the killed P_n chain (with any common embedding of its cemetery state).

**Limit of this repair.** Removing the atom does not ensure inverse-angle integrability. On the positive-probability event that both vectors have exactly the same two-coordinate support, the continuous angle density is positive near zero, and E[1/theta' | D^c] is still infinite. [Theorem 1 (Duflo (1997), Theorem 1.3.15) of arXiv:2606.21111, 'On Elephant Random Walk with Delayed Amnesia'] Let $\{M_n, \mathcal{F}_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a square-integrable martingale with predictable quadratic variation $\{\langle M\rangle_n\}_{n\ge 0}$. Also, let $\langle M\rangle_\infty=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle M\rangle_n$. Then,\vspace{.1cm}\\
\noindent{(i)}  $\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n=M_\infty$ a.s. on $\{\langle M\rangle_\infty < \infty\}$, where $M_\infty$ is a finite random variable, and\vspace{.1cm}\\		
\noindent{(ii)}  $\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n/\langle M\rangle_n=0$ a.s. on $\{\langle M\rangle_\infty = \infty\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 2 (Self-loop erasure and finite absorption) of arXiv:2605.09641, 'The Ballot Event for Two-Player Coupon Collection: A Renewal--Catalan Asymptotic'] Consider the original simultaneous-round chain, stopped when it first reaches the success boundary for $A$, the unsafe boundary $g=-1$, or the simultaneous terminal point $(d,0)$.  If one deletes all rounds in which neither distinct-coupon count changes, then the induced sequence of nonself transitions is a Markov chain whose transition probabilities are proportional to the three weights displayed below.  Consequently all hitting probabilities of these absorbing sets are unchanged by self-loop erasure.

Moreover, the changed-state chain is absorbed after at most $2d-(2s+g)$ nonself transitions when started from an interior state $(s,g)$.  In particular, all stopping times below are almost surely finite and bounded by $2d$.

[Proposition 43 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $a\in C([-L,L])$. For every fixed $0\le m<1$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\frac{\cH(c\sigma^{m-1})}{\sigma^m}
-\max_{[-L,L]}a+o(1)
\]
and
\[
\lim_{\sigma\to0}\frac{\sigma}{|\log\sigma|}\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\frac{c(1-m)}{R_+}.
\]
If, in addition, for some $K>0$ and $\nu>1$,
\[
J(R_+-t)=Kt^\nu(1+o(1))\quad\hbox{as }t\downarrow0,
\]
then, with $p=\nu+1$ and $A=K\Gamma(p)$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\frac{c}{R_+\sigma}
\left[
(1-m)|\log\sigma|+p\log|\log\sigma|+C_{m,c,J}+o(1)
\right],
\]
where
\[
C_{m,c,J}=\log c+p\log(1-m)-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1.
\]

Since
\[

\sigma^{-m}c\sigma^{m-1}=\frac c\sigma,
\]
the leading edge asymptotic for $\cH$ yields the normalized limit.

For the refinement put $A=K\Gamma(p)$. Laplace's method at the right edge yields
\[
M(s)=Ae^{R_+s}s^{-p}(1+o(1)),\qquad
M'(s)=R_+Ae^{R_+s}s^{-p}(1+o(1)).
\]
Thus, for $M'(s(v))=v$,
\[
R_+s(v)=\log v+p\log\log v-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)+o(1),
\]
while $M(s(v))=v/R_++o(v)$. Therefore

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \label[definition]{def:finitebasics}
    For a finite graph $G$ and $\lambda\ge 0$, the \emph{hard-core model on $G$ at fugacity $\lambda$} is the probability measure $\mu_{G,\lambda}$ on $\cI(G)$ such that
    \[ \mu_{G,\lambda}(I) = \frac{\lambda^{|I|}}{Z_G(\lambda)}. \]
    
    When the graph and fugacity are clear from context, we consider $I\sim\mu_{G,\lambda}$, identify a vertex $u$ with the indicator random variable for the event $u\in I$, and write $\overline{u}$ for the indicator of $u\notin I$. Then $\mu_{G,\lambda}(u)$ is the marginal of $u$ and $\mu_{G,\lambda}(\overline{u})=1-\mu_{G,\lambda}(u)$.
    
    In keeping with statistical physics terminology, we refer to the state of a vertex $u$ being in or out of an independent set as the \emph{spin} of $u$. One can think of an independent set $I\in\cI(G)$ as an assignment of spins in $\{0,1\}$ to the vertices of $G$ such that vertices in $I$ receive spin $1$ and vertices in the complement of $I$ receive spin $0$.
    For convenience when working with this formulation, we write $\Omega(G)$ for the set of functions $\sigma:V(G)\to\{0,1\}$ such that $\sigma^{-1}(1)\in\cI(G)$.

Convention $\hat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}dx$. (a) (Always, as an $L^1$ identity) If $f\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, the periodization $Pf(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)$ converges absolutely for a.e. $x$, $Pf\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ with $\|Pf\|_{L^1(\mathbb T)}\le\|f\|_1$, and $\widehat{Pf}(k)=\hat f(k)$ for all $k\in\mathbb Z$. (b) (Pointwise identity) If in addition $\sum_nf(x+n)$ converges for every $x$ to a continuous function and $\sum_k|\hat f(k)|<\infty$, then $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i kx}$ for every $x$; taking $x=0$, $\sum_nf(n)=\sum_k\hat f(k)$. (c) (Convenient sufficient condition) If $f$ is continuous and there are $C,\delta>0$ with $|f(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ and $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|)^{-1-\delta}$, then (b) applies and both series converge absolutely; this holds for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. (d) Scaled and multidimensional forms: for $T>0$, $\sum_nf(nT)=T^{-1}\sum_k\hat f(k/T)$; for $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ and the lattice $\mathbb Z^d$, $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i k\cdot x}$; more generally for a full-rank lattice $\Lambda$ with dual $\Lambda^*$ and covolume $|\Lambda|$, $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(\lambda)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\sum_{\mu\in\Lambda^*}\hat f(\mu)$. Classic application (Jacobi theta transformation): $\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2t}=t^{-1/2}\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2/t}$ for $t>0$.
(a): f integrable on R
(b): the periodization converges everywhere to a continuous function AND the Fourier transform is absolutely summable over the integers
(c): f continuous with (1+|x|)^{-1-delta} decay of both f and its transform
integrability alone does NOT give the pointwise identity

[Theorem 31 (Combined clumsy-careless collector) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] For fixed $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$,
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        \frac{1}{(S;S)_\infty}
        \frac{n!}{n^n}Q^nS^{n(n+1)/2}.
\]
If $T_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ is the first post-thinning completion time from the empty collection, then
\[
        \mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \Rightarrow \Exp(1).
\]
Moreover, for every fixed $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb\bigl(\mu_n^{\alpha,\beta}T_n^{\alpha,\beta}\bigr)^r\to r!.
\]
Consequently,
\[
        \Ebb T_n^{\alpha,\beta}
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty
        \frac{n^n}{n!}Q^{-n}S^{-n(n+1)/2},
\]
and
\[
        \Var(T_n^{\alpha,\beta})
        \sim
        (S;S)_\infty^2
        \left(\frac{n^n}{n!}\right)^2
        Q^{-2n}S^{-n(n+1)}.
\]

Let T be a triangulation of an n-dimensional simplex Delta^n with vertices v_0, ..., v_n. Suppose the vertices of T are colored with {0, 1, ..., n} such that each vertex of T lying on a face of Delta^n is colored with the index of one of the vertices spanning that face. Then T contains an odd number of fully colored n-simplices (simplices whose vertices receive all n+1 colors).
T is a simplicial triangulation of Delta^n
Coloring satisfies Sperner boundary condition

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): (S14 (33),(33a),(34).) Choosing floor(n/2) disjoint cycle edges and using their NAE constraints gives n - log_2 L_n >= floor(n/2) * log_2(4/3). With beta = log_2(4/3), for n >= 14 one has 2*beta*floor(n/2) >= beta(n-1) >= (n+2)/3 >= ceil(n/3); the middle inequality holds at n = 14 and thereafter the left side has larger slope because beta > 1/3. The ten remaining values 4 <= n <= 13 follow from (L_4,...,L_13) = (7,11,18,29,47,76,123,199,322,521). This proves ceil(n/3) <= 2(n - log_2 L_n) for all n >= 4. Notes: beta = 0.4150375 > 1/3 is the whole slope argument. Re-verified here for 4 <= n <= 200 (no violations), well beyond the proof's own split at n = 14; the ten small cases were checked individually and all hold.

[Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ be two finite sets, $\rho$ and $\gamma$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ respectively, and $f: \Omega \to 2^{\Sigma}$ be a function\footnote{Here, $2^{\Sigma}$ is the power set of $\Sigma$.}. For each $\eta \in \Sigma$, let
    $f^{-1}(\eta):=\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \eta \in f(\omega)\}.$
     Suppose that $ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega, \eta \in \Sigma} \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)] > 0$ and then define a coupling probability measure on $\Omega\times\Sigma$ by
	\[\mathscr{P}[\omega,\eta]\propto \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)],~\forall (\omega, \eta)\in\Omega\times\Sigma. \] 

	\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$, denoted by  $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]  \propto \gamma[f(\omega)]\rho[\omega]$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. 
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$, denoted by $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta] \propto  \rho[f^{-1}(\eta)] \gamma[\eta] $ for each $\eta \in \Sigma$.   

\item[(c)] For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]\neq 0$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot | \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is $\gamma[\cdot \mid f(\omega)]$.
        \item[(d)]   For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot|\eta] $ on $\Omega$ is $\rho[\cdot \mid f^{-1}(\eta)]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765

body: Z^2 bond FPP with iid weights in [a, b], 0 < a <= b. Let T_+ denote the passage time between two wall points confined to the upper half-plane H. Then for every r >= 1, P(T_+ - E T_+ >= t sqrt(r)) <= exp(-a t^2 / (8 b^3)) for t in (0, 4 b^2 sqrt(r)/a). Derivation: modified log-Sobolev tensorization over the edge weights (BLM Theorem 6.15 applied conditionally), the deterministic bound #G_+ <= (b/a) r on the number of edges lying in every H-geodesic (from subpath optimality and the weight band), and Herbst-Chernoff with lambda in (0, 1/b]. The deterministic edge-count bound makes any variational choice of an auxiliary parameter redundant; the earlier form of this lemma carried such a parameter and a constant of a/(16 b^3), and an independent referee (2026-08-10) confirmed all constants and derived this two-fold improvement by removing the parameter outright. The lower tail is NOT covered by this route.

body:
For probability mass functions p and q on a finite set and an event A with p(A) > 0 and q(A) > 0, d_TV(p(.|A), q(.|A)) <= d_TV(p, q) / max(p(A), q(A)). In particular, if p(A) = q(A) = a, conditioning on A multiplies the total variation distance by at most 1/a. The constant is sharp: for all masses a, b in (0, 1] and every conditional distance c with max(a, b) c >= |a - b| there are laws with these values for which equality holds.

[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(K\) be a \(G\)-field and let \(\chi:G\to K^\times\) be a \(1\)-cocycle.
  If \(z\) is transcendental over \(K\), then the formula
  \[
    \gamma(z)=\chi(\gamma)z\quad(\gamma\in G)
  \]
  extends the action on \(K\) to a \(G\)-field structure on \(K(z)\).
  If \(D\trianglelefteq G\), \(\chi|_D=1\), and \(D\) acts trivially on \(K\), then \(D\) acts trivially on \(K(z)\).

body: For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For delta < 2 the boundary point 0 is reached and a boundary convention (absorbing or instantaneously reflecting) must be specified; for delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0 and no convention is needed. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI]

Let $f$ be a weakly stabilizing functional on finite simplicial complexes satisfying the moment condition. Then there exists $\sigma^2 \in [0, \infty)$ such that for every sequence of cubes $(W_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $W_n \to \mathbb{R}^d$, $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{Var}(f(\Delta_{W_n}))}{|W_n|} = \sigma^2$. Furthermore, if the limiting random variable $Z$ associated with $f$ satisfies $\mathbb{P}(Z \neq 0) > 0$, then $\sigma^2 > 0$.

[Proposition 3 (Final-size reduction through susceptibility heterogeneity) of arXiv:2608.22122, '2608.22122'] Assume that
\[

\]
and compare the heterogeneous epidemic with the homogeneous model
\(\Lambda\equiv 1\), keeping \(\tau\), \(\gamma\), and the initial condition
\((s_0,\iota_0,r_0)\) fixed. Let \(A_\infty\) and \(r_\infty\) denote the
limiting cumulative infection pressure and removed proportion in the
heterogeneous model, and let \(A_\infty^{\rm hom}\) and
\(r_\infty^{\rm hom}\) denote the corresponding quantities in the
homogeneous model. Then
\[
A_\infty\leq A_\infty^{\rm hom},
\qquad
r_\infty\leq r_\infty^{\rm hom}.
\]
If the law of \(\Lambda\) is nondegenerate and \(\iota_0>0\), the inequalities
are strict.

body:
Fix finitely many inputs x^1,...,x^m in R^n_in and a finite T>0. For clarity restrict to a positive definite input Gram matrix V_0^{alpha beta}=<x^alpha,x^beta>/n_in. All layers have width n, zero biases, and mutually independent standard Gaussian weight entries. Equivalently, start from this deterministic V_0 and, conditional on V_l, draw n independent Gaussian m-vectors G_i with covariance V_l; update V_{l+1}^{alpha beta}=(c_n/n) sum_i phi_n(G_i^alpha)phi_n(G_i^beta). This is the covariance Markov chain of the Gaussian network, up to the harmless first-layer index shift. Let d_n/n tend to T. Choose fixed real c_+,c_-, slopes s_+=1+c_+/sqrt(n), s_-=1+c_-/sqrt(n), phi_n(x)=s_+ max(x,0)+s_- min(x,0), and c_n=(E[phi_n(g)^2])^(-1) for standard Gaussian g. Then V_{floor(nt)}, with upper-triangular entries viewed as a vector, converges in distribution on finite time intervals in the Skorohod topology to the covariance diffusion dV=b(V)dt+Sigma(V)^(1/2)dB, started at V_0. For alpha<=beta and gamma<=delta, Sigma_{alpha beta,gamma delta}(V)=V^{alpha gamma}V^{beta delta}+V^{alpha delta}V^{beta gamma}. Set rho_{alpha beta}=V^{alpha beta}/sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta}), nu(rho)=(c_+-c_-)^2/(2pi) [sqrt(1-rho^2)-rho arccos(rho)], and b_{alpha beta}(V)=sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta})nu(rho_{alpha beta}). The limiting scalar outputs at time T, conditional on V_T, form a centered Gaussian vector with covariance V_T; their unconditional law is the resulting Gaussian mixture. This result concerns width-dependent shaped activations and does not assert the same covariance diffusion for ordinary fixed ReLU.
A fixed finite collection of inputs with positive definite normalized Gram matrix (explicit restriction of the source)
Independent iid N(0,1) weights, no biases, constant width n
Fixed c_+,c_-; slopes 1+c_+/sqrt(n),1+c_-/sqrt(n)
Exact Gaussian variance normalization c_n; depth/width tends to finite T

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), novelty unresolved. For fixed real PSD H with h=tr(H)>0 and L=lambda_max(H)>0, SPD M with m=lambda_min(M), and row-Stiefel flow Ydot=M^(-1)YH(I-Y^TY), captured energy a=tr(HY^TY) obeys 0<=adot<=2La/m and a(t)<=a(0)exp(2Lt/m). If G is r-by-p iid standard Gaussian, M=GG^T and Y(0)=M^(-1/2)G, then for delta_G,delta_O>0 with sum<1 and p>=4r(r+1)/delta_G, E q(t)>=(1-delta_G-delta_O)h[1-r exp(4Lt/p)/(p delta_O)]_+, where q=h-a. For p>=16r(r+1), rank(H)=r, positive eigenvalues in [mu^2,1], and 0<rho<1, any integer C029 entry quantile T satisfying sup_spectrum E q(T)<=rho mu^2/64 must satisfy T>(p/4)log(p/(8r)). This concerns reduced time only; it is not an original-GD lower bound or the missing Gaussian entry upper bound.

Gaussian corollary uses G standard normal, 1<=r<=p, positive delta_G and delta_O with sum<1 and stated dimension threshold

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d746d249960c14956818a55178d85e8db1a9f5857398be1c88ff6d492fee9a04","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d7/d746d249960c14956818a55178d85e8db1a9f5857398be1c88ff6d492fee9a04.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7a29374bdacee610e730cb3d6e0e30dadb9ac76fb670940ae67e269565dc983d","bundle_entry_key":"weighted-stiefel-capture-growth","bundle_id":"population.t419-weighted-stiefel-capture-delay-022","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Weighted Stiefel gradient flow and Gaussian random subspaces","draft":"w705/bundle_022.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.riemannian:weighted-stiefel-captured-energy-growth-and-gaussian-entry-delay","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C036 v1: a necessary reduced-flow entry time

Kind: bound. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.
This is a diagnostic for C029's reduced-flow entry quantile, not an
original-GD hitting-time theorem or a scored frontier move. The hardest
open piece remains an upper bound on Gaussian basin-entry time that can
be transferred to original GD with useful constants.

Let H be a fixed real PSD p-by-p matrix of positive trace h and largest
eigenvalue L>0. Let M be SPD r-by-r, 1<=r<=p, and let Y(t) solve

    Y'=M^(-1)YH(I-P), P=Y^T Y, YY^T=I_r.

Write m=lambda_min(M)>0, a(t)=tr(HP(t)), q(t)=h-a(t).
For t>=0, the deterministic captured-energy bound is

    a(t)<=a(0) exp(2Lt/m),
    q(t)>=max{0,h-a(0) exp(2Lt/m)}.

Indeed X=YH(I-P) gives a'=2 tr(M^(-1)XX^T). Since P is an orthogonal
projector, XX^T<=YH^2Y^T in PSD order. Also H^2<=LH, hence

    0<=a'<=2/m tr(YH^2Y^T)<=2L a/m.

Gronwall proves the assertion. In particular, if a(0)>0 and a trajectory
reaches q<=b with 0<=b<h and a(0)<h-b, its hitting time is at least

    (m/(2L)) log((h-b)/a(0)).

If a(0)=0, the same differential inequality makes a stay zero, so the
positive-capture threshold is never reached. No division by a(0) is
used in that case. When a(0)>=h-b the lower bound is simply zero.

## Gaussian initialization, without multiplying event probabilities

Let G be r-by-p iid standard normal, M=GG^T and
Y(0)=M^(-1/2)G; full row rank holds almost surely. For any
delta_G,delta_O>0 with delta_G+delta_O<1, suppose

    p>=4r(r+1)/delta_G.

Then with probability at least 1-delta_G-delta_O, simultaneously

    m>=p/2,  a(0)<=r h/(p delta_O).

To verify the first event, the diagonal Gram entries have variance 2p,
and its r(r-1) off-diagonal entries have variance p and mean zero.
Thus E||GG^T-pI||_F^2=p r(r+1). Markov gives
P[||GG^T-pI||_op>p/2]<=4r(r+1)/p<=delta_G.
The norm event implies m>=p/2.

For the second event, G has a right-orthogonally invariant law. Its
rank-r row projector P(0) consequently has mean (r/p)I: invariance
makes the expectation scalar, and its trace is r. Therefore
E a(0)=(r/p)h, and Markov yields the asserted upper-tail bound.
These two events need not be independent; their intersection is
bounded by a union bound. On it, for every t>=0,

    q(t)>=h [1-r exp(4Lt/p)/(p delta_O)]_+.

This gives both a simultaneous-in-time probabilistic lower envelope
and the unconditional expectation bound

    E q(t)>=(1-delta_G-delta_O) h
             [1-r exp(4Lt/p)/(p delta_O)]_+.

The discarded event contributes a nonnegative residual; no conditional
expectation is replaced by an unconditional product.

## Consequence for C029's particular quantile

Take delta_G=delta_O=1/4 and p>=16r(r+1). Normalize the singular values
of the exact rank-r target to lie in [mu,1], 0<mu<=1, so H has
eigenvalues lambda_i^2 and zeros, h>=r mu^2 and L<=1. Put

    t0=(p/4) log(p/(8r))>0.

For every t<=t0 the preceding expectation bound gives
E q(t)>=h/4>=r mu^2/4. For any 0<rho<1, C029's integer T satisfying
sup_lambda E q(T)<=rho mu^2/64 must therefore obey T>t0, because
r mu^2/4>rho mu^2/64. This lower bound is uniform over the normalized
spectral box, including repeated and unequal positive eigenvalues.

This shows an intrinsic dimension-dependent delay in that *reduced*
entry quantile. It does not identify its optimal order, supply the
missing upper bound, or lower-bound original GD: translating a reduced
lower bound requires separate tracking and error-margin estimates.

Sources: C029 reduced equation and quantile definition; direct
Gaussian second moments (also used in C032), projector invariance,
PSD trace inequalities and Gronwall. Prior-art status and independent
audit are unresolved; the flat-spectrum special case is not claimed
as new.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7e53973b7646342ce69fff35bbd9fbecd9bafebd0aa1ecb1c07691eed626ae95","revision_digest":"sha256:c8a0a3f38e88cff19ec66fb9e1edada064b5d69bbff2244522162e44e193b645","source_id":"own-work:T419-C036:v1","source_revision":"v1-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2511.13559, 'Asymptotic analysis of rare events in high dimensions'] Suppose $D$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assume:D} and let $D_\la$ be as in~\eqref{D-Dla}. Let $R=24+6(\log\la)/d$, fix an arbitrary constant $c_{\psi}$, and suppose
\begin{align}
R\e\max(1,\delta_2(R\e),\delta_3(R\e))&\leq \min\left(1/3,\rho_0\right),\\

(\delta_2^2+\delta_3^2+\delta_4( R\e))\frac {d^2}{\la} &\leq c_{\psi},
\end{align}
where $\rho_0$ is as in Assumption~\ref{assume:D}. Then
\bs
\mathbb P\left(\mathcal N\left(0_{d+1}, \,I_{d+1}\right)\in  D_\la\right) &= \frac{e^{-\la/2}\left(1+\Rem_1\right)}{\sqrt{2\pi\la\det H}},\\
|\Rem_1| &\leq C(c_\psi,\tfrac{\log\la}{d}) \left(\left(\delta_2^2+\delta_3^2 +\delta_4( R\e)\right)\frac{d^2}{\la} + \frac1\la\right).
\es (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
{\rm e} ^{-16\delta -2M}\leq \frac{{\rm{d}} (g_{\ast}\Theta_1)}{{\rm{d}} \Theta_1}(\xi, \eta)\leq {\rm e} ^{16\delta +2M}.
\]
where, $M$ is the constant for which $(G,d_{{\mathcal G}})$ is $M$ quasi-ruled. In particular, the measure $\Theta_1$ is quasi-invariant under the action of $G$ on $\partial^2 G$.

[Theo 2 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] Let $h>0$. Fix   a bounded operator $A$ in $L^2(\R^n)$. Let 
      $ \sigma _h^{\rm Wick} (A)$  and  $\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A $ be respectively the Wick symbol  and 
      the  Berezin symbol of $A$ defined in  (\ref{symb-Wick}) and (\ref{Foll}). 
      Then, 
      
      i)  We have, for every $(X,Y)\in\R^{4n}$,
      
    \be   (\partial _{x_j } + i \partial _{\xi_j }) 
    (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A) (X , Y) = 0 ,\quad
     (\partial _{y_j } - i \partial _{\eta_j })
       (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A)    (X , Y) = 0.\ee 
      
      
      ii) The following equality holds true, $$ 
       \forall\,X\in\R^{2n},\  (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A)  (X , X) = 
    \sigma _h^{\rm Wick} (A) (X).$$
      
      iii) If  $A\in C_h$ then we have,
      
      $$ \forall\, (X,Y)\in\R^{4n},\ | (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A) (X , Y)   | \leq d_hA (X-Y) 
      e^{ \frac { 1 }  { 4h } |X-Y|^2  } .$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] For the standard cohomogeneity-one adjoint action of \(SU(3)\) on \(S^7\),
there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isometric smooth invariant Einstein
metrics.  They may be normalized by
\[
 \Ric(g_n)=6g_n,
\]
and have principal orbit \(SU(3)/T^2\) and two singular orbits
\(\mathbb{CP}^2\).

More precisely, the metrics can be chosen so that, if \(b_n\) denotes the
scale of the initial singular orbit and \(\beta_n\) its anisotropy parameter,
then
\[
 b_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \beta_n\longrightarrow c_*<0,
\]
where \(c_*\) is the Ricci-flat threshold of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  Moreover, the sequence may be indexed so that, for some phase constant
\(\theta_*\in\mathbb R/\pi\mathbb Z\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{15}}2\log\frac1{b_n}
 =n\pi+\theta_*+o(1),
\]
and consequently
\[
 \frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}\longrightarrow e^{-2\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
\]
Let \(h_2\) denote the nonnormal Einstein metric on \(SU(3)/T^2\)
whose Ricci-flat cone is
\[
 dr^2+r^2h_2,
 \qquad
 f_1=f_2=\frac r{\sqrt5},\quad
 f_3=\sqrt{\frac25}\,r,
\]
and let \(g_{\RF,*}\) be the complete Ricci-flat threshold metric of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  If \(p_n^\pm\) are points on the two
singular orbits, then
\[
 (S^7,b_n^{-2}g_n,p_n^\pm)
 \longrightarrow (M_*,g_{\RF,*},p_*)
\]
in pointed smooth Cheeger--Gromov sense.  On the complementary scale,
\[
 g_n\longrightarrow dt^2+\sin^2t\,h_2
\]
smoothly locally on \((0,\pi)\times SU(3)/T^2\).  Finally, there are
constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
 c b_n^{-2}\le \sup_{S^7}|\Rm(g_n)|\le C b_n^{-2}.
\]
Let \(K_{02}^{(n)}\) denotes the sectional curvature of \(g_n\) in the
two-plane spanned by the radial direction and a unit vector tangent to
the third isotropy summand. At eithe singular orbit,
$$
 b_n^2K_{02}^{(n)}\longrightarrow-\frac{1+2c_*^2}{2}.
$$
Consequently,
$$
 \frac{|K_{02}^{(n+1)}|}{|K_{02}^{(n)}|}
 \longrightarrow e^{4\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main theorem

[Proposition guessing strategy symmetry of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $I_j^*=I_{n-j+1}^*$ for all $1\leq j\leq n$, that is, the best guesses in position $j$ and in position $n-j+1$ are the same.
    \begin{proof}
        From the vertical symmetry axis of $M$ described in Theorem $(positionmatrix of the paper)$, we have $p_{i,j}=p_{i,n-j+1}$, so the $j$th and $n-j+1$st columns are equal. Therefore, their argmaxes are equal.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    n\operatorname{dist}_{L^2(\gamma_n)}(g,\mathcal{H}_n)^2
  \end{equation}
  where $\mathcal{H}_n$ is the space of holomorphic functions on
  $\mathbb{C}^n$ that are in $L^2(\gamma_n)$.

body: [Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] Fix $(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)\in \Gamma_{\text{sub}}^k$ and let $r_1< r_m < r_2$ denote the three distinct real roots (each having a multiplicity of one) of $\Delta_k$ in $\mc S$. Then we have $t_{\text{mix}}^n = \Omega(\exp (\Theta(n)))$. Furthermore, for any  constant $p\neq r_m$ and any sufficiently small $\delta,\epsilon>0$, we have $\PP_p(T_{\text{enter}}^n(B_{\delta}({r^*}))>C\log n/\epsilon)\leq \epsilon$ for some positive constant $C$ and for all sufficiently large $n$  where $r^*=r_1\indic{p<r_m}+r_2\indic{p>r_m}$. For any $i\in \{1,2\}$, we also have $T_{\text{exit}}^n(B_\delta(r_i))=\Omega(\exp(\Theta(n)))$ w.h.p. for any starting state $X^n(0)\in B_{\delta/2}(r_i)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.11071

        \gamma_{u,n}(\xi)
        \right|
        \longrightarrow0
        \qquad(n\to\infty)
\]
almost surely on \(\mathcal{Z}_{K_1}\cap\{Z_\infty>0\}\).

body:
[Lem 32 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} does not hold, then in any local
   maximizer $(\vvvv,\xxxx,\vwww)$ of the function $F_\diamond$ defined by \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, the vector $\vwww$ must be entrywise positive.
\begin{proof}
    If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} does not hold, we have $\hv_1 > 0$, $\hx > 0$, or $\mu_1 < \alpha$. We assume for contradiction that $\vwww$ is not entrywise positive, and divide the analysis into a few cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 1:} $\hv_1 > 0$ or $\hx > 0$. In this case, let  $\www_{j_1}$ be a positive entry of $\vwww$, which must exist due to the constraint $(\mu,\vwww) = 1$. Now suppose for contradiction that we have $\www_{j_2} = 0$. For small positive $\delta$, the replacement
\[(\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2})
\mapsto \bigg(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta
    \bigg)\]
increases the value of the budget
    \[\frac1\alpha
    \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\]
by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$. It follows that we may replace $\vvv_1$ with $\vvv_1 + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, or $\xxxx$ with $\xxxx + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, while remaining inside the set $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$. Recalling
\eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, we can do this in a way which increases the value of $F_\diamond$ by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, contradicting the assumption that we were at a local maximizer.

\item \emph{Case 2:} $\hv_1 < 0$, $\hx \le 0$, and $\mu_1 < \alpha$.
We divide further into two cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 2a:} $\vvvv$ is not identically zero.
    As above, let $\www_{j_1} > 0$ and $\www_{j_2} = 0$.
    Further let $\vvv_{j_3} > 0$, and note that $\hv_{j_3} \le \hv_1 < 0$.
    Therefore the replacement
    \[
        (\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2},\vvv_{j_3}) \mapsto
        \lt(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta,
        \vvv_{j_3} - \Theta(\delta^{1/2})\rt)
    \]
    improves \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$.
    This gives a contradiction.

\item     \emph{Case 2b:} $\vvvv$ is identically zero. Then the constraints defining $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$ reduce to
 \beq
        
        1 + \xxxx \le \frac1\alpha \bigg(\sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\,, \quad
        (\mu,\vwww) = 1\,.\eeq
    Since $\mu_1 < \alpha$, we have $\vwww \neq (1/\mu_1, 0, \ldots, 0)$.
   Thus there must exist at least one index $j_1\ge2$ for which $\www_{j_1}$ is positive.
    If $\www_1 = 0$, then the replacement
    \[(\www_1,\www_{j_1}) \mapsto
        \bigg(\delta,\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta\bigg)\] improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}
while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
    Therefore we must have $\www_1 > 0$.
    Finally, if $\www_{j_2} = 0$ for any $j_2 \ge 2$, the replacement
    \[
        (\www_1,\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2}) \rightarrow
        \lt(\www_1 + \delta^{2/3}, \www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta^{2/3} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta \rt)
    \]
    improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{2/3})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
This concludes the proof.
\end{proof}

body: Let H be an inner product space with norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x,x>). If H is real, the inner product is recovered from the norm by <x,y> = (||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) / 4 for all x, y in H. If H is complex, <x,y> = (1/4) sum_{k=0}^3 i^k ||x + i^k y||^2, equivalently <x,y> = (1/4)[(||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) + i(||x+iy||^2 - ||x-iy||^2)]. Combined with the parallelogram-law characterization, this shows a norm comes from an inner product exactly when it satisfies the parallelogram law, and in that case the identity above is the only possible inner product inducing it. [standard, e.g. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Polarization Identity for Inner Product Spaces

[Theorem thm:exist of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] {\rm[Jan-Ras-20-aop]} There exists a probability space $(\widehat\Omega,\widehat{\mathfrak{S}},\widehat\mathbb{P})$,  equipped with an additive group of continuous bijections $\widehat{T}=\{\widehat{T}_x:x\in\mathbb{Z}^2\}$ and satisfying the hypotheses of Section (sec:probsp of the paper), on which there exists a stochastic process
\begin{align}    
    \bigl({\widehat B}^{h{\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}}}(x,y) : x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),\, {\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{+,-\}\bigr)
\end{align}
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}  [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt
\item \textup{(}No $\pm$ distinction at fixed $h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$, 
\[
\widehat\mathbb{P}\bigl\{{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,y)\bigr\}=1.
\]
When ${\widehat B}^{h-}({\widehat\omega},x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}({\widehat\omega},x,y)$, call the common value ${\widehat B}^h({\widehat\omega}, x,y)$.
\item \textup{(}Generalized Busemann function\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U), {\widehat B}^h \in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}$.  

\item \textup{(}Mean $-h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),$ $\widehat\mathbb{E}[{\widehat B}^h(0,e_i)] = -h \cdot e_i.$
\item \textup{(}Monotonicity\textup{)} For $h,h'\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$ with $h \cdot e_1 \leq h' \cdot e_1$, all $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost every ${\widehat\omega}$
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1)  
\]
and
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2).
\]
\item \textup{(}Left-/right-continuity\textup{)} For $\widehat\mathbb{P}$ almost all ${\widehat\omega}$, for all $h\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \nearrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) \qquad \text{ and } {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \searrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
\item \textup{(}Backward independence\textup{)} For any $I \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the random variables $\{\omega_x, {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) : y \geq x,\, x \in I,\, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)\}$ are independent of the  weights  $\{\omega_x : \forall z\in I , \, x  \not\geq z \}$ behind $I$.\qedhere
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:exist of arXiv:2507.08757

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have a family $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ of resistance metrics coupled with $\Gamma$ where $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}\colon (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \times (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \to [0,\infty)$. Then it is associated with a weak \clekp{} resistance form if and only if the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item The metric $\rmetres{C}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ is continuous with respect to $\dpathY$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. The conditional law of the collection $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ given $\Gamma\setminus\Gamma_{U^*}$ and $(\rmetres{V'}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V' \in \metregions[\C\setminus\ol{U}]}$ is almost surely measurable with respect to~$U^*$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. There exists a probability kernel $\mu^{U^*}$ such that for each $z \in \C$, the conditional law of $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U+z]}$ given $(U+z)^*$ is $(T_z)_* \mu^{U^*}(\cdot -z)$ where $T_z \FR(x,y) = \FR(x-z,y-z)$ denotes translation by $z$.

  \item Let $V,V' \in \metregions$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $x,y \in \ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$ such that for every $u \in V' \setminus V$ there is a point $z \in \ol{V}$ that separates $u$ from $x,y$ in $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$. Then
  \[ \rmetres{V}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V'}{x}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item Suppose that $V_1,V_2 \in \metregions$ with $\ol{V_1} \cap \ol{V_2} = \{z\}$ (where the closure is taken with respect to $d_{\ol{V}}$, see Section~\ref{subsec:main_results}). If $x \in \ol{V_1} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, $y \in \ol{V_2} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, then
  \[ \rmetres{V_1 \cup V_2}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V_1}{x}{z}{\Gamma} + \rmetres{V_2}{z}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item There exists a countable set $\{z_m\}_{m \in \N} \subseteq \Upsilon_\Gamma$ that is dense with respect to $\dpathY$ and such that the following holds. Suppose that $V \in \metregions$ consists of a single connected component and let $\CL \in \Gamma$ be a loop contained in $\ol{V}$ and intersecting $\partial V$. Then there exist two distinct points $a,b \in \CL \cap \partial V$ such that the following holds for sufficiently large $m \in \N$. Let $V_{a,b}$ (resp.\ $V_{b,a}$) be the collection of components of $V \setminus \CL$ that are connected to the counterclockwise arc of $\partial V$ from $a$ to $b$ (resp.\ from $b$ to $a$) by an admissible path within $V$. Let $A = \{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}$, $A_{a,b} = A \cap \ol{V_{a,b}}$, $A_{b,a} = A \cap \ol{V_{b,a}}$, and let $w, w_{a,b}, w_{b,a}$ be the weight functions associated with $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A}$, $\rmetres{V_{a,b}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{a,b}}$, $\rmetres{V_{b,a}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{b,a}}$, respectively. Then
  \[
   w(x,y) =
   \begin{cases}
    w_{a,b}(a,b)+w_{b,a}(a,b) ,& \{x,y\} = \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{a,b}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{a,b} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{b,a}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{b,a} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\
    0 ,& \text{otherwise.}
   \end{cases}
  \]
 \end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 25 of arXiv:2512.04807

[1 6 (\cite{HX24a}) of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] If the chain $X$ is ergodic, then its mean first passage times are all finite and satisfy 
\be

\mu_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}=1+\sum_{j \in S, j \ne i_1}\mu_{i_1ji_2\ldots i_{m-1}}p_{ji_2\ldots i_m}
\ee
for any $i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_m \in S$. In tensor form, (\ref{mfpteqn}) can be written as 
$$\mu={\cal E}+(\mu-\mu_d)\boxtimes {\cal P},$$
where $\cal E$ is the tensor of all ones and of the same size as $\cal P$, and where $\mu_d$ is the diagonal tensor obtained from $\mu$. Moreover, as a linear system, (\ref{mfpteqn}) is nonsingular if and only if the chain $X$ is ergodic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let g be a norm on R^2 that is even in the first coordinate (g(-h, m) = g(h, m)), as every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm is. For fixed m, the map h -> g((h, m)) is even and convex, hence minimized at h = 0, so g((h, m)) >= g((0, m)) = |m| g(e_2). Consequently, for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) with j = r + m, m > 0 (longitudinal overshoot past the far endpoint): g(v) + g((0,r) - v) - g((0,r)) >= (r + m) g(e_2) + m g(e_2) - r g(e_2) = 2 m g(e_2), and symmetrically for j = -m < 0. The dogleg excess grows at least LINEARLY in the overshoot, with the explicit constant 2 g(e_2), using convexity and symmetry alone - no curvature hypothesis of any kind. The bound is tight as h -> 0. Use: in localization arguments it kills union sites with longitudinal overshoot at a rate no curvature assumption needs to fund, letting curvature windows be quoted only where they are literally assumed. Numerical attack: 0 violations in 300,000 trials on an anisotropic convex norm, worst ratio 1.000019.

[Lemma 25 (Dirichlet append step) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $Y$ be a projection generated by a $d$-dimensional $p$-ball through the sign-Dirichlet representation. Appending one coordinate with coefficient $c\ge0$ gives
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde Y=(1-T)^\alpha Y+cT^\alpha\eps,
\end{equation}
where $\eps$ is a Rademacher sign and
\[
 T\sim\operatorname{Beta}(\alpha,1+d\alpha)
\]
is independent of $Y$ and $\eps$.

body: Ramsey's theorem (graph form): for every pair of integers r >= 1 and c >= 1 there is an N = R_c(r) such that ANY colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at least N vertices with c colours (c finite and fixed in advance) contains a monochromatic complete subgraph on r vertices. With unboundedly many colours the statement fails - colour every edge differently - so the finiteness of the palette is essential. R(3,3) = 6 is the party-of-six exemplar.
title: Ramsey's theorem

[Lemma lem:Modd of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Denote
\[
\mathcal{M}_D(z_1,z_2)
=
\mu^{\rm exc}_{D}
\bigl(\indx_\gamma(z_1)+\indx_\gamma(z_2)\text{ odd}\bigr).
\]
We have that
\[
\mathcal{M}_D(z_1,z_2)<+\infty
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{M}_D(z_1,z_2)
=
\lim_{\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0}
\mu^{\rm exc}_{D}
\bigl(
\indx_\gamma(z_1)+\indx_\gamma(z_2)\text{ odd},\,
\gamma\subset D_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)
\bigr).
\]
Further, we have the explicit formula
$$\exp\Big(-\frac{\pi}{4}\mathcal{M}_D(z_1,z_2)\Big) = \hat q$$

where $\hat q$ is the complementary nome to nome $q$ that is by Lemma (lem:parametr of the paper) uniquely defined via 
$$\exp\Big(\pi G_D(z_1,z_2)\Big) 
= \dfrac{\theta_3(q^{1/2})}{\theta_2(q^{1/2})}.$$
title: Lemma lem:Modd of arXiv:2604.15146
